title: Redaction: drop /PCAdded from rewritten content streams so redacted added text does not stay in the file
author: storybored379
body:
Text added with Edit ▸ Add content keeps its source string in the stream dictionary's /PCAdded.
Applying a redaction rewrote the stream's glyphs but copied the dictionary unchanged, so the
redacted text survived in the saved PDF (also after a full save and Remove Hidden Information).
The redacted item now stays as plain drawn content and is no longer editable.

title: Organize: deleted pages leave the file even when something still points at them
author: storybored379
body:
Delete Pages only took the pages out of the page tree. A bookmark or link that went to a
deleted page, or a form field with a widget on it, still referenced the page object, so a full
save kept the whole page — its content included — in the file (delete a confidential page
that has a link or bookmark to it, Save As, and its text is still there; only Sanitize removed
it). The form also kept the deleted page's fields, which still exported and filled.

The deleted page objects are now freed. Widgets on them leave the form, taking fields with no
widget left with them, and bookmarks and links that went to them lose that destination (they
already showed none) instead of pointing at a missing page.

title: Optimizer: Audit space usage counts images PrintCraft added as images

title: Forms: CSV import keeps values that span lines
author: storybored379
body:
A quoted CSV value may hold line breaks, and Export data writes multiline text fields that way.
The importer split the file into lines before reading quotes, so such a value was cut at its first
line break and every later column was lost: exporting a form with a multiline field to CSV and
importing it again silently dropped data.

CSV records now end only at unquoted line breaks (CRLF or LF); doubled quotes and quoted commas
work as before, and blank lines are skipped, so a header with no record is still rejected as an
unknown format. Tab-delimited text is read exactly as before.

### How it was found and tested
- Found while driving the headless MCP server (`printcraft-cli mcp`); repro: `form_export_data` to CSV with a multiline text field, then import.
- Regression test `csv_values_may_span_lines`; verified it **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.

title: Forms: multi-select list values survive XML, CSV and text import

title: Edit text: a paragraph's new colour no longer spills into the text after it
author: storybored379
body:
Rewriting a paragraph (`text_edit`, Format text) draws it in its own text object, then sets the
text state back for what follows, but not the fill colour. Changing one paragraph's colour
therefore also coloured every paragraph after it in the same content stream (recolour the first
paragraph of a page red and the rest of the page turns red).

The rewritten paragraph is now wrapped in `q … Q`, so its colour and any other graphics state
stay with it. The `q` goes in before the paragraph's `BT`, outside any text object.

### How it was found and tested
- Found while driving the headless MCP server (`printcraft-cli mcp`); repro: `text_edit` with a colour on paragraph 1 of a multi-paragraph page, then `page_render`.
- Regression test `a_new_paragraph_colour_does_not_spill_into_the_text_after_it`; verified it **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.

title: Edit text: a rewritten paragraph keeps its place in the text object it shares
author: storybored379
body:
A rewritten paragraph was drawn again just before the `BT` of its text object. When earlier
paragraphs shared that `BT … ET` (as on text-only pages), the paragraph moved ahead of them in the
content stream: reading order changed (screen readers, copy, `pdftotext -raw`) and
`text_paragraphs` renumbered, so after `text_edit` on paragraph 2, a following `text_edit` on
paragraph 1 rewrote the already edited paragraph instead of the first one.

When text shown earlier in the same text object stays, the text object is now split where the
paragraph was (`ET`, the paragraph, then `BT` again), and the second half resumes from the same
text line matrix and text state, so what follows is positioned exactly as before. Text objects
that start with the paragraph are rewritten as before.

### How it was found and tested
- Found while driving the headless MCP server (`printcraft-cli mcp`); repro: `text_edit` paragraph 2, then paragraph 1, then `text_extract`.
- Regression test `a_rewritten_paragraph_keeps_its_place_in_a_shared_text_object`; verified it **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.

title: Never crash: forms scripts can't overflow the stack or the date arithmetic
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §4). This PR fixes **real crashes a PDF can trigger**.

| Crash | Input | Fix | Regression test (failed before the fix) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stack overflow, which aborts the app (`catch_unwind` can't stop it) | A format script with deeply nested arguments, e.g. `AFNumber_Format([[[[…` or `new Array(new Array(…` | Parser nesting capped at 64 | `af::never_crash_tests::deeply_nested_script_arguments_are_rejected` (SIGABRT before) |

title: Never crash: hostile form scripts can't overflow the stack
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §4). This PR fixes a **real crash a PDF can trigger**.

**The crash:** boa (0.22) parses and compiles recursively, one level per nesting, with no depth limit of its own. About **100 nested parentheses** in a field or document-level script overflow a 2 MiB stack. On the 8 MiB main thread it takes a few hundred. The process then aborts, and `catch_unwind` can't stop that. Per level, measured on a 2 MiB stack: parentheses, arrays, functions and templates cost about 20 KiB; `!`, `-`, `?:`, `typeof` and `=>` about 2 to 7 KiB; `+` chains about 200 B.

**The fix:** `printcraft_js::run` now:
1. Refuses a script that no form needs: longer than 256 KiB, brackets nested more than 64 deep, more than 64 prefix operators in a row, or more than 4096 `?`. It skips strings and comments when counting. A refused script fails with an error, as a syntax error would.
2. Runs the engine on its own thread with a 1 GiB stack. That is address space, committed only as it's used. Together with the length limit it covers every construct that nests without brackets. If the engine panics, the script fails with an error and the app keeps running. On wasm the script still runs inline.

I checked worst cases just under the limit (`a=>`, `if(1)`, `typeof`, `a=`, `x**`, `new`, `void`, `1+` and `a.` chains of about 256 KiB): **none overflowed**. Some of them make boa's parser take minutes, though: `x**` 54 s, `a.` 22 min, and `a=`/`a=>` were still running after 25 min. That is a hang (denial of service), not a crash. I left it out of scope here and flag it for follow-up.

**Regression tests:**
- `deeply_nested_scripts_fail_instead_of_crashing` aborted the test process before this change.
- `ordinary_nesting_still_runs` checks that normal nesting, and brackets inside strings and comments, are unaffected.

## Checks
- On this branch alone: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test,…

title: Never crash: last-resort guard around edits, opens, saves and UI commands
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §4). The last-resort guard: a panic that escapes the rules becomes an error message, and the user's documents stay intact.

- `printcraft_engine::guard(f)` wraps `catch_unwind` and returns `Result<T, String>` with the panic message.
- `Session::apply`: the edit runs on a copy of the document (`next`), so a panic leaves the document unchanged and reports `… failed unexpectedly (…); the document was not changed`. A panic while refreshing the view after an edit rolls the edit back, using the existing rollback path.
- `Session::open`: the whole open (structure, form, marks, links, signatures) is guarded and a panic becomes `OpenError::Invalid`. The cos parse and the renderer were already guarded.
- `save_bytes`, `save_full_bytes` and `export_data`: a panic becomes a write error.
- `PrintCraftApp::execute` (every menu, toolbar, palette and shortcut command): a panic shows a notice and the app keeps running.
- The desktop app installs a panic hook that logs every panic to stderr, with a backtrace when `RUST_BACKTRACE` is set.

**Already in place:** autosave and crash recovery (`RecoveryStore`) for anything that still escapes, such as a panic inside egui's frame loop. Also `catch_unwind` around page rendering, inspection and attachment extraction in `printcraft-render`. `panic = "unwind"` is the default and nothing overrides it.

**Test:** `guard_turns_a_panic_into_an_error`.

## Checks
- On this branch alone: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm, assets, deny, parity): **all 8 steps pass** on a local merge of every never-crash branch onto `main` (8f1f4e7).

Independent of the other never-crash PRs and mergeable in any order; best after the steering PR #11. It touches no file that another open PR is changing.

title: Tests: frame budgets take turns and keep the best of three rounds
author: echelon
body:
The frame-budget tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/perf.rs` have been failing intermittently on the Ubuntu and Windows runners (41-52 ms average against the 40 ms budget; macOS passes).

- The two tests ran **in parallel**, each with its own render workers, on 3-4 vCPU runners. They now take turns (a `Mutex`, poison-tolerant).
- Each measurement is the **best of up to three rounds**, re-measured only when a round is over budget. Noise from other processes only adds time, so the best round is the UI's own cost; a real regression is over budget in every round and still fails.

title: Nightly fuzz: stop the runner's out-of-memory deaths (and the fuzzer's false passes)
author: echelon
body:
The nightly `fuzz (mutation, 15 min)` job has failed every night: the runner is killed a few minutes in ("The runner has received a shutdown signal") and the findings are lost.

**Cause.** Reproduced locally with the nightly's seed (41): fuzzed inputs drove a single `check-one` child to 2–6 GB, and the job runs two at a time on a 16 GB runner. Three allocation paths, all sized by the input:

| Where | What | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lopdf` (bootstrap inspector) | PNG predictor rows sized from `/Columns` before reading data: `/Columns 4294967295` → two 4 GiB rows | Vendored lopdf 0.45.0 (MIT) refuses rows longer than the data; saturating row widths. Load-time stream decoding also gets a 256 MiB limit (it had none) | `inspect::tests::png_predictor_rows_longer_than_the_data_are_refused_before_allocating` |
| `hayro` tiling patterns | Cell pixmap = `/XStep` × scale, bounded only by `u16` → 2 GB | Vendored patch `tiling_cell_scale`: cell ≤ 3000 px a side (lower resolution, same geometry) | `raster::tests::tiling_cells_stay_small_whatever_the_step` |

Each test fails without its fix. Patches are marked `PrintCraft patch:` and listed in `vendor/README.md`.

title: Issue #8: prefer the integrated GPU; the save prompt answers to the keyboard
author: echelon
body:
Addresses #8. Not verified on the reporter's hardware (NVIDIA Optimus), so the issue stays open until they confirm.

**Illegible window after screen lock (NVIDIA Optimus).** egui-wgpu defaults to `PowerPreference::HighPerformance`, so on hybrid-graphics laptops PrintCraft ran on the discrete NVIDIA GPU (the reporter's Plasma Optimus showed this). NVIDIA's driver can lose or corrupt GPU memory across suspend and screen lock unless video-memory preservation is enabled; corrupted textures (the font atlas) give exactly the garbled text, only partly fixed by resizing. PrintCraft now asks for the **low-power (integrated) adapter** unless `WGPU_POWER_PREF` is set. A PDF app has no use for the discrete GPU, and this saves battery; machines with one GPU are unaffected. Checked that the app starts and renders normally.

**Quit dialog ignored the keyboard.** "Save changes?" now takes:
- **Enter**: Save (the default button)
- **Escape**: Cancel
- **Cmd/Ctrl+D**: Don't save (macOS convention), and **Alt+D / Alt+N** (the mnemonics the reporter tried)

Two bugs underneath: the canvas consumed Escape before the dialog saw it, and command shortcuts still ran under the modal (Cmd+D opened Document properties behind it). The prompt's keys are now read first and nothing else runs while it is open.

Test: `editing::the_save_prompt_answers_to_the_keyboard` (each Don't-save key closes without saving and runs no command; Escape cancels; Enter saves the edit).

Workaround for 0.1.1 users: `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low printcraft`.

Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `test --workspace`, layers, wasm pass locally.

title: Issue #28: Help ▸ Check for updates (opt-in check at start)
author: echelon
body:
Addresses #28 (the update **checker**; see below for installing).

**What it does**
- **Help ▸ Check for updates…** asks GitHub for the latest release. If it's newer than the running version, the dialog offers **Download** (the release page, where every platform's installer is) or **Later**; otherwise it says the version is up to date, or why the check failed.
- **Check for updates when PrintCraft starts**: opt-in (off by default, since it contacts GitHub without being asked), remembered in settings, and silent unless a newer version exists.
- Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.

**How**
- `ui-egui` gets an `updates` module (version comparison, background thread, dialog) with **no network code**: the desktop app supplies the source; without one (web build, tests) the command opens the releases page.
- The desktop app makes one HTTPS request (`ureq` over rustls with the **OS's trusted roots** via `rustls-native-certs`, 10 s timeout, 1 MiB cap). The answer is untrusted: only a page under `github.com/storytold/printcraft/releases/` is ever offered.
- Licences: `webpki-roots`/`webpki-root-certs` (CDLA-Permissive-2.0) aren't on our allowlist, so no bundled root list; `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` passes.

**Not included: installing in place.** A self-updater must verify what it installs, which means signed release artifacts (code-signing certificates and a signing key), a maintainer decision. Until then, Download opens the release page.

**Tests**: `ui-egui/tests/updates.rs` (versions compare numerically; newer → Download/Later; up to date; failure message; the check at start is opt-in and quiet; the preference persists), `apps/printcraft/src/updates.rs` (answers parsed, only our release pages offered) plus an `#[ignore]`d live test, run once locally against GitHub. Parity entry `view.check-for-updates` (partial: no in-place install).

Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `test --workspace`, layers, wasm, assets, parity, deny pass locally.

title: Fix text editing layout and preserve source PDF font styles
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## Summary

This PR improves text editing for PDF page content and FreeText annotations, including automatic box resizing, source-style preservation, Japanese/CJK replacement support, and safer form-script generation.

Replacement text is no longer constrained by the original narrow bounding box, old text is removed cleanly, and edited content preserves the original PDF typography whenever possible.

## What changed

### Edit text & images

- Reprojects editor boxes during zoom, scrolling, and page rotation.
- Expands single-line editor boxes horizontally as replacement text grows.
- Preserves paragraph width for multiline text and reflows it vertically.
- Keeps editor geometry aligned with the original PDF text.
- Improves hover, active, and selected text-box states.
- Uses topmost hit testing for overlapping text regions.
- Removes duplicate or overlapping text copies that could leave old text or fake-bold artifacts visible.
- Preserves original leading, spacing, and source color when no formatting override is requested.
- Supports Japanese and other non-WinAnsi replacement characters without lossy `?` substitution.
- Generates a bounded Type3 fallback using Shippori Mincho glyph outlines when the original PDF font cannot encode the replacement.
- Adds `/ToUnicode` mappings so Japanese fallback text remains selectable, searchable, and copyable.
- Preserves the existing original-font fast path whenever the source font can encode the complete replacement.

- Detects source font family from PDF font metadata.
- Detects bold and italic styles from:

title: Never crash: JBIG2 images can't decode billions of pixels
author: echelon
body:
A fuzz run on `main` (cancelled partway by a merge) found a new hang in JBIG2 decoding: a symbol dictionary that decoded for minutes. In JBIG2 each bitmap side may be 65535, and up to 65535 symbols are decoded pixel by pixel.

Vendors **hayro-jbig2 0.3.0** (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) with two bounds, marked `PrintCraft patch:` and listed in `vendor/README.md`:
- at most **2^28 pixels per bitmap** (the renderer's `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`), including the page bitmap (`reinitialize`), the halftone grid and the grayscale image;
- at most **2^26 symbol pixels per symbol dictionary** (real dictionaries hold about a million).

The finding now finishes in about 1 s. Regression test `raster::tests::jbig2_regions_of_billions_of_pixels_are_refused`: a synthetic JBIG2 stream with a 65535 × 65535 page and generic region behind a small `/Width`/`/Height`; it timed out until the page-bitmap path was capped too.

title: Never crash: Type 1 font programs can't hang or overflow the stack (skrifa 0.47)
author: echelon
body:
The fuzz run on `main` after #43 found one hang, in **Type 1 font parsing**: `read-fonts` 0.39 (through `skrifa` 0.42, used by `hayro-interpret`) looked ahead after every integer token by parsing the next token, which looked ahead again, recursing through a whole run of numbers. A long run hung, and **20,000 numbers overflowed the stack and aborted the process**, a crash from any PDF with such an embedded font.

Upstream fixed the tokenizer (a non-recursive look-ahead). The vendored `hayro-interpret` now depends on **`skrifa` 0.47** (`read-fonts` 0.44), with its one API change (`Charset::glyph_id` returns `Option`). Recorded in `vendor/README.md`.

title: Issue #37: on Windows, draw with Direct3D 12 (OpenGL fallback), never load Vulkan drivers
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #37.

**Cause:** wgpu's default backends on Windows include Vulkan, and creating a Vulkan instance loads **every installed Vulkan driver** into the process. On the reporter's machine (Intel UHD 630 plus RTX 5060 Ti), Intel's Vulkan driver `igvk64.dll` crashed PrintCraft with `0xC0000005` before the window appeared. The reporter's own test confirms it: `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` also crashes (heap corruption), while `dx12` and `gl` start normally.

**Fix:** on Windows, PrintCraft now asks wgpu for **Direct3D 12, with OpenGL as fallback**. D3D12 is the native, best-supported backend there, so Vulkan drivers are never loaded. `WGPU_BACKEND` still overrides it. The low-power GPU preference from #8/#31 stays, in the same `configure_gpu` (`WGPU_POWER_PREF` overrides it).

**Test:** `gpu_backends_avoid_vulkan_on_windows_and_prefer_low_power` checks the configuration. It's a no-op off Windows, and the Windows CI job runs it. The crash itself can't be reproduced without that driver, but this is exactly the configuration the reporter confirmed works.

Workaround for 0.2.0 users until the next release: set `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`.

title: Edit text: move and resize existing text boxes (#40)
author: echelon
body:
Closes #40, requested by @TCB13.

In **Edit a PDF ▸ Edit text**:
- **Drag a paragraph's box to move it.** The box follows the pointer, and releasing applies the move.
- **Drag the handle on its right edge to resize it.** The paragraph rewraps to the new width, keeping its font, size, colour and line spacing.
- **A click still opens it for typing**, as before. Each move or resize is one undoable *Edit text* step.

**How:**
- `BlockStyle` gains `offset` and `width`.
- `rewrite_block` applies the move as a `cm` inside the paragraph's own `q … Q`, so nothing after it shifts. The `cm` is converted back through the CTM's linear part, so a page-space drag lands in the right place even when the text is drawn under a scaling or rotating `cm`. The CTM is now recorded at each line's origin.
- Untrusted numbers (the automation tool passes them through) are checked: non-finite values are refused, and widths are clamped between one character and 14 400 pt.
- The width handle only shows on upright pages: on a quarter-turned page, the screen's horizontal is the text's vertical.
- `text_edit` (automation, MCP) takes `dx`, `dy` and `width` too.

**Tests:**
- Engine `paragraphs_move_and_rewrap_to_a_new_width`: a move, a move under `0.5 0 0 0.5 0 0 cm` (it would land at half the distance without the conversion), a narrower and a wider rewrap, and non-finite and zero inputs.
- kittest `dragging_a_paragraph_moves_it_and_its_edge_rewraps_it`: real pointer drags for both gestures. It passed 15 of 15 local runs.
- Automation `editing_existing_text_through_tools`: the new arguments.
- I also rendered a headless move and rewrap to check visually.

Gates: fmt, workspace clippy `-D warnings` and all workspace tests pass locally. Parity: new `edit.text-move-resize`, shipped.

title: Export detected tables to office formats

## Summary

The Word/HTML/RTF exporters now detect tables in a page's text layout and emit real table markup instead of loose paragraphs.

A single-cell spanning row next to a multi-column run (a header band or totals row) joins the table, and missing cells become empty cells.

- `crates/export/src/lib.rs::two_column_body_text_is_not_mistaken_for_a_table` — false-positive guard.

No new dependencies or assets.

title: Signatures: RFC 3161 timestamps, document timestamps, DSS/VRI and revocation verification
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## Summary

Extends the `sign` crate from PAdES B-B toward B-T / B-LT / B-LTA: RFC 3161 signature timestamps, standalone document timestamps, a Document Security Store with per-signature VRI, and CRL/OCSP revocation verification wired into signature validation.

## Changes

- `timestamp` module: RFC 3161 request/response/TSTInfo parsing and validation (size-capped, imprint- and signature-checked), plus the TSA-side signer used by the deterministic test authority. `sign_with_timestamp` attaches the TSA token as an unsigned attribute over the signature value (PAdES B-T).
- The transport is the caller's: a `TimestampAuthority` trait. The crate never opens a socket, matching the network-free stance of the JS crate; a rejected or malformed token fails the signing before any file is produced.
- `timestamp_document` appends a standalone `/ETSI.RFC3161` document timestamp covering the whole file; validation discovers and verifies these dictionaries (imprint over the signed bytes, token signature, TSA certificate validity) and reports the trusted time.
- `dss::embed` merges caller-supplied evidence into the catalog `/DSS` with `/VRI` entries keyed per signature (uppercase-hex SHA-1 of `/Contents`), deduplicating byte-identical blobs against any existing store; the change classifier treats the store as a permitted incremental change.
- `revocation` module: RFC 5280 CRLs and RFC 6960 OCSP responses are parsed and verified (issuer/responder signature, delegated responder's OCSP-signing EKU, CertID hash match, validity windows); validation checks the evidence embedded in the DSS and a verified revocation invalidates the signature.
- Certificate-validity checks prefer the verified RFC 3161 time over the `/M` clock claim.
- Parity: `sign.pades-bt`, `sign.document-timestamp`, `sign.ltv`, `sign.pades-blta`, `sign.verification-time` and `sign.ocsp-crl` move from planned to partial with cited tests; the notes name what is still missing (evidence fetching, timestamp-server configuratio…

author: justinjohn0306
body:
## Summary

The non-network half of #63, split out per the review there. This PR contains everything from the timestamp/LTV slice that never opens a socket; the fetcher and tools wait for the network-policy decision and remain on #63.

## What's here

- `timestamp`: RFC 3161 request/response/TSTInfo parsing and validation (size-capped), the TSA-side signer behind the deterministic test authority, and `sign_with_timestamp` (PAdES B-T) with the transport behind the `TimestampAuthority` trait — no implementation of it ships in this PR.
- `timestamp_document`: the standalone `/ETSI.RFC3161` document timestamp; validation discovers and verifies these dictionaries.
- `dss::embed`: merges caller-supplied evidence into the catalog `/DSS` with `/VRI` per signature, deduplicating blobs; the change classifier treats the store as a permitted change.
- `revocation`: RFC 5280 CRL and RFC 6960 OCSP parsing/verification, checked against the DSS during validation.
- Engine methods (`sign_with_timestamp`, `timestamp_document`, `embed_ltv`) so the features are headless-reachable once a transport exists.

## Review items from #63 addressed here

- **OCSP encodings (blocker 4):** `good` is `[0] IMPLICIT NULL` (0x80), `revoked` is `[1] IMPLICIT RevokedInfo` (value is the RevokedInfo contents), `unknown` is `[2] IMPLICIT`, `nextUpdate` is `[0] EXPLICIT`, and `byKey` is `[2] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING` (unwrapped before hashing). The fixtures now use the real encodings.
- **Delegated responders:** the responder's certificate must verify against the issuer's key (in addition to the OCSP-signing EKU and issuer-name match) before its answer counts — forged "good"/"revoked" evidence from a minted certificate is rejected.
- **TSA trust anchoring (blocker 3, first step):** a document timestamp is only **Valid** when the TSA certificate chains to the trust store; otherwise the verdict is **Unknown** with an explanatory detail, and the same anchoring is applied to embedded signature-timestamp tokens vi…

title: Windows ARM64: fix the intermittent WARP crash in tests, remove the diagnostic job
author: echelon
body:
Follow-up to #66, which was merged before this fix and with my four temporary diagnostic commits in it.

**The crash:** on GitHub's Windows 11 ARM64 runner, `tests/view.rs` died with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` in about 1 run in 4. That would turn `main` red intermittently.
- **Where:** a crash dump analysed with `cdb` on the runner puts it inside Microsoft's WARP software GPU: `d3d10warp!PixelJitProgram::ClassifyVars`, on WARP's own thread pool, while compiling a shader. The runner has no GPU, so wgpu uses WARP.
- **Trigger:** the two tests that render pixels compiling shaders on two separate devices at once.
- **Evidence:**
  - single-threaded, or each test alone: 0 crashes in 180 runs;
  - in parallel: 7 crashes in 30;
  - in parallel with 16 MB thread stacks: 6 crashes in 30, so stack size isn't the cause.
- **Scope:** this isn't our code, and the app can't hit it: it has one device, on a real GPU.

**Fix:**
- Those two tests take a per-binary lock for their whole run, declared before the harness so it's released after the device drops. kittest creates its wgpu device lazily, on the first `render()`, so only rendering tests touch WARP. No other test binary renders from more than one test.
- The temporary `diag-view` job is removed. The workflow is now identical to its reviewed pre-diagnostic version.

title: Fonts: use craft-fonts as an optional build input; move the Japanese fonts out
author: echelon
body:
Moves PrintCraft's Japanese font out of the repo and makes [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) an **optional build input** ([craftrules `standards/fonts.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/fonts.md), recipe from craft-fonts' `docs/integration.md`). It is not in any `Cargo.toml`, and `build.rs` uses no network.

## What changes

- **Removed:** `assets/fonts/ShipporiMincho-Regular.ttf` (8,677,284 bytes) and `assets/fonts/OFL-ShipporiMincho.txt`, plus their two `[[asset]]` entries. Inter, JetBrains Mono and Dancing Script stay. The `[[fetched]]` Shippori entry used by `cargo xtask demo-pdf` stays as it was, because that is a pinned download and not a committed file.
- **`printcraft-fonts`** (the lowest crate both the editor and the UI use) has the `build.rs` recipe and `CraftFont`/`CRAFT_FONTS`.
  - `SHIPPORI_MINCHO` is now `Option<&[u8]>`, filled from `CRAFT_FONTS`.
  - `shippori_glyph` is now `japanese_glyph`. It reads `document_japanese_font()`, which tries Shippori Mincho, then BIZ UDMincho, then any `Jpan` face.
  - `GlyphError::NoFont` is new.
  - **On wasm32 only BIZ UDPGothic Regular is embedded.** Size figures are below.
- **Editing PDF text** (`printcraft-edit`): the Type 3 Japanese fallback draws its glyphs from the craft-fonts face, and `substituted` reports `"<family> Type3"`. If the build has no Japanese face, `replace_line` and `replace_block` return a clear `EditError::Invalid` and leave the page untouched. It never panics. There is no system-font fallback here because this layer has no font discovery.

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #70, reported by @SlayerSv.

**Before:** in two-page view, **Next page** (Ctrl/⌘ + →) went to the right-hand page of the spread already on screen. The view had nothing to scroll to, and the current page snapped back to the left-hand page, so it never moved. Previous page worked because it always lands on an earlier row.

**Now:** next and previous page step a whole spread at a time in two-page view, as Acrobat does:

title: Export to Word: files open in Word again (#72)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #72, reported by @joostiphone.

**Cause:** text extracted from a PDF can contain C0 control characters (common when a font has no usable `/ToUnicode` map). XML forbids them, and Word refuses the whole document over a single one, with exactly the reported message: *Word experienced an error trying to open the file.* I reproduced it by opening our exports in Microsoft Word.

**Fix (`printcraft-export`):**
- The Word, HTML and RTF writers drop the characters XML 1.0 forbids: C0 controls other than tab, line feed and carriage return, plus U+FFFE/U+FFFF. One `allowed()` check is shared by all three writers.
- **Long pages:** a till receipt is often taller than Word's 22 in maximum, and Word read that height as negative. The page size is now kept between 0.1 and 22 in. Margins shrink on small pages (at most ⅛ of the page) so text keeps room, and images fit the real text width instead of an assumed 6.5 in.
- A non-finite font size falls back to 12 pt.
- Zip entries get a valid DOS date (1980-01-01) instead of zero.

**Tests:**
- New `word_opens_text_with_control_characters_and_long_pages` inflates `word/document.xml` and checks the dropped characters, the 22 in clamp, the size fallback, the RTF text and narrow-page margins.
- **Checked in Microsoft Word (Windows, via COM):** before the fix, files with control characters or U+FFFF failed with the reported error. After it, they open, along with a 33 in receipt with a 40-row table, and narrow, tiny and wide pages.

Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and the export and engine export tests pass locally. Parity: `create.export-docx` (still partial) and `create.export-rtf` cite the new test.

title: macOS: open PDFs from Finder, Open With and the Dock (#73)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #73, reported by @KrzysztofKiser.

**Cause:** macOS doesn't pass a file opened from Finder, Open With or the Dock on the command line. It sends the app an *open documents* Apple event. winit doesn't handle that event, so AppKit's fallback answered *"PrintCraft cannot open files in the PDF document format"*. The bundle also declared no PDF document type: its `Info.plist` still carried the image-editor types it was copied from (`.pcraft`, PSB, QOI).

**Fix:**
- **`Info.plist`:** declares PDF (by extension and MIME type) as a document type, role *Editor*, rank *Alternate*. PrintCraft appears under **Open With** and can be made the default (Get Info ▸ Open with ▸ Change All), without taking over from the system's viewer on install.
- **`apps/printcraft/src/apple_events.rs`:** registers *open documents* and *quit* Apple-event handlers before the launch event arrives, so a double-click that starts the app is caught too. The Objective-C interop needs `unsafe`, which the workspace forbids, so this uses `fmv-macos-events` (`=0.1.0`, MIT OR Apache-2.0), the same small audited wrapper PhotoCraft uses, pinned exactly. winit's application delegate is left alone.
- **`printcraft-ui-egui`:** new `OsEvent` and `PrintCraftApp::os_events`, polled every frame. *Open* opens each file the way File ▸ Open does. *Quit* (the Dock's Quit, logging out) closes the window like its close button, so unsaved changes are still asked about.

A second commit cleans up the other leftovers from the image editor: the `.deb`/`.rpm` description, the AppStream categories, keywords and screenshot (it now lists `application/pdf` and points at one of our screenshots), the MSI comment and the web embedding example.

**Tests:** kittest `files_and_quit_from_the_operating_system` feeds `OsEvent::Open` with a real file path (the file opens in a tab) and `OsEvent::Quit` (the window is asked to close).

title: UI: sharper, higher-contrast text, most visible on Windows (#76)
author: bflatastic
body:
Refs #76, reported by @Hasin-ai. Also confirmed by @nrunje.

**Blurry text.** egui renders each glyph at one of four quarter-pixel horizontal offsets ("sub-pixel binning"). Its own docs note this makes text blurrier. It's most visible at the 100–150 % display scaling common on Windows, where one point is one or two pixels. Glyphs now sit on whole pixels.

**Low contrast.**
- In the light theme, egui blends glyph edges linearly, so dark text reads thin and grey next to the system's own text. A mild gamma (0.75) on coverage darkens the edges. The dark theme keeps egui's own curve.
- The faintest text colour (hints, the zoom level, captions) was 3.3:1 on white and 3.9:1 in the dark theme, below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for small text. It's now `#6B6B73` / `#97979E`.
- New test `theme::text_is_readable_on_every_surface` computes the WCAG contrast of `text`, `text_muted` and `text_faint` against `chrome`, `panel`, `card` and `pasteboard` in both themes, and requires 4.5:1.

**How I checked:** I made headless renders (`--example shot`) of the Home view with each candidate setting at 1× and compared zoomed crops. At 1×, pixel-aligned glyphs give visibly crisper stems, and the 0.75 gamma adds weight without looking bold. egui's dark-mode curve looked too heavy for light mode. At 2× (Retina, 200 %) the difference is negligible.

**The console window** in the issue title was fixed in 0.2.1 by #58. I checked the published 0.2.1 x64 and x86 builds: `printcraft.exe` is a GUI-subsystem program. Only `printcraft-cli.exe` (the command-line tool shipped beside it) opens a console.

**Not changed:** egui's text rasteriser has no ClearType-style sub-pixel (RGB) antialiasing. That would be an egui-level change, so PrintCraft's text will stay greyscale-antialiased.

Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `xtask parity` and the ui-egui lib and `ui` tests pass locally. Parity: `view.theme-light-dark` cites the new test.

title: Add text: clicking elsewhere keeps the text and starts a new box (#74)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #74, reported by @KrzysztofKiser.

**Cause:** with **Edit a PDF ▸ Text**, clicking elsewhere on the page replaced the box being typed with a new empty one, and the text was lost. A real mouse click usually reaches egui as press and release in the same frame. The page handled that click, and opened the new box, before the in-place editor noticed its text box losing focus, so the old draft was simply overwritten. Synthetic test clicks spread the press and release over two frames, which hid the bug.

**Now:**
- **A click elsewhere keeps the box being typed and starts a new one** where you clicked, as the issue asks. The page click finishes the open box first, using one `finish()` shared with the editor. Both input timings end the same way, so the Text tool no longer drops back to Select after one box.
- **✓ Done and ✕ Discard** sit beside the box being typed, as the issue also suggests. Done keeps the text and goes back to Select. Discard (or Escape) throws it away. Pressing either one doesn't count as a click away.
- The box just kept isn't left selected while you type the next one, so the Format panel styles the new text.
- The Edit panel's hint mentions the new flow.
- Clean-up: `content_ui::page_input` returns a `bool`. Its `Outcome::done` was never set.

**Tests:**
- New kittest `clicking_elsewhere_keeps_the_text_and_starts_a_new_box` covers a slow click (press and release in separate frames), a quick one (both in one frame), and Discard.
- `typing_moving_styling_and_deleting_added_content` now finishes with Done.
- **Real app on Windows**, driven with OS mouse and keyboard input (`SendInput`) through the control channel: before the fix, *Hello* vanished when I clicked elsewhere. After it, *Hello* and *World* both stay and a third box opens with ✓/✕.

Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `xtask parity` and every ui-egui test binary pass locally. Parity: `edit.add-text` cites the new test.

title: fix: print: read lpstat untranslated so printers show on non-English macOS
author: rutkk
body:
On a Mac whose interface language isn't English, the Print dialog listed no printers except for Print to PDF. `lpstat -p -d` follows the UI language (here Polish: "drukarka … jest bezczynna", "domyślny cel systemowy: …"), and parse_lpstat only knows the English "printer " and "system default destination:" prefixes, so it matched nothing.

- lpstat currently runs with LC_ALL=C and LANG=C, which is enough on Linux. macOS CUPS ignores both and follows AppleLanguages unless the SOFTWARE environment variable is set, in which case it uses LANG. This PR fixes this issue by setting the SOFTWARE environment variable.
- New test: localized output parses to nothing, and the command sets all three variables.

Checked on macOS with a Polish UI: only SOFTWARE=1 LANG=C gives English output, and the dialog now lists every printer with the right default and successfully prints.

title: Security: ask before opening links from documents (#90, #91)
author: jcl-bit
body:
Fixes #90, fixes #91.

## Problem
A PDF could open any address without asking: a link click, a push button's URI action, a one-line button script that `button_script` maps to a URI action, or `app.launchURL` from JavaScript (which is on by default). That let a document send form data to an outside site, or hand `file:`, `smb:` and app-handler addresses (`ms-settings:` etc.) to the operating system.

## Change
All four paths now go through one gate, `PdfCraftApp::request_document_url`. PdfCraft's own links (Help, About, updates) still use `open_url`.

- `engine::links::document_url` accepts only `http`, `https` and `mailto`, up to 2048 characters. It refuses control, zero-width, bidi-override and non-space whitespace characters, malformed schemes, and web addresses without a host. Plain spaces are allowed outside the host, because real documents use them (`mailto:...?subject=Order form`).
- Accepted addresses wait in an "Open this web page?" dialog (or "Write this email?" for mailto). It shows the host the address really goes to and the full address. `engine::links::host` drops `user:password@` and treats `\` like `/` the way browsers do, so `https://a.example\@b.example` shows `a.example`, not `b.example`.
- Cancel is the highlighted button, and Escape or clicking outside cancels. While one request is waiting, further ones are dropped, so a script can't stack up dialogs.
- Refused addresses are reported in a notice and never opened.
- Preferences ▸ JavaScript now says a script needs permission to open a web page, which resolves the wording mismatch noted in #90.

## Tests
- Engine unit tests for the address policy and host parsing, including the userinfo and backslash spoofs.
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/document_links.rs` drives the real link click, button URI action, button one-line script, `app.launchURL`, Cancel and Escape paths. All of them fail against the previous code.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows x64 (731 tests, after rebasing onto the PdfCraft r…

Fixes #96. Since issue #8, the desktop app always asks wgpu for the low-power GPU. title: Add middle-click scrolling and select-all in Organize Pages

title: Add faux-redaction audit (paint-order and colour-aware, fail-closed)
author: ejbarraza
body:
## What this adds

A document-verification check for the "is this PDF actually safe to share?" question: a **faux-redaction audit** that detects opaque rectangles drawn over text that is still extractable underneath, plus `/Redact` annotations that were marked but never applied. A properly applied redaction removes the text, so it never flags.

Reworked per the Oct 8 review — this is now **audit-only** (the sanitize-for-sharing half is dropped; #162 covers it):

- **Paint order**: a rectangle counts as a cover only when painted strictly *after* the text it overlaps. Positions come from walking the page's content streams joined (one stream in pieces, §7.8.2), so each rectangle records `(content-stream index, operator index)`; rectangles inside a form XObject carry the `Do` operator's position.
- **Colour-aware**: the WCAG contrast ratio between the text colour and the cover must be below 3.0. Page backgrounds, table shading and highlight marks no longer flag.
- **Fail closed**: `audit_redactions` returns `Result`. Undecodable content streams (`decoded_strict`) and malformed `/Annots` are errors, never an empty finding list; the operator bound is an error, not a silent truncation.
- **State across streams**: one graphics state walks the whole joined stream, so a `cm` or fill colour set in an earlier stream is still in force later (#150). Form XObjects still isolate their state at `Do`.
- **Parity**: `protect.audit-faux-redactions` is marked `partial`, not shipped.

## Wiring

- New `pdfcraft-audit` crate (`crates/audit/`).
- Engine: `Document::audit_redactions() -> Result<Vec<AuditFinding>, String>`.
- Automation: `doc_audit_redactions` tool (read-only).
- CLI: `pdfcraft-cli audit <file.pdf>` prints findings as JSON and exits 1 when any are found, so CI can gate on it.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit`: 9 passed, including new tests for paint order (`background_before…

title: M3: Add middle-click autoscroll on Linux
author: Frumpy9
body:
Adds middle-click scrolling to the document viewer and Organize Pages grid in the Linux desktop app.

Click the mouse wheel once to toggle scrolling on, then release it and move the pointer up or down to scroll. Click the wheel again or press Escape to stop.

A Chromium-style speed curve gives gentle scrolling near the initial click and accelerates farther away. Returning within 15 screen points of that click pauses immediately while keeping scrolling enabled. Scrolling follows elapsed frame time to keep its speed consistent across display refresh rates and document zoom levels.

This makes long documents easier to navigate on Linux without repeatedly turning the wheel or dragging the scrollbar. Middle-button scrolling does not activate editing tools or change page selections.

The custom scrolling handler is enabled only for Linux. Windows and other targets retain their existing middle-button input behavior.

title: Render: round page rasters up so the last partial row and column are drawn (#102)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #102.

At 72 dpi an A4 page (595.28×841.89 pt) rendered as 595×841, where pdftoppm gives 596×842. The whole-page render passed hayro no size, so hayro floored the scaled page size. Anything touching the right or bottom edge lost its last partial pixel at every resolution.

- `printcraft-render`:
  - A new `device_pixels(pt, scale)` rounds up. It ignores float noise up to 1/100 px, so Letter at 150 dpi stays 1275 px.
  - The untiled render passes this size to hayro as width/height, still capped at `MAX_SIDE`.
  - The partial edge pixels are anti-aliased against the white page.
- `printcraft-ui-egui`: the canvas tile grid uses the same helper instead of `round()`. Tiled pages now get tiles for the partial row and column too.
- The vendored hayro is unchanged.

Testing:
- New test `raster::tests::fractional_page_sizes_round_up`, which fails (595×841) without the fix. It checks that a fractional MediaBox:
  - renders 596×842 with partly covered edge pixels;
  - renders 2481 px wide at 300 dpi;
  - gives a corner tile that matches the whole-page render.
- `printcraft-cli render a4.pdf --page 1 --dpi 72` gives 596×842, and `--dpi 300` gives 2481×3508.
- Pass:
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test` for render, engine, automation, optimize, ui-egui and cli. These are all the crates that depend on render.

title: Forms: check box and radio button styles (#94)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #94, requested by @KrzysztofKiser.

**Field Properties ▸ Options ▸ Check Box Style** (*Button Style* for radio buttons) offers **Check, Circle, Cross, Diamond, Square, Star**, the same six as Acrobat.

**How:**
- **Stored the standard way.** The style goes in each widget's `/MK /CA`, using Acrobat's ZapfDingbats codes (`4 l 8 u n H`), so other viewers draw the same mark. Styles set by other apps are read back the same way. The defaults are unchanged: a check for check boxes, a circle for radio buttons.
- **Drawn as paths.** PrintCraft draws the mark as vector paths (like the existing check and dot), so no symbol font is needed.

title: Windows: register PrintCraft as a PDF handler, so it can be the default (#107)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #107, reported by @nakamark-hub.

**Cause:** the MSI registered no file association for PDFs. In *Open with ▸ Choose an app on your PC*, the only "PrintCraft" a user could pick was the Start Menu entry. That entry is an *advertised* Windows Installer shortcut, not the executable, so Windows can't run it as a file handler: *"This app can't run on your PC"*. Launched normally, the app works, as the reporter's screenshots show.

**Fix:** the MSI now uses Windows' **Default Programs** registration, all under HKLM, written by the existing per-machine component:
- `Software\Classes\PrintCraft.Document`: the ProgID (*PDF Document*), its icon and `"printcraft.exe" "%1"` open command.
- `Software\Classes\.pdf\OpenWithProgids\PrintCraft.Document`, so PrintCraft is listed under **Open with**.
- `Software\Classes\Applications\printcraft.exe`: friendly name, supported types (`.pdf`) and open command.
- `Software\PrintCraft\Capabilities` (name, description, icon, `FileAssociations\.pdf`), listed in `Software\RegisteredApplications`, so it appears in **Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Default apps**.

It **never takes over an existing default**: `.pdf`'s own default value is untouched, so the user chooses, and Windows' own default-app protection stays in charge. Uninstalling removes the values with the component.

**Checked locally with WiX 5.0.2** (installed into a scratch folder, not globally):
- `wix build` succeeds.
- `wix msi validate` passes ICE validation. The only note is the existing ICE61, because same-version upgrades are deliberate.
- `wix msi decompile` shows exactly the 13 registry values above.

I didn't install the MSI on this machine. The release job builds and signs the real one.

**For the portable zip:** it installs nothing, so its users can still pick `printcraft.exe` itself (not a shortcut) in *Choose an app on your PC*.

title: M9: read BER signatures (DocuSign, Documenso); classify later changes narrowly
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
Real-world signatures (DocuSign, Telekom QES, Documenso) are BER: indefinite lengths and segmented OCTET STRINGs, which the strict DER reader turned away ("DER signature wrong" on a file Acrobat validates). Behind that, later revisions that add DSS data or rewrite the XMP were classified as tampering. This PR reads the BER and classifies later changes narrowly.

**Scope.** After the review it no longer contains algorithms (#386), CA checks, or trust sets; those are separate PRs, each based on `main`. `crates/sign` only, plus docs/parity.

## What changed
- **`cms`:** the CMS structure is read with `Tlv::parse_ber`, the reader #453 added for PKCS #12 (depth-bounded, segments joined). Certificates and signed attributes are still verified over their own exact bytes; signed attributes written with an indefinite length are re-encoded as DER first (RFC 5652 §5.4). The details say the signature was BER. High tag numbers are *not* read (this PR used to; nothing needs them).
- **`pdf`:** validation data added after signing is a permitted change, but only objects reached through `/DSS` `/Certs|CRLs|OCSPs|VRI` by the keys the standard defines, with the shape of their role, and new or only grown since signing.
- **`pdf`:** only the signed catalog's `/Metadata` is the document's XMP. A `/Type /Metadata` or `/Type /DSS` *label* on any other dictionary or stream, even one it already had when signed, makes nothing permitted.

## Review (echelon)
1. **`dss_objects` bypass:** fixed. `/DSS << /X 5 0 R >>` plus a rewrite of the page's contents stays "page content" (`a_dss_entry_does_not_make_the_object_it_names_part_of_the_store`, `an_existing_*`, at every DocMDP level).

3. **Built-in trust:** out of this PR (CA checks and trust sets are separate; the trust sets are opt-in, and the EU list is loaded at run time instead of embedded).

title: macOS: File ▸ Open and file pickers no longer crash the app
author: AutoHenry
body:
On macOS 27, choosing **File ▸ Open** in PrintCraft 0.2.1 and then clicking in the window aborts the app (SIGABRT, `panic_cannot_unwind`).

**Cause.** `open_dialog` calls the blocking `rfd::FileDialog::pick_file()`, which runs `-[NSOpenPanel runModal]`: a nested run loop inside winit's `ApplicationDelegate::handle_event` (we are still inside the eframe frame that ran the menu command). A mouse/gesture event that arrives while the panel is up makes winit queue a closure on the run loop (`maybe_queue_event`). AppKit's gesture handling drains that closure inside the modal loop, it re-enters `handle_event`, and winit panics ("tried to handle event while another event is currently being handled"). The panic is inside an Objective-C block, so it can't unwind and the process aborts. The `printcraft_engine::guard` around commands can't catch it. Deferring the call to the next frame doesn't help either, because every frame runs inside that handler. winit 0.30.13 still has this path.

Crash stack (trimmed):
```
core::panicking::panic_cannot_unwind
block2 … winit::platform_impl::macos::observer::RunLoop::queue_closure<ApplicationDelegate::maybe_queue_event>
__CFRunLoopDoBlocks ← -[NSRunLoop runUntilDate:] ← _NSGestureRecognizerSortAndSendDelayedEvents
-[NSApplication _doModalLoop:peek:] ← -[NSSavePanel runModal]
rfd::backend::macos::file_dialog::pick_file
printcraft_ui_egui::PrintCraftApp::open_dialog ← commands::execute ← chrome::main_menu
eframe … WgpuWinitApp::run_ui_and_paint ← winit ApplicationDelegate::handle_event
```

**Fix.**
- New `crates/ui-egui/src/pickers.rs`. Native pickers use `rfd::AsyncFileDialog`, which on macOS starts the panel as a sheet (`beginSheetModalForWindow`) and returns at once. The future is created on the main thread, as rfd requires. A worker thread waits for it with `pollster`, which is already in the tree through wgpu. The result is queued and used on a later frame (`process_picked`), followed by a repaint request.

title: Edit text: the graphics state carries over between a page's content streams
author: Checkov23
body:
## Problem

A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2): a `cm`, a `q` that is still open, the font or the fill colour set in one piece still apply in the next. Edit text read every piece with a fresh graphics state.

AutoCAD's PDF export relies on this. Its first stream scales the whole page (`0.12 0 0 0.12 0 0 cm`, without `q`) and the drawing follows in the next streams. In Edit text mode the text boxes of such a plan therefore sat about eight times too far from the origin, off the page, and none of the plan's labels could be selected or edited.

## Fix

`interpret` now starts from the state the previous stream left (`Carry`: the text and graphics state plus the `q` stack) and hands its own state on. `text_lines` threads one `Carry` through a page's streams. A page with a single content stream behaves as before.

## Tests

`the_graphics_state_carries_over_between_content_streams` builds a page from two streams, the scale in the first and the text in the second, and checks:

- the line's box and size on the page,
- that rewriting and moving the paragraph keeps it in page space at its size,
- that a `q` opened in one stream and closed in the next restores the state.

The test fails without the change and passes with it. `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p printcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p printcraft-edit` pass.

Also checked by hand on a site plan exported from AutoCAD (a real project, so I can't attach it): its 495 text lines now sit on the page, and an edited label keeps its original font.

title: Redact: operators split across a page's content streams are redacted whole
author: EthanSuquet
body:
⚠️ **Data-leak fix:** on affected files, Apply drew the redaction box but left the marked text extractable, and Verify reported the page clean.

A page's /Contents array is one content stream in pieces, and a writer
may split it between any two tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2). Some office
and layout exporters do: a TJ array ends one piece and its TJ operator
starts the next, or a marked-content dictionary closes in the next piece.

Redaction parsed each piece on its own, so such an operator was cut off
from its operands. Glyphs shown by a split TJ were never checked against
the marks: Apply drew the black box but left the text in the file, and
Verify reported nothing under the box. When the piece holding the
operands was rewritten for another mark, they were dropped, so the text
after it vanished and the next piece began with an operator without
operands, which other readers reject.

process() now parses the pieces joined, gives each operator back to the
piece its keyword is in, and rewrites every piece a split operator spans.
Pages whose pieces split only between operators are unchanged.



**Tests:** `operators_split_across_content_streams_are_redacted_whole`: before the fix, Verify counts 0 glyphs under the mark and Apply removes 0; after, both see 4. All 18 other redact tests still pass, plus the engine and automation redact tests. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p printcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. On a batch of real-world PDFs, 6 files with split streams now redact cleanly, and the outputs open without errors in another reader.

Found on real exported documents (not attachable); the test reproduces it synthetically.

title: Edit text: keep the tokens a content stream shares with its neighbours
author: EthanSuquet
body:
A page's /Contents array is one content stream in pieces, and a writer
may split it between any two tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2): a TJ array
can end one piece with its operator starting the next, and a
marked-content dictionary can close at the start of the next piece.

Replacing a line or rewriting a paragraph re-serialized the parsed
operators of the line's piece, and the parser keeps neither operands
left at the end of a piece nor a dictionary's closing >> at its start.
The edit dropped them: the text after the edited line vanished, and the
page was left with an operator without operands (TJ, BDC), which other
readers reject.

The piece is now rewritten by splicing: only the replaced, inserted and
removed operators change, and every other byte is copied as it was.



**Tests:** `editing_text_keeps_the_tokens_a_stream_shares_with_its_neighbours` covers line and paragraph edits. It fails before the fix ("the text after the line is gone") and passes after; all 24 other edit tests and the engine and automation text tests pass. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p printcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. It does not touch the hunks #150 changes.

Found on real exported documents (not attachable); the test reproduces it synthetically.

title: M8: harden redaction (sanitize + independent proof, fail-closed, signed refusal, new /ID)
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Apply Redactions either removes the content and says what it checked, or fails without changing the document.

- **Apply is one operation.** Redaction and sanitizing run together on a clone and are committed only on success. Content that cannot be placed or read (fonts without usable metrics, vertical writing, damaged or oversized streams, malformed marks) fails closed with a named error that never contains page text.
- **Independent proof.** A separate pass re-reads the output (raw bytes, decoded streams, strings, Info, XMP, annotations, attachments, revisions, in every string encoding) and, on Save, the exact bytes about to be written. It says "checked", not "guaranteed".
- **Safe save.** Signed documents are refused up front. Undo/redo is cleared and the dialog requires an acknowledgement. Redacted output is written atomically with owner-only permissions, to a new path unless `overwrite_source` is given. Any spelling of the source path counts as the source, and removing hidden information in place needs the same opt-in.
- **#389.** A partly redacted scan leaves no extractable original after a full save, whether the image is inherited, drawn by a form without resources, shared by two pages, Flate or JPEG. The eight apply → save → reopen → extract regressions are HT's; the `Co-authored-by` trailer is kept on the commit that carries them.
- **Search & Redact patterns:** IBAN (mod 97), cards (Luhn), IPv4/IPv6, UK postcode, US ZIP, ISO/US dates, international phone.
- `create::from_text` writes exact Helvetica `/Widths` (from the existing exact standard-14 metrics) so text made by the app can be redacted.

title: Security: --root confinement leaks and escapes (#136, #137)
author: jcl-bit
body:
## What and why

Fixes #136, fixes #137.

`--root DIR` is the boundary for `pdfcraft-cli run` and the MCP server, so an agent or a script someone else wrote can only touch one folder. This closes the two reported holes in it, plus a third one found while reviewing the fix. One commit each.

**1. `Automation: --root refuses every outside path the same way (#136)`**

`resolve` canonicalized a path before checking it against the root. An existing outside path got "is outside the allowed directory" and a missing one got the OS error, which made it an existence oracle for the whole disk. Containment is now decided before anything about an outside path is reported:

- `..` is resolved by name first, as Windows already does, so a path can't pass through an outside folder on its way back in. (On Unix, `../outside/../root/x` used to answer differently depending on whether `outside` exists.)
- On Windows, another network share or device namespace (`\\host\share`, `//host/share`, `\\?\UNC\…`, `\\.\…`, `\\?\GLOBALROOT\…`) is refused by name, without contacting the host. Checking whether one exists would open an SMB connection.
- The deepest existing ancestor, links followed, must be inside the root before anything is said about the rest. A broken link is refused too, so whether its target exists stays hidden.

Every outside path now gets `<path> is outside the allowed directory <root>`. That holds whether it exists or not, whether it is a file or a folder, for reads and writes, and through a link or a missing folder. "Not found" and other filesystem errors are still reported for paths inside the root.

**2. `CLI: script images stay inside --root (#137)`**

A script step's `"out"` PNG was written with `std::fs::write`, never through the root check. It now goes through the new `Automation::write_output`, which uses the same resolver and atomic write as a tool's output. Outside paths are refused and nothing is written, and relative paths resolve inside the root. Without `--root`, …

title: macOS: declare PDF by UTI so Open With recommends PrintCraft
author: ShauryaSwarup
body:
Follow-up to #73 (fixed by #82). Fixes #177.

## Problem
#82 declared the PDF document type by extension (`pdf`) and MIME type (`application/pdf`) only. On modern macOS that is not enough: LaunchServices keeps those as plain tags instead of resolving them to `com.adobe.pdf`, so

- PrintCraft is greyed out under Open With with `Enable: Recommended Applications` (user must switch to `All Applications`), and
- a forced open fails with `PrintCraft cannot open files in the "PDF document" format`.

(This stacks on the installed v0.2.1 release DMG (`printcraft-0.2.1-macos-universal.dmg`; app reports 0.2.1 / build `dcb0023`) predating #82 entirely — its `Info.plist` has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes` at all, only the sibling image editor's `pcraft`/`psb`/`qoi` types. A post-merge build is needed to see any of this.)

## Fix
Adds `LSItemContentTypes: com.adobe.pdf` to the existing `CFBundleDocumentTypes` entry in `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`, keeping extension + MIME for backward compatibility. Role stays `Editor`, rank stays `Alternate`, so the app is offered without hijacking the default from Preview.

## Verification (local, macOS 27.0 (Golden Gate) arm64)
- Rendered the template exactly like `package.sh` does: `plutil -lint` OK, `xmllint --noout` OK (the `packaging-lint` gate).
- A/B with `lsregister -f` on two copies of the app + `lsregister -dump`:
  - before (extension+MIME only): `bindings: .pdf, application/pdf`, no UTI claim;
  - after (this patch): `bindings: com.adobe.pdf`, `claimed UTIs: com.adobe.pdf`, `rank: Alternate, roles: Editor` — same shape as the system's PDF handlers.
- No code changes, so the Rust gates (`cargo fmt`, `clippy`, `cargo test`) are unaffected; the touched gate is `packaging-lint`, which passes.

title: Checkboxes with an indirect /AP /N state dictionary are drawn (#180)
author: ebastos
body:
Fixes #180.

**Cause.** `hayro-syntax` recovers a stream whose `/Length` is wrong by scanning ahead for the bytes `stream`. Quartz writes a checkbox's `/AP /N` as an indirect dictionary of states (`<< /Yes 5 0 R /Off 6 0 R >>`). That dictionary was parsed as whatever stream came next in the file. It has no `/BBox`, so the appearance was dropped and the widget was skipped. The same dictionary written inline still drew, which is why only some of the boxes on a page disappeared.

The renderer asks for `/N` as a stream first (`ap.get::<Stream>(N)`), then falls back to a state dictionary selected by `/AS`. Once the dictionary is no longer reported as a stream, that fallback draws the checked appearance. The renderer is unchanged.

**Fix.** `stream` has to be the next token after the dictionary. Comments and whitespace are still skipped, and a wrong `/Length` still recovers, because that keyword sits directly after the dict. Marked `PdfCraft patch:` in `vendor/hayro-syntax`.

**Tests.**

- `raster::tests::indirect_appearance_state_dict_is_not_another_stream` is the regression CI runs (`pdfcraft-render` is a workspace member). The widget's `/AP /N` is an indirect state dictionary, and the next object is a decoy blue stream. The checked appearance is red. Before the parser change, pixel (20, 80) was white `[255, 255, 255, 255]` and the test failed. After it, the pixel is the `/Yes` red.
- `raster::tests::widget_appearance_states` still covers the inline state dictionary.
- In `hayro-syntax`, `dictionary_is_not_a_later_objects_stream` is the direct parser check. It failed on the old scanner (the dictionary was accepted as a stream) and passes now, along with the existing `stream` and `stream_fallback` tests. That crate is not a workspace member, so `cargo test --workspace` does not compile it. I ran `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/hayro-syntax/Cargo.toml --lib object::stream::tests` (3 passed). `vendor/README.md` cites the render test, which is the one CI runs.

title: M13: AI assistant with a bring-your-own OpenAI-compatible provider
author: Alishahed
body:
## Summary

Implements the M13 AI provider (`misc.ai-provider`, `misc.ai-summary`, `misc.ai-ask`, and `create.translate` as partial): the AI assistant tools that were placeholders now work with a model the user chooses, through any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio or a hosted service). **Off by default.** Nothing is sent until the user asks.

- **Preferences ▸ AI assistant:** an on/off switch, the endpoint URL, the model and an optional API key, saved with the other settings.
- **AI assistant panel** (right rail, and View ▸ Side panels):
  - **Summarize:** the whole document.
  - **Ask:** pages cited in the answer (`p. 3`, `page 3`, `[Page 3]`) become buttons that go to the page.
  - **Translate:** the current page, into the language typed.
- The **All tools ▸ AI assistant** items are registered commands (`ai.summary`, `ai.ask`, `ai.translate`). They show as ready once a provider is set up; until then they open Preferences.

## Design

- `engine::ai` builds the request and reads the answer, and has no network code. The document text is sent with `[Page n]` markers so answers can cite pages, cut at 120,000 characters (the answer says when). The prompt treats the document as content, not instructions.
- The UI receives the sender as `PdfCraftApp::ai_provider`, the same pattern as `update_source`, so `ui-egui` stays network-free and the web build shows "needs the desktop app".
- `apps/pdfcraft/src/ai.rs` sends the POST over the existing `ureq` dependency. It uses OS roots for HTTPS, follows no redirects (so the document and key are never resent elsewhere), caps the answer size, uses a 600 s timeout and reports the server's own error message.
- **Never panic:**
  - Endpoint answers are untrusted. Malformed JSON, error objects, null or empty content, content parts and `<think>` reasoning blocks are all handled.
  - Settings read from the file are capped.
  - The worker runs under `engine::guard`, so a panicking provider show…

author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #143.

The Windows MSI had no desktop shortcut, no reliable Start Menu entry, and no confirmation that setup finished. This PR adds a desktop-shortcut option, a set of native setup dialogs ending in a "Setup completed successfully" screen, and shortcuts that link straight to `pdfcraft.exe`. It applies to all three MSIs that `release.yml` builds: x64, x86 and ARM64.

### Desktop shortcut (`pdfcraft.wxs`)

title: Proposal: professional task screens — OCR Verify, Measure, side-by-side Compare, Batch queue, A11y panels, PDF/A dock (+ Workspaces strip)
author: eliets2
body:
## What this is

A design proposal (docs-only, no code changes) for promoting six professional workflows from dialogs to **persistent task screens**, plus a **Workspaces strip** to host them. Written after a screen-by-screen comparison of PdfCraft against GlyphPDF (a Qt6 PDF workstation built by the same author) and against Acrobat Pro's own tool-workspace structure.

**Full proposal:** [docs/proposals/2026-10-04-professional-task-screens.md](https://github.com/eliets2/printcraft/blob/docs/proposal-professional-task-screens/docs/proposals/2026-10-04-professional-task-screens.md)

## Why screens, not dialogs

Your Organize-pages screen already proves the pattern in this codebase: page organization is spatial and iterative, so it got a persistent card-grid with a contextual toolbar instead of a dialog. Three more workflows are the same class of task and currently open as dialogs over the reader:

- **OCR correction** — recognition is never trusted; correcting low-confidence words against the source image needs source, text, and magnified crop visible *simultaneously*. A dialog cannot hold that.
- **Accessibility repair** — the 32-rule checker finds issues; fixing them (Tags tree, Reading Order) is a persistent editing workflow.
- **Comparison review** — the comparison moment users pay for is seeing two documents with linked scrolling and walking the changes; the report is the artifact, not the workflow.

Acrobat Pro — the parity target in ROADMAP.md — makes all of these persistent tool workspaces. Screen-for-screen, they are where Pro earns its price.

## The six screens (layouts in the doc)

| Screen | Core idea |
|---|---|
| **OCR Verify** | 4-pane correction splitter: page list / source scan with confidence-colored word boxes / editable recognized text / zoomed word crop with alternates. A `ReviewState` machine so Run never sticks. |
| **Measure** | Right dock: calibration presets + custom ratio, distance/perimeter/area, snap, live readouts. Honesty contract: uncal…

title: Print: add cut-and-stack page order
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Adds **Cut and stack** under Print > Multiple. Handy for numbered tickets or cards: print several pages on each sheet, cut the sheet stack into piles, then put the piles together in page order.

For 10 pages at 4 per sheet, the sheets are:

```text
1   4   7   10
2   5   8   blank
3   6   9   blank
```

Keep sheet 1 at the top of each pile, then stack the piles left to right, top to bottom. Cut marks line up in the gutters, and unused cells stay blank.

Uses the existing scaling, page ranges, reverse order and live preview. CLI/MCP callers can use `doc_print` with `layout: "multiple"`, `order: "cut-stack"` and `per_sheet: 4`. This is single-sided for now; duplex settings return an error instead of producing the wrong order.

Also guards n-up grid multiplication from overflow, and refuses grids or page sizes that cannot be laid out. Before this fix, an excessively large grid could overflow and panic. It now returns an error, and the regression test passes. The automation test also fails without the new order handler.

Validation on Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.99.0:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 gates passed, including strict Clippy, 776 workspace tests (4 ignored), all 27 WASM crates, layering, assets, dependency audit and parity.
- Simulated cutting and restacking for 666 page-count/grid/orientation combinations; partial sheets, selected/reversed pages and duplicate pages are covered.
- UI test selects the order, navigates the preview, saves/reopens the PDF and checks duplex refusal. Also checked the native dialog through its control channel.
- Drove the real CLI with a synthetic 10-page file, inspected the rendered sheets and checked the print-ready PDF with qpdf. No physical printer test.

No new dependencies or asset files. The existing n-up parity entry records this as an extension, so the Acrobat parity count does not increase.

title: CLI: exit cleanly when stdout pipe closes
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Fixes #135.

`pdfcraft-cli tools | head -1` panicked when the reader closed stdout, exiting with status 101. The CLI's `println!` calls now use fallible writes and flushes. A broken pipe from these writes stops the command quietly with status 0; other stdout failures return status 1 with a diagnostic. File, tool and argument errors still fail normally.

The subprocess tests cover readers that are already closed, a reader stopping after one line, normal JSON output and other write failures. They also check that a closed pipe stops a script before its next edit. The tests for early closure and failed writes reproduce panics on unmodified main.

On Ubuntu 24.04 and Rust 1.99.0, `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight gates with CI's pinned craft-fonts input: 802 workspace tests passed (4 ignored), strict Clippy and all 27 WASM crates passed. `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features` also passed. title: Add DPI choices when creating PDFs from images
author: DWAA1660
body:
Create PDF from Images selected the image's resolution automatically, without a way to override the resulting printed page size. The import dialog now offers embedded resolution, 72 DPI (one point per pixel), or custom DPI from 1 to 1200. Embedded DPI uses the existing readers: PNG pHYs, JPEG JFIF density, TIFF resolution tags, and JPEG 2000 resolution boxes. DPI changes page sizing without resampling; JPEG bytes and transparency are kept. The existing maximum PDF page size still applies. The dialog uses the current UI localization lookup, with English fallback for new labels.

The Windows MSI adds **Create PDF with PdfCraft…** to the context menu for supported image extensions. It invokes `pdfcraft --create-images <image>` to open the same DPI chooser. This Explorer entry handles a single image; the app's image picker and startup flag support multiple images in one PDF. Context-menu integration in this PR is scoped to the Windows MSI.

Fixes #190.

title: Measure: add distance, perimeter and area tools
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Adds distance, perimeter and area under Measure objects, with live readings, drawing-scale calibration, snapping and CSV export. This implements the 2D measuring workflow requested in #119.

Measurements are saved as standard PDF LineDimension, PolyLineDimension and PolygonDimension annotations with rectilinear Measure dictionaries and numeric appearances. Drawing scales are stored in page viewports; the first vertex chooses the scale, and existing measurements keep theirs. The normal comment tools handle moving, restyling, deleting and undo. Imported appearances that cannot be reproduced are preserved.

All eight cargo xtask ci gates passed on Ubuntu 24.04 with Rust 1.99.0 and the pinned craft-fonts input: 888 workspace tests passed, four ignored, strict Clippy, layering, 29 WASM crates, assets, dependency audit and parity checks. The CLI also builds without MCP. Tests cover calibrated geometry, viewport precedence, rotated and cropped pages, UserUnit, malformed input, permissions, all snapping targets, cyclic forms, undo, save/reopen and CSV confinement. I also drove the desktop control channel and real CLI on a synthetic drawing, checked the saved PDF with qpdf, and inspected its rendering in PdfCraft and Poppler.

This adds seven tested parity entries and eight automation tools without new third-party dependencies or binary assets. The new controls include Japanese and Chinese translations.

Scope is rectilinear 2D measuring with single-unit decimal scales. Compound or fractional imported scales and geospatial/3D measuring remain unsupported. Snapping follows vector paths and transformed forms, with bounded work and reported limits; it does not interpret raster edges, glyph outlines, clipping or optional-content visibility.

title: Add a PR template, and record the review practice and external-PR bar
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

`plan/` is gitignored and local-only, so a clone has no STATUS, architecture or execution plan — and `CLAUDE.md` step 1 sends every session to `plan/STATUS.md`, which is not there. This adds `docs/plan/` as a committed replacement, derived from this repository rather than from the missing notes: the layer table from `xtask/src/layers.rs`, the baseline from a measured `cargo xtask parity` on `827c61b`.

It also writes down two things that were not written down anywhere: how an update is reviewed, and the bar an external PR is held to.

### Three parts

**The plan** (`docs/plan/{README,STATUS,architecture,execution-plan}.md`). Phase order puts foundation before features.

**Review at four zooms** (§1.2–§1.3). Every update is reviewed outward — clause, function, file/module, project — as it is made, not in one pass at the end, so a defect never has code built on top of it. Tests mirror the same zooms, and a test is proved to fail before the fix by actually reverting the fix.

**The external-PR bar** (§1.4). Provenance first, because an Adobe-derived asset, a committed font or copied copyleft code cannot be undone later; then no new panic path or `unsafe`; then `--root` confinement on paths reached by *nested* dispatch, opt-in-only MCP and control channel, no new outbound network; then a headless `automation` tool, tests at the right zoom, an honest `parity/` entry.

### Two findings this surfaced

- **`xtask corpus` clones `mozilla/pdf.js` at HEAD with no commit pin and no sha256** (`xtask/src/gates.rs`), and corpus tests skip silently when it is absent — so the corpus sweep measures a moving target. AGENTS.md §2 requires pinned, verified fixtures. Queued as D1, the next task.
- **`.gitignore` had `plan/` unanchored**, which matches a `plan` directory at any depth — it would have silently ignored `docs/plan/` too. Now `/plan/`, so the original local-only notes stay ignored and the committed plan does not.

## How it was verified
