title: M3: harden render and CLI failure surfaces
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Several bounded-work and failure cases were either silent or broader than the request that caused them:

- content skipped by the existing per-page safety budget could still look like a clean render;
- non-edit CLI commands ignored misspelled long options;
- render work had no deterministic counters for proving reuse or regression behavior;
- a whole-page raster could be silently reduced by hard size caps;
- a failed render was remembered at page/kind scope, preventing unrelated scales, tiles, or generations from recovering.

## Root cause

The renderer had internal safety limits and watchdog state, but the result surface did not carry truncation warnings, the watchdog key did not include the full request identity, and CLI parsing used permissive flag lookup. Size clamping was also shared by interactive and export callers without an explicit refusal mode.

## Change

- Add typed `RenderWarning::ContentTruncated` propagation from the vendored interpreter into `RenderedPage` for single-threaded and pooled rendering.
- Reject unknown options in all non-edit CLI commands before file I/O; preserve the existing edit parser.
- Add `RenderStats` counters to `PageRenderer` and `RenderPool` for parser builds, page interpretations, requests, tiles, text interpretations, and rasterizations.
- Add a generated 5,000-operator heavy-vector fixture with trailing text and counter assertions.
- Add `RenderConfig::reject_oversize`; CLI render and engine export now refuse silently reduced whole-page rasters while tiled requests remain available.
- Key stuck/failure state by page, request kind, tile, scale bits, and caller tag.

## Before

- A skipped nested content stream could return pixels with no typed indication of incompleteness.
- `--passwrod`-style options were ignored by several commands and execution continued.
- A page-level stuck result could poison later requests for the same page.
- Export could report success for a raster smaller than the requested scale.

title: M3: tiles skip paths that can't paint them (item 5 of #623)
author: cyfung1031
body:
First step for item 5 of #623.

## Problem

Pages larger than 4096 device pixels are drawn as 1024 px tiles. Each tile renders the whole page with an offset, and hayro sets up and draws every path on the page. vello then discards whatever falls outside the tile, but only after the expensive part: setting up the paint and, for strokes, kurbo's stroke expansion.

On #623's sample, a 64 × 64 tile cost about as much as a 1024 × 1024 one. In a sampling profile of small-tile renders, stroking took about half the samples, and kurbo's stroke expansion alone 23%.

## Fix

**hayro, vendored patch (9): `may_paint_canvas`.** Before a fill or stroke is set up, a box around everything it can paint is checked against the canvas, and a path whose box misses the canvas is skipped. The box is built from:

- the path's points and control points (a curve stays inside their hull);
- for a stroke, its reach: half the line width times the larger of the miter limit and √2. kurbo draws a miter only when its tip is within `limit × width / 2` of the vertex, and √2 covers square caps;
- 0.5 user units more, covering vello's stroke tolerance (at most 0.25 user units) and kurbo's approximation of round joins and caps (1e-3);
- mapped to device space, plus 2 pixels for antialiasing.

Empty paths, boxes that aren't finite, and strokes whose miter limit isn't finite are always drawn.

**Where it applies.** `fill_path`, `stroke_path` and rectangle fills. Glyph outlines and Type 3 glyph paths go through these too. Images, shadings (`sh`), clip paths, soft masks and groups are unchanged.

**Why skipping can't affect later drawing.** A skipped draw only skips the state it sets for itself: transform, fill rule, stroke and paint. Every draw sets these before drawing, and image draws set their own paint transform.

**What still runs per tile.** Interpretation itself still runs: parsing the content and keeping the graphics state. Removing that is item 5's display list (ADR-0004).

title: Wayland: IME keeps working after a seat loses a capability (winit#4747)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On Wayland, IME (fcitx5, IBus) stops working in a running PdfCraft after the seat loses any capability, for example when a touch screen or tablet is unplugged or a remote-desktop session (Sunshine) ends, and stays broken until PdfCraft is restarted. This keeps the seat's text input until the seat itself goes away.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4747](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4747) (reviewed head `2060ab0f88`) to the vendored winit 0.30.13. It is the same change, applied to 0.30's file layout.

### PdfCraft impact

Every egui `TextEdit` (Search, form fields, the JavaScript console, comments, stamp and signature fields, the command palette) gets IME input on Wayland through winit's `zwp_text_input_v3`.

### Root cause

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/seat/mod.rs`: `SeatHandler::remove_capability` destroyed `seat_state.text_input` whichever capability was removed. The text input comes from `zwp_text_input_manager_v3`, not from a capability, and `new_capability` only recreates it when a capability is *added*. A seat that just loses one is left without a text input for the rest of the session. `remove_seat` dropped the seat state without destroying its text input.

### Change

- `remove_capability` no longer touches the text input.
- `remove_seat` destroys it with the seat.

Nothing else in seat handling changes (the tablet handling next to it is left as it was, as upstream does).

### Not included

Nothing else from winit master.

### Verification

- Upstream reproduced the bug and the fix at protocol level (`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`: the unpatched client sends `zwp_text_input_v3.destroy` on a touch capability removal and never recreates it; the patched one only releases `wl_touch`) and end to end with fcitx5.
- Not run here: this machine has no Wayland session. To check by hand: Wayland with fcitx5 or IBus, compose in Search, add then remove a touch or virtual input device (or connect and disconnect a Sunshine client), switch to an…

title: Windows: the Korean IME composition caret sits after the syllable (winit#4746)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

With the Microsoft Korean IME on Windows, winit reports the composition's cursor at the start of the syllable (`Ime::Preedit("한", Some((0, 0)))`). egui 0.36.2 recognises that exact report on Windows and drops the range (a workaround in `egui-winit`), so PdfCraft shows **no caret at all** while Korean is being composed. With this change winit reports the cursor at the end (`Some((3, 3))`), and egui draws the caret after the syllable.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4746](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4746) (reviewed head `3787f3d644`) to the vendored winit 0.30.13. It is the same change.

### PdfCraft impact

Korean composition in every egui text field on Windows: Search, form fields, the JavaScript console, comments.

### Root cause

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/windows/ime.rs`, `get_composing_text_and_cursor`: when a composition has no target clause, winit calls `ImmGetCompositionStringW(GCS_CURSORPOS)` without checking that the `WM_IME_COMPOSITION` `lParam` has `GCS_CURSORPOS` set. The Microsoft Korean IME never sets it (`lParam` is `0x6018`: `GCS_COMPSTR | GCS_COMPATTR | CS_INSERTCHAR | CS_NOMOVECARET`), so the read gives 0.

### Change

`WM_IME_COMPOSITION` passes its `lParam` on. When there is no target clause, the cursor comes from `GCS_CURSORPOS` only if that flag is set; otherwise it goes at the end of the composition. Firefox reads the cursor the same way, and SDL fixed the same bug by putting it at the end.

IMEs that report a target clause or a cursor position (Japanese, Chinese) take the same path as before, and commits are unchanged.

### Not included

Nothing else from winit master.

### Verification

- Upstream checked it on Windows 11 with the Microsoft Korean IME: `한` now gives `Preedit("한", Some((3, 3)))`, `안녕` is the same per syllable, the Hanja candidate window opens at the caret, and commits are unchanged.
- Not run here: this machine has no Windows. To check by hand: Windows 11, Microsoft Korean IME, type 한 / 안녕 / 한…

title: Windows: a window closed maximized reopens without a white flash (winit#4587)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On Windows, PdfCraft closed while maximized came back with a white, unpainted window before its first frame. eframe creates the window hidden, restores the saved maximized state (`app.ron`, `persist_window`) and shows the window after the first frame is drawn. But winit applies "maximized" with `ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE)`, which **shows** a hidden window. This keeps a hidden window hidden while its maximized state is set, and shows it maximized with a single `SW_MAXIMIZE`.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4587](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4587) (reviewed head `9f8beaf502`, approved upstream by kchibisov), which fixes [winit#4586](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4586). It is the later, focus-safe form of [winit#4575](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4575), whose author found the same startup flash in an eframe app with a saved maximized window ([egui#7746](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/7746)).

### PdfCraft impact

Every Windows launch after closing PdfCraft maximized.

### Root cause

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/windows/window_state.rs`, `WindowFlags::apply_diff`. Over the start-up sequence, the window is created hidden, then:

- `set_maximized(true)` while hidden calls `ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE)`, which shows the unpainted window, then `ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)`;
- after the first frame, `set_visible(true)` calls `SW_SHOW`, then `SW_MAXIMIZE` again.

Winit#4586 also shows the window's focus state going wrong on this path.

### Change

- While the target state is hidden, maximizing (and un-maximizing) doesn't call `ShowWindow`.
- A hidden window that becomes visible while maximized is shown with one `SW_MAXIMIZE`.
- Transitions between two visible states make exactly the same `ShowWindow` calls as before.

### Not included

- #4575's other change: it calls `SW_MINIMIZE` on every flag change while the window is minimized, which can move activation to another window. eframe never minimizes a hidden window.
- Noth…

title: X11: the input method follows the text field that has focus (winit#4727)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On X11, the input method (IBus, fcitx5) doesn't follow PdfCraft's text fields. egui allows IME when a field gains focus and disallows it when the field loses focus. Each change makes winit replace the window's X input context, and the new context stays unfocused until the window itself loses and regains focus, which doesn't happen while the user moves between Search, form fields and the page. This focuses the replacement context once the queued requests are handled.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4727](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4727) (reviewed head `a65eb5b000`) to the vendored winit 0.30.13. It is the same change, applied to 0.30's file layout.

### PdfCraft impact

IME in every egui text field on X11, each time focus moves between fields or between a field and the canvas.

### Root cause

- `vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/ime/mod.rs`: `Ime::set_ime_allowed` destroys the window's XIC and creates a new one (`create_context`), discarding the result.
- `vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs`: the new XIC is focused only by the `FocusIn` handler.
- egui calls `Window::set_ime_allowed` from `egui-winit` every time a text field gains or loses focus, while the X11 window keeps the focus, so no `FocusIn` follows.

### Change

- `Ime::set_ime_allowed` returns `create_context`'s `Result<bool, _>` (whether a context was replaced). It is internal; no public API changes.
- While draining the queued IME requests, the event processor remembers the last context replaced for the active window, and afterwards focuses it once, so contexts replaced again in the same batch aren't focused in between.

### Not included

Nothing else from winit master.

### Verification

- Not run here: this machine has no X11 session. To check by hand, with IBus and with fcitx5: compose in Search, click a form field and compose at once, alternate quickly between two fields, then click the page and back. The first key after each switch must co…

title: macOS: IME text committed after the marked text is cleared isn't lost (winit#4650)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On macOS, text committed through IME is lost in PdfCraft's text fields when the input method clears its marked text before inserting. This happens with:

- Apple Korean, for the key that ends a syllable: typing 한 then `5` (or `;`) gives 한 without the 5.
- Input methods that end a composition with `unmarkText` before `insertText` (rust-windowing/winit#3925).
- A commit made outside a key press (a candidate clicked with the mouse, dictation): the next key, such as Backspace, is swallowed.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4650](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4650) (reviewed head `565e504d43`), the 0.30 backport of [winit#4651](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4651), which is **merged on winit master** (5ea1b78d29). It also includes the part of [winit#4748](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4748) (reviewed head `41e556b432`) that fixes #4651's out-of-key-press case. The other macOS PRs in this batch build on this one.

### PdfCraft impact

IME input in every egui text field on macOS: Search, form fields, the JavaScript console, comments, the command palette.

### Root cause

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs`:

- `insertText:` reports `Ime::Commit` only while marked text is left (`hasMarkedText()`). Apple Korean calls `setMarkedText("한")`, `insertText("한")`, `setMarkedText("")`, `insertText("5")`, so the `5` arrives with no marked text: it is neither committed nor sent as a key, because `keyDown:` treats the key as consumed by IME.
- After any commit the view is left `Committed`. Outside a key press, no `keyDown:` follows to clear the marked text and reset the state, so the next key is swallowed.

### Change

- `pending_commit`: set by `setMarkedText`, cleared by a commit and when IME is disallowed. `insertText` commits when a composition was started, rather than when marked text is left. Other `insertText` calls (ordinary typing) still reach the app as `KeyboardInput`, which #4576's broader approach would have …

title: macOS: an unfinished composition doesn't come back in the next text field (winit#4745)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On macOS, an unfinished IME composition comes back after focus leaves a text field. Compose 하 in Search, click the page, click back into a field and type ㄱ ㅏ: the result is 학, then 하 committed again plus 가, instead of 가. In Japanese, か, click away and back, then s a becomes 傘 instead of さ. This tells the input method to discard its composition when IME is disallowed.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4745](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4745) (reviewed head `c69b1f1471`) to the vendored winit 0.30.13. It is the same change, placed in 0.30's `set_ime_allowed(false)` path, which corresponds to master's `disable_ime`.

### PdfCraft impact

Switching between any egui text field and the canvas, the toolbar or another field while composing. egui disallows IME when a text field loses focus.

### Root cause

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs`, `WinitView::set_ime_allowed(false)` clears winit's own marked text but never tells AppKit. The `NSTextInputContext` keeps the composition, and continues it when IME is allowed again.

### Change

When IME is disallowed with marked text present, call `NSTextInputContext::discardMarkedText()` before the existing reset. If AppKit calls `unmarkText` back from `discardMarkedText`, IME is still enabled at that point, so its `Preedit("")` comes before `Ime::Disabled`. The `RefCell` borrow in the check ends before the call.

### Not included

Nothing else from winit master.

### How the macOS changes were checked

A scratch winit app (not committed) built against the vendored winit, first unpatched, then with each patch. It picks an input source on its own input context (`NSTextInputContext.selectedKeyboardInputSource`), posts key events made from `CGEventCreateKeyboardEvent` to itself, so AppKit routes them through `keyDown:` and `interpretKeyEvents`, and the **real** input method composes them. It prints winit's `Ime` and `KeyboardInput` events, and AppKit's `NSTextInputClient` calls from winit's own trace…

title: macOS: emoji from the emoji picker reach text fields (winit#4749)
author: cyfung1031
body:
> **Builds on https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676** (macOS IME commit state: `pending_commit`, `in_key_down`). This branch contains that PR's commit; please review the last commit only. Once https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676 is merged, this diff reduces to the last commit.

## Summary

On macOS, emoji picked with the emoji picker (Fn/Globe-E, Control-Command-Space) never reach PdfCraft's text fields. The picker inserts its text with `insertText:replacementRange:` outside any key press and without a composition, and winit 0.30.13 only reports `insertText` during a key press or a composition. This reports that text as `Ime::Commit`.

Port of the emoji-picker part of [rust-windowing/winit#4749](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4749) (reviewed head `73c6976c30`), the 0.30 backport of [winit#4748](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4748) (reviewed head `41e556b432`), which upstream also writes on top of `pending_commit`.

### PdfCraft impact

Emoji, and other text a system service inserts outside a key press, in every egui text field on macOS.

### Change

In `insertText:`, outside `keyDown:`, with IME allowed, no composition pending, and non-empty, non-control text: send `Ime::Enabled` if needed, then `Ime::Commit(text)`.

### Not included: dictation's `selectedRange`

#4748 also makes `selectedRange` report a caret while IME is allowed, so that dictation can start. **This is deliberately left out.** On macOS 14.7.1, a valid `selectedRange` switches on press-and-hold (the accent menu, enabled by default) for every held key in a winit window. Holding `e` in a field then kept sending `e` key events under the accent menu, and the accent chosen with `1` arrived as a separate `Commit("è")` after `eeeeeeeeeeeee1`. Without it, a held key repeats as before. Dictation therefore stays unavailable, as it is on `main`.

A scratch winit app (not committed) built against the vendored winit, first un…

title: macOS: Space in Apple Korean with no syllable in progress types one space (winit#4478)
author: cyfung1031
body:
> **Builds on https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676** (macOS IME commit state: `pending_commit`, `in_key_down`). This branch contains that PR's commit; please review the last commit only. Once https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676 is merged, this diff reduces to the last commit.

## Summary

On macOS with Apple Korean, Space types **two** spaces in PdfCraft when no syllable is in progress: a second space, or a space after a digit or punctuation. This is the double space of [alacritty#8079](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/8079). With this change a key whose text was committed through IME is not also sent as `KeyboardInput`.

Related upstream PR: [rust-windowing/winit#4478](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4478) (reviewed head `dfb23bff7d`), which aims at the same double space. Its changes don't reach the call order seen here, so this is a narrow re-implementation of its goal on top of the commit state from the macOS IME commit PR. It is not a copy of #4478 (see below), and it should go upstream with #4478.

### PdfCraft impact

Typing Korean with spaces in any egui text field on macOS.

### Root cause

AppKit's calls for that Space (traced on macOS 14.7.1) are `setMarkedText(" ")`, `insertText(" ")` (winit sends `Ime::Commit(" ")` and enters the committed state), then `setMarkedText("")`. The last call returns winit's state to the ground state, so `keyDown:` sees no IME input and also sends `KeyboardInput` with text `" "`. `egui-winit` turns that text into `Event::Text`, and the field gets two spaces.

### Change

`keyDown:` records whether the key it is handling committed IME text (`committed_in_key_down`, set in `insertText:`). It then doesn't also send the key as `KeyboardInput`, unless AppKit forwards it as a command through `doCommandBySelector:`. So Enter after a syllable still commits the syllable and sends Enter. `keyDown:` consumes the record for every key (`Cell::replace`), so keys typed after IME is disallowed ar…

title: macOS: the first Apple Korean key in a fresh PdfCraft composes (winit#4744)
author: cyfung1031
body:
> **Builds on https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676** (macOS IME commit state: `pending_commit`, `in_key_down`). This branch contains that PR's commit; please review the last commit only. Once https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/676 is merged, this diff reduces to the last commit.

## Summary

On macOS, the first Korean word typed in a freshly started PdfCraft comes out broken: g k s Space gives **ㅎㅏㄴ** instead of **한**. On the first key, Apple Korean can call `insertText` with the raw compatibility jamo instead of starting a composition. winit sends it to the app as an ordinary key, and the next keys compose without it. This interprets that one key a second time, synchronously, before it is sent, and only in exactly that situation.

Port of [rust-windowing/winit#4744](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4744) (reviewed head `5c5c4db9af`; related [winit#3095](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/3095)), whose author reproduced it with eframe 0.36 on winit 0.30.13.

### PdfCraft impact

The first Korean key in Search, a form field or any egui text field after each launch.

### Change

- `ime_startup.rs` (`ImeStartup`) is copied from #4744 with its seven tests: the policy that decides on the retry.
- `view.rs`: `keyDown:` asks the policy before `interpretKeyEvents`, and retries the same retained event once afterwards only if every condition holds:
  - Apple Korean is the input source, IME is allowed and not yet composing, and there is no pending commit or marked text;
  - no Command, Control or Option, and the key is not an auto-repeat;
  - the view is the key window's first responder;
  - the interpretation's only callback was one `insertText` of that same single jamo;
  - focus and input source are unchanged afterwards.

  `setMarkedText`, `unmarkText` and `doCommandBySelector` cancel a retry, and allowing or disallowing IME resets the policy.
- There is no timer, no key queue, no text rewriting, and no `RefCell` borrow across AppK…

title: create: lift TIFF decoding buffer limit to allow print-sized images (#665)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #665.

### Summary
Importing a large TIFF image via `doc_create {"from": "images"}` failed with `decoder limits exceeded` whenever the decoded image buffer exceeded 256 MiB (such as a 12000x16000 CMYK poster TIFF). Meanwhile, PNGs of equivalent and larger dimensions decoded without issue.

The default limits in the `tiff` crate cap the decoded buffer size to 256 MiB (`256 * 1024 * 1024`).

### Changes
- In `crates/create/src/lib.rs`: configured the TIFF decoder with `Decoder::with_limits(Limits::unlimited())`, lifting the artificial buffer ceiling to match PNG decoding behavior.
- Updated `contributors/people.toml` for Hathor875.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (all 9 unit tests pass)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- `cargo xtask layers` (ok, 34 crates clean)

title: Chinese: one installed Han face for both Chinese scripts, on the Latin baseline
author: misswell
body:
## What this fixes

Chinese renders as tofu boxes in the interface and in PDF file names (#651), and a document whose Chinese CID font is not embedded cannot be read at all. This is @sll1679339710-arch's #426 carried to its conclusion, plus the page-rendering half of #455 — both kept as their own commits with their original authorship.

## How

- **One locator, not two.** `crates/fonts/src/system.rs` finds one installed Chinese (Han) face — for the interface *and* the page renderer, on macOS, Windows and Linux. Candidates are accepted only if a face parses and maps every probe character, with bounded reads and a size cap.
- **Reading a page.** The renderer substitutes that face for a non-embedded Chinese CID font so the page can be read on screen. Drawing only: nothing is embedded, copied, shipped or committed (AGENTS.md §1.4).
- **Both scripts.** `zh-hant` asks for the Han face too, not just `zh-hans`. egui draws each character with the first face that has it, so with Japanese faces first, shared Han characters come out in Japanese shapes and characters no Japanese face has land in yet another face.
- **The baseline.** egui places a glyph `face ascent + (primary row − face row) / 2` below the top of its row. Every Chinese face's row is far taller than Inter's, so Chinese sat above the Latin beside it and out of the top of the line. `ui_y_offset_factor` derives the correction from the two faces' own metrics — visual only, no layout moves — so it holds for whichever face the machine carries.
- **Dialog margins.** `Frame::popup`'s inner margin is the 8 pt meant for menus and tooltips, so a dialog's text touched its border — most visible in Chinese, whose glyphs fill their box. All five modals now draw with 20 × 16 pt.
- **Gates.** The interface-font test can no longer pass by finding nothing: the macOS release job runs it with `PDFCRAFT_TEST_REQUIRE_CJK=1` before signing, and the Windows job runs the same test on a real host.

- **Web/wasm st…

title: Sign: decide Windows store keys in code every platform builds (follow-up to #646)
author: jcl-bit
body:
#646 fixed the Windows build that #386 broke, by adding `_` arms to the two `PublicKey` matches in `crates/sign/src/windows.rs`. That module only builds on Windows, so the next new `PublicKey` variant will either break the Windows build again (if someone removes the `_`) or, more likely now, fall into `_` without anyone deciding whether the certificate store should sign with it. This moves those two decisions into `keys.rs`, which every platform builds, with every variant named, and tests them on Linux and macOS as well as Windows. Behaviour doesn't change.

## The change

- `crates/sign/src/keys.rs`, two new `PublicKey` methods and a small `StoreKey` enum. Both methods name every variant, with no `_` arm:
  - `store_signing_key()`: what a key store must hold to sign for this certificate (`StoreKey::Rsa`, or `StoreKey::Ecdsa(bits)` for P-256/P-384), or `None` for keys PdfCraft only verifies with (P-521, brainpool P-256/384/512, Ed25519, `Unsupported`).
  - `store_signature_der(raw)`: CNG's signature as CMS carries it (RSA unchanged, ECDSA's fixed-size `r ‖ s` as DER). The verify-only kinds return `SignError::Unsupported`, as #646 does.
- `crates/sign/src/windows.rs`: both matches now call those methods, so it has no `_` arms left. `identities()` still skips the verify-only kinds. Two messages change wording because they now live in platform-neutral code: "CNG returned an invalid P-256 signature" becomes "the key store returned an invalid P-256 signature", and #646's "signing with this key type through the Windows certificate store" becomes "signing with ECDSA P-521 keys" (naming the key).
- `crates/sign/tests/store_keys.rs`: new, see Tests.

## Why

- `windows.rs` is `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` (`lib.rs`), so only the Windows jobs compile it. #386 added six `PublicKey` variants, passed Linux and macOS CI, and turned every Windows job red (E0004 at `windows.rs:26` and `:66`) until #646.
- `keys.rs` already matches exhaustively on `PublicKey` in `key_bits`, `spki`…

title: M14: Arabic interface language
author: abdelhaqelamraoui
body:
A 2,136-entry Arabic catalog (six CLDR plural forms, Arabic month and weekday names), selected by `ar` and every `ar-*` locale. egui joins Arabic letters but places words left to right, so the catalog is put into display order when it loads (bidi::display_rtl); placeholders, keyboard shortcuts and caption colons stay in place. The craft-fonts pin moves to the revision with Noto Sans Arabic. crates/fonts/build.rs now refuses to embed Adobe type designs, so the Noto Sans CJK SC in that revision is never embedded (AGENTS.md §1.1).

title: M14: View menu, tooltips and Keyboard shortcuts show Ctrl, not ⌘, off macOS
author: Toddpe
body:

On Linux and Windows, View ▸ Zoom and Page navigation showed macOS shortcuts (`⌘1`, `⇧⌘+`, `⌘[`), while the registered items under them showed `Ctrl+K`. The Zoom items were hand-written with literal `"⌘…"` strings. The registered items are formatted by `Shortcut::label(mac)`.

-    mac = cfg!(target_os = "macos") || cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32")

title: M3: test stitched render partitions against whole-page output
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Rendering a page in tiles is expected to produce the same pixels as rendering the whole page, but existing coverage checks only one crop against a whole render. It does not verify stitching a full page from multiple adjacent render requests or varied tile boundaries.

## Root cause

There was no regression test comparing the fully stitched RGBA output across horizontal bands and regular and irregular tile grids.

## Change

Add a synthetic PDF fixture with a fill, crossing stroke, text, and image. Render it whole, stitch tiles from several partition layouts, and compare all RGBA bytes.

## Before

No full-page stitched partition equivalence assertion covered these layouts.

## After

The test asserts byte-for-byte equality for 2, 4, and 8 horizontal bands, 1024×1024 tiles, and irregular 127×131 tiles.

## Unchanged behavior

This is test-only; no production rendering code or output changed.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib stitched_render_partitions_match_a_whole_render` — passed (1 test).
- `cargo fmt --check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace clippy/tests were not run because the requested local disk constraint rules out a full build; rely on CI for those gates.

## Risk

Test-only change; runtime risk is low. It exercises adjacent tile edges against vector paths, text, and an image at multiple partition sizes.

## Independent scope

Standalone; it does not depend on another PR.

title: M5: unify annotation flag parsing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Annotation flag consumers interpreted `/F` differently. Editing protections converted any real number to `i64`, while summaries and properties required an integer. A malformed fractional `/F 128.5` therefore appeared unlocked but rejected edits as locked.

## Root cause

The edit path read `/F` with `as_f64`; other annotation paths independently read it with `as_int`.

## Change

Add one annotation flag reader and use it for edit protection, properties, summaries, and Fill & Sign visibility.

## Before

A regression test using `/F 128.5` failed: summaries said unlocked, but updating the annotation returned “locked”.

## After

All `pdfcraft-annot` flag consumers use the integer-domain reader. The other `/F` readers (crates/render/src/inspect.rs, crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs, crates/forms/src/lib.rs, vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs) are unchanged by this PR. The malformed fractional value is ignored consistently; valid integer lock behavior remains covered by the existing locked-comment test.

## Unchanged behavior

Valid integer flag handling and annotation appearance generation are unchanged.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot --lib` — passed (30 tests).
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace clippy/tests were not run because the requested local disk constraint rules out a full build; rely on CI for those gates.

## Risk

The change is limited to consistent reading of annotation flags; it adds no new flag semantics.

## Independent scope

Standalone; it does not depend on another PR.

title: M3: make render watchdog regressions deterministic
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Render-worker watchdog tests used sleeps and elapsed-time assertions to hold work long enough for timeout, retry, and request-replacement behavior to occur. Scheduler delays could make these tests slow or unstable.

## Root cause

Test hooks simulated slow parsing and rendering with `thread::sleep`, so synchronization depended on wall-clock time.

## Change

Replace delay hooks with test-only parse and render gates. Tests now wait for workers to enter specific shared or private phases, trigger timeout checks while work is held, and release abandoned workers through barriers. The tests cover slow parsing, shared-timeout private retries, exhausted retry budgets, request replacement, deduplicated in-flight work, watchdog replacement, and late-result suppression.

## Before

Several tests waited for 50 ms to 10 seconds, polled worker state, or depended on watchdog thresholds to create the desired interleaving.

## After

The tests coordinate entry, timeout, release, and completion explicitly. They run without artificial parse or render delays.

## Unchanged behavior

Only test code and test-only hooks changed. Production timeout policy and worker behavior are unchanged.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` — 151 passed.
- Seven converted synchronization tests passed 20/20 repeated runs each.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- The earlier full Linux CI job failed in the unrelated `pdfcraft-ui-egui` test `canvas::tests::many_open_documents_share_one_raster_allowance_and_close_releases_handles`; this branch does not change UI or raster-budget behavior. The updated commit has a fresh CI run pending.
- Full workspace clippy/tests were not run locally because the requested disk constraint rules out a full workspace build; CI provides those gates.

## Risk

This is limited to deterministic test coordination; production timeout policy remains unchanged. …

title: M7: normalize PDF font descriptor flags to u32
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

PdfCraft’s font metrics reader accepted a `/FontDescriptor /Flags` value larger than `u32::MAX` by saturating the float-to-`u32` cast. The renderer’s `get::<u32>` reader rejects values outside that domain, so the two font paths could disagree about bold/italic bits.

## Root cause

The metrics path clamped negatives and cast directly to `u32`; the rendering path converts the descriptor value to `u32` and treats failed conversion as no flags.

## Change

Normalize descriptor flags through the same `u32` domain before using the italic and bold bits. Add coverage for a valid bitfield, negative integer, out-of-range integer, wrong type, and missing value.

## Before

The new out-of-range test failed because `4_294_967_296` became `u32::MAX`, setting both tested style bits.

## After

Out-of-domain values contribute no descriptor bits, matching the renderer. Valid in-range bits remain effective.

## Unchanged behavior

Font metrics, weight and angle overrides, and rendering code are unchanged.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts --lib` — passed (24 tests).
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace clippy/tests were not run because the requested local disk constraint rules out a full build; rely on CI for those gates.

## Risk

The change is limited to out-of-domain descriptor flags; valid `u32` flag values retain their existing interpretation.

## Independent scope

Standalone; it does not depend on another PR.

title: M6: reject out-of-domain field flags
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem
Field `/Ff` values outside the unsigned 32-bit domain can set unintended flags. For example, `/Ff -1` is cast to `u32::MAX`, causing a button checkbox to be reported as a pushbutton and read-only.

## Root cause
The field-tree reader converted a signed PDF integer with `as u32`, which wraps negative and oversized values.

## Change
Added one field-flag reader that accepts only values representable as `u32`. Invalid values are ignored like other unparseable inherited attributes. Added coverage for a valid value, a negative value, an overflowing value, a wrong type, and a missing value.

## Before
`/Ff -1` and `/Ff 4295032832` were interpreted as the pushbutton bit; the negative case also set every other flag.

## After
Only the valid `/Ff 65536` fixture is a pushbutton. Invalid or absent values yield the default checkbox kind and zero flags.

## Unchanged behavior
Valid existing field flag combinations and field authoring/writing behavior are unchanged.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms --lib` — 50 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace build/tests were skipped to respect the local disk limit; repository CI will run them.

## Risk
Low. This changes interpretation only for malformed `/Ff` values that cannot be represented as an unsigned 32-bit field bitfield. It adds no allocation, threading, or dependency changes.

## Independent scope
This PR is isolated from the font, annotation, render-partition, and watchdog changes.

title: M2: cancel obsolete in-flight requests
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Replacing the latest render queue could leave an obsolete in-flight page consuming the only worker. A visible replacement then waited for the obsolete render to finish.

On base `68e91d4815ed43212895589411aa3d21b2a84bc3`, the original regression showed request A holding the worker for about 10 seconds before request B could complete. A narrower publication race remained: if A was removed after the worker’s first obsolescence check but before its busy slot was published, `set_queue` could not cancel A during that interval.

## Change

- Give every active request separate cancellation and result-validity tokens.
- Have `set_queue` identify active requests removed from the latest demand and cancel them before waking workers.
- Recheck obsolescence immediately after publishing the busy slot, clearing the slot and skipping parser acquisition when the request was removed in the publication gap.
- Pass the request token into the interpreter and parser-acquisition wait path.
- Require all relevant validity tokens before publishing a result, so canceled or retired-parser work cannot reach the caller.
- Keep the existing watchdog, pool-drop cancellation, deduplication, and retry behavior.

## Regression coverage

`request_removed_before_busy_publication_skips_parser_acquisition` uses a test-only gate to pause request A after its first obsolescence check and before busy publication. It replaces A with B, releases the worker, and verifies A never enters parser acquisition, B renders once, and no stale result is delivered. Without the recheck added here, request A would pass its only obsolescence check, publish its busy slot after B had replaced it, and then enter parser acquisition, so this test's assertion that only B enters parser acquisition would fail. This is reasoned from the code; the prior implementation was not run against this test, because the gate it uses is new in this PR.

`replacing_an_in_flight_request_does_not_delay_the_replacement` is new in this P…

title: About dialog test: wait for each control to stop moving before clicking it (#671)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #671.

## What was wrong
The About dialog is a modal centred on its own size. Switching to **Contributors** grows it, and for a few frames it recentres, so every control in it moves: the **Table** toggle sits at y=378, then 355, then 341 (1400×900 harness). `about_dialog_has_contributors_and_models_tabs` waited a fixed four frames (#656) before clicking Table. Since the 0.5.0 contributors refresh (5 → 78 names) that isn't always enough: deterministic on some Debian machines, intermittent on the GitHub runners (as the follow-up comment on #671 found). The click lands where the button *was*, the table never opens, and the test fails at `links.rs:78` with `No nodes found matching the query: By { label: "PRs" }`.

Clicking after one frame instead of four reproduces exactly that failure, which confirms the mechanism.

## Fix
A small `settled` helper in `crates/ui-egui/tests/links.rs` runs frames until the target node exists and its rect is the same on two frames in a row, then returns it. The test uses it before every click and lookup, so it no longer depends on how many frames the modal needs.

On whether it's user-facing: the dialog itself works. The toggle only moves for the two or three frames after a tab switch, and a real click comes long after that, so no product change is needed.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test links`: 5 passed (repeated runs)
- With the old fixed wait shortened to one frame, the old test fails at links.rs:78 with the reported error; the new test passes either way
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

No duplicates of #671 among open or closed issues. #656 was the earlier fixed-frame workaround for the same test.

title: M14: side panels keep their width after a resize
author: Toddpe
body:
## Summary

After you drag the side panel to a new width, it creeps wider again whenever the pointer moves. egui stores a resizable panel's width as whatever its content used at the end of each frame (`containers/panel.rs`, `PanelState`). So a row wider than the panel widens it on every repaint, up to `size_range` max (520 px). The width is saved between sessions, which is why a narrowed Bookmarks panel looks like it "returns to its original size".

Two rows overflowed:

```diff
 right_panel ▸ Bookmarks ▸ search row        (label · field · 8 px · 26 px clear)
-  field.desired_width(available - 32)       // 2 px too wide → +2 px per repaint
+  field.desired_width(available - CLEAR - item_spacing.x)

 right_panel ▸ Comments ▸ selected comment ▸ reply
-  [ field (available - 56) ][ Post ]        // fits only a 48 px "Post"
+  [ field (full width)            ]
+                           [ Post ]         // right-aligned, any language
```

Post stays after the field rather than going in a button-first right-to-left row or `Sides::shrink_left`, because egui's Tab order follows the order widgets are added.

## Evidence

- **Before** (`main`): the new tests fail as the width climbs:
  ```text
  bookmarks::the_panel_keeps_its_width_while_the_pointer_moves
    add bookmark; 30 × (hover_at; run frame)  →  358.0 → 418.0   (+2 px per frame)
  comments::the_panel_keeps_its_width_with_a_reply_box_open
    post comment; type reply; language = ru; hover "Опубликовать"; 30 frames  →  516.3 → 520.0 (max)
  ```
  **After:** both hold their width. The existing `the_panel_posts_comments_and_replies` still posts through the moved Post button.

  In the running app (`pdfcraft --control`), after dragging the Bookmarks edge 60 px and 30 `ui.move`s, the panel stays at x=500.0. With a Russian reply open and Post hovered 20 times, the Comments panel holds its width, with Post right-aligned under the field.

title: M2: pin output across worker counts
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem
The render worker count varies by host, but there was no test directly asserting that exact page pixels are independent of that count.

## Root cause
The pool tests covered scheduling and worker lifecycle, while pixel goldens used a single-threaded `PageRenderer`.

## Change
Added a deterministic two-page fixture with distinct solid-color content. It compares each page's dimensions and exact RGBA bytes from a single-threaded reference against `RenderPool` configurations with 1, 2, and 4 workers.

## Before
Worker lifecycle and per-page rendering were covered separately; worker-count pixel equivalence was not asserted.

## After
The same page requests must produce byte-identical pixels for each tested pool size. Production worker selection is unchanged.

## Unchanged behavior
No rendering code, scheduling, thread count policy, or golden outputs changed.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib page_pixels_are_invariant_to_render_worker_count` — passed for 1, 2, and 4 workers.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace tests were skipped to respect the local disk limit; repository CI will run them.

## Risk
Low. Test-only; uses a tiny in-memory PDF and bounded worker counts.

## Independent scope

title: M2: decouple content tokenization from slices
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

The content parser's typed layer is coupled directly to the current slice-backed `UntypedIter`. That makes a future chunked tokenizer change the typed dispatch surface at the same time as byte-boundary handling.

## Change

- Add the reader-agnostic `ContentTokenizer` interface for producing borrowed content instructions.
- Keep `UntypedIter<'a>` as the existing slice-backed implementation with unchanged parsing behavior.
- Make `TypedIter` generic over a tokenizer while preserving the existing `TypedIter::new` and `TypedIter<'a>` API shape.
- Add `TypedIter::from_tokenizer` so a future streaming tokenizer can reuse typed operator dispatch without another parser fork.
- The only changed file is `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`, a patch to the vendored crate.

No streaming implementation is included in this PR.

## Regression coverage

The synthetic content corpus covers comments, numbers, names and escaped names, literal and hex strings, arrays, dictionaries, `TJ`, inline images, whitespace, and adjacent operators. The expected operator sequence remains exactly `TJ`, `BI`, `q`, `Q`.

The boundary helper rejoins the two halves of the corpus at every possible split and requires the same operator sequence each time. It does not yet feed the halves to the tokenizer separately, so it does not exercise a split stream; chunked-input coverage belongs with the streaming tokenizer.

## Verification

- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/pdfcraft-render-target cargo test --manifest-path vendor/hayro-syntax/Cargo.toml --lib content::tests` — 2 passed
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/pdfcraft-render-target cargo check -p pdfcraft-render --lib` — passed

title: M2: cover inherited form resource contexts
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem
A cached PDF object can be interpreted differently under different resource dictionaries. The same indirect Form XObject must resolve the named color space in the page that invokes it.

## Root cause
This PR adds a regression fixture for the context dependency; it makes no production change because the current renderer resolves the fixture correctly.

## Change
Both pages reference the same indirect Form XObject (`4 0 R`). Its content uses `/CS1`; one page maps `/CS1` to `/DeviceRGB`, and the other maps it to a valid calibrated RGB space with a different transfer curve. The test checks successful renders and verifies that each page's painted pixel differs and is non-white.

## Before
The test suite had no fixture documenting different results for one shared indirect Form XObject under page-specific inherited resources.

## After
The test pins that the shared object resolves `/CS1` in each calling page's context. Current page pixels differ as required; single-context production behavior is unchanged.

## Unchanged behavior
No cache key, renderer code, pixels outside the painted form, warnings, memory use, or thread count is changed.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib shared_form_xobject_uses_each_pages_resource_context` — passed.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace tests were skipped to respect the local disk limit; repository CI will run them.

## Risk
Low. Test-only, using a small in-memory PDF.

## Independent scope
This fixture does not change any cache and is independent of the worker-count, partition-equivalence, and flag-domain PRs.

title: M5: preserve strokes with malformed interior colors
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem
A malformed optional `/IC` interior-color value made an otherwise valid annotation appearance fail to build. A Square with valid `/Rect` and `/C` but two-component `/IC` therefore received no display appearance, hiding its border.

## Root cause
`appearance::build` propagated `/IC` parse failure with `?` for Square, Circle, Polygon, Line, and PolyLine appearances, even though their strokes remain meaningful without a fill color.

## Change
Malformed `/IC` now follows the subtype's absent-color fallback: no fill for Square, Circle, and Polygon; the stroke color for Line and PolyLine line endings. The test covers all five subtypes and verifies display-copy generation creates a drawable Square appearance without changing the source document.

## Before
The regression test failed at Square: `appearance::build` returned `None`, and `with_missing_appearances` produced no display copy.

## After
All five valid shapes build an appearance when `/IC` is malformed. The Square display appearance contains its red stroke and unfilled rectangle path.

## Unchanged behavior
Valid `/IC` values keep their existing appearance. Malformed required stroke colors and invalid geometry remain rejected. Unknown `/LE` values still refuse redraw, preserving the existing protection for unsupported decorations.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot --lib` — 30 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full workspace build/tests were skipped to respect the local disk limit; repository CI will run them.

## Risk
Low. The change affects only malformed optional interior colors; no new dependencies, allocations, or threads.

## Independent scope
This is one annotation appearance fallback and is independent of the flag-domain, rendering-fixture, and watchdog PRs.

title: M2: cover form recursion cycles

## Tests

title: Windows: single instance, launches started together share one window (#282, #317)
author: benimaru327
body:
## What this is

This builds on #602 by @art804 (single-instance hand-off over a Unix domain socket) and fixes a race found when running it on Windows. The branch holds two commits:

1. #602's commit, unchanged apart from a merge conflict in `apps/pdfcraft/Cargo.toml` (main has since added `winsafe` in the same place; both entries are kept, in one `cfg(target_os = "windows")` table).
2. The fix described below.

If you would rather take the fix into #602 itself, the second commit applies on its own on top of that branch.

Refs #282, #317.

## The race

Selecting several PDFs in Explorer and pressing Enter starts one process per file at the same moment. With #602 as written, a launch can find the socket already bound by another launch that is not listening yet:

- connecting fails,
- clearing the socket fails with `Access is denied (os error 5)`,
- the launch logs `single instance off: can't clear …instance-Console.sock` and opens a window of its own.

Starting three `pdfcraft.exe <file>` processes together, with nothing running, gave two windows in 2 of 3 rounds.

## The fix

- Launches take turns through a lock on a file beside the socket (`instance-<session>.lock`, `std::fs::File::try_lock`). It is held only while a launch finds out whether it is the first, so the first one is listening before the next one looks. The file is never deleted; Windows releases the lock when the process ends. If the lock can't be had within 5 s, the launch goes on as before.
- A socket that can't be cleared because another launch holds it (`PermissionDenied`) is tried again instead of giving up.

No new dependency.

## Testing

On Windows, real processes, release build:

- A second launch with a file while one is running: exits in about 0.1 s, one process remains.
- Three launches at the same moment with nothing running, six rounds after the fix: one process every time, no warnings in the log.

These real-process runs were done on the branch based on `c110c57`; the branch was then reba…

author: cyfung1031

## Problem

`/UserUnit` (PDF 1.6) gives the size of a page's user-space unit in points. It is used for pages larger than 200 inches: large-format CAD and engineering drawings, banners, maps. PdfCraft ignored it everywhere except the measuring tools, so a `/UserUnit 2` page was shown, extracted, printed and edited at half its size.

The measuring tools did apply it, so the page geometry disagreed with itself on such pages. For example, the snapping tolerance mixed the measure crate's "points" with the viewer's user units.

A 288 × 288-unit page with `/UserUnit 2`: PdfCraft shows it at 4 × 4 in, Acrobat at 8 × 8 in.

title: M3: make multi-document raster allowance test deterministic
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

The multi-document raster allowance regression test could submit a real thumbnail render while checking its synthetic texture against an obsolete byte threshold. Its result depended on whether the native worker completed first.

## Historical context

PR #419 introduced the test when the thumbnail slot was 132×176. PR #529 intentionally raised the production slot to 240×320 to improve high-DPI rendering. That quality improvement remains unchanged.

## Root cause

The fixture hard-coded a THUMB_TAG request at the default scale and a 132×171 result. Production now derives each request's scale and tag from page dimensions, pixels-per-point, the thumbnail dimensions and the existing memory allowance. The synthetic result therefore did not satisfy current demand. finish_render_frame() could queue a legitimate native render that raced the test fixture and replaced its smaller texture before the budget assertion.

## Change

- Derive each synthetic request from thumbnail_requests() after recording real thumbnail demand.
- Compute result dimensions and bytes using the production scale and dimension helpers.
- Assert the cached tag and texture dimensions match the derived request.
- Recompute the queue after injecting the result and establish a quiescent queue before application frame finalization.
- Check all six views before retirement, hidden-view cleanup, active-view ownership and close behavior, and verify the fixture starts no native render.
- Replace the `total <= 132 * 171 * 4` check with exact equality to the active view's thumbnail bytes, and keep a `total <= THUMB_BYTES` allowance check.

## Before

The target test passed on the unchanged baseline, but the synthetic request's default scale and tag differed from the current production request. This structural mismatch shows that the old fixture could depend on the worker scheduling race.

## After

The synthetic thumbnail exactly satisfies current demand. Application frame finalization does not submit a…

title: Issue #666: images made into a PDF keep their ICC profile
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #666

`doc_create {"from":"images"}` (and `image_xobject`, which stamps, image signatures and inserted images use) dropped the ICC profile embedded in a JPEG or PNG. A CMYK JPEG became untagged `/DeviceCMYK`, so nothing in the file said which CMYK space its numbers were in.

- **JPEG:** the `APP2 ICC_PROFILE` chunks are joined in sequence-number order. If a chunk is missing or repeated, the profile is ignored.
- **PNG:** the `iCCP` profile is read.
- A profile is kept when its header is sound (`acsp`) and its colour space matches the image (`GRAY`/`RGB `/`CMYK` for 1/3/4 components). It becomes `[/ICCBased <stream>]` with `/N` and the device space as `/Alternate`, so readers that can't use the profile fall back to what they drew before. Otherwise the image keeps its device space, as it does today.
- JPEG data is still embedded byte for byte, and an Adobe CMYK JPEG keeps its inverted `/Decode`.
- Images in one document that carry the same profile share one profile object.
- `extract_images` already handled `/ICCBased`, so exported images are unchanged.

Not covered: TIFF ICC profiles (tag 34675) are not read yet. The parity notes for `create.from-images` say so. #667 (the `pdfa_convert` output intent) is a separate change.

The image-embedding code shared by `from_images_with_resolution` and `image_xobject` now lives in one helper, `add_image`.

### Tests
- `crates/create/src/tests.rs::embedded_icc_profiles_tag_the_image_colour_space` (new, synthetic fixtures built in the test). It fails on `main` and passes with this change. It covers:
  - a CMYK JPEG whose profile is split over two `APP2` chunks written out of order, which gives `/ICCBased` with N 4, `/Alternate /DeviceCMYK`, the exact profile bytes, `/Decode` kept and the JPEG bytes unchanged;
  - two images with the same profile, which share one profile object;
  - an RGB PNG with `iCCP`, which gives `/ICCBased` with N 3;

title: Issue #727: tell the user when GitHub rate-limits update checks
author: ShauryaSwarup
body:
Fixes #727.

## Problem

When GitHub's anonymous rate limit (60 requests/hour per public IP) runs out, Help ▸ Check for updates reports `couldn't reach GitHub (http status: 403)` — which reads like the app or the network is broken. Reproduced with the app's own request headers: GitHub answers `403 API rate limit exceeded` with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`.

## Fix

`latest_release` now reads error statuses itself (`http_status_as_error(false)`) instead of letting ureq turn them into opaque errors:

- **403** → names the cause and the wait from `X-RateLimit-Reset`: "GitHub is limiting update checks for now (shared hourly quota); try again in about N minutes" (rounded up, singular/plural handled), falling back to "try again later" when the header is missing, unparsable, or already past.
- **Other non-2xx** → keeps the exact old message, byte for byte.
- No new dependencies; no unwrap/expect/panics (checked arithmetic, `checked_sub`, fallbacks throughout).

## Verification

- New unit test `rate_limit_messages_name_the_wait` (naming, rounding, and all fallback shapes).
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p pdfcraft updates` → 2 passed, 1 ignored (live-network test, as designed).
- Full-workspace gates left to CI: a full local rebuild is impractical on this machine (release profile dylibs are unloadable under macOS 27's dyld with both Homebrew and official toolchains — possibly worth its own issue).

title: PDF/A: no sRGB output intent for CMYK documents, and pdfa_verify checks the intent's colour space (#667)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
`pdfa_convert` always added the generated **sRGB** output intent when a document had none, including documents whose only content is `/DeviceCMYK` (e.g. a CMYK JPEG made into a PDF with `doc_create`). `pdfa_verify` then reported `"compliant": true`, because it only checked that *some* PDF/A output intent existed. ISO 19005-2 §6.2.4.3 allows DeviceCMYK only under a CMYK output intent, and DeviceRGB only under an RGB one, so the file was both mislabelled and wrongly reported as compliant.

## The fix (`crates/preflight`)
- **verify** reads the PDF/A output intent's destination profile (`/N`, falling back to the ICC header's data colour space) and reports:
  - "DeviceCMYK is used, but the PDF/A output intent isn't a CMYK profile" (6.2.4.3, not fixable)
  - "DeviceRGB is used, but the PDF/A output intent isn't an RGB profile" (6.2.4.3, not fixable)
- **convert** adds the sRGB intent only when the document has no DeviceCMYK. A CMYK document now keeps the existing "DeviceCMYK is used: it needs a CMYK output intent (not added automatically)" issue in `remaining` instead of getting a wrong intent, so `pdfa_convert` no longer claims compliance for it.
- Device colour detection now tells gray, RGB and CMYK apart (gray is fine under any intent).
- Parity notes for `pdfa_verify` / `pdfa_convert` updated.

Not in this PR: letting the caller supply a CMYK output intent (e.g. `"output_intent": "FOGRA39.icc"`), which the issue also suggests. That needs a decision on the tool/UI surface, so this change only stops the wrong intent and the false "compliant".

## How tested
- New regression tests in `crates/preflight/src/tests.rs`:
  - `convert_does_not_give_cmyk_documents_an_srgb_output_intent`: a page painting a DeviceCMYK image (the issue's repro). No sRGB intent is added and the CMYK-intent issue remains, not fixable.
  - `verify_reports_an_output_intent_that_does_not_match_device_colour`: CMYK under an sRGB intent (what convert used to write) is reported; CMYK + …

title: On-page text boxes keep a dark caret on their white backgrounds in the dark theme (#655)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #655.

The text boxes PdfCraft draws on the page have fixed light backgrounds in every theme, but the caret took its colour from the theme. In the dark theme egui's caret is pale (`Visuals::dark()`), so it was white on white and could not be seen.

This happens in four on-page editors, and all four are fixed:
- editing existing text (`edit_text_ui.rs`, white box),
- filling a form text field (`forms_ui.rs`, pale yellow field),
- typing text with Fill & Sign (`fill_sign.rs`, white box),
- adding a new text box (`content_ui.rs`, white box).

Inside those boxes only, the editor now sets `text_cursor.stroke.color` from a small helper, `caret_color_on(fill)`, which returns black on light fills and white on dark ones. The rest of the theme is not changed: dialogs and panels keep the theme's caret, and the light theme looks the same as before (dark caret).

Test: `caret_contrasts_with_its_fill` checks that the caret is black on the white and pale yellow fills and white on a black fill.

title: M2: text turned at any angle reads as lines along its own baseline
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

The text layer (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) sorts every glyph into the nearest of four writing directions (right, down, left, up) and lays it out by its axis-aligned box. That is right for horizontal and vertical text. It goes wrong for text turned to other angles, such as CAD dimension labels, rotated stamps, seals and diagonal watermarks:

- At 30° and 60°, words written with `TJ` offsets lose their spaces (`Rotatedlabelone`).
- At 37° and 45°, the words of one line come out as separate lines in reverse order (`one\nlabel\nRotated`).
- Two lines 13 pt apart at 37°–45° interleave letter by letter (`FiSrset clionned t elixnte here`).
- Lines at 30° and −30° that cross each other become two-letter fragments.
- Text set along a curve comes out in fragments (`VED ST AMP \nT\nE\nX\nCU\nR\nT`).

The cause is that a turned glyph's axis-aligned box is taller and wider than the glyph, so neighbouring glyphs' boxes overlap. The word gaps between them disappear, and boxes from the next line overlap the current one.

## Minimal reproducer

One Helvetica line with `TJ` word gaps, turned 37°:

```
BT /F1 12 Tf 0.798636 0.601815 -0.601815 0.798636 100 200 Tm [(Rotated) -400 (label) -400 (one)] TJ ET
```

On `main` this extracts as `one\nlabel\nRotated`. The tests below build every case with lopdf.

## Expected behavior

Turned text reads as lines along its own baseline, with its word gaps, in the same order it has when horizontal. Horizontal, vertical and quarter-turn text stays exactly as it is.

## Cause

`TextDevice::draw_glyph` kept only the glyph's bounding box and its direction rounded to a quarter turn. `extract_page` then laid each quarter's glyphs out in that quarter's frame.

## Change

- `TextGlyph` gains `quad`, the glyph's drawn em box as four corners in view space, and `direction`, a unit vector of the writing direction. `rect` stays the bounding box (of `quad`), so every current user is unchanged.
- **Glyphs near a quarter turn keep the existing path.*…

title: M3: document why fixed-zoom sizes differ from Acrobat (no runtime change)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

Documents why PdfCraft's fixed zoom percentages draw a page at a different size from Acrobat's at the same percentage, with the measurements behind that conclusion. This PR makes no runtime change. It changes parity metadata only, so no behaviour changes and no code changes are included.

Changed file: `parity/acrobat-features.toml`, notes for `view.zoom-to-percent` and `view.zoom-actual-size`. Status, commands, tools and evidence are unchanged. No Rust source changed.

## Cause

PdfCraft defines 100% as the 96-dpi basis: one PDF point is 96/72 logical pixels (`PT` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`). Acrobat's fixed-percentage display follows its Page Display Resolution preference, which Adobe documents as "Use System Setting" or "Custom Resolution". The measured rule is:

    logical px per PDF point = resolution (ppi) / 72 × zoom

The rule matches every Custom resolution tested below. PdfCraft has no matching preference, so its percentages always use 96 ppi.

## Measurements

Setup: one Mac with a built-in Retina display (1512 × 982 logical points, 2× backing scale) and Acrobat DC. The probe is a synthetic A4 PDF with a 100 × 100 pt blue square. No Acrobat bundle was inspected, and no Acrobat screenshot or output is committed. Each value is the square's measured width in logical pixels divided by 100 pt. Edge pixels add about half a logical pixel, so the values can read up to about 0.005 high. Each Acrobat setting was restored to its original value after measuring.

| Setting | 100% measured (formula) | 75% measured (formula) |
|---|---|---|
| PdfCraft (fixed 96 dpi) | 1.333 | 1.000 |
| Acrobat, Custom 96 ppi | 1.340 (1.333) | 1.000 (1.000) |
| Acrobat, Custom 110 ppi | 1.533 (1.528) | 1.150 (1.146) |
| Acrobat, Custom 120 ppi | 1.670 (1.667) | 1.250 (1.250) |
| Acrobat, Use System Setting (reads 127 ppi) | 1.768 (1.764) | not measured |

- Custom resolution sets the fixed-percentage scale by the formula at all three values tested. A 15% gap appears on…

title: fix(macos): render Simplified Chinese menus with an installed Chinese font
author: C0deH0st
body:
macOS releases currently embed Japanese CJK faces but no Hans face, while the installed-font fallback only probes Arabic. Simplified Chinese menu labels therefore fall through to missing glyphs.

Use one installed Chinese collection (PingFang or STHeiti) when the macOS Simplified Chinese interface has no embedded Hans face. Place it before the Japanese faces in every UI family so shared and Simplified-only characters use one baseline. Give Chinese collections a separate bounded size limit, since STHeiti exceeds the existing 32 MiB limit. Keep the existing fallback for other modes and respect PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0.

title: Sign: smart cards and tokens in the Windows store ask for their PIN (#694)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Fixes #694.

## The problem

Signing with a Windows store identity whose key is on a smart card or USB token fails with `Error code 80090022` (NTE_SILENT_CONTEXT) and never shows a PIN dialog.

`identities()` acquires every key with `CRYPT_ACQUIRE_SILENT_FLAG` so that listing can't prompt, and signing reused that handle after `set_silent(false)`. That only drops `NCRYPT_SILENT_FLAG` from `NCryptSignHash`: a provider handle that was opened silently stays silent, so a card that needs its PIN refuses instead of asking.

## The change

- `WindowsKey` keeps the certificate context and acquires a fresh, non-silent key handle when it signs, so the provider can show its own dialog. Listing is unchanged and still silent.
- Second commit: `windows::find` fills `chain` with the issuers Windows chains the certificate to (without the root), so the signature embeds them as it does for a `.p12`. A token certificate is normally issued by an intermediate CA; without it the signature validates only where the reader already has that CA. `identities()` still builds no chains.

## Checked

- By hand with a qualified certificate on a SafeNet token (SafeNet Smart Card Key Storage Provider, RSA-2048) on Windows 11: 0.5.0 fails with 80090022, this branch shows the SafeNet PIN dialog and signs.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign --test pdf -- --ignored windows_store`: the existing software-key round trip, and the new `a_windows_store_identity_signs_with_its_issuers` (a temporary root, issuer and signer; the signature validates against the root alone).
- The test cleanup guard now also removes the public copy `New-SelfSignedCertificate` leaves in Current User > Intermediate Certification Authorities. The existing test left three behind on every run.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`.

title: M2: overlapping text runs stay whole; placement in arrange, bounded checks
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Two text runs that overprint each other on one baseline are merged into one segment, and the segment's glyphs are sorted by x. The letters of the two runs therefore come out interleaved. For example, "Alpha beta gamma" and "Delta epsilon zeta" drawn from the same origin extract as `ADleplhtaa  ebpestialo gna zmemtaa`, and a line drawn twice extracts as `BBeeffoorree`. This happens to horizontal and turned text alike.

## Rebase

This is the previous PR head (`a06d88c`, based on `68e91d4`) rebased onto `main` (`1c33e6f`, which contains #735). The old commits are replaced by seven new commits on the same branch. The previous head is kept as `backup/fix-text-overlap-runs-a06d88c` locally.

- The run model lives in `arrange()`, not in `layout()`. `arrange()` keeps its fake-bold filter and `kept` mapping. Runs, segments and collisions use indices into the filtered `Vec<&TextGlyph>`, and the returned order is mapped through `kept`. `layout()` is unchanged.
- Turned text needs no separate path. `arrange_flow()` already lays out each flow in its own baseline frame, so the overprint fix applies there too.
- The helpers take `&TextGlyph` and do not clone glyphs.

## Bounds for the new quadratic paths (requested in review)

Each of these is its own commit, measured against the commit before it.

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Zero-width marks inserted into `placed` (`marks × placed`) | per-mark search and `Vec::insert` | one cursor pass, linear in marks + placed (`d47d398`) |
| `collide` pair sweep when many glyphs start at one x | every pair, quadratic | `COLLIDE_PAIRS_PER_GLYPH = 16` pair tests per glyph of the segment; a denser segment joins all its text runs into one component, one pass (`db3e741`) |
| `breaks.contains()` per glyph | linear per glyph | breaks sorted once, `binary_search` (`1b3aef6`) |
| Word gap: `idx.iter().position()` per gap (on `main` too) | linear per gap | per-glyph position table written per segment, never cleared (`89d35ae`) …

title: M9: the signer's certificate must allow document signing (key usage, EKU, critical extensions)
author: bartalos86
body:
## Summary

Signature validation now checks that the signer's certificate may sign documents. Before this change, a document signed with a trusted TLS-server or encryption-only certificate was reported **Valid**. The 2026-10-09 ROADMAP entry on the #144 review listed this as still missing: "key usage and extended key usage of the signer, … unknown critical extensions".

`Certificate::signing_problem` (in `crates/sign/src/x509.rs`) applies three checks from RFC 5280 §4.2.1.3, §4.2.1.12 and §4.2:

- **Key usage:** if a keyUsage extension is present, it must include digitalSignature or nonRepudiation.
- **Extended key usage:** if an EKU extension is present, it must include a document-signing purpose. The accepted purposes are anyExtendedKeyUsage, emailProtection, codeSigning, documentSigning (RFC 9336), Adobe Authentic Documents (1.2.840.113583.1.1.5) and Microsoft document signing (1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.12).
- **Critical extensions:** the certificate may not have a critical extension that PdfCraft doesn't process. These OIDs are recorded while parsing in `Certificate::unknown_critical`. Certificate policies and subject/issuer alternative names don't count as unknown: policies are accepted as any policy.

When a check fails, the verdict becomes **Unknown** rather than Valid. This is the same treatment as a signer certificate that was expired at signing time. The signature details say which check failed. A revocation or a disallowed change still makes the signature Invalid.

A second, separate commit fixes `parity/acrobat-features.toml` on main. #649 and #650 each added `evidence` and `notes` to `form.field-list`, so the file had duplicate keys and `cargo xtask parity` failed.

## Tests

title: Extract pages: a File name field names the extracted files (#737)
author: DWAA1660

title: M9: sign and timestamp encrypted documents
author: silverhadch
body:
Signing a password-protected PDF failed with "not supported: signing encrypted documents". The writer encrypted every string, including the signature's /Contents placeholder, which the signer patches in place after hashing.

- cos: a signature dictionary's /Contents is never encrypted or decrypted (ISO 32000-2 §7.6.2), identified by /Type /Sig|/DocTimeStamp or by /Contents + /ByteRange. Existing signatures in encrypted files now read their real CMS and survive rewrites of their dictionary.
- sign: the blanket refusal is replaced by the document's permissions (Table 22) when opened with the user password: existing fields and document timestamps need fill-forms, new fields need annotate + modify, certifying needs modify. Refusals name the permissions password.
- Tests for all four algorithms, counter-signing, tampering, permissions, document timestamps and the sign_document tool; parity entry sign.encrypted-documents; ROADMAP log.

title: M4: bookmarks from tagged headings (organize.bookmarks-from-structure)
author: bartalos86
body:
## Summary

New feature, roughly Acrobat's "New Bookmarks From Structure", for headings only. In a tagged document, **Bookmark options ▸ New bookmarks from structure** turns the headings into bookmarks. It is also the command `bookmark.from_structure` and the agent tool `bookmark_from_structure`. Before this, the parity entry `organize.bookmarks-from-structure` (P1, M4) was `planned`.

How it works:

- **Reading the headings:** `pdfcraft_a11y::headings` (new file `crates/a11y/src/headings.rs`) walks the structure tree.
  - `H1`–`H6` are read through the role map. A plain `H` takes its level from the number of `Sect`/`Part`/`Art` elements around it.
  - The title is the element's `/ActualText`. Without one, it is the text of the heading's marked content drawn on the page, decoded with `pdfcraft_fonts::pdf::Metrics` (ToUnicode or encoding). After that come `/Alt` and `/T`. Headings with no text, or no page, are skipped.
- **Writing the bookmarks:** `pdfcraft_organize::add_bookmark_tree` (in `outline.rs`) nests the entries by level under a new first top-level bookmark, "Untitled", as Acrobat does.
  - Each item goes to the heading's page (`/XYZ null null null`, the same as a new bookmark) and links to its structure element with `/SE` (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3).
  - All pages are checked before anything is written. Each item's links (`/Parent`, `/Next` and so on) are set once, and `/Count` is recomputed once.
- **The edit:** `Edit::BookmarksFromStructure` is one undo step. Like the other bookmark edits, it needs the assemble permission.
  - An untagged document gets an error that says why: "this document has no tagged headings to make bookmarks from".
- **The UI:** the Bookmarks panel's options menu now also shows when the document has no bookmarks, if the panel is editable, so that a tagged document without bookmarks can use the new item.

title: Exported images keep their transparency, JPEG cut-outs included (#645)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
Export a PDF ▸ Image ▸ Export all images (and Edit ▸ Save image as) lost transparency, so cut-out images came out on a solid white or black background (#645):
- A JPEG with an `/SMask` (the usual cut-out photo) was written as the bare JPEG.
- Soft masks of a different size from the image, and JPEG-compressed soft masks, were dropped.
- Stencil `/Mask` images and colour-key `/Mask` arrays were ignored.

## The fix (`crates/create/src/extract.rs`)
- An image with transparency (`/SMask`, stencil `/Mask` or colour-key `/Mask`) is written as a PNG with that transparency as alpha. This includes JPEG images, which are decoded with the `image` crate's JPEG decoder (zune-jpeg, already in the tree; I enabled the `jpeg` feature in `pdfcraft-create`). JPEGs without transparency are still written byte for byte. A JPEG that fails to decode falls back to the old behaviour.
- Soft and stencil masks of a different size are scaled to the image's size. Their `/Decode` inversion is applied, and `/Matte` pre-blending is undone for grey and RGB images.
- Image sizes are checked (positive, at most 100 Mpx) before use. On main, a negative `/Width` made `image_file` (Save image as) overflow and panic.
- JPX, JBIG2 and CCITT masks are still left out (the image is exported opaque). The parity notes for `create.export-all-images` say so.

## How it was tested
- New tests in `crates/create/src/tests.rs`: `jpeg_images_with_a_soft_mask_export_as_png_with_alpha`, `soft_masks_of_another_size_and_stencil_and_colour_key_masks_become_alpha` (scaled soft mask, stencil mask, colour key, matte) and `damaged_masks_and_sizes_never_panic`. All three fail on main; the last one panics.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (14 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask parity` all pass.

Fixes #645
