title: Single instance: enable tab handoff in Windows portable mode (#889)
author: A-viral-dev
body:
## What was wrong
When using the portable Windows package (`pdfcraft-0.5.0-windows-x64-portable.zip`), opening multiple PDFs from File Explorer or the terminal always spawns a separate process and new window for every single file. Single-instance tab handoff was explicitly disabled whenever `portable::data_dir().is_some()`.

## The fix
- In `apps/pdfcraft/src/single_instance.rs`, allow `socket_path()` to use `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PdfCraft\instance-<session>.sock` for portable packages on Windows.
- Because `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is already protected by the user's Windows ACLs, no other user account can tamper with or intercept the temporary IPC socket.
- Falls back to `portable::data_dir()` if `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is unavailable.
- Portable users now get multiple documents opened as tabs in the existing window by default.

Fixes #889
Related: #282, #317

title: fix(text): Turkish dotted and dotless i match in case-insensitive search
author: snipeTR
body:
## Summary

Case-insensitive search can't find Turkish words that contain the dotted or dotless i. Searching for `istanbul` doesn't find `İSTANBUL`, and `ırmak` / `kış` don't find `IRMAK` / `KIŞ` (or the reverse).

`PageText::find` is used by Find, by Search & Redact (both the phrase and the word-list modes) and by the automation text search. So this also means a Turkish word in a redaction list can be **left unredacted** when it appears in a different case on the page.

## Root cause

`PageText::find_opts` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) folds both the query and the page text with `str::to_lowercase`, which doesn't depend on locale:

- `İ` (U+0130) lowercases to `i` + U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE (two characters), so `İSTANBUL` folds to `i̇stanbul` and never equals `istanbul`.
- `I` lowercases to `i`, while `ı` (U+0131) stays `ı`, so `IRMAK` folds to `irmak` and never equals `ırmak`.

## Fix

A small `fold_case` helper replaces `to_lowercase` in the case-insensitive branch:

- `I`, `i`, `İ` and `ı` all fold to `i`.
- Every other character uses its own `char::to_lowercase`.

The result keeps exactly one character per input character. `İ` was the only character whose lowercase form was longer than itself.

Case-sensitive search is unchanged.

**Why lenient folding and not locale-based (tr/az) folding:** search can't know the document's language, and the UI language is no reliable stand-in for it. Under locale-free folding, Turkish text can't be matched case-insensitively at all. Under Turkish rules, `I` would stop matching `i`, which would break English. Treating the four letters as one only adds matches where `ı` or `İ` is involved; matching for text without them is unchanged.

## Tests

title: Automation: add text_clip tool for spatial bounding-box extraction (#885)
author: A-viral-dev
body:
## What was wrong
When processing structured PDF documents (such as table cells, key-value forms, and multi-column reports) headlessly via MCP or CLI automation, agents must currently extract either entire pages via `text_extract` or all page lines via `text_lines` and manually implement spatial bounding-box filtering and reading-order reconstruction.

## The fix
- Added `text_clip` tool to `crates/automation`: extracts text located within a bounding box `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` on a given page (points, origin top-left).
- Filters glyphs using center-point containment within the specified rectangle.
- Reconstructs word spacing and line breaks in reading order, returning both full extracted `text` and structured `lines` with bounding boxes.
- Registered with schema `{"doc": ..., "page": ..., "rect": [...]}` and marked read-only.
- Added end-to-end test `text_clip_spatial_extraction` in `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs`.

Fixes #885

title: M11: Reduce file size and Optimize PDF drop images nothing draws, such as a deleted image
author: taylorandrew07-lab
body:
## What this fixes

Deleting an image with **Edit a PDF** removes it from the page, but its data stayed in the file, even after **Reduce file size** or **Optimize PDF**, which rewrite the whole file.

On a one-page scan (227 KB) whose image was deleted, the page is blank (`page_images` lists 0 images), yet Reduce and Optimize both wrote a 227 KB copy. A blank page is about 1 KB. (With #849, Reduce would even say "already as small as it can be made", which is wrong here.)

**Why:** delete removes the drawing operation (`Do`) from the content stream, but the image stays listed in the page's `/Resources /XObject`. A full rewrite keeps everything still referenced, and the optimizer only looked at images that pages draw, so nothing dropped it. Files from other tools that list images they never draw had the same problem.

(A normal Save is an incremental update, so the original bytes stay in the file there by design; Redact and Remove Hidden Information are the tools for removing data. This PR is about the rewrites.)

## The change

Clean Up (run by both Reduce file size and Optimize PDF) now drops image and form XObjects that a page lists in its resources but nothing draws (`crates/optimize/src/unused.rs`).

Removing a name that something still draws would make content disappear, and viewers (PdfCraft's renderer included) look names up through parent resources, so the rule is deliberately simple and errs on the side of keeping:
- **Only a page's own resources are cleaned:** dictionaries nothing else refers to. Resources shared with other pages, forms or appearances, and inherited ones, are left alone.
- **A name goes only if it is written nowhere** in any stream the document still uses, found by scanning the bytes wherever the name appears. Nothing can draw a resource by name without writing the name in a stream, whichever resources a viewer then looks it up in. The old content stream that Edit a PDF replaced is no longer used, so it doesn't count.
- **If any stream can'…

title: Viewer: Continuous scrolling is an independent checkbox over the base layout (#752)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #752.

Page display now matches Acrobat: the base layout (**Single page** or **Two-page view**) is a radio choice, and **Continuous scrolling** is a separate checkbox, so every combination is reachable. This also adds the previously missing **Two-page view, one spread at a time** mode.

### Model
`PageLayout` now has just `Single` and `TwoUp`; a separate `continuous` flag on the view (and on the default view preferences) decides whether it scrolls. A single `display_token` (`single` | `continuous` | `two-up` | `two-page`) serialises both for settings and the control channel — keeping the earlier `continuous`/`single`/`two-up` names working and adding `two-page` for the new mode. The PDF's own `/PageLayout` request maps to the right `(layout, continuous)` pair, including plain two-up (previously forced to continuous).

### UI & commands

- `view.continuous` toggles the checkbox; `view.layout.single` / `view.layout.two_up` switch the base layout without touching scrolling. The former `view.layout.continuous` command is removed (its state is Single + continuous); the `layout` / `default-layout` options plus a new `continuous` option cover scripting and the control channel.
- When not scrolling, the wheel and the arrow / Page keys turn whole **spreads** in Two-page view, and only the current page or spread is laid out.

### Tests
New `notches_turn_two_page_spreads` and `two_page_view_shows_one_spread_at_a_time_until_continuous`, plus updated layout/command/persistence tests. title: Issue #870: keys leave the document under a dialog alone
author: jay-tau
body:
Closes #870.

## The problem

While Preferences, or any other dialog, was open, keyboard shortcuts still acted on the document behind it:

- ⌘W / Ctrl+W closed the file (#870), and ⌘⇧W closed all files.
- ⌘Z undid the last edit, and ⌘F opened Find.
- In Organize Pages, **Delete or Backspace deleted the selected pages** behind the dialog. The page grid also took the Escape meant to close the dialog, so Escape cleared the page selection and left the dialog open.

The "Save changes?" prompt already kept its keys to itself ("nothing may run underneath it"), but the other modals didn't.

## The change

- `PdfCraftApp::modal_open()` is true while any modal is up: a dialog, the save, password and link prompts, or the update check.
- `shortcuts()` returns early when it's true, the same way it already does for the save prompt. So neither the registered shortcuts nor the canvas shortcuts reach the document.
- The organize grid's keys (Delete/Backspace, Escape, copy/cut/paste pages) now use the existing `unobstructed` flag, which was only used for autoscroll. That flag now comes from `modal_open()` too, so the password, link and update prompts also block page input and autoscroll.

⌘W under a dialog now does nothing; the issue allowed either this or closing the dialog. It matches how the save prompt treats ⌘W, and Escape or Cancel still closes the dialog.

## Checked

- New kittest `keys_leave_the_document_under_a_dialog_alone` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/editing.rs`. With Preferences open over Organize Pages and a page selected, it presses ⌘W, ⌘⇧W, ⌘Z, ⌘D, ⌘F, Delete and Backspace. Each time the file must stay open with its edit and pages intact, Find closed and Preferences still showing. Then Escape must close Preferences and leave the page selection as it was, and ⌘W must work again. On `main` the test fails at the first key: ⌘W asks to close the file.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` (all …

title: fix(redact): Turkish, German, French and Italian month names in the Dates pattern
author: snipeTR
body:
## Problem

The **Dates** pattern of Search & Redact (`crates/redact/src/patterns.rs`) only knew English month names. Dates such as `10 Ekim 2026`, `3 Mayıs 2025`, `5 Şubat 2024` or `5. Oktober 2026` were not found, so a redaction by pattern left them visible. Numeric dates (`10.10.2026`) and `10 October 2026` were already found.

**Root cause:**
- `MONTHS` lists only English names.
- `month()` lowercases with `str::to_lowercase`. That function is locale-free, so `"MAYIS"` becomes `"mayis"`, never `"mayıs"`. `"EKİM"` becomes `"eki̇m"`, one character longer than the original text.

## Fix

- Month names for English, Turkish, German, French and Italian (most Latin-script UI languages that write "day month-name year"), plus English and Turkish abbreviations (`Oca`, `Şub.`, `Ağu`, …).
- Names are compared one character at a time. `I`, `i`, `İ` and `ı` fold to `i`, and every other character folds to its own lowercase. Any case matches, and a match always covers exactly the original characters.
- A day may end in a full stop before the month name (`5. Oktober 2026`).
- Unchanged:
  - The whole-word check: `Martı`, `Ekimde` and `Oktoberfest` don't match.
  - A month name still needs a day and a year.

Not included: Spanish and Portuguese (`5 de octubre de 2024`) need the `de` connectors, and Czech and Hungarian use other word orders or genitive forms. I left those for a separate change.

## Tests

- New: `dates_with_turkish_month_names_in_any_case`
  - Full names in mixed, lower and upper case, including `5 ŞUBAT 2024`, `3 MAYIS 2025` and `1 EKİM 2026`.
  - Abbreviations, with and without a full stop.
  - Negative cases: words that only begin like a month, and a month without a day or year.
- New: `dates_with_german_french_and_italian_month_names`, with negative cases.
- New: `case_folding_keeps_one_character_per_character`.
- The existing `dates` and `phone_numbers` tests are unchanged and pass.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-…

title: fix(redact): the Email pattern finds internationalized addresses
author: snipeTR
body:
## Problem

The **Email addresses** pattern of Search & Redact (`crates/redact/src/patterns.rs`, `email()`) accepted only ASCII letters and digits. Internationalized addresses were not found at all, so a redaction by pattern left them visible. Examples:
- `ayşe.yılmaz@örnek.com.tr`
- `müller@bücher.de`
- `иван@пример.рф`

These are RFC 6531 local parts and IDN domains.

**Root cause:** the local part, the domain labels and the TLD were all checked with `is_ascii_alphanumeric` / `is_ascii_alphabetic`.

## Fix

- A new `address_char` accepts ASCII letters and digits, plus letters and digits of any script written with spaces between words. It is used for the local part and the domain.
- The TLD must be alphabetic (any script) and at least two characters long, counted in characters, not bytes.
- Letters of scripts written **without** spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, full-width forms) still don't count.
  - In such text, an address often runs straight into the words around it, e.g. `メールはtaro@example.jpまで`.
  - Accepting those letters would swallow the surrounding sentence into the match and over-redact it. The match there is unchanged: `taro@example.jp`.
- Everything else is unchanged:
  - A domain needs a dot.
  - A dot only continues the domain when a letter or digit follows it.
  - `bob@host` and `x@y.z` still don't match.

## Tests

- New: `internationalized_emails`
  - Turkish (lower and upper case), German, Russian and Spanish addresses.
  - Japanese and Chinese text around ASCII addresses, which must not be swallowed.
  - Negative cases: no dot, a one-letter TLD, a numeric TLD.
- The existing `emails` test is unchanged and passes.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation`: all pass.

title: M14: interface size preference; Auto follows GNOME text scaling
author: mitul72
body:
Closes #456.

## Scope

- **The Interface size picker (50–250 %) works on every platform.**
- **Auto only follows GNOME.** It reads GNOME's text scaling setting, so it covers GNOME and desktops that use GNOME's settings (`org.gnome.desktop.interface`, e.g. Ubuntu). On KDE, Cinnamon, Windows and other desktops, Auto is 100 %, the same as before this PR, and users can still pick a size by hand. macOS and the web have no separate text scale to follow.

## Problem

The interface size can't be adjusted, and it doesn't follow the desktop's text scaling:

- **#456**: on a 1080p display the system reports at 200 %, the interface opens oversized and there is no way to shrink it.
- **On a 1× display** (here 2560×1440 at scale 1, GNOME 51, Wayland), the interface looks pixelated next to GTK apps. PdfCraft renders at the right resolution: `pixels_per_point` is 1.0, the surface is full size, and page rasters map one texel to one screen pixel. But GNOME's text scaling (Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Large Text, `text-scaling-factor` 1.25) isn't applied, so PdfCraft's labels stay at 13 px while the rest of the desktop draws text 25 % larger.

## Change

- **Preferences ▸ Interface size**: Auto (default), or 50–250 %. 50 % brings an interface the system draws at 200 % back to 100 % (#456). Saved as `ui_scale` (null = Auto); control channel option `ui-scale=auto|125|125%`.
- **Auto** follows GNOME's text scaling. On Linux/BSD the desktop app reads `org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor` once at launch through `gsettings`, with a 500 ms limit and a 256-byte read cap. Without GNOME's setting (no `gsettings`, or a value missing or out of range), Auto is 100 %. Other platforms get 100 %; display scaling there already reaches egui as `pixels_per_point`.
- The size is applied as egui's zoom factor. `pixels_per_point` grows with it, so page rasters stay device-exact (`canvas::render_scale` / `texel_aligned`).
- The factor is re-applied only when it changes, so a zoom set elsewhere (k…

title: fix(create): read UTF-16, byte-order-marked and Windows code page text files
author: snipeTR
body:
## Problem

Plain-text files were decoded with `String::from_utf8_lossy` in three places:
- `Session::convert_to_pdf`: Create PDF and Combine from a `.txt` file (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`).
- The automation `create` tool with a text `path` (`crates/automation/src/lib.rs`).
- Search & Redact ▸ Multiple words, when the word list is loaded from a file (`crates/ui-egui/src/files.rs`).

This went wrong for common Windows files:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| UTF-16 LE with BOM (Notepad "Unicode") | `??G?r?????e? ?a?u?s? ?K???l?n?` | `Grüße aus Köln` |
| UTF-8 with BOM | stray character before the text | BOM dropped |
| Windows-1252 | `Cr�me br�l�e` | `Crème brûlée` |
| Windows-1254 (Turkish) | `K�� �stanbul` | `Kış İstanbul` |

For a redaction word list this means the listed words were never found, so they stayed visible.

## Fix

A new `pdfcraft_create::decode_text` (re-exported by the engine) works in this order:
1. If there is a byte order mark, it picks UTF-8, UTF-16 LE or UTF-16 BE and drops the mark.
2. Otherwise, valid UTF-8 is kept as it is.
3. Otherwise, the bytes are decoded as a Windows code page:
   - **1254** when the bytes 1254 uses for `Ğ İ Ş ğ ı ş` (0xD0 0xDD 0xDE 0xF0 0xFD 0xFE) appear and none of `á í ó ú` do;
   - **1252** otherwise.

The two code pages differ only in those six bytes. Among Western languages, only Icelandic and Faroese use them (as `Ð Ý Þ ð ý þ`), and both always write `á í ó ú`, which Turkish never does. A test covers this case.

`encoding_rs` is already in the build through the vendored lopdf, so the new dependency adds no crate (`Cargo.lock` gains one line).

Out of scope: characters such as `ğ ş ı İ` are still written as `?` by the Helvetica/WinAnsi text-to-PDF path (#506). This PR only makes sure the right characters reach it. Characters WinAnsi has (`ç ö ü é è û €` …) now come out correctly.

## Tests

- `pdfcraft-create`: `text_files_are_decoded_by_byte_order_mark_then_utf8_then_code_page`
  - UTF-8 with and without…

title: M14: native macOS menu bar (#80)
author: menezesd
body:
## What

macOS applications put their menus in the menu bar at the top of the screen, not in a popup inside the window. PdfCraft now builds that bar from the same command registry the in-window menu uses, so labels, shortcuts and enabled/disabled state stay in step.

Menus: the application menu (About, Preferences…, Services, Hide / Hide Others / Show All, Quit), File (with a live Open Recent), Edit, Pages, View, the standard Window menu and Help. The View menu keeps the document view's zoom, navigation, page display, theme and side-panel items around the registry's own View commands; panel and page-display choices carry checks. The bar re-syncs every frame (labels, enablement, checks, recent files).

## How

- `crates/ui-egui/src/macos_menu.rs` builds and syncs the bar.
- `muda` (a safe AppKit wrapper; the workspace forbids `unsafe`) installs it through `NSApplication.mainMenu` on the UI thread. Accelerators are set for commands safe to press in a text field; Undo/Redo keep ⌘Z/⇧⌘Z with egui, which knows whether a field has the keyboard.
- The in-window menu button is hidden only when the bar is installed, so the UI tests keep driving the in-window menu.
- The menu code is macOS-only (`#[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]`); nothing changes on other platforms.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` — new unit tests for the menu-id helpers and accelerator mapping; the in-window menu and all existing menu tests still pass.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -p pdfcraft --all-targets` — clean.
- Live on macOS (arm64), both the debug build and the packaged `/Applications` bundle: the bar is present (Apple, PdfCraft, File, Edit, View, Pages, Window, Help); clicking an item ran its command; ⌘K opened the command palette; the in-window menu was gone.

Closes #80.

title: fix(crypt): R2–R4 passwords with non-ASCII characters open (PDFDocEncoding)
author: snipeTR
body:
## Problem

A PDF protected with RC4 or AES-128 (security handler revisions 2–4) and a password containing non-ASCII characters could not be opened with the correct password.

Revisions 2–4 take the password in **PDFDocEncoding** (ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.3.2, Algorithm 2). PdfCraft authenticates an encrypted file in two places, and neither of them did this:

| Where | What it did | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `pdfcraft-crypt` (`legacy_password`) | Latin-1, every other character dropped | `ı` (0x9A) and `€` (0xA0) vanished: `ılık€` became `lk` |
| vendored `hayro-syntax` (`crypto/mod.rs`, `// TODO: Convert to PDFDocEncoding`) | UTF-8 bytes | **every** non-ASCII password failed, even `Çok güzel` |
| engine owner fallback (`open_unguarded`) | recovered user password turned into Latin-1 `char`s | the renderer read them back as UTF-8, so the result was wrong again |

I checked this end to end with files protected by **qpdf 12.4.2**. qpdf writes PDFDocEncoding, and writes UTF-8 bytes (with a warning) when PDFDocEncoding can't hold a character. On `main`, `Session::open`:
- returns `WrongPassword` for `Çok güzel` (RC4-128), `ılık€` (RC4-128) and `Öğretmen` (owner);
- opens `şifre` (AES-128, UTF-8 bytes) only through the renderer, while `pdfcraft-cos` fails to authenticate (`info.encrypted == false`).

With this PR, all of them open, and wrong passwords are still refused.

## Fix

- **`pdfcraft-crypt`**
  - R2–R4 passwords are encoded in PDFDocEncoding.
  - When opening a file whose password has characters PDFDocEncoding lacks (`ğ ş İ`), its UTF-8 bytes are tried too, since that is what qpdf writes for them. pdf.js also tries more than one byte form for R6.
  - The PDFDocEncoding table moves here from `pdfcraft-cos`. Cos depends on crypt and now uses `pdfcraft_crypt::pdfdoc_char`. `pdfdoc_char` and `pdfdoc_byte` are re-exported by cos.
  - New encryption is unchanged for ASCII. The engine already refuses non-ASCII passwords for RC4 and AES-128.
- **`hayro-syntax`** (vendored patch …

title: Edit PDF: select and move multiple objects together (#844)
author: Tevinhead
body:
Fixes #844.

In **Edit a PDF → Edit text & images**, Shift/Ctrl/Command-click or an empty-space marquee selects several recognised objects on one page. Dragging previews their common movement and commits it as one undo step. Existing paragraphs, Image/Form artwork, and added text/images can be moved together; added items are listed once. Escape, focus loss, tab/Home changes and modal dialogs cancel previews; unfinished text stays in its editor, and document changes invalidate stale selections. Foreground text and added notes remain selectable over page background artwork.

The engine resolves the entire selection before changing the graph. Existing text keeps its encoded glyph strings, font resources and kerning: temporary numeric `TJ` offsets and text rise move the original show operators, then restore the state for unselected neighbours. Quotes and operators split between content streams are handled. Images keep their data and Forms their nested resources. Added streams change their outer placement, preserving glyphs, image crop/flip/rotation and orientation after page rotation; shared streams are copied before editing. Saves remain incremental.

CLI and MCP share `object_list` and `object_move`, with generation-scoped kind/index references, displayed-point offsets, and an optional generation guard. Counts, geometry, stream decoding and graphics-state depth are bounded in both the original and resulting page. Invalid or unsupported targets refuse the whole move, preserving generation, document state and redo history.

Scope: same-page translation of the existing editor's recognised objects. Arbitrary paths, inline images, cross-page transfer, group resizing and arrange/align remain separate work. Vertical and clipping text are refused. The general object-editor parity entry stays **partial**. New selection, refusal and undo labels are translated in all 16 catalogs; provenance digests are updated. See [the guide](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/82b1093b7…

title: Linux: match the desktop scale instead of the panel's DPI
author: gyurix
body:
XRandR reports the panel's physical DPI while the desktop renders at 96, so winit scales every window up and the app looks zoomed for no reason. Pin WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR to 1 in the desktop launcher so menu and panel launches match the desktop.

Same fix as the local WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1 default; baked into the shipped launcher so installs work without system patches. Terminal launches can still export their own value.

title: Added linux and windows drag support
author: Heaplyn
body:
Problem

Dragging a PDF onto the window did nothing on Linux. The session was Wayland, and winit 0.30's Wayland backend doesn't implement file drag and drop (no HoveredFile or DroppedFile events), so dropped_files was always empty.

The page grid also couldn't follow the pointer during a drag. drag_pointer::in_window only had a macOS implementation, and winit sends no pointer moves while files are dragged.

Changes

- apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs: on Linux and FreeBSD, when both WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY are set, nd) through an event_loop_builder hook, because winit delivers drops on X11. WINIT_UNIX_BACKENDoverrides this, and a Wayland-only session stays on Wayland.
- crates/ui-egui/src/drag_pointer.rs: new in_window for Linux, FreeBSD and Windows. It reads the ption crate and converts pixels to egui points relative to the window. The stub now covers only theremaining targets, such as wasm. 
- Cargo.toml files: mouse_position is a target-specific dependency, and winit (already in the treereeBSD dependency of the app. Cargo.lock is updated.

title: Windows printing: mixed portrait/landscape as one job; note when the driver has no standard two-sided option (needs #599)
author: bulgariamitko
body:
> **Depends on #599 (native Windows printing). Merge #599 first.** This branch is built on #599 (with current `main` merged, the same as `bulgariamitko:pr599-merge-main`), so until #599 is in, the diff here also shows #599's commits. Only the last commit, 7afb579, belongs to this PR.

Two follow-ups to #599 that I raised in [my test results there](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/599#issuecomment-6088828583). Both use only the standard Windows Print Schema, with nothing specific to a printer brand or model.

### 1. Mixed portrait and landscape print as one job
#599 sends one PrintTicket per job, so a document with portrait and landscape pages (orientation **Auto**, which is the default) was refused with "requires one sheet size and orientation per job". Many office PDFs mix the two.

Now, when the sheets are the same paper size in both orientations, the sheets in the other orientation get a quarter turn (`/Rotate`) onto the first sheet's orientation. That is what a driver does with a landscape job. The document goes out as **one job**, so two-sided sheets and collated copies stay in order. Splitting into several jobs would break both. Sheets of genuinely different sizes are still refused, as before. CUPS is unchanged, since it handles mixed orientation itself.

- `spool::one_orientation`: platform-independent, with a unit test (`mixed_orientations_turn_onto_the_first_sheets_orientation`) covering portrait-first, landscape-first, nothing to turn, and different sizes.
- `spool/windows.rs`: `submit` uses it before checking sheet sizes.

### 2. A note when the driver has no standard two-sided option
Some drivers expose two-sided printing only under their own Print Schema feature names, not the standard `psk:JobDuplexAllDocumentsContiguously` that #599 sets. Those drivers ignore the request and use their own default. Whether the standard option exists is readable from any driver's PrintCapabilities, so:

- `spool::support(printer)` returns `Support { two_sided …

title: Issue #568: honour the document's copy permission (Table 22, bit 5)
author: jay-tau
body:
Fixes #568.

ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.1: "PDF readers shall respect the intent of the document creator by restricting user access to an encrypted PDF file according to the permissions contained in the file." Table 22, bit 5: "Copy or otherwise extract text and graphics from the document. However, for the limited purpose of providing this content to assistive technology, a PDF reader should behave as if this bit was set to 1."

PdfCraft already read the bit (Document Properties ▸ Security shows "Content copying: Not allowed"), but nothing enforced it: ⌘C copied selected text out of such files.

## What changes when a file withholds copying
- **Engine:** `Document::allows_copying` / `check_copying`, plus `Needs::Copying`, which disables Take a snapshot, Export to image/text/Word/HTML/RTF and Export all images. Save Image As (`page_image_file`) refuses too.
- **UI:** ⌘C handling moves from `canvas::shortcuts` (which can't see the document) into the app. A refused copy, snapshot or export says "The document's security settings don't allow copying text and images" (translated in every full catalog). The snapshot tool and the exports check again when they act, because the snapshot tool stays selected when you switch tabs.
- **Automation:** `text_extract` (and the MCP text resources built on it), `text_paragraphs`, `doc_export_text` / `doc_export_images` / `doc_export_all_images`, `doc_export_office` and `image_save` refuse with the engine's `NotPermitted` error.

## Unchanged
- Find / `text_find`, Read aloud, AccessKit and the accessibility tools: the spec exempts assistive technology, and searching isn't copying.
- Extract pages, Combine and page copy/paste stay governed by the assemble bit, as before (`protected_files_that_can_be_combined_are_flagged` asserts this).
- `page_render` (it's how an agent sees the page) and Copy text on a comment.
- Documents opened with the owner password, and unencrypted documents.

## Tests
- engine: `copy_restricted_documents_refuse_extraction…

title: Select tool picks up a signature placed over a form field
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #916.

## Problem
With the **Select** tool, a signature (or any movable comment) placed over a form field can't be dragged. The cursor shows Move, but a hand-speed drag leaves the signature where it is. #822 fixed this for the Fill & Sign tools; Select still had the gap.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: with Select, `forms_ui::page_input` runs before `comments::page_input`. Over a field it reports the press as consumed (`is_pointer_button_down_on`). egui fires `drag_started` a few pixels after the press. At hand speed the pointer is still over the field on that frame, so the comments code never starts the Move gesture. Fast drags that leave the field first happen to work.

## Fix
- **New `comments::select_grabs`.** With the Select tool, it says whether the press (or the hover, with no button down) is on a comment that would move (anything but text markup) or on the selected comment's resize handles.
  - When it does, the form field doesn't take the press, and the existing Select logic moves, selects or resizes the comment.
  - Elsewhere, fields fill as before.
- **Shared hit logic.** `fill_grabs` and `select_grabs` now share one `grabs` helper, which takes a predicate for the comments it picks up. Fill & Sign behaviour is unchanged.
- **Parity:** `form.fill-sign-signature` cites the new test.

## Testing
- [x] New test `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs::select_tool_picks_up_a_signature_over_a_form_field`, on `tests/data/form.pdf`:
  - It puts a signature over the `city` field and drags it in 40 small steps, as a hand does.
  - Before the fix it failed with the signature still on the field (`[150.0, 174.0, …] != [150.0, 254.0, …]`).
  - It also checks that the field isn't focused by the drag, and that a click on the field away from the signature still focuses it.
- [x] Tested by hand on Linux (KDE Plasma, Wayland) in a release build, on the real form where I hit the bug. Before: Move cursor, but the drag did nothing. After: the signature drags off the…

title: Fill & Sign: Add text keeps what was typed on click-away, and its box grows
author: dsskaggs-ai
body:
## What happens today (v0.4.0, still on `main`)

With **Fill & Sign ▸ Add text** selected:

1. **Typed text disappears.** Type into the box, then click elsewhere on the page. The text vanishes and no annotation is added.
2. **The box never grows.** It stays at its starting width while you type, so the text scrolls out of view.

Found while filling a scanned lease amendment on macOS.

## Causes

1. `canvas.rs` runs `fill_sign::page_input` before `fill_sign::type_box` in the same frame. The click-away reached `page_input` first, which replaced `view.fill_text` with a new empty `TypeBox`, so `type_box` never saw the old box lose focus and nothing was committed. (Pressing Enter worked, which is why `text_marks_and_date` didn't catch it.)
2. `type_box` puts its `TextEdit` in an `egui::Area`. The Area's max rect is last frame's size, and `TextEdit` clamps its width to `ui.available_width()`, so `desired_width` could never exceed the first frame's width.

## Fix

- `page_input` (Add text): swap in the new box and return the old one, if non-empty, as a `FillAction::Edit` built with `typed()`, the same edit `type_box` produces on lost focus.
- `type_box`: call `ui.set_min_width(width)` before adding the `TextEdit`, so the Area can grow (and shrink) with its text. Width is now counted in chars rather than bytes.

## Tests

Two new kittest tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs`. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- `clicking_elsewhere_with_add_text_keeps_the_typed_text`: on `main` there are no annotations, `left: []`.
- `the_type_box_grows_as_text_is_typed`: on `main` the box stays at `96 -> 96` px.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` (all 30 test binaries) pass locally on macOS (Apple Silicon).

title: Add document-processing SDK and REST service with Python and TypeScript SDKs (#872)
author: richfrem
body:
Closes #872

## Summary

Adds the document-processing SDK and self-hostable REST service proposed in #872, as an open-source, memory-safe alternative to proprietary PDF libraries and hosted PDF APIs. It is a thin layer over the existing `pdfcraft-automation` / `pdfcraft-engine` tools; no engine logic is duplicated.

- **`crates/sdk` (`pdfcraft-sdk`)**: in-process Rust client. `LocalClient` offers `merge`, `split` and `render_page` through an `OperationExecutor` port. - **`crates/rest` (`pdfcraft-rest`)**: self-hostable REST service and a `RestClient` with the same semantics as `LocalClient`. Bounded executor, job repository, loopback HTTP server with bearer token, request-size and header limits (413 / 431).
- **`sdks/python`, `sdks/typescript`**: Python and TypeScript SDKs mirroring the Rust API, an OpenAPI 3.1 contract and a contract drift check.
- **`docs/sdk/`**: SDK guide, API reference, and runnable examples (below).
- **`xtask/src/layers.rs`**: registers `sdk` and `rest` as L7 crates.

Each language has a runnable `sdk_capability_tour` that exercises the SDK API and writes a 5-page showcase PDF, plus a README with prerequisites and exact commands. Start at the [examples index](https://github.com/richfrem/pdfcraft/blob/upstream-main/docs/sdk/examples/README.md).

title: Drawn signatures and drawings resize from their handles
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Refs #331.

## Problem
#331 asked for placed signatures to be resizable. #335 and #355 added handles for **typed and image** signatures, which are stamps. A **drawn** signature is an Ink annotation, and it still can't be resized:
- with the Select tool, a selected drawn signature has no handles;
- the engine refuses `ResizeAnnotation` on it ("Ink comments can't be resized").

It is always placed 150 pt wide, so it can't be fitted into a signature line.

## Fix
- **`crates/annot`:** `set_rect` handles Ink.
  - It scales the `/InkList` strokes into the new rectangle.
  - It keeps each side's margin between the strokes and `/Rect` (half the line width plus a little), so the line isn't clipped.
  - It regenerates the appearance, as `erase_ink` does.
  - A stroke with no extent on one axis (a straight line) is centred on that axis instead of being scaled.
  - A rectangle too small to hold the margins is refused with `Invalid`.
- **`crates/ui-egui`:** Ink is `resizable` with the 8 handles.
  - A drawn Fill & Sign signature keeps its shape from the corners, the same way image signatures do (`aspect_ratio` from its rectangle).
  - Other drawings (pencil comments) resize freely, like shapes.
- **Parity:** the new tests are cited as evidence on `form.fill-sign-signature` and `comment.pencil`.

## Testing
- [x] `crates/annot/src/tests.rs::drawings_resize_by_scaling_their_strokes` checks:
  - `/Rect` is exactly the requested rectangle;
  - every point keeps its place relative to the drawing's bounds, inside the same margins;
  - the appearance is redrawn at the new coordinates;
  - a too-small rectangle is refused.

  Before the fix it failed with `Invalid("Ink comments can't be resized")`.
- [x] `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs::drawn_signatures_resize_from_their_corners` places a drawn signature, then drags its top-right handle at hand speed. It checks:
  - the resize cursor;
  - one "Resize comment" undo step;
  - wider with the same aspect ratio, opposite corner fixed;
  …

title: Edit text: white or pale text is edited on a dark box instead of vanishing on white (#913)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
The inline **Edit text** box (`edit_text_ui::overlay`) is always filled white and draws the paragraph in its own colour. White text taken from a coloured banner (the certificate header in #913) is therefore white on white while you edit it: it vanishes, and only the selection highlight shows it is there.

## The fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/edit_text_ui.rs`: new `editor_fill(text)` picks the editor box's background from the text colour: white, or a dark grey (`#262626`), whichever has the higher WCAG contrast ratio with the text. Black, navy, red or mid-grey text keeps the white box as before; white, yellow, orange or light-grey text gets the dark box. The caret colour follows the box (black on white, white on dark), so it stays visible in both themes.

Nothing about the saved PDF changes; this is only the on-screen editor.

## How tested
- New unit test `edit_text_ui::tests::pale_text_is_edited_on_a_dark_box` (pale colours get the dark box with at least 4.5:1 contrast; dark/saturated colours keep white).
- Visual check with a throwaway kittest render (not committed): a page with white Helvetica-Bold on a navy banner, opened in Edit text. On main the box is blank white; with the fix the text reads white on dark grey, and a black line on the same page still edits on white.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo +1.99.0 clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Notes
- #734 (caret colour for #655) touches the same `Frame` line in `overlay`; whichever lands second needs a one-line merge (the caret here already contrasts with whichever fill is used).
- Duplicates: none found (searched "text disappears", "edit text white/invisible", "edit text background color").

Fixes #913

author: YingQiu0871
body:

_Requested by **Yuning Gu** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0134ggTjXPRkk9bjyY9ADiai?thread=cmsg_0134ggTjXPRkk9bjyY9ADiai2LGxNvoRXaGipQomryUgTS)_

title: M9: stream structure-tree checks without a total-element cutoff
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

The structure-tree checks (alternate text, tables, lists and headings) first copied the whole structure tree into a vector of elements, and stopped adding elements at 2,000,000. Elements past that point were never checked, so a missing figure or an irregular table late in a large file went unreported. This change reads the tree once with an explicit stack and reports each element as it opens and closes; each rule keeps only the state it needs. The cap is removed. The report still lists the first 200 findings per rule and counts the rest.

## Problem and root cause

`structure::Tree::read` materialises every structure element (type, parent, children, annotation references and cloned attribute dictionaries) before any rule runs, and `Reader::kids` stops at `MAX_ELEMENTS = 2_000_000`. That cap is a correctness cap, not a presentation limit: elements after it are absent from all 13 structure rules. `check()` also built the tree on every run, even when no structure rule was selected.

## Scope and non-goals

- In scope: the 13 rules that read the structure tree (`crates/a11y/src/structure.rs`), their call site in `crates/a11y/src/lib.rs`, the tree-existence flag used by four page rules in `crates/a11y/src/content.rs`, and their tests.
- Non-goals: heading extraction caps (`MAX_HEADINGS` and the visit, depth and title guards in `headings.rs`), page-content decode limits, PDF/UA policy, finding wording, the 200-finding presentation limit (unchanged), the public API (unchanged), and dependencies (unchanged).

Every rule that reads the structure tree, and what this change does with it:

| figures-alt-text, other-elements-alt-text, nested-alt-text | local: the element and its open ancestors | yes |
| table-rows, table-cells, list-items, lbl-lbody | local: the element and its parent's type | yes |
| table-summary | local: the element's own attributes | yes |

title: M3: middle-button autoscroll works the same on every platform (#915)
author: Toddpe
body:
Closes #915.

## Summary

Middle-button autoscroll now behaves the same on Linux, Windows and macOS. A short press latches it on, as Linux did. Holding the button scrolls while held and stops on release, which is how the reporter says Acrobat behaves on Windows.

```diff
 AutoScroll::update(ui, viewport, organize)        // crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs
-  if !cfg!(target_os = "linux") → update_drag()   // Windows/macOS: 1:1 pan while held
   on middle press in the viewport
     anchor = press position
+    pressed_at = now
+  on middle release
+    if now - pressed_at >= HOLD (0.5 s)           // a hold
+      cancel; still block input this frame        //   stop, normal cursor back
+    else                                          // a short press
+      keep scrolling (latched)                    //   next middle press stops it
   scroll = Chromium curve(vertical distance from anchor), 15 pt dead zone   // unchanged
```

| | Short press (< 0.5 s) | Hold (≥ 0.5 s) |
|---|---|---|
| Linux before | latched | latched |
| Windows / macOS before | nothing | 1:1 pan (both axes) |
| **Every platform now** | **latched until the next middle press** | **scrolls while held, stops on release** |

**#565 is still fixed.** `blocks_input()` (`middle_gesture` in `canvas.rs`) is true from the press through the release frame of both gestures. Page tools still never see the middle button, and its regression test now runs as a hold on every platform.

## Evidence

- **Before** (`main`'s `autoscroll.rs` with the new tests): the hold tests fail.
  ```text
  comments::a_middle_drag_with_a_drawing_tool_scrolls_instead_of_drawing                    FAILED  "releasing a hold stops scrolling"
  ```

title: fix(macos): close the empty main window with Command-W
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Fixes #869.

On macOS, Command-W correctly closes an open document tab. However, when no document tabs remain, pressing Command-W does nothing.

The expected macOS behavior is to close the empty main window.

## Root cause

The shortcut dispatcher always routes Command-W through `file.close`, which requires an active document.

Without an active document, the command is disabled, so no window-close action occurs.

## Changes

- Detect Command-W when no document is active on macOS.
- Send `egui::ViewportCommand::Close` through the existing window-close path.
- Preserve the normal document-tab closing behavior.
- Leave non-macOS and WebAssembly behavior unchanged.
- Add regression tests covering:
  - Command-W with no tabs on macOS.
  - Command-W with no tabs on Windows.
  - Command-W with an open document on macOS.

## Validation

- Reviewed the implementation against the current upstream source.
- Added two focused UI regression tests.
- Tests and formatting checks have not been executed.
- CI remains unchecked.

title: fix(xfdf): combine imported annotation flags with bitwise OR
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Importing XFDF annotations with repeated flag names can silently change their behavior.

For example:

- `print,print` can become `nozoom`.
- `readonly,readonly` can become `locked`.

This happens because annotation flags are bitmasks, but the importer adds their numeric values.

Repeated flags should not enable unrelated properties.

## Root cause

In `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs`, `annot_from_xml()` converts flag names into their corresponding numeric values and combines them using `sum()`.

Adding identical bit values can carry into another flag's bit position.

## Changes

- Replace arithmetic addition with bitwise OR when combining XFDF annotation flags.
- Preserve case-insensitive flag recognition.
- Make repeated flags idempotent.
- Add a synthetic XFDF import regression test.

The regression test verifies:

- Repeated `print` flags combined with `nozoom`.
- Repeated `readonly` flags.
- Multiple repetitions of the same flag.
- The actual `/F` value of the imported annotation.

## Validation

- Reviewed the importer and the existing XFDF test patterns.
- Added an integration-level regression test using synthetic XFDF input.
- Tests and formatting checks have not been executed.
- CI remains unchecked.

## Scope

This is a localized correction to XFDF annotation flag parsing. It does not change unrelated annotation properties or PDF import behavior.

title: M9: visible digital signatures can show a drawn, typed or image graphic (#193)
author: kestrel99
body:

Acrobat's Configure Signature Appearance can put artwork where the large name goes, and #193 asks for that. - **Engine:** `SignatureImage::graphic()` and `typed_signature_graphic(text)`, so the UI and the tools build graphics the same way Fill & Sign does.

title: fix(ui): bookmark, comment and command filters match Turkish İ/ı in any case
author: snipeTR
body:
## Problem

Three filters lowercased with `str::to_lowercase`, which follows no locale:
- the bookmark filter (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, `outline_matches`);
- the Comments panel filter (`crates/ui-egui/src/comments_panel.rs`, `matches`);
- the command palette (`crates/ui-egui/src/palette.rs`, `score`).

`İ` turns into `i` plus a combining dot, and `ı` has no case pair. So `istanbul` didn't find the bookmark `İSTANBUL ŞUBESİ`, and `imzalayın` didn't find a comment `Lütfen İMZALAYIN`. This is the same root cause #892 fixed for Find and Search & Redact.

## Fix

- `pdfcraft_render::text::fold_case` (merged in #892) is now public; no new helper.
- The three filters fold both the query and the text with it. `I`, `i`, `İ` and `ı` count as one letter, and every other character folds to its own lowercase.

## Tests

- New: `panels::bookmark_filter::titles_match_in_any_case_with_turkish_i`.
- New: `comments_panel::filter::comments_match_in_any_case_with_turkish_i`.
- New: `palette::search::commands_match_in_any_case_with_turkish_i`.
- All three fail with `to_lowercase`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render`: all pass.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib --test bookmarks --test comments --test commands --test redact --test text_select`: all pass.

## Related

Follow-up to #892 (merged), which added `fold_case` for Find and Search & Redact. Based on current `main`; not stacked on any other PR.

title: M3: select and highlight text while middle-button autoscroll is on
author: Toddpe
body:
> **Builds on https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/927** (middle-button autoscroll on every platform). This branch contains that PR's commit, so please review only the last commit, `5bda767`. Once #927 is merged, this diff reduces to that commit.

## Summary

You can now select or highlight text while middle-button autoscroll runs. While autoscroll is latched (from a short middle click), the text tools keep the left button:
- A **drag** selects or highlights, and scrolling continues.
- A plain left **click** stops scrolling, and also acts as an ordinary click on the page.

```diff
 AutoScroll::update(ui, viewport, organize, select_text)            // crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs
+  latched = active && the middle button is not held
+  if select_text && latched && left press inside the viewport → selecting = true   // not a cancel
-  block_input = active || owned click || middle press/down/release
+  block_input = (active && !(select_text && latched)) || owned click || middle press/down/release
+  on left release while selecting:
+    egui click → cancel(), input not blocked (an ordinary click on the page)
+    drag       → keep scrolling
```

`select_text` is the viewer's existing `selects_text`: Select, Column select, the markup tools (Highlight, Underline, Strikethrough, Replace text) and Redact. Organize Pages passes `false`. The selection already re-maps the pointer to the page every frame while `dragged()`, so its end follows the text as the page scrolls under a still pointer.

**Unchanged:**

title: Fix/noissue hyphenated print label ranges s20261010 t220019 z f82d4
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

The printing range parser supports logical PDF page labels.

However, ranges containing page labels with hyphens can fail.

For example:

A-1-A-3

The parser splits at the first hyphen, incorrectly interpreting
the range as starting at "A" instead of "A-1".

Single hyphenated labels already work, but ranges between them
are incorrectly parsed.

## Changes

- Resolve ranges using known logical page labels.
- Support ranges between hyphenated labels.
- Preserve exact-label precedence.
- Support ascending and descending label ranges.
- Support open-ended ranges starting or ending at hyphenated labels.
- Support combinations of logical labels and numeric page indices.
- Continue checking candidate delimiters when an earlier
  interpretation is invalid.
- Preserve existing numeric range behavior.

## Examples

Supported expressions include:

- A-1
- A-1-A-3
- A-3-A-1
- A-2-
- -A-2
- A-2-5
- B-1-B-2

## Regression Tests

Added `page_selection_handles_ranges_between_hyphenated_labels`.

The test covers:

- Exact logical labels
- Forward and reversed ranges
- Open-ended ranges
- Mixed numeric and logical endpoints
- Ambiguous hyphen positions

## Scope

Changes are limited to print-range parsing.

Printer discovery, spooling and platform-specific printing
backends are unchanged.

## Validation

Reviewed against upstream main.
Regression tests added but not executed.
CI not checked.

title: Render visible pages before thumbnails and text extraction
author: gyurix
body:
Diagnosed slow PDF opening: engine open is fast (doc_open ~15ms, inspect ~4ms, text ~10ms on a 247KB/4pp Illustrator file), while first-page raster dominates and scales with pixels (231ms@36dpi, 869ms@72dpi, 3478ms@150dpi).

On open, prepare_render_queue admitted the visible page pixels together with Pages-panel thumbnails and background text extraction, so the 7 render workers spent the first seconds on background interpretations while the visible page stayed blank.

This change holds thumbnails and text until no visible main-page raster is still missing (errored pages never block; grid/print previews unaffected). Demand is re-evaluated next frame once pixels arrive.

title: demo-pdf: two fixes so xtask demo-pdf and xtask screenshots work on Windows
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
On Windows 11 (x64, current Chrome), both `cargo xtask demo-pdf` and `cargo xtask screenshots`
always failed with:

```
xtask screenshots: error: Chrome produced 1 pages but the showcase layout expects 12;
a page probably overflowed - check dist/demo/build/chrome.pdf
```

Two independent bugs, both fixed here. Everything works end to end after them: the full
`cargo xtask screenshots` run produces all 13 scenes on Windows.

## 1. `file_url` builds `file:////?/C:/...` from Windows verbatim paths

Windows `Path::canonicalize` returns a verbatim `\\?\C:\...` path. After the backslash-to-slash
swap that becomes `//?/C:/...`, which the leading-slash branch misreads as an absolute Unix path,
so the URL passed to Chrome is `file:////?/C:/...`. Chrome fails to load it, prints one blank
page, and the page-count check aborts the build. macOS and Linux never hit this because
`canonicalize` does not produce a verbatim prefix there.

Fix: strip the `//?/` prefix before classifying the path shape. A regression test
(`demo_pdf::tests::file_url_has_no_verbatim_prefix`) covers it.

## 2. The completion poll accepts Skia's incremental writes as final

Chrome writes the print-to-pdf output incrementally, and every increment ends with its own
`%%EOF`. The poll saw a stable ~29 KB increment (one page of twelve), treated it as finished,
and killed Chrome mid-print. Waiting for process exit alone is not enough either, because some
Chrome builds linger after writing — that is why the poll exists.

Fix: require the file size to stay quiet for 10 consecutive 500 ms polls before treating the
file as finished. Chrome that exits normally is still handled by the existing exit branch.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p xtask` — 33 passed, including the new regression test.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p xtask -- -D warnings` — clean.
- Full `cargo xtask screenshots` on Windows 11 x64: all 13 scenes rendered, `ATTRIBUTION.md`
  rewritten, and `cargo xtask assets` passes on the result.

title: render: don't let a hostile page-tree /Count abort inspection
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
Found by `cargo xtask fuzz --time 900 --seed 42` on Windows 11: a 355-byte mutated PDF whose
`/Type /Pages` node carries `/Count 4294967295` aborts `pdfcraft-cli check-one` with a failed
allocation of 51,539,607,552 bytes — 4294967295 × 12 bytes, one entry per page from
`lopdf::document::PageTreeIter` collected into `Vec<(u32, (u32, u16))>` by lopdf's
`Document::get_pages`. An allocation failure is an abort, not a panic, so the engine's
`catch_unwind` guard cannot catch it — and AGENTS.md §4 requires a malformed PDF to produce an
error the user (or agent) can act on, never a crash.

Reproduces on `main` as of 2026-10-10 (`cargo xtask fuzz` runs nightly on Linux with a
`ulimit -v` address-space cap; Windows has no equivalent, and this finding came out of a Windows
run). The input is synthetic (mutated from the fuzzer's own `synthetic-0` seed); the same shape
is reproducible with a hand-written minimal document:

```
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj
2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 4294967295 >> endobj
3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 200 200] >> endobj
```

## The fix

The `Structure` trait's default `get_pages` already walks the page tree the way §4 asks for:
a depth cap of 256, a seen-set against cycles, and checked `u32` page numbering — it counts the
real pages and ignores the hostile `/Count`. The `impl Structure for lopdf::Document` overrode
that with a delegation to lopdf's own walk, which pre-allocates by `/Count`. This patch simply
drops the override, so the bounded default takes over for the lopdf bootstrap path too
(`LazyStructure` and the cos implementation already use bounded walks).

## Testing

- New synthetic regression test `structure::tests::a_hostile_page_count_does_not_abort_inspection`
  (a hand-written minimal document, no corpus-derived data): `Structure::get_pages` returns the
  one real page and does not abort.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-rend…

title: M7: shard Japanese Type 3 fallback fonts across large edits
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

A Japanese replacement with more than 240 unique characters was refused with "Japanese replacement has too many unique characters". That limit belongs to one generated Type 3 font (its codes run 1 to 240), not to the user's text. This change splits the fallback characters into several generated fonts, each within the existing 240-glyph bound, and switches font only where the text moves to another font. The per-font bound stays; only the aggregate rejection goes. A paragraph whose move or width is refused now leaves the document unchanged, where it used to leave unreferenced fallback fonts behind.

## Problem and root cause

- `type3_font` in `crates/edit/src/text.rs` returned an error as soon as the text had 241 unique characters. One Type 3 font cannot hold more than 240 glyphs, so the limit was a property of the font, not of the text.
- `text_lines` and `group_blocks` joined a line only when its runs shared one font resource name, so a replacement split across fonts would have read back as several lines.
- `rewrite_block` created the fallback fonts before it checked the paragraph's move and width. A refused move left the new font objects in the document.

## Scope and non-goals

- In scope: the Japanese Type 3 fallback in `replace_line` and `rewrite_block` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`), and its tests in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs`.
- Partitioning is deterministic: unique characters in order of first appearance, `MAX_TYPE3_GLYPHS` (240) per font, codes restarting at 1 in each font. Font names are `PCJp`, `PCJp1`, `PCJp2`, and so on, and each font has its own ToUnicode map. A replacement that fits one font produces the same bytes as before.
- Reader change: runs join across the subset fonts of one fallback face only when both fonts are Type 3 with `/Name /PCJapanese`, the name this code writes. Every other document keeps the resource-name rule.
- Refused edits: the move and width checks (and the check that the paragraph's space can be moved in) now run befo…

title: Typed signatures draw Cyrillic and Greek letters (#846)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
Typed signatures and initials are drawn from Dancing Script's glyph outlines (`pdfcraft_fonts::script_outline`). Dancing Script only covers Latin and Vietnamese, so `script_outline` skipped every Cyrillic or Greek character. A Serbian Cyrillic name like "Саша Дермановић" came out with no outlines: no preview, and nothing to place.

## The fix
- `crates/fonts/src/script.rs`: `script_outline` now falls back to the bundled **Inter Regular** for characters the script face lacks. The fallback glyphs are slanted about 12° so they lean like the script, and scaled so their capitals match Dancing Script's cap height. Latin text is drawn exactly as before. Characters neither face has (Hebrew, CJK, …) are still skipped, as they are now.

title: ui: the system font fallback can serve Simplified Chinese (fixes #500)
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
Fixes #500 (all Chinese UI characters render as tofu boxes on Windows).

## Cause

The last-resort system font (`system_fonts::fallback`) was probed with the Arabic letter alef
against `segoeui.ttf`/`tahoma.ttf`/`arial.ttf`. None of those has a single CJK glyph, so the
fallback could never serve the Chinese interface. A build whose only embedded CJK face is the
Japanese set (BIZ UDPGothic via craft-fonts) draws Simplified-only characters as tofu, while
zh-hant mostly survives on the traditional-form overlap — exactly the split reported in the
issue ("Simplified Chinese is affected, Traditional Chinese is not").

## The fix

`system_fonts::fallback` now takes the same `prefer_hans` flag the theme already computes for
the CJK ordering (lib.rs: `lang.code() == "zh-hans"`), and when it is set:

- the probe becomes a Simplified-only character (U+8FD9 这), which Japanese faces and Segoe UI
  lack — a face that maps it can actually draw the zh-hans interface;
- the per-platform candidates gain the standard CJK faces, probed first: Microsoft YaHei UI
  (`msyh.ttc`, ships with every Windows 10/11), SimSun, DengXian and JhengHei on Windows;
  PingFang, Hiragino Sans GB and Songti on macOS; Noto Sans CJK and WenQuanYi on Linux.

The Arabic case keeps its previous candidates and probe, unchanged for everyone else. The face
is still read at runtime from the user's machine, one face, never embedded or shipped
(AGENTS.md §1.4), and `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` still turns it off.

## Before / after (Windows 11, headless shot, `--language zh-hans`)

Before (`PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0`):

title: M7: shard Arabic generated glyph fonts instead of rejecting large text
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

An added Arabic text item with more than 3,840 distinct glyphs was rejected by a fixed item-wide limit (`MAX_ARABIC_FONTS` = 16 fonts of 240 glyphs), although every generated font already holds at most 240 glyphs. This change removes that limit: an item now gets one Type 3 font per 240 distinct glyphs it needs. Per-font limits, the rule that every outline is read before anything is written, and the output below the old limit are unchanged.

## Problem and root cause

`draw_arabic` in `crates/edit/src/added.rs` already split the distinct glyph keys into 240-glyph fonts (`keys.chunks(GLYPHS_PER_FONT)`). The item-wide check `keys.len() > GLYPHS_PER_FONT * MAX_ARABIC_FONTS` sat on top of that split and protected nothing new: a Type 3 font only needs its own codes 1 to 240, and that per-font bound stays. The root cause is that the cap was applied to the whole item, so text was rejected for a representation choice, not for a format limit.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope:
- `crates/edit/src/added.rs`: remove the aggregate check and `MAX_ARABIC_FONTS`. Move the drawing core into `draw_laid_arabic`, which takes the laid-out lines and the outline source as parameters. `draw_arabic` passes the craft-fonts face's outlines, so behaviour is unchanged. The per-font name check uses a hash set instead of scanning the page's font dictionary.
- `crates/edit/src/added/arabic_tests.rs` (new): seven tests that inject shaped clusters and outlines, so they run without the Arabic face.

Non-goals: Arabic shaping, bidi, glyph positions and advances, font assets, other add-text limits, interface text, documentation, `contributors/`, and `vendor/`. `GLYPHS_PER_FONT` stays 240.

## Before and after behaviour

Before: an item with more than 3,840 distinct glyph keys returns `Invalid("the text uses too many different Arabic glyphs; split it into several boxes")`.

After: the item is drawn with `ceil(keys / 240)` fonts. Glyph `k` is shown from font `k / 240` with code `k % 240 + 1`, …

title: automation: the root-confinement test plants a junction when symlinks are denied
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
Fixes #948.

On Windows as a standard user (no administrator rights, Developer Mode off),
`cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test hostile_args` fails on main with 15 false
confinement leaks over 141 tools:

```
root confinement: 510 escape attempts over 141 tools, 495 refused, 15 leaks
  doc_save accepted path="link-out/outside.pdf"
  ...
```

## Cause

The test plants `root/link-out` as a symbolic link and ignores the error when the link
cannot be made (`let _ = std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(...)`). Creating a symlink on
Windows needs administrator rights or Developer Mode, so for a standard user the link never
exists — but the escape attempt through `link-out/outside.pdf` still runs, and every tool
that accepts that root-relative path is reported as a leak. CI never sees this because
GitHub's Windows runners run as administrator.

## The fix

`plant_link` falls back to a **directory junction** (`mklink /J`), which a standard Windows
user can create without privileges and which resolves through path lookups the same way — so
the test keeps its full escape coverage on Windows instead of dropping it. When neither a
symlink nor a junction can be made, the caller drops the link-based escape attempts rather
than reporting phantom leaks.

## Testing

- Windows 11 x64: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test hostile_args` — 2 passed (the
  full escape sweep runs, through the link).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.

title: fonts: typed signatures draw Cyrillic and Greek in the bundled Inter face
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
Fixes #846 (typed signatures do not render Serbian Cyrillic).

## Cause

`script_outline` skipped every character the Dancing Script face lacks — and the face's cmap
has **no Cyrillic at all** (not even the Russian letters), so a Serbian typed signature like
«Ђорђе Јовановић» produced a completely empty outline: nothing was drawn, no error shown.

## The fix

Characters the script face lacks now draw in the **bundled Inter face**, which carries Latin,
Greek and Cyrillic including all the Serbian letters (Ђ Ђ, Ћ Ћ, Џ Џ, Ј, Њ Њ, Љ Љ — verified in
its cmap). Each fallback glyph is drawn in its own em scale and advanced by its own width, so
the line stays on one baseline. Inter is already shipped in `assets/fonts/`, so the
no-system-fonts-in-PDFs rule (AGENTS.md §1.4) holds — the signature appearance still embeds
only open, bundled faces.

A mixed-script name renders half in the script face and half in Inter; that is a visible
improvement over invisible text, and the preview shows the user exactly what will be saved.

## Testing

- New regression test `script::tests::serbian_cyrillic_draws_in_the_fallback_face`:
  a mixed Latin/Cyrillic name draws non-empty outlines and advances, a pure-Cyrillic name is
  not empty (it was), and characters neither face has (an emoji) are still skipped.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts` — 35 passed; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo fmt --check` — clean.

title: Tests: skip the symlink escape when no link could be planted (#948)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #948.

On Windows, a standard user without Developer Mode can't create a symbolic link, so `no_tool_escapes_the_root`'s `std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(&base, root.join("link-out"))` fails — and the `let _ =` swallowed the error. Without the link, `link-out/outside.pdf` is just an ordinary path **inside** the root:

- the write tools (`doc_save`, `doc_print`, `doc_optimize`, …) accept it, correctly;
- the read tools (`page_insert_file`, …) then find the file those writers left there.

So the test reported ~15 false confinement "leaks" while nothing actually left the root (its second net, checking for files created/modified/deleted outside the root, stays clean). CI doesn't hit this because GitHub's Windows runners run as administrator.

**Fix:** keep the result of the symlink call and only add the `link-out/outside.pdf` escape when the link was really made — the same guard the staging symlink tests in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` already use. When the link exists (Linux, admin/Developer-Mode Windows) the escape is still exercised exactly as before.

Verified on Windows 11 as a standard user: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test hostile_args` now passes (it prints `symbolic link escapes not checked: …` and skips that one escape); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --tests -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Fill & Sign and FreeText: draw text outside WinAnsi instead of writing ? (#506)
author: kogasura
body:
Refs #506 (first part: FreeText appearances). Also fixes the same `?` in text-box and callout comments.

## What the user sees

Fill & Sign ▸ Text writes its appearance in Helvetica with WinAnsiEncoding, so any letter outside Western European is saved as `?`. `/Contents` keeps the real text, but every viewer shows, prints and extracts the appearance.

| Typed | Before (saved file, PdfCraft and MuPDF) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `山田太郎　東京都江東区1-2-3` | `???????????1-2-3` | `山田太郎　東京都江東区1-2-3` |
| `Dvořák` | `Dvo?ák` | `Dvořák` |
| `Ελληνικά` | `????????` | `Ελληνικά` |
| `Plain ASCII ok` | unchanged | unchanged (byte for byte) |

This was checked on Windows 11 with `pdfcraft-cli run --script` (`fill_sign_add`, then `doc_save` with and without `flatten_fill_sign`). The results were rendered with `pdfcraft-cli render` and MuPDF, and the text was extracted with PyMuPDF. The flattened file gives the same result.

## How it works

The same approach as the Japanese fallback in `edit/src/text.rs` and the Arabic support in #403: craft-fonts outlines become Type 3 glyphs with a ToUnicode map. Nothing is embedded, and the text stays searchable.

- **`pdfcraft-fonts`, new `type3` module**

  - `build_type3` builds the fonts: codes 1–240 per font, at most 4 fonts, flate CharProcs, and a ToUnicode CMap in blocks of 100.
  - Proportional Greek and Cyrillic, as in `edit`.
  - It takes an `add` callback, so `edit`'s two builders could move onto it later.
- **`pdfcraft-annot`**
  - FreeText lines are split into WinAnsi runs (`/Helv`, exactly as before) and fallback runs (`/PCJp0`…).
  - `text_measure` and `text_wrap` measure exactly what is drawn, and `/Q` alignment uses them.
  - `build` stays pure: the Type 3 parts are inline…

title: M10: OCR engines, confidence, preprocessing and a review workflow
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Recognize Text gets pluggable engines, optional cleaning of the scan before it is read, an editable text layer, and a review workflow.

- **Engines and merging:** the bundled ocrs engine, plus tesseract as an optional external process (never bundled, never started unless asked). With both engines, words are merged by confidence; a tesseract word beats an ocrs word of unknown confidence only at 70 or more. "Automatic" now means both engines, confidence-weighted.
- **Preprocessing:** optional cleaning steps before recognition. The 300 dpi normalization runs only when a cleaning step is on (see "look at first").
- **Editable text layer:** recognized words can be written as editable text in a Type3 face, with Unicode text planned per face; `add_type3_fonts` no longer reuses a font name on a later page.
- **Verify screen:** review a recognition word by word: accept a page or all pages, correct words, strike words out, add to a dictionary, re-read a page or a region. Review marks follow the words when a page or region is re-read, and the document guard is refreshed after every accepted page (accepting several pages in a row used to fail from the second).
- **Batch:** Recognize Text in multiple files refuses same-name inputs up front, and an editable or review output never overwrites an existing file.
- **Headless:** `ocr_recognize`, `ocr_recognize_files`, `ocr_words`, `ocr_review_apply`, `ocr_dictionary` and `ocr_status`. `ocr_recognize` now refuses `out` unless the output mode is editable, and checks it against `--root`.
- Tesseract hardening: an invalid `PDFCRAFT_TESSERACT` fails closed instead of falling back to `PATH`; the temp directory is created 0700; `--list-langs` and `--version` are also read from stderr; the UI reads a cached engine status refreshed by a background probe instead of waiting on a process.
- 21 interface catalogs carry the new strings.

Eight commits: fonts/edit (Type3 Unicode planning); a test-timeout fix for the hostile-XFA…

title: M10: stream Create Multiple sources without a fixed file-count cutoff
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

Create ▸ Multiple files and `doc_create_multiple` (combine mode) refused any selection above a fixed 1,000 files, and dropping files on a page grid silently ignored those past 1,000. This PR removes the count limit and combines the sources one at a time: `pdfcraft_organize::Combiner` takes one source at a time, `Session::combine_each` drives it from a lazy iterator, and the desktop picker and grid drop read each file when its turn comes. Peak memory now follows one source plus the output being built, not the total of all sources. Output bytes for ordinary inputs are unchanged.

## Problem and root cause

- `MAX_CREATE_FILES = 1000` was enforced in four places: the engine constant; the automation count check and schema `maxItems`; the UI staging (`take(max)`: the rest were dropped, and the notice said "the first N files"); and the grid drop (`take(MAX)`, which dropped the rest silently).
- The cap was the only memory bound, and it bounded memory by count, not by bytes. Underneath it, the combine held every source at once: the automation tool and `stage_create_multiple` converted every source into a vector before combining; `Session::combine_ranges` opened every source document before copying any page; and the desktop picker read every picked file into memory (`use_paths`) before staging.
- `organize::combine_selected` kept each source's `Document` alive until the end, because the bookmark and PDF/X steps read the sources last. Callers therefore had to keep every source alive as well.

## Scope and non-goals

Scope:
- Remove `MAX_CREATE_FILES`, the automation count check and schema `maxItems`, the UI truncation and the grid-drop cap.
- Create ▸ Multiple files (UI and automation, combine mode) stream their sources one at a time through `Combiner` and `Session::combine_each`. The desktop picker passes paths and grid drops keep path-backed files, so each is read when its turn comes.
- `combine_selected` becomes a loop over `Combiner::add` and `Combiner::finis…

title: ui: bookmarks and page thumbnails open in Read mode
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:

title: M11: print production starts here — the ink inventory behind Output Preview
author: Mawfyy
body:
## What

New `pdfcraft-prepress` crate: the separations a document actually uses, read from the content streams and resources. This is the data Acrobat's Output Preview stands on, and the first of the 18 planned print-production features (M11, gap 18).

- **Process channels** of DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK, ICC-based (by `/N`), CalGray and CalRGB, honouring the resources' `DefaultGray`/`DefaultRGB`/`DefaultCMYK`.
- **Spot inks** of `/Separation` and `/DeviceN` spaces, named as the PDF names them (with `#xx` escapes decoded), including the special `None` and `All` inks with their own kind.
- **Highest tint per ink** from the colour operators (`k`, `rg`, `g`, `sc`/`scn` and the stroke forms), clamped to 0..1; images and shadings report their inks **without** a tint, since those tints live outside the content stream.
- **Overprint pages**: `gs` with `/OP`/`/op` (and `/op` defaulting to `/OP`, per ISO 32000-2 §11.3.5), counting the paints that happen under it.

Exposed as `Document::inks` / `inks_of` and the read-only `prepress_inks` tool (1-based `page` for one page). No panics: forms are walked with the page's resources as fallback, nested forms are depth-bounded at 12, malformed content is skipped.

Parity: `print.output-preview` and `print.separations` move from *planned* to *partial*, with the missing halves named (the viewer panel, per-separation rendering, area coverage).

## Verification

- 12 unit tests in `crates/prepress/src/tests.rs` (CMYK/gray/RGB + `q`/`Q`, a Pantone Separation, `None`/`All`, DeviceN, overprint on/off, a form XObject without its own resources, a cyclic form, an image, ICCBased+Indexed, per-page reads).
- `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs::inks_and_overprint_through_tools` end to end: CMYK + Pantone + overprint through `doc_open` → `prepress_inks`, page range checked.
- Smoke run against real PDFs (`/usr/share/cups/data/classified.pdf`, IJS spec, ImageMagick tutorial, speex manual): gray-only, gray+RGB and RGB reports all come out as expected.…

title: fix(links): stop slicing chars with a lowercased offset (close #816)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

`text.to_lowercase()` produced a longer char buffer than the source `chars` when the input had U+0130 ('İ'), so the original export's `find_urls` sliced `chars[i..j]` with a `lc`-derived index and panicked (`range start index 41 out of range for slice of length 39`).

Iterate `chars` indices only and lowercase only the small prefix used for scheme matching (`http://`, `https://`, `www.`). The case-insensitive scheme detection still works, but boundary and length checks use original indices.

Closes #816.

title: xfa, xfdf: refuse XML nested past 1024 levels instead of aborting the process
author: pkibiego
