Both crates that hand attacker-supplied XML to `roxmltree` now measure the element nesting depth first and refuse anything past 1,024 levels. `crates/xfa/src/data.rs` gets the same guard at its two parse sites, and both crates' parse options carry `nodes_limit`.

| Crate | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `pdfcraft-xfa` | `src/lib.rs` (the scanner), `src/parse.rs`, `src/data.rs`, `src/tests.rs` |
| `pdfcraft-xfdf` | `src/lib.rs` (the scanner, `walk_xfdf` depth bound, `nodes_limit`), `src/tests.rs` |

## Why: roxmltree recurses with the nesting depth, so deep XML aborts the process

```
thread 'main' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
```

That is `abort()`, not a panic, so the `catch_unwind` guard around document operations cannot intercept it - the process dies. Measured on the default 8 MiB stack: 100, 1,000 and 3,000 levels parse fine, 10,000 aborts. The same 10,000-deep document parses on a 512 MiB stack, which is what shows the recursion is proportional to depth rather than runaway.

Two entry points take attacker-supplied text:

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XFDF import, 50,000 nested `<field>` (1.4 MB) | **SIGABRT**, core dumped, 288 ms | `the file nests XML elements 50003 deep, past the 1024 the reader accepts`, 54 ms, 19 MB |
| XFDF import, 200,000 nested (5.9 MB) | **SIGABRT**, 364 ms | same refusal with 200003 deep, 73 ms, 23 MB |
| XFA template, 10,000 nested (`pdfcraft_xfa::parse`) | **SIGABRT** in the crate's own test run | clean error |
| XFDF with 2,000,000 siblings (93 MB) | clean error, 1,082 MB, 2,323 ms | `nodes limit reached`, 289 MB, 1,299 ms |

The XFDF rows were driven end to end through `pdfcraft-cli run --script` with the `doc_import_data` tool, inside a memory-capped scope. The XFA row is the crate's own test, because `pdfcraft-cli info` and `text` never parse the template.

## Why the check has to run before the parse

The obvious fix - cap the depth in our own walks - does not…

title: M11: strip redundant ASCII stream wrappers during optimization
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

The optimizer's clean-up now removes an outer ASCII85 or ASCIIHex layer from non-image streams whose filter chain starts with it (for example `[/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]` becomes `[/FlateDecode]`), when the serialized replacement is smaller. The inner encoded bytes are kept exactly, and the decoded stream bytes are unchanged. Streams that do not qualify are left alone.

## Problem and root cause

`optimize_with_progress` in `crates/optimize/src/lib.rs` Flate-compresses only streams with no `/Filter` (`flate_unencoded`). A stream that carries an ASCII wrapper is skipped entirely, so the wrapper's expansion (about 25% for ASCII85, 100% for ASCIIHex) stays in the file. Legacy text-safe transport produces this shape.

## Scope and non-goals

- Eligible: a `/Filter` array whose first name is `ASCII85Decode` or `ASCIIHexDecode`, with at least one more filter; no `/DecodeParms`; not `/Subtype /Image`; not `/Type /ObjStm`, `/Metadata` or `/XRef`; raw size at least 64 bytes.
- Excluded: streams whose chain contains `Crypt`; single-filter ASCII streams; single-Flate streams (unchanged, as before); `/DecodeParms` are never rewritten.
- The wrapper is removed from the `/Filter` array and the rest of the array keeps its names and order. The inner filters are not decoded.
- No UI change. The rule runs under the existing `flate_unencoded` setting (default on), so turning that setting off also turns this off.
- `Report::streams_compressed` counts stripped streams as well.

## Design and invariants

- `Stream::decoded_first_filter_strict(max)` (new, `crates/cos/src/object.rs`) decodes only the first filter, using the existing strict `pdfcraft_filters::decode`. The bound is the stored size. ASCII85 output is at most 4/5 of its text and ASCIIHex output is at most 1/2, so valid input never reaches the bound; a corrupt wrapper is an error and the stream is left unchanged.
- A candidate replaces the stream only if its stored size is smaller. The size is the serialized dict…

title: text_find stops reading pages once its limit is reached (#971)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
`text_find` asked `page_texts` for **every** page before looking at a single match, so `limit` only capped the JSON array, not the work: `limit: 1` on the 9,156-page VCF manual meant extracting (and caching the geometry of) the whole document, and a late page that failed extraction could fail a search already satisfied on page 1. A capped result also only said `count: 500`, which reads like the total.

## The fix (`crates/automation`)
- **Item 1:** pages are read in document order in batches (8 first, doubling to 128, still extracted in parallel within a batch). The search stops as soon as it finds one match past `limit`, so later pages are never extracted or cached.
- **Item 3:** the result now has `complete` (true only when the search ran to the end of the document). A capped result also carries `next: { "start_page": P, "skip": K }`, and the new optional `start_page` / `skip` arguments take exactly that to continue without repeats or gaps (`skip` handles a page with several matches). The schema descriptions say so.
- **Item 4 (partly):** pages after the point where the limit is satisfied are no longer touched, so their extraction errors can't fail the call. A failing page *inside* the searched range still fails it, as before.
- **Item 2 (partly):** only the pages a search actually reached are cached. A byte/LRU budget for the automation text cache isn't in this PR, and neither are items 5–6.
- ROADMAP.md log line added.

## How it was tested
New unit test `tests::a_bounded_text_find_reads_only_the_pages_it_needs_and_says_it_stopped` (200-page synthetic fixture):
- `"Page 1"` with `limit: 1` returns page 1, `complete: false`, `next: {start_page: 10, skip: 0}`, and leaves at most 24 of 200 pages in the text cache.
- Following `next` with `limit: 3` for `"1"` (two matches on pages like 11 and 101, so `skip` matters) gives exactly the same matches in the same order as one unbounded search, which reports `complete: true` and no `next`.

title: M14: a chosen interface size is absolute, as in PhotoCraft
author: mitul72
body:
Follow-up to #902, from @Quicksilver151's comment there (#456).

## Problem

In #902 a chosen Interface size multiplied the display scale the system reports. On a 1080p screen whose system reports 200 %, "100%" therefore still drew at 200 %, while PhotoCraft's "100%" draws at a true 100 % on the same machine. The two sibling apps disagreed on what a percentage means.

## Change

- A chosen size is now **absolute**, as in PhotoCraft (`display_scale` in its `prefs_ui.rs`): the zoom factor is the chosen size divided by the display's scale, so "100%" is one screen pixel per point whatever the display reports.
- **Auto is unchanged**: the display's scale times GNOME's text scaling. Its menu entry now shows the size it actually draws at (e.g. "Auto (200%)" on a 2× display).
- The menu offers PhotoCraft's sizes: 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250, 300 %. The 50 % entry existed only to undo a 2× display scale, which an absolute 100 % now does directly. Settings and the control channel still accept 50–300 %.
- The zoom is still re-applied only when it changes; it is recomputed from the display's scale every frame, so moving the window to a monitor with a different scale keeps a chosen size absolute.
- Trade-off (the same as PhotoCraft's): on a HiDPI display, a chosen 100 % draws at one pixel per point, i.e. smaller than the system's default. Auto, the default, still follows the display.

## Testing

- `ui_scale` tests: a chosen size draws at the same size on 1×, 1.25×, 2× and 3× displays; an unusable display scale counts as 1×; Auto keeps the display's scale.
- The end-to-end kittest now runs on a simulated 2× display: Auto draws at 2.5 (2× display × 1.25 text scale), "100%" at 1.0, "150%" at 1.5, and back to Auto at 2.5.
- Only these tests were run locally; the full `cargo xtask ci` is left to CI.

author: echelon
body:
Follow-up to #847, fixing what review found after merge.

- **Actual size:** sheets were drawn into `MarginBounds`, i.e. inside .NET's default 1-inch margins, so every job printed at about 76% on Letter. Each sheet now prints at 100% from the page edge on the driver's paper closest to its size (within ⅛ in), turned landscape when wide; shrunk only when no paper is large enough. Matches CUPS' `fit-to-page=false`.

Without a source (tests) the dialog reads printers synchronously as before, so kittest stays deterministic and never selects a real printer. A list arriving late preselects the default only if the user hasn't picked one.
- **Parity:** #847's evidence named `a_print_job_reaches_the_windows_spooler`, which doesn't exist; `cargo xtask parity` now exits 0. The raster-only limit is stated in the parity notes and README as the PR described.

title: Chinese UI falls back to an installed CJK font (#826)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## What
Fixes [#826](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/826): Simplified Chinese UI text renders as missing-glyph (tofu) boxes in release builds.

## Why
The last-resort interface font (`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs`) loaded a **single** installed face selected only by an Arabic probe (`segoeui.ttf` / `SFArabic.ttf` / Noto Arabic). A release built without a craft-fonts `Hans` face — which is every current release, since `AGENTS.md` §1.1 bars Noto CJK — therefore had no Chinese glyphs anywhere, matching the reporters' screenshots on macOS and Windows.

## Change
- `system_fonts::fallback()` now returns a `Vec` and loads **one installed face per script**: the existing Arabic group, plus a CJK group probed with 欢 (U+6B22, Simplified-only, so the chosen face provably covers Simplified Chinese rather than only shared Han). Candidates: Microsoft YaHei / SimSun / JhengHei (Windows), PingFang / STHeiti / Hiragino Sans GB (macOS), Noto Sans CJK / WenQuanYi (Linux). Paths are de-duplicated so a file is never loaded twice.
- `theme::installed_font_definitions` appends each face as `system-fallback-{i}` to the end of every family, after the embedded faces, so a bundled craft-fonts face still wins when present.
- These are installed, read at runtime, never embedded or shipped (AGENTS.md §1.4); `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` still turns them off.

This is the desktop runtime fallback. The web build and desktops with no CJK font installed still want an openly licensed `Hans` face bundled in craft-fonts — tracked as the remainder of gap 5.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test fonts` and `--lib system_fonts`: all pass. On Windows (`msyh.ttc` present) the updated `system_fallback_fills_missing_scripts` test exercises the CJK branch and asserts Simplified Chinese (`简体中文欢迎`) has real glyphs in every UI family.

title: M10: enhance camera images: straighten a page from four corners (engine + tool, part 1 of #1008)
author: magdale76
body:
Part 1 of #1008: the engine and the headless tool for straightening a photographed page from four corners (`ocr.camera-perspective`). The UI follows in a second PR on top of this one.

## What it does

`Session::enhance_camera_page(id, page, corners)` takes four corners in PDF user space (any order; they must form a convex quadrilateral), renders the page at its picture's own resolution (at most 600 dpi, 300 dpi for a page without a picture, at most 40 MP), warps the quadrilateral to an upright rectangle as large as its longer opposite sides, and replaces what the page shows with that picture through `Edit::ReplacePages`, as one undoable step labelled *Enhance camera image*. The page keeps the photo's physical size; its comments, links and bookmarks stay (Replace Pages semantics).

- **geom** (`perspective.rs`, no dependencies): a 3×3 homography solve (Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, then a check that the four points really map) and `order_quad`, which puts corners in reading order and refuses concave, degenerate or non-finite input with `None`.
- **engine** (`camera.rs`): `warp` (bilinear, premultiplied RGBA composited over white; outside the page is white; output capped at 40 MP) and the `Session` method.
- **automation**: `page_enhance_camera` (`doc`, `page`, `corners` as 8 numbers in top-left-origin points, like the other tools).
- **parity**: `ocr.camera-perspective` → `partial`; the notes say what is missing (UI, automatic edge detection, contrast and background clean-up, document types).

Never-crash: no `unwrap`/indexing on input-derived values in non-test code; bad corners, a wrong buffer size and corners far outside the page are errors or capped, with tests.

## Tests

- `geom`: corner mapping, identity, inverse round trip, collinear/non-finite refusal, corner ordering, concave/degenerate refusal.
- `engine`: `warp` on a tilted quad, corner order independence, transparency → white, bad input; end to end, a synthetic photo (a tilted white sheet …

A native-speaker review of the Italian catalog (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/it.tsv`): 47 entries changed, written from the meaning of the English labels as the catalog header asks (no other product's strings consulted). **Meaning**
- `Margins (in)` → *Margini (pollici)*: "in" read as the Italian preposition.

title: M4, #569: Combine files takes images and text files
author: mlkonrad
body:
Fixes #569.

Combine files now takes images and plain text as well as PDFs. PNG, JPEG, TIFF (every page of a multi-page one), GIF, BMP, JPEG 2000 and `.txt` files become PDFs as they're added (Add files…, drops, folder scans), so each one is an ordinary card or row with its pages, thumbnails and page range. It reuses `Session::convert_to_pdf` from Create ▸ Multiple files (#361) through a new `Session::as_pdf`. PDFs pass through unread, so protected ones still go through Unlock…, and so does a file named `.pdf` without a `%PDF-` header, which the reader may still open.

### Files that can't be read
Before, a damaged file was refused when you added it. Now it joins the list: its card shows a red ✕ with the reason, the Warnings column says "Can't be read: …", and the footer counts it under "needs attention". This applies to a broken image, a damaged PDF, or a type that can't be converted, such as a dropped `.docx`. Clicking Combine then asks **"Leave out files that can't be read?"** and names each such file and why. **Combine the rest** goes on without them; Cancel (or Escape) changes nothing. If fewer than two readable files would be left, Combine stays disabled and its tooltip says why. Password-protected files still block Combine until they're unlocked, as before.

### Also
- The picker offers "PDF, images and text". The empty state, the folder tooltips and the folder notices say what's accepted.
- `doc_combine` accepts the same file types.
- A converted file's bookmark drops its extension: "scan", not "scan.png".
- Separate commit: **a PNG whose header claims more than 2 GiB of pixels is refused before its buffer is allocated.** The png crate's limits don't cover the caller's frame buffer, so a few-KB PNG claiming 60000×60000 RGBA made Create allocate and fill 14.4 GB. This uses the same ceiling TIFF pages already have. It was reachable from Create and Insert pages before this change; Combine's drops and folder scans make it easier to hit.

title: Edit text: support Devanagari system font fallback and Indic pre-base matra reordering
author: krinry
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes garbled and misplaced Hindi/Devanagari text during inline text editing and PDF content processing.

### Root Cause
1. **Missing Devanagari UI Fallback Font:**
   The interface font fallback loader in `crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` only probed for Arabic (`PROBE = '\u{0627}'`), omitting Devanagari glyph coverage (`0x0900..=0x097F`). When editing text containing Hindi characters in the egui text editor, missing glyphs resulted in tofu/replacement characters.
2. **Visual vs Logical Pre-base Vowel (ि Matra) Ordering:**
   In PDF content streams, glyphs are often positioned in visual display order. For Devanagari pre-base vowel signs like 'ि' (`\u{093F}`), the glyph sits before the consonant visually (`\u{093F}\u{0915}` instead of logical `\u{0915}\u{093F}`). When extracted glyph-by-glyph, this resulted in orphan combining marks and corrupted conjuncts (e.g. `◌िक` or `◌िस्थ◌ित` instead of `कि` / `स्थिति`).

### Changes
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs`:**
  - Added `devanagari_fallback()` and `DEVANAGARI_PROBE = '\u{0915}'`.
  - Added candidate system font search paths across Linux (Google Noto, Lohit, Droid), Windows (Nirmala, Mangal, Aparajita, Utsaah), and macOS (DevanagariMT, Kohinoor, DevanagariSangamMN).
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`:**
  - Defined `SYSTEM_DEVANAGARI_FALLBACK = "system-devanagari-fallback"`.
  - Registered the Devanagari fallback into all font family stacks (Proportional, Monospace, Medium, SemiBold).
  - Ensured `install_fonts` delegates to `install_fonts_for(ctx, false)` so system fallbacks take effect consistently.
- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs`:**
  - Implemented `reorder_indic_visual_to_logical` and `reorder_indic_logical_to_visual` to reorder orphaned pre-base vowels around their respective consonant clusters (including halants, nuktas, and conjuncts).
  - Applied visual-to-logical reordering upon extracting text in `text_lines` and `reading_lines`.

title: M10: Enhance camera image cleans the photo up and chooses its look (part 4 of #1008, closes #1034)
author: magdale76
body:
Closes #1034. Part 4 of the camera-image work, on top of #1027 (← #1019 ← #1018): only the last commit is new here. I'll rebase as the earlier parts land.

## What it does

After *Enhance page*, the bar now offers a **look** — *Original*, *Colour*, *Greyscale*, *Black and white* — and a **Clean-up** slider (0–100). A page is enhanced in *Colour* at 50 by default. Choosing a look or letting go of the slider enhances the page again **from the straightened photo** (never on top of the previous result) and turns it as before, so the history keeps one *Enhance camera image* step (plus one turn), never a pile of them. If the top of the history is no longer those steps, the slider goes back instead of undoing someone else's edit.

`camera_clean`, pure Rust, no new dependencies:
- **clean:** estimates the paper's illumination per channel on a coarse grid (each block's 90th percentile, lifted to the 75th percentile of the 5×5 blocks around it, so a stamp or a picture up to about half that neighbourhood isn't taken for paper, then smoothed) and divides it out. Room-light colour casts, shadows and darker edges go and the paper turns white. A contrast stretch grows with the level, and from 60 isolated dark pixels are removed. Colour ink (stamps, blue pen) stays colour.
- **apply(look):** *Original* is the photo as taken; *Greyscale* is the cleaned page in grey. *Black and white* evens the lighting fully, thresholds the page (the level is the threshold: higher keeps fainter strokes black) and despeckles. It is stored as **PNG**, losslessly, since JPEG would smear grey around every letter.

Headless: `page_enhance_camera` takes `mode` (`original`, `colour`, `greyscale`, `bw`) and `level` (0–100), and refuses anything else. `Session::enhance_camera_page_at(look, level)`.

Four new labels (*Clean-up*, *Original*, *Greyscale*, *Black and white*) are translated in every catalog with UI coverage, plus es, pl and zh-hant; `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes are updated.

Resolves #1024

### Summary
Multi-click text selection (double-click word, triple-click line, quadruple-click page) was previously evaluated on pointer button release (`egui`'s `response.double_clicked()` / `triple_clicked()`). In native editors, Acrobat, and web browsers, double/triple click text highlights immediately on the down-stroke (`primary_pressed()`), before the user lifts the mouse button.

title: Return renderer initialization errors to the OpenGL startup fallback
author: huferyliu
body:
On this Windows 11 host, the official 0.6.0 x86 EXE exits with code 101 before showing a usable window: NVIDIA/DX12 fails to create `egui_pipeline` with `0x80070057`, and renderer creation invokes wgpu's default panic handler. The app's existing OpenGL startup retry therefore never receives an error to handle.

This change wraps renderer creation in the existing scoped GPU-error handler and returns `WgpuError::CreateRenderer`. Auto startup can then reach its existing OpenGL fallback before the app is created. It does not repair the underlying DX12 shader compilation failure or change explicit renderer choices.

Changes:

- A real-GPU regression alternates invalid/valid pipelines on the same device (`[3, 1, 3, 1]`) to check error propagation and device reuse. The unguarded constructor panicked; the guarded version passes.
- An independent commit fixes the hostile-argument test fixture when Windows refuses symbolic-link creation with OS error 1314. It reports the unavailable fixture and only exercises the link path when it exists; the other confinement cases remain.
- Windows reproduction, scope and acceptance instructions are documented in `docs/windows-renderer-startup.md`, with the required roadmap notes.

Validation on the contribution branch based on `bbbe60015c571ebfc39708ee07777b89e267122a`:

- The GPU regression passed with `PDFCRAFT_TEST_REQUIRE_GPU=1` and process-scoped Vulkan; no unavailable-device branch was skipped.
- A native x86 GUI build (PE `0x014c`, subsystem `2`) was executed with both renderer variables unset. title: Forms: encode appearances with the existing simple font
author: piero-83
body:
Filling a field that reuses a simple font with custom Encoding/Differences currently writes WinAnsi bytes into that font. Italian curly apostrophes and em dashes can therefore show different glyphs after blur/save. A subset font can also lack newly entered characters.

Read the reused font's encoding with the existing Metrics API and check every displayed value before choosing it. title: Edit images: moving or resizing a clipped image moves its own clip too (#1022)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1022.

PowerPoint (and other exporters) paint each picture inside its own clip:

```
q  x y w h re  W* n  w 0 0 h x y cm  /Im Do  Q
```

`change_image` wrapped only the `Do` in `q cm … Q`, so the clip set before it stayed where it was and the moved or enlarged image was cut off at its old rectangle.

**What changes**

- When the `Do` sits alone in `q [cm…] re W|W* n cm Do Q`, the clip belongs to that image only. `change_image` (move, resize, rotate, flip) and the group move (`translate_images`, used by `move_objects`) now put one `cm` right before the `re` instead of wrapping the `Do`. The clip and the image then get the same user-space transform, so the image is fully visible at its new place.
- A `cm` added by an earlier edit is accepted between `q` and `re`, so the second and later drags of the same image still take the clip along.
- A clip that also covers other content (the `Do` is not alone between the clip and its `Q`) is left exactly as before. Non-rectangular clips are not touched either.
- `docs/editing-images.md` says this.

Images under a shared or non-rectangular clip still behave as before (clipped by the shared clip); explaining that in the UI, as the issue suggests, is a separate decision.

**Test**

`moving_an_image_moves_its_own_clip_too` builds a page with the issue's pattern and checks, after save/reopen where relevant, that the clip rectangle in user space matches the image box after a resize, after a second edit of the same image, after a group move following it, and after a group move on a fresh page. It also checks that a shared clip stays where it was. It fails on main (the clip stays at 100,100–300,200).

title: macOS: "Reopen the files that were open" starts from the system reopen-windows setting (#871)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Closes #871

## Problem

Preferences ▸ "Reopen the files that were open when PdfCraft last closed" always starts unchecked. On macOS the system already has this choice: System Settings ▸ Desktop & Dock ▸ Windows ▸ "Close windows when quitting an application". A user who turned that off (`NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows = 1`) expects apps to bring their windows back, and PdfCraft ignored it.

## Change

`apps/pdfcraft/src/reopen.rs` (new, modelled on `text_scale.rs`): reads `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` once at launch through `/usr/bin/defaults read -g`, with the same 500 ms guard as the `gsettings` read. The key is absent when the user never changed the setting, and `defaults` then fails; that means the system default, close windows when quitting, so the preference stays off. Only an explicit `1`/`true` turns it on.

`main.rs`: the value is applied right after `PdfCraftApp::new()` and before `restore()`, so it is the starting value only. A choice the user made in Preferences is persisted as `reopen_last_session` and wins on every later launch, exactly as before. Existing installations are therefore unaffected; the setting only matters on a first launch or when the saved preferences have no such key.

Other systems have no equivalent setting and keep starting off. The web build is untouched.

I chose "default to it" rather than "follow it live" (both are mentioned in the issue): following it live would make the checkbox in Preferences meaningless, and the checkbox is the only place where a Windows or Linux user can make the choice.

## Tests

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
| `cargo test -p pdfcraft --bin pdfcraft -- reopen` (new: `only_a_set_flag_keeps_windows`, `reading_the_system_default_never_fails`) | 2 passed |

title: macOS: the tab strip is the 28 pt band the traffic lights are centred in (#789)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Closes #789

## Cause

On macOS the window has no system title bar (`with_fullsize_content_view`, `with_titlebar_shown(false)` in `main.rs`), and AppKit draws the traffic lights itself, centred in its standard 28 pt title-bar band at the top of the window. PdfCraft's tab strip, which doubles as the title bar there, is 38 pt tall with 30 pt tabs, so the lights sat about 5 pt above the strip's centre line and the tabs' centre.

Neither winit 0.30 nor eframe 0.36 offers a way to move the lights, and doing it directly means AppKit calls (`unsafe`, which the workspace forbids; `objc2-app-kit` exposes `standardWindowButton` and `setFrameOrigin` safely, but reaching the buttons' superview to resize the title-bar container is not). So the strip now fits the lights, rather than the other way round, the same way storytold/wordcraft#255 solved it for WordCraft's title bar.

## Change

macOS only (`integrated_titlebar`, which `main.rs` sets on macOS only). Linux, Windows and the web build keep the 38 pt strip and 30 pt tabs; nothing changes there.

- **Tab strip** (`chrome.rs`): 28 pt tall on macOS, so the lights are vertically centred in it. Tabs shrink from 30 to 26 pt and the Home, theme and shortcuts buttons from 28 to 24 pt, keeping a 1–2 pt margin above and below. Content starts at `MAC_CONTENT_LEFT` = the end of the three lights (12 pt buttons, 20 pt pitch, first one at about 10 pt) plus the 8 pt gap the lights keep from the top of the window, instead of a flat 80 pt. The width reserved for the right-hand controls follows the button size.

title: M2, #1060: axial and radial shadings draw as native gradients (InDesign fades 10× faster)
author: mlkonrad
body:
Fixes #1060.

## Problem

A user reported that large PDFs render page by page slowly ("often having to wait a couple of seconds for a new page"), on both the portable and ARM64 builds. With their file, [*Mobily Annual Report 2025 - English.pdf*](https://ir.mobily.link/2025/pdfs/Mobily%20Annual%20Report%202025%20-%20English.pdf) (public; 144 pages, InDesign, 16 MB), some pages take 5–11 s in PdfCraft. MuPDF draws the same pages in 0.2–0.4 s, and Firefox shows them almost at once.

## Cause

InDesign writes fades and feathers as **luminosity soft masks whose group is a single extended axial `sh`**, a gradient that covers the whole page. Page 4 has 40 of them. hayro 0.7 draws a shading by evaluating the PDF shading function and colour space once per device pixel, on one thread (`render_shading_texture`). That comes to 40 × ~4 M pixels per page at 144 dpi.

Measured on page 4 at 144 dpi:

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 15.8 s |
| ExtGState soft masks removed | 0.76 s |
| image soft masks removed | 13.0 s |
| transparency groups removed | 15.7 s |

## Fix

hayro 0.8.0 (2026-10-04) already fixes this. Its new `gradient` module turns axial and radial shadings into native sRGB gradient stops, and `vello_cpu` draws them. This PR backports that code as vendored patches instead of moving the whole vendored copy to 0.8, which would mean re-porting about 45 local patches:

- **hayro-interpret (23):** `gradient.rs` from 0.8.0, adapted to 0.7's `EncodedShadingType::RadialAxial` variant, plus `stitching_bounds` on `Function`, `Type3` and `ShadingFunction`. Stops are placed within 0.01 per channel, with a stop at every stitching bound. A shading is only converted when a native gradient draws it exactly: extended past the drawn box, and for radial with no background colour. Everything else keeps the sampled texture path.
- **hayro (10):** `set_paint` paints a converted shading as a `vello_cpu` linear or two-point radial gradient. One difference from upstream: upstream shi…

title: fix(ui): preserve scroll position when collapsing or resizing sidebars (#1056)
author: omarelders
body:
﻿## Description
Fixes #1056.

When sidebars (bookmarks, comments, search, etc.) are collapsed, expanded, or resized, the available canvas width changes. In `Fit::Width` (default) and `Fit::Page` modes, `view.fit_zoom` adjusts `view.zoom` to match the newly available dimensions. Previously, egui's `ScrollArea` retained the absolute point scroll offset from the prior frame, which caused the view to autoscroll away from the current reading position (an error that compounded with the page index).

This PR records the previous zoom before `fit_zoom` runs. If `view.zoom` changes and no active user zoom gesture or navigation (`goto` / `goto_point`) is in flight, it finds the visible page and fractional offset at the top of the viewport from the prior frame's `screen_rects` and sets `zoom_anchor` so egui anchors the visible reading position across the resize.

## Verification
- Added automated regression test `sidebar_collapse_and_resize_preserves_scroll_position` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/view.rs`.
- Verified test fails before the fix (collapsing the panel caused view to jump from page 2 to page 1) and passes with the fix.
- Verified all 32 tests in `tests/view.rs` pass.
- Verified clean build and zero warnings with `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`.

title: Text: keep runs drawn right-to-left on one line intact (#1062)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1062.

When two runs on the same line were drawn right-hand run first, `pdfcraft-cli text` produced `20. 019.4` instead of `20.0 19.4`.

Cause: in `arrange` (crates/render/src/text.rs), the glyphs of a line are sorted by x, but the word-gap space was placed before glyph `c.max(p)`, which is the later of the two in content order. That trick exists for right-to-left runs, which are reversed (visual to logical) before the spaces are placed. For left-to-right text drawn out of order, it put the space before the last glyph of the left run (`20.` + space + `0`), so the digit moved to the other word.

Fix: for a gap between two left-to-right glyphs, mark the space before `c`, the right-hand glyph, which is already in x order. If either glyph is RTL, the old logic stays, so RTL handling does not change.

The same code path handles the real-world case in the issue (different fonts, baselines up to ~2 pt apart that still merge into one line), so it is fixed as well.

Test: `runs_drawn_right_to_left_keep_their_own_glyphs_and_the_space_between` draws `19.4` before `20.0` and expects `20.0 19.4`. On main it gives `20. 019.4`.

title: UI: draw Simplified Chinese from an installed CJK face
author: guoyinchen
body:
## Problem

Simplified Chinese labels render as replacement boxes. The embedded set has no `Hans` face — craft-fonts' Noto Sans CJK SC is barred by AGENTS.md §1.1 (Source Han), so releases have no Chinese face of their own (#826, #688, #728, #758). On top of that the runtime system fallback (`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs`) only probed for Arabic, so it never filled the gap: with craft-fonts, shared characters draw from the Japanese faces while Simplified-only ones (开, 门, 欢, …) fall through to tofu; without craft-fonts every character does.

## Change

- **`system_fonts.rs`** — the single installed face (AGENTS.md §1.3) is now chosen to draw **both** CJK and Arabic (macOS: `Arial Unicode.ttf`), with the Arabic-only face kept as the fallback when that is all the machine has. Probe selection is per-face: a face must map every probe character of the set it is tried for.
- **`theme.rs`** — in Simplified Chinese mode, when the installed face draws CJK and craft-fonts brought no `Hans` face (the release state), it *leads* the CJK fallbacks (right after the Latin face) instead of staying last. One line then keeps one baseline — the `ui_cjk_fonts` rationale: otherwise the Japanese faces draw the shared characters while Simplified-only ones fall through and the mixed vertical metrics sink them below the line. With an embedded `Hans` face, ordering is unchanged.
- **Tests** — multi-probe face selection in `system_fonts.rs`; `system_fallback_fills_missing_scripts` asserts the Chinese-mode lead (position right after the Latin face) and that `简体中文欢迎` lays out at full glyph widths when the lead applies.

## Notes

- `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` behavior is unchanged (published screenshots omit the fallback entirely).
- Nothing new is embedded, shipped or committed: the face is read at runtime only (AGENTS.md §1.3–§1.4), so this is not a delivery path for a real `Hans` face — that remains craft-fonts work.
- Quality gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace …

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across PDFCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for PDFCraft.

title: Text extraction: word gaps follow position on the line, not drawing order (#1062)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
Fixes #1062.

`layout` sorts a line's glyphs left to right, but it put the space for a word gap before whichever of the two glyphs came later in the content stream (`c.max(p)`). When the right-hand run is drawn first, that is the last glyph of the left run, so `20.0 19.4` came out as `20. 019.4`.

The same rule was also wrong for right-to-left lines. With `שלום עולם` drawn left to right, the space landed one letter early (`שלו םעולם`).

Word gaps are now marked by position on the line, and reversed together with the glyphs of right-to-left runs.

Test: `word_gaps_follow_position_not_drawing_order` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` covers the issue's draw order and a two-word Hebrew line.

title: M12: XFA script time limits start when the engine is ready
author: arcanii
body:
## What was wrong

Two UI tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/xfa.rs` fail now and then, usually together:

- `xfa_buttons_run_their_scripts_in_the_app`: the row that `addRow` should add is missing;
- `messages_from_scripts_run_on_open_show_right_away`: no "Welcome to the form" notice.

They aren't waiting too few frames: the scripts run synchronously inside `open_bytes`. The fault is in the app. An XFA script that runs unasked (initialize, calculate) has a 1 s wall-clock limit, and `run_within` started that clock before the script engine existed, so the limit also counted:

- starting the script's thread;
- `Context::default()`: about 2 ms as a rule, but about 63 ms for the first one in a process, which sets up boa's shared tables (two scripts starting together both wait for it);
- the engine's first parse and compile.

A first script costs 110–170 ms on an idle machine. Under load that can pass 1 s. The script is then abandoned, and an abandoned script turns all of the form's scripts off for the document, with the error only in the JavaScript console:

```
Error: form[0].page1[0] (initialize): the script ran longer than 1.0 s and was abandoned
Error: The form's scripts were stopped: one ran too long; 2 more were skipped
```

A user gets the same by opening an XFA form while the machine is busy: the form quietly stops calculating.

To see it: 40 busy-loop processes on a 32-core machine, then 8 copies of the `xfa` test binary at once. On upstream `bbbe600`, in five such rounds, **25 of 40 runs fail** (between 1 and 8 of the 8 in a round).

## What changed

The time limit now measures the script, not the engine's start-up.

- `run_within` (`crates/js/src/xfa.rs`): the script's closure is handed a `started` callback and calls it once the engine is ready. The caller waits for that within a start-up limit of its own (10 s, so nothing waits forever), then for the outcome within the script's limit, which is unchanged. A script that returns without calling `started` (one refuse…

title: Linux: StartupWMClass is the window's app id
author: atoslins
body:
`packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.desktop` says `StartupWMClass=pdfcraft`, but the window carries the app id `ai.storyteller.pdfcraft` (`APP_ID`, through `with_app_id`), natively on Wayland and under XWayland alike. The key is meant to name the class the window maps with ([Desktop Entry spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/recognized-keys.html)), so anything that matches a window to its launcher by it never matches PdfCraft. One concrete effect: on X11 the window manager ends a launch's startup notification when a window with that class maps (mutter: `find_startup_sequence_by_wmclass` in `src/core/display.c`), so with `StartupNotify=true` the busy cursor runs until its timeout instead.

VectorCraft, GridCraft and WordCraft already use the app id. This PR does the same, and adds a test that reads the entry and compares its `StartupWMClass` with `APP_ID`, so they can't drift apart again (they never matched: the entry started as `StartupWMClass=printcraft` next to the app id `ai.storyteller.printcraft`, and the rename carried that over).

Not covered here: GNOME on Wayland ends startup notification through an xdg-activation token, not the class, so this doesn't change what PhotoCraft fixed in #2089/#2097 by turning `StartupNotify` off. PdfCraft still has it on.

**Checked**
- Window class with PdfCraft 0.6.0 on Hyprland 0.56.2: `ai.storyteller.pdfcraft` both on Wayland and with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= pdfcraft` (XWayland).
- The new test fails on `main` (`left: Some("pdfcraft")`, `right: Some("ai.storyteller.pdfcraft")`) and passes with the change.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft --bin pdfcraft`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Linux: draw on the GPU the Wayland compositor draws with
author: atoslins
body:
**Problem.** On a hybrid laptop whose Wayland compositor runs on the discrete GPU, PdfCraft 0.6.0 opens an empty window: nothing drawn, no error in the log, the process idle. The built-in panel hangs off the integrated GPU, so the panel rule (#8, #445/#558) picks it:

```
pdfcraft: drawing on Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-P) (IntegratedGpu, Vulkan)
```

The compositor takes those frames and shows nothing. Nothing fails, so the OpenGL fallback never starts. `WGPU_POWER_PREF=high` works around it. PhotoCraft 0.7.0 works out of the box on the same machine: it keeps the system's order, and Mesa's device-select layer puts the compositor's GPU first.

Machine: Intel Raptor Lake-P iGPU (`8086:a7a8`, drives the eDP panel) + RTX 3050 Laptop (`10de:25ac`), Arch Linux, kernel 7.2, Mesa 26.2.2, NVIDIA 610.57.04, Hyprland 0.56.2 with `AQ_DRM_DEVICES=<nvidia>:<intel>`. That setting makes the NVIDIA GPU the compositor's primary; it is needed to drive a 240 Hz HDMI monitor wired to the NVIDIA GPU without a cross-GPU copy per frame. Desktops whose compositor is told to use the discrete GPU are in the same spot.

**Change.** Which GPU drives a display stands in for which GPU the compositor draws with. Under Wayland the compositor says so itself: the `main_device` of its linux-dmabuf feedback (protocol version 4), the device it imports client buffers on. Mesa's device-select layer reads the same event for the same purpose (`default_dmabuf_feedback_main_device` in `src/vulkan/device-select-layer/device_select_wayland.c`).

- `compositor_gpu.rs` asks for it on a short-lived connection of its own, before the window opens. It maps the `dev_t` to PCI ids through `/sys/dev/char/MAJOR:MINOR/device/{vendor,device}`.
- `pick_adapter` ranks the adapter with those ids first. The rest of the order is unchanged.
- No answer leaves the existing rules in charge: X11, a compositor without linux-dmabuf v4, a GPU that no adapter matches. `WGPU_POWER_PREF` still overrides.
- Nothing panics: each failure falls …

title: M3: Accelerate coarse wheel scrolling
author: chiranjeevi-max
body:
Closes #1072

title: Explain signature-image dimension limits when import is rejected

title: XFA: single-block forms paginate, open in their saved state, and show their signatures
author: EULArule
body:
Relates to #60.

Some dynamic XFA forms put the whole form in one wrapped (`lr-tb`) subform. PdfCraft laid these out as a single page with most of the content missing or cut off. This branch makes such a form lay out as the form's own saved layout describes it.

**What it fixes**

- **One page instead of many.** A block that can't flow (wrapped, positioned or fixed-height) and is taller than a content area is now spread over the following pages. Breaks fall between lines, images and fields; a field or draw is kept whole unless it is taller than a page.
- **Missing table rows.** Repeating subforms inside wrapped containers now get one instance per data row.
- **Text boxes that didn't grow.** A multi-line text field with no fixed height grows to hold its text. If it is taller than a page it is drawn as static text across pages, with a warning that it can't be edited there.
- **Overlapping text.** Text that overflows a fixed-height box is scaled down (to 70% at most) instead of running over what follows.
- **Rows and labels a script had changed before saving.** The form packet's saved `presence`, `access` and captions are applied to the template, so rows shown before saving appear, locked fields stay locked, and a button keeps its saved label.
- **Sections far taller than they should be.** A flowed subform no longer stretches to a leftover `minH`. A public form whose own form packet records 3 pages laid out as 4 before this change and lays out as 3 now.
- **Boxes around borderless fields.** A text field with no border in its `<ui>` no longer gets a black box. Check boxes keep theirs.
- **Blank lines after every line.** A CR LF pair is one line break, not two.
- **Text measurement.** Times text is measured with Times widths rather than scaled Helvetica widths.
- **Signed signature boxes were empty.** A laid-out signature box takes the value and appearance of the signed AcroForm field with the same SOM name, and is read-only. The engine no longer redraws a signed box as …

title: Security: fix 10 verified audit findings in redaction, signature validation, and untrusted-input handling
author: JeremyYao
body:
# Security fixes from audit run-2 (verified high/medium findings)

Branch: `security/audit-run2-fixes` (6 commits off `main` at bbbe600) · 14 files, +807/−33 · **not yet opened as a PR.**

These fixes address ten independently verified findings from the run-2 security audit. Each was confirmed by reproducing it in a sandbox against `bbbe600`, and each fix ships with a synthetic regression test proven to fail without the change. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` are all green (2142 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored).

Scope note: only the ten **confirmed** findings are fixed here. One lead (the `/Encrypt` display-vs-signer split) remains **needs-validation** and is deliberately not touched. Severities are the verifier's; four were downgraded from the hunter's proposal and are included at the user's request.

## Confidentiality — redaction and sanitize (high)

- **Redaction left the originals in the file.** Covered or cleaned image/form XObjects kept their resource names, so the forced full-rewrite save still contained the original pixels and form text; Remove Hidden Information behaved the same. Now the dropped/replaced names are pruned from a page's (and a rewritten form's) resources when the surviving content no longer draws them. *(v3-064)*
- **Redacting an XFA form left the value in the XFA datasets packet**, where a later relayout could restore it on the page. Applying redactions to an XFA form now drops `/XFA` and `/NeedsRendering`, leaving a plain already-laid-out AcroForm. *(v3-067)*
- **Vertical-writing (CJK) text under a mark was never removed** yet apply reported success, because the removal geometry only laid glyphs out horizontally. Apply now **fails closed** (`RedactError::VerticalText`) rather than ship a document with unredacted vertical text. Full vertical-text removal is noted as a future enhancement. *(v3-062)*
- **Imported comment files could tamper with redaction marks.** An XFDF/FDF …

title: UI: a tool chosen with no document open asks for a file and runs on it
author: michelleDeko
body:
## What changes

When no document is open, clicking a tool that needs one in the tool panel or the
command palette (for example Export a PDF ▸ Microsoft Word) used to show only a
toast: "Open a document first". Now the Open picker appears, titled with the
tool's name. The chosen file opens and the tool runs on it right away.

- **Cancel:** nothing opens, nothing runs, no toast.
- **Encrypted PDFs:** the tool runs once the correct password is in. A wrong
  password keeps it waiting. Cancelling the password prompt drops it.
- **Images and text files** are converted to a PDF first, as with File ▸ Open,
  and the tool then runs on that PDF.
- **Menus and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged:** Ctrl+S with no document still
  says "Open a document first".
- **Web build:** the picker opens the file, and the user chooses the tool again.
  Browsers read the file asynchronously, so there is no hook to run the tool after it.

## How

- `run_command` (used by the tool panel and the palette) checks four things: the
  command is a catalogue tool, it needs a document, none is open, and that is why
  it's disabled. Then it calls the new `open_then_run`.
- `open_then_run` asks for the file through the existing non-blocking
  `ask_one`/`process_picked` path, opens it with `open_path`, then calls `execute`.
- `PasswordPrompt` gains `then: Option<&'static str>`. `submit_password` runs that
  command after a successful unlock, and keeps it when the password is wrong.
- The Open picker's filters moved into `open_picker()`, shared with `open_dialog`.

## Tests

- New: `a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it`
  (`crates/ui-egui/tests/commands.rs`) covers the picked file opening, the export
  dialog appearing, and nothing happening when the picker is cancelled.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: all pass
- `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean
- Not run: the full `cargo test --workspace`, the …

title: Print: start PowerShell on Windows by its full path
author: jcl-bit
body:
`spool::powershell_command` passes the bare name `powershell` to `std::process::Command::new`. On Windows, Rust resolves a bare name in the directory of the running executable before System32 ([std docs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html), "Platform-specific behavior"). So a `powershell.exe` sitting next to a portable `pdfcraft.exe` runs instead of Windows PowerShell, every time the Print dialog lists printers and on every job, and it receives the job's `PDFCRAFT_*` environment variables, including the path of the document being printed.

This PR names it by its full path under `%SystemRoot%`, the same way `open_printer_preferences` already names `rundll32` in the same file.

How I checked it, in Windows Sandbox with a harmless stand-in `powershell.exe` that only writes a marker file and prints one line:

| Build | Stand-in | Result |
|---|---|---|
| bbbe600 | next to a portable copy | the stand-in ran for both the printer list and the job, from the CLI and from the desktop app |
| bbbe600 | in the current directory only | not run (the current directory isn't searched) |
| this PR | next to a portable copy | not run; the real printer was listed and the job spooled; the process audit shows `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` |

Scope: only the portable zip is exposed. The MSI is per-machine and installs to Program Files. #847 isn't in a release yet, so nothing shipped is affected if this lands before 0.7.0.

Tests: `windows_starts_powershell_by_its_full_path` fails with the bare name and passes with the fix. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` are clean. The whole `pdfcraft-print` test suite passes (25 of 25), run in Windows Sandbox with the Generic / Text Only driver installed first so that `the_print_script_renders_the_job_and_reaches_the_spooler` really queued its job rather than skipping. title: M14: text the fonts can't draw is kept and reported, never written as ? silently
author: kekeandzeyu
body:
PdfCraft draws generated text in the standard fonts (Helvetica, WinAnsi). Several paths wrote characters those fonts can't draw (Chinese, Greek, Czech's ř, …) as `?` and reported success. This PR makes every one of them say so, following @echelon's review on #327: form values and comments keep the text as typed and warn, as Acrobat keeps them; refusal stays where the `?` would be permanent page content.

Refs #125, #194, #222, #327, #566. Independent of #879 (no craft-fonts dependency). Based on current `main`.

## Kept as typed, and said
- **Form values and button captions:** `/V` (or `/MK /CA`) is stored as typed and the appearance draws `?` for those characters. The form sets `/NeedAppearances`, so other viewers draw the field from its value with fonts that have them. Not in a document that declares PDF/A, which forbids the flag; there the warning says the `?` shows everywhere.
- **Text boxes, callouts, Fill & Sign text, measurement labels, dynamic stamps' by-lines:** stored as typed, drawn with `?`.
- **How it is said:** the annotation carries a private mark, `/PCUndrawn` (the first such character, like the existing `PC*` keys). After each edit the engine reports what that edit newly drew with `?` (`Document::edit_notices`, `TextNotice`). The interface shows a notice in the UI language (two new strings, in the 14 catalogs that have #510's message); tools return it as `warnings` (`form_fill`, `form_add_field`, `comment_add`, `fill_sign_add`, …). Later unrelated edits, failed edits, undo and redo don't repeat it.

- **Redrawing** a value another program stored (a property change, a dynamic XFA layout, sanitize) draws and marks it instead of failing, so an edit to one field never fails because of another field's value.

title: Comments: line breaks saved as CR show in comment text
author: nicholasyoannou
body: This PR fixes line breaks in comments, and handling of \r\n. Acrobat saves the line breaks in a comment's /Contents as CR, e.g. "first line\r\rsecond paragraph". egui draws CR as nothing and only breaks lines at LF, so the comments panel, the hover popup and the edit box ran the paragraphs together ("first linesecond paragraph"). title: Cap unbounded editing and text caches; index form fields once
author: chiranjeevi-max
body:
Two independent fixes. No behavior changes.

1. Cap editing and text-layer caches that grew without bound

The cos editing cache kept every touched object until save, so editing a large document pinned its whole object graph. It is now bounded like the scan reader: 1024 objects / 32 MB of owned bytes, 256 object streams / 32 MB, evicting to the newcomer. Returned objects outlive eviction and clones share the caches, so this only costs re-parsing.

Same shape in the viewer: every visited page's text layer stayed for the whole session. Now retains visible, selected and matched pages plus a 24-page prefetch window each frame; evicted pages re-extract on revisit. Skipped while a search is active, where demand still wants every page. Failures are never evicted (bytes-free to remember; evicting one would re-request and re-fail it every frame).

`cli info` on a 1024-page/147 KB file, debug build, same host and command: 66.7 MB -> ~54.0 MB RSS (3 runs, tight).

2. Index form fields once per refresh instead of once per field

The form-scope refresh ran a linear find over all fields for every field, O(F^2) on each keystroke; forms reach 10k fields. One name index up front, O(F). entry().or_insert() keeps the old first-match semantics for repeated field names, pinned by a new test with two same-named widgets.

Verification: cos 45, engine 141, ui-egui 232 tests green; clippy -D warnings and -D clippy::perf clean; each new bound fails with its fix disabled (checked by mutation).

Discovery is bounded and runs off the UI thread. Interface fallback fonts never enter exported PDFs.

title: Heavy pages: cull off-tile images, cache decodes, preview backdrops, calmer queues
author: MaksPV
body:
**Benchmark:  sheet ~5050 pt, 2,104 images, 9 MB of content.**  
On `main`: ~10 s to open; at 1000% zoom it hangs on the blurry/low-detail render (“soap” in the original); at 1200% the app crashed; RSS grows during operation. On the branch: RSS is stable at ~3 GB with no growth.

Measurements (single render, dev profile, p. 24):

| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| tile 1024 @1000% | 4300 ms | 612 ms |
| tile 2048 @1000% | 4960 ms | 1535 ms |
| whole page @96dpi | 10500 ms | ~10000 ms (unchanged — everything is visible there) |
| backdrop 2048 | 6760 ms | 5960 ms (LOD preview) |
| 1200% zoom | crash | survives |

What was done:

1. **Culling images outside the tile** (`vendor/hayro`, patch 10). Paths were already culled, but images were not: each tile decoded, resampled, and rasterized all 2,104. Now images are discarded before decode using the stream box (decoding only shrinks it — safe). Pixels are byte-for-byte identical; the test `skipping_paths_off_the_canvas_changes_no_pixel` was extended to cover images.
2. **Decode cache** (`vendor/hayro-interpret`, patch 23). `DecodedImageCache`: pixels keyed by `(stream, target)` with a 64 MB budget per worker. On this PDF it gives ~5% (decode is not the bottleneck); it removes repeated decoding during pans/zooms.
3. **LOD preview** (wired end-to-end: `RenderRequest` → `InterpreterSettings` → device; hayro patch 11 + interpret `preview`). Backdrop/thumbnails/grid/sign-drag skip images <16 px. Tiles, whole pages, printing, and export always draw everything. The preview may differ by these pixels (on the backdrop it is visually indistinguishable; transient under sharp tiles); finals do not change. Test: `preview_renders_skip_tiny_images_but_finals_draw_everything`.
4. **UI queue/tiles** (`canvas.rs`): zoom/pan holds only for slow pages (`slow_pages`, 500 ms — fast pages have no delays); tile side grows with zoom and dimensions (giant — ~8 tiles instead of 28); center-first order; keys by exact coordinates; limit on Edit-text…

title: M5: add Android and iOS applications with native PDF access and all UI languages
author: lukashold
body:

The host accepts only one-use imports from the system picker or document-open events. Save cancellation, provider errors and edits made during a save preserve unsaved state. Full license and source-access notices are bundled. title: Content edits on heavy documents: narrow refresh, cached appearances, per-page invalidation
author: MaksPV
body:
On a heavy document (72 MB, 202 pages, 27 thousand annotations without appearance), every content-edit commit — drag, resize, text input — hung the UI for ~1.5 s before re-rendering started, even on light pages. Cause: synchronous full `refresh` on every edit.

Measurements (dev, `doc_open + page_add_text` on this file, breakdown by stages):
- before: refresh 1.46 s = write 26 ms + inspect 466 ms + display 830–970 ms (rebuilding 27,414 appearances ~650 ms + write ~130 ms) + lists ~150 ms;
- after: commit ~0.3 s, a second consecutive edit is the same, no growth.

What was done:

1. **`Scope::Content`** (engine): edits touching only page content, resources, and added/marks (MoveObjects, EditTextLine/Block, EditPageImage, AddText/Image, UpdateContent/DeleteContent, ReplaceImage, marks) skip full `inspect`. Instead, `refresh_content`: working bytes + lightweight `check_pages` (parsing and verifying the page count — the guarantee against rolling back a broken edit is preserved) + display bytes + pool. `added`/`marks` are reread only if the edit touches them; undo/redo rereads both.
2. **`AppearanceCache`** (`pdfcraft-annot`): built appearances are reused while edits do not touch annotations (content edits touch none); cleanup on Comments/Full. `set_appearance` was split into build/apply halves; a hit skips rendering.
3. **`check_pages`** (`pdfcraft-render`): lightweight post-edit validation.
4. **UI**: single-page edits invalidate only their own page (`page_changed`); other tiles/text/thumbs stay alive.
5. **XFA**: dataset synchronization was extended to the new scope (previously these edits were Full and sync always ran).

Unchanged: save is not written on edit (as before), undo remained cheap (CoW), structural edits/comments/forms follow the old paths.

Verified: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` — all green. New tests: `cached_appearances_are_reused_while_annotations_are_unchanged` (annot), `content_edi…

title: Print: architectural paper presets and PDF scale controls (#599 follow-up)
author: durtyrobbin
body:
Architectural drawings still have only Letter/Legal/Tabloid/A3/A4/A5 available in Print. This carries the missing paper controls from @durtyrobbin's #599 onto `main` at `afb586e`, following the maintainer's invitation, while keeping the #847/#1007 printing backend and background jobs.

- Adds ARCH A/B/C/D/E1/E, ANSI C/D/E and A0/A1/A2 to the shared GUI/CLI/MCP paper catalog; existing preset indices stay unchanged.
- Restores **Match page at 100%** for standard-sized current pages, setting Actual size and Auto orientation without changing the chosen page range.
- Shows the selected preview sheet's **PDF scale** and dimensions. The wording explicitly distinguishes PDF geometry from driver paper/scaling; this does not add strict PrintTicket validation or native/vector Windows submission.
- Includes engine, saved-file automation and GUI regressions, a synthetic offscreen dialog example, required localization catalogs and attribution hashes.

The [feature-by-feature audit](https://github.com/durtyrobbin/pdfcraft/blob/plotter-paper-controls/docs/printing-pr599-audit.md) compares #599, #847 and #1007, distinguishes behavioral overlap from evidence of reuse, and preserves the remaining native/vector, driver-validation and managed-endpoint gaps for separate review. title: Issue #995 & #1077: unlock a restricted document with its permissions password
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Closes #995
Closes #1077

## In short

Some password-protected PDFs opened in PdfCraft but couldn't be edited and the app gave the user **no place to type the password** that would allow it. People who knew the right password were stuck. This PR adds that missing step that is PdfCraft now asks for the password when it's needed and once it's entered the document can be edited, its protection changed or removed and saved.

## Why it happened

A PDF can be protected with **two different passwords** and they do different things:

- **Open password**: needed just to *open and read* the file.
- **Permissions password** (also called "owner" or "editing" password): needed to *edit* the file or to change or remove its protection.

A file can have only one of them or both. A very common setup is **only a permissions password** where anyone can open and read the file but nobody can change it without the password.

PdfCraft only ever asked for a password **when opening a file and only if it couldn't open it without one**. A file with only a permissions password opens fine without a password so PdfCraft never asked. It then saw that the file was restricted and blocked editing which is correct. But:

- the "This document is secured" banner had one button **Security settings** which only *showed* the settings and let you do nothing there.
- **Protect using password** and **Remove security** were greyed out.
- the hint said "open it with the permissions password" but the file never shows a password box so there was nowhere to type it.

So a user who owned the file and knew its password had no way to unlock it.

The same thing happened with files that have **both passwords set to different values**: opening with the open password let you read the file but it stayed locked for editing with no way to enter the second password.

## What the issues reported and how each is solved

**#995 "Cant remove the Security of PDF":** *"I have some secured PDFs that I want to edit but I have no wa…

author: jcl-bit
body:
This picks up craft-print's native Windows printing from storytold/craft-libs#28, so PdfCraft prints on Windows without PowerShell. On PCs where App Control for Business or AppLocker enforce script rules, main lists the printers but every job fails with "Cannot create type. Only core types are supported in this language mode" (#1107).

The native backend started here as this PR, carrying the approach from #599 by @durtyrobbin with @bulgariamitko's merge and print-shop testing as the reference. After #1015 moved the spooler into craft-libs, the code went there instead (craft-libs#28, merged by @skylartaylor, who also moved winprint to storytold's fork and bounded the PDF parsing). What's left for PdfCraft is the pin and the cargo-deny entries, so I've replaced this branch with that. Both #599 authors stay credited as co-authors on the commit.

- `Cargo.toml`: craft-print rev `d991bf6` to `f03ec27` (craft-libs#28).

## What this changes

A layer that is switched off in a document was printed anyway.

`pdfcraft_print::impose` builds the print-ready PDF from a fresh catalog with only `/Type` and `/Pages`, so the document's `/OCProperties` was not carried over. title: Comments panel: show Persian and Arabic comments in reading order (#1079)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #1079

Comment bodies and replies in Persian or Arabic showed their words in the wrong order. The Comments panel drew them with a plain wrapping egui label. egui shapes each Arabic-script run right to left, so the letters join correctly, but it places the runs left to right in logical order, so a sentence comes out with its words reversed.

The app already had `bidi::visual` for one-line file names. Comments wrap, though, and the bidi reordering has to happen per line after the line breaks are chosen. So this adds `bidi::wrap`, which:

- takes each paragraph's direction from its first strong character (like `dir="auto"`), so a Persian comment reads right to left while an English one with an Arabic phrase stays left to right
- breaks lines between words in reading order, and splits a word wider than the panel between characters
- reorders each line with unicode-bidi (UAX #9), so Latin words and numbers inside RTL text read left to right and brackets mirror

A new `widgets::wrapped_text` paints those lines and puts right-to-left lines against the right edge. A collapsed card shows the first line, with the ellipsis on the left for RTL. Text with no RTL characters still uses the same egui label as before. Author names (card header, replies, the author filter, author group headings) go through `bidi::visual_auto`, a one-line version of the same thing. Catalog strings are left alone because the Arabic UI catalog is already in display order.

While doing this I found that Persian digits (۱۴۰۲) and Arabic-Indic digits came out reversed. They are Arabic script, so the shaper lays them out right to left. The shared reordering now passes them in reversed so they show up in the right order. This also fixes them in file names that go through `bidi::visual`. No new dependency: `unicode-bidi` was already a direct dependency of `pdfcraft-ui-egui`.

Testing:

- unit tests on `bidi::wrap` and `visual_auto` with Persian (including ZWNJ words), Arabic, Hebrew, mixed Latin/number …

title: M2: bound the total size of page-label prefixes
author: ymote
body:
## What

Both page-label readers decode each range's prefix into a string of its own:
- render's `Inspector::page_labels`, for its range table;
- Organize's `checked_ranges`, for the ranges it returns.

Ranges may share one prefix object, so a small file can ask for a copy per range. Within the existing 200,000-entry tree limit (`MAX_LABEL_TREE_WORK`), that is about 200 MiB of copies of one 1,024-byte prefix. For example, a file of a few MB whose `/Nums` names one dictionary with a 1 KB `/P` 200,000 times.

This PR adds `MAX_PREFIX_TOTAL_BYTES` (4 MiB) beside `MAX_LABEL_TOTAL_BYTES` in `pdfcraft_cos::page_labels`. Both readers now count every decoded prefix and refuse the tree past it, before any label is made, as they refuse a tree past the other limits:
- inspection keeps the physical page numbers and adds one warning;
- Organize returns its error, and relabelling such a tree changes nothing.

The per-prefix limits (2,050 raw bytes, 1,024 decoded) and the 200,000-entry limit are unchanged.

## Valid documents

- **Inspection:** it already refuses labels over 4 MiB in total. Every range that starts inside the document puts its prefix into at least its first page's label. So for those ranges the new limit refuses nothing the label total wouldn't.
- **Organize:** it has had no aggregate label limit since #845. A document is refused only if its ranges hold more than 4 MiB of prefix text in all, for example 10,000 one-page ranges with prefixes of over 420 bytes each.

## Tests

- `inspect::tests::page_label_limits_bound_the_total_of_decoded_prefixes`: 5,000 ranges sharing one 1,000-byte prefix, on a three-page document, are refused and the labels stay physical. Exactly 4 MiB of prefixes is still read.
- organize `tests::page_label_prefixes_are_bounded_in_total`: the same tree is refused, and `number_pages` on it fails and changes nothing. Exactly 4 MiB is still read.

Both tests fail with the limit lifted.

title: Linux: prefer server DPI over panel physical DPI in vendored winit
author: gyurix
body:
Supersedes #908 — drops the WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1 launcher pin per @echelon.

Why the pin was wrong: it forced 1x on every X11 install, breaking HiDPI (4K laptop, 2x desktop) where Xft.dpi / server DPI is correct, and it overrode the user's desktop scale.

What this does instead (vendor/winit/.../x11/util/randr.rs):
default_dpi_factor() policy, WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR override untouched:
1. Xft.dpi / 96 when set (highest priority, preserves HiDPI),
2. else X-screen calc_dpi_factor(screen_px, screen_mm) — the desktop's configured DPI (e.g. 96 despite dense EDID),
3. else RandR calc_dpi_factor(output_px, output_mm) physical fallback.

Fixes Xorg running a dense panel at 96 DPI (only winit apps looked zoomed) while keeping configured 144/192 DPI screens at 1.5x/2.0x.

Tests: 4 unit tests in randr.rs + guard test apps/pdfcraft/tests/winit_x11_dpi.rs. Verified: 4/4 pass, release build OK, reinstalled locally 0.6.0, Exec clean.

Reinstalled locally with fix to double-check correctness.

title: Windows printing: two-sided binds on the chosen edge; note drivers that ignore Two-sided
author: bulgariamitko
body:
Small follow-up on main's Windows printing (#847 / #1007), as suggested when #912 was closed. It contains two generic changes; nothing in it is specific to a printer brand or model.

### 1. Fix: "Flip on long edge" and "Flip on short edge" were swapped on Windows
`windows_print.ps1` mapped `long-edge` to `[System.Drawing.Printing.Duplex]::Horizontal` and `short-edge` to `Vertical`. Those values are DEVMODE's `DMDUP_HORIZONTAL` (short-edge binding) and `DMDUP_VERTICAL` (long-edge binding), so every two-sided job on Windows bound on the wrong edge.

I checked this with the KONICA MINOLTA Universal PCL driver on a file port, reading the PJL in the output:

| Two-sided | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Off | `DUPLEX = OFF`, `BINDING = LEFT` | same |
| Flip on long edge | `DUPLEX = ON`, **`BINDING = TOP`** | `DUPLEX = ON`, `BINDING = LEFT` |
| Flip on short edge | `DUPLEX = ON`, **`BINDING = LEFT`** | `DUPLEX = ON`, `BINDING = TOP` |

A unit test (`the_windows_print_script_binds_long_edge_on_the_long_edge`) pins the mapping. It runs on every platform.

### 2. Note when the driver doesn't take two-sided settings
Some drivers expose two-sided printing only through their own settings. For those, the Two-sided choice has no effect, and they keep their own default even when Two-sided is **Off**. On the PC I tested, two PostScript drivers printed two-sided with Off selected.

Windows already reports this for every driver: `Win32_Printer.Capabilities` includes `3` (Duplex Printing) only when the driver handles two-sided printing. The printer list already comes from `Win32_Printer`, so:
- `POWERSHELL_PRINTERS` also reads `Capabilities`. Each line gets a tab and `2`/`1`, and `[char]9` is used so the `-Command` script needs no extra quoting. A line without that suffix parses exactly as before.
- `spool::Printer` gains `two_sided: Option<bool>`. It is `None` on CUPS, which maps `sides` itself.
- The `printers` tool includes `two_sided` when it is known.
- The Print dialog shows a …

title: M4: rename colliding form field names when combining (organize.field-name-conflicts)
author: edurbs
body:
Combining files, or inserting pages from one into another, registered incoming form fields under names the destination already used. Fields of one fully-qualified name are one field, so the values silently blurred together — both directions kept a `Text1`, and filling one filled "both".

**organize.field-name-conflicts (P1, M4)** — rename by default, nothing silent:

- **Rename by fully-qualified name** (`parent.T.child`), counting names that hang only off page widgets even when `/AcroForm` never lists them, and also between two incoming fields of one import. A colliding field's own `/T` takes the first free variant (`Text1` → `Text1-1`, `-2`, …), so children keep their place in the tree and repeated pages join the renamed field.
- **Merge on request**: `field_conflicts: "merge"` on `doc_combine` (and the `FieldConflicts` policy on the engine op) keeps the older one-field behaviour.
- **Reported everywhere it happens**:
  - inserting into an open document notes each rename in the repair log, with the caveat that scripts referring to the old names were not rewritten, and the undo step's label counts them (`Insert pages from b.pdf — 1 field renamed`); undo restores the original names;
  - `doc_combine` lists `renamed_fields: [[old, new], …]` in its result when fields were renamed;
  - the Combine tab's Warnings column previews the renames per file before anything is combined (`1 field name collides with earlier files and will be renamed: Text1 → Text1-1`), computed once per list by an in-order pre-scan.

title: Gap 12: render oracle compares ten generated pages with Poppler and MuPDF
author: rp6186030
body:
Part of gap 12 (docs/gaps.md). It doesn't close it: there's no Acrobat side-by-side yet, and no forms, signatures or interop suite.

## What it does
`cargo xtask render-oracle [--out DIR]` builds ten one-page PDFs at run time and renders each with PdfCraft, Poppler (`pdftoppm`) and MuPDF (`mutool draw`) at 144 dpi. Poppler and MuPDF run only as external processes. Each page targets a known renderer weak spot:

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| vector | caps, joins, dashes, 0.1 pt and zero-width hairlines, even-odd |
| text-standard14 | Helvetica, Times, Courier, outline and fill+stroke modes, rotated, spaced and 7 pt text |
| text-type3 | `d0` and `d1` glyphs, character spacing, `Tz`, skew, rotation |
| shading | axial with extend, stitched function, radial, focal shading pattern |
| tiling-pattern | checks, TikZ-style "north east lines" (#794), thin rotated hatch, uncoloured dots |
| transparency | constant alpha, Multiply/Screen/Difference, group opacity, luminosity soft mask |
| images | upscaled RGB, gray, stencil mask, indexed and rotated inline images |
| clipping | nested, even-odd, rotated and text (`7 Tr`) clipping |
| color-spaces | DeviceCMYK, Separation, CalRGB |
| lab | CIE Lab |

**How it compares:** a pixel counts as different only when no pixel within one step of it in the other render is within 32 levels on every channel, checked both ways, so anti-aliasing doesn't count. A page **fails** when its share of differing pixels against the *closer* oracle exceeds its limit. Each limit is the measured share × 1.5 or + 0.5, whichever is larger, rounded up to a half. The measurements come from Ubuntu 24.04's Poppler 24.02 and MuPDF 1.23.10 and are recorded in the source. A blank render must also exceed every limit at least 2.5 times over, so no limit can hide a page that isn't drawn.

Every page, its three renders and a difference image (red on faint grey) are written to `target/render-oracle/`. Each render times out after 60 s. The build and timeout helpers ar…

author: Byxis

**Draft: builds on #1135 (printing keeps a layer that is off). That PR's commit is the first of the three here; the other two are new: `M7: watermark shown on screen only or in print only` and `M7: the print preview draws the layers as they are when printing`. Add/Update Watermark can limit a watermark to the screen or to print: two check boxes, "Show when displaying on screen" and "Show when printing", both on by default, and `show_on_screen` / `show_when_printing` on `doc_watermark`. title: Windows: Explorer PDF actions and default-app prompt
author: lukashold
body:
The existing Explorer Edit action does not cover conversion, reviewed combination or email-draft preparation. This adds localized classic context-menu actions to convert supported images/plain text, review and combine them with PDFs, and prepare an unsent email draft with PDF attachments. After an existing PDF opens successfully, PdfCraft can also offer the supported Windows Default Apps settings.

Convert opens new unsaved PDFs. Combine reuses the sortable review workspace and preserves subsequent Explorer requests. Email first reviews the attachments and destination, prepares a unique durable bundle containing an unsent `.eml` plus separate PDFs, then opens the registered mail handler. A bounded background worker handles email preparation and cancellation; it never sends mail or overwrites sources. The root-confined `doc_email_draft` automation tool prepares the same bundle without launching a client.

The Default Apps offer appears at most once per desktop session after a successful existing-PDF open. “Do not ask again” persists through Yes, Later, Close and Escape, and Preferences can re-enable it. Failed/password-pending opens, newly converted PDFs and automation sessions do not prompt. Association detection is read-only and honors per-user precedence; PdfCraft never writes protected UserChoice values. The prompt waits until other editing or email-review dialogs close.

The bounded typed single-instance protocol preserves action boundaries and defers incoming Explorer requests while an editing dialog or background PDF open is active. The queue is limited to 100 paths and 1 MiB of path text; sources are limited to 64 MiB each, with a 128 MiB aggregate source-buffer budget and a separate 128 MiB mail-attachment limit. Menu resources reuse all 22 current interface languages with English fallback. MSI registration covers 38 verbs across 13 supported extensions and is removed on uninstall.
