title: fix(cos): a nonpositive crypt-filter /Length no longer overflows (#1816)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1816. A V4 encryption dictionary whose standard crypt filter has a zero or negative `/Length` no longer overflows while the document is opened.

**Cause.** `encrypt_dict` reads the `StdCF` `/Length` as bytes when it's at most 32 and multiplies it by 8. That arm admitted every negative `i64`, so a large negative value overflowed: a panic with overflow checks, a wrapped key length without them.

**Fix.** A length that isn't positive means nothing, so it's read as if absent: the existing V4 default of 128 bits. The check runs before any arithmetic. Positive values behave exactly as before.

This also fixes small negatives such as `-1`. They didn't overflow, but became a negative bit length, which the crypt crate clamped to a 40-bit key. So an AES-128 document with such a value failed to open even with the right (empty) password.

I chose to read the value as absent rather than refuse the file, as the issue suggests, because the key length for V4 is otherwise fully determined. That matches how this function already treats a stale `/Length` on the dictionary itself.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos -j 2`: all passed

**Test.** `a_nonpositive_crypt_filter_length_reads_as_the_default_key_length` (in `tests/encryption.rs`) works through document opening:

1. It protects the fixture with AES-128 and an empty user password.
2. It rewrites `StdCF /Length` in an incremental update to each of: `i64::MIN`, the values on either side of `i64::MIN / 8` (the multiplication boundary), `-1`, `0`, `16` (bytes) and `128` (bits).
3. It reopens the file and requires the decrypted page content.

The test fails in two ways when parts of the fix are reverted:

- Without the fix, it panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` at `security.rs:45`.
- With only an overflow guard (negatives above `i64::MIN / 8` still admitted), the document fai…

title: fix(audit): find rectangle covers closed with h or painted with b/b* (#1817)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1817. The redaction audit now finds an opaque rectangular cover over extractable text in two cases where it reported nothing before:

- an `re` rectangle followed by a redundant `h`;
- a rectangle (either `re` or `m`/`l`) painted with `b` or `b*`.

**Cause.** Two gaps in `crates/audit/src/cover.rs`:

1. The `h` handler turned an `re` rectangle, whose subpath is already closed, into `Path::Other`.
2. The fill branch listed `f`, `F`, `f*`, `B` and `B*`, but not the close-fill-stroke operators `b` and `b*`.

**Fix.**

- Under `h`, a rectangle stays a rectangle: `re` closes its own subpath (ISO 32000-2 §8.5.2.2), so closing it again changes nothing.
- `b` and `b*` join the fill branch. They close the path before filling it, and filling closes the path anyway, so the shape that gets filled is the same.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-audit -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit -j 2`: 13 passed

**Tests.**

- `rectangle_drawn_as_a_path_covers_text_like_re` gains five covers. Each must give the same finding, rectangle and covered text as the `re f` control:
  - `re h f`
  - `re b`
  - `re h b*`
  - `m`/`l` with `b`
  - `m`/`l` + `h` with `b*`
- `non_rectangular_path_is_not_a_cover` gains a triangle painted with `b` and a trapezoid painted with `b*`. Both still give no finding, so `b`/`b*` don't make every shape a cover.

I checked each half of the fix separately:

- With the `h` change reverted, the first test fails (`left: 0` findings).
- With `b`/`b*` removed from the fill branch, it fails as well.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing outside tests
- [x] No `unsafe`

- [x] No assets. Behaviour from ISO 32000-2 §8.5.2–8.5.3 (path construction and painting operators).

title: fix(sign): an unreadable extendedKeyUsage allows no purpose (#1807)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1807. A signer certificate whose extendedKeyUsage (EKU) is malformed no longer reads as unrestricted. Before, its signature could be Valid.

**Cause.** `Extensions::read` set `extended_key_usage` only when the EKU parsed, so a malformed one stayed `None`. `signing_problem` reads `None` as "no EKU, no restriction". EKU is also on `PROCESSED_EXTENSIONS`, so a malformed *critical* EKU passed the unknown-critical check as well. Two more encodings were accepted leniently:

- a value that wasn't a SEQUENCE, such as a SET, whose children were read anyway;
- a SEQUENCE with a non-OID member, which was dropped while the readable members were kept.

**Fix.** EKU now fails closed, the way this file already handles keyUsage ("present restricts the key even when it doesn't parse") and basicConstraints:

- A present EKU always sets `extended_key_usage = Some(..)`.
- It must be a SEQUENCE whose members are all OIDs (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.12). Anything else yields an empty purpose set, so `signing_problem` reports "not issued for signing documents" and the verdict is not Valid.
- Well-formed EKUs read exactly as before.

`revocation.rs`, which requires the OCSP-signing purpose on a delegated responder, already refused a `None` EKU, and refuses an empty set the same way. Its behaviour doesn't change.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2`: all passed

**Test.** `an_unreadable_extended_key_usage_allows_no_purpose` (in `tests/chain.rs`) issues root-signed signer certificates with digitalSignature and one of four malformed EKUs:

1. truncated DER, critical;
2. truncated DER, non-critical;
3. a SET containing anyExtendedKeyUsage;
4. a SEQUENCE of an INTEGER and anyExtendedKeyUsage.

Each must parse to an empty purpose set and get an `Unknown` verdict with the "not issued for signing documents" detail. As a control, the same anyExtendedKeyUsa…

title: ui: Save as in the toolbar, and the find field docked beside the command search
author: bottelliemanuele-maker

title: Report an error when the OCR worker thread cannot start (#1819)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1819.

Both OCR entry points (Recognize text on the open document, and Recognize text in files) dropped the `Builder::spawn` error with `.ok()` and then registered the run as active. With no worker to publish a result, the progress stayed up forever, every later attempt was refused with "Text recognition is already running", and Cancel only set a flag nobody read.

Now both paths go through a small `spawn_ocr_worker` helper. If the thread cannot start, the OS error is shown as a toast (`notify_error`, like other OS messages) and the run is **not** registered, so the user can simply try again. This follows the issue's first suggested remedy ("register active work only after successful spawn"); the Optimize dialog handles the same failure with the same "No worker" check.

`PdfCraftApp::fail_spawn` is a test-only switch (like `run_inline`) that makes the helper fail as it would under resource pressure.

## Tests
`recognition_that_cannot_start_a_thread_reports_an_error_and_can_retry` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ocr.rs` covers both paths: after a failed start, `ocr_run` / `ocr_batch` stay empty, the error is shown, and a second attempt is not refused as "already running". It does not need the OCR models, because the worker never runs. Before this change the run stays registered and the retry is refused.

title: Report an image mask that can't be decoded instead of exporting it opaque (#1814)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1814.

`soft_mask` and `stencil_mask` returned `Option`, so a mask that was present but couldn't be decoded (a CCITT/JBIG2/JPX mask, an unsupported bit depth, truncated data) looked the same as no mask at all. A JPEG with such a mask then went out through the "no transparency" fast path as an opaque JPEG, and export reported success.

Both now return `Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, String>`: `Ok(None)` when the image has no mask, an error when it has one that can't be decoded. `image()` propagates the error, so `extract_images` lists the image under `skipped` with the reason (as it already does for JPEG 2000, JBIG2 and CCITT images themselves), and `image_file` returns the error. Supported masks and images without a mask export as before.

One small behaviour change: an image whose `/SMask` can't be decoded no longer falls back to its `/Mask`; it is reported, since the soft mask takes precedence and dropping it would still lose the intended transparency.

Test: `undecodable_masks_are_an_error_not_silently_dropped` builds a JPEG with a CCITT stencil `/Mask` and checks the image is skipped, not exported. Without the fix it is exported as an opaque JPEG. The existing `damaged_masks_and_sizes_never_panic` still covers malformed masks without panicking.

title: Optimize: give a resized image its own soft mask instead of overwriting a shared one (#1812)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1812.

When Optimize/Reduce downsampled an image with a soft mask, it wrote the resampled mask back over the original `/SMask` object. If another image shared that mask (for example one drawn small enough to be left alone), its mask was resized too, so it lost alpha-edge detail or no longer matched its own dimensions.

The resampled mask is now added as a new object and only the resized image's `/SMask` points to it. The shared original stays as it was for every other image. If nothing else uses the original, the full save drops it because it is no longer reachable, so the size savings don't change.

Tests:
- New `a_soft_mask_shared_with_an_image_that_is_not_resized_stays_as_it_was`: two images share one 800 px mask; one is drawn at 800 ppi and gets downsampled, the other at 100 ppi and does not. The resized image gets its own 150 px mask, and the other keeps the original mask unchanged (same reference, width and bytes). Without the fix this fails, because the original mask is overwritten.
- `images_are_measured_where_drawn_and_downsampled` now follows the image's `/SMask` reference to find the resized mask, since the mask is no longer resized in place.

title: Publish action wizard outputs without replacing existing files (#1805)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1805.

`action_run` picked an output name with `exists()` and then wrote it with `write_atomic`, whose rename replaces whatever is at the target. If another process (a second CLI/MCP job, or any other writer) created that name between the check and the rename, the earlier file was silently replaced and both jobs reported success. `exists()` also follows links, so a dangling link at the target name looked free and was replaced.

**Fix**

`action_run` now publishes each output through `batch::publish`, the helper that batch processing already uses (now `pub(crate)`). It writes a temp file in the output folder and moves it into place with `persist_noclobber`. If the name is taken at that moment, it tries `<stem> (2).pdf`, `<stem> (3).pdf` and so on. An existing entry is never replaced. The naming is the same as before (`report.pdf`, then `report (2).pdf`, ...), so the existing `action_run_keeps_outputs_with_duplicate_input_basenames` test still passes unchanged. The `unused` import in `a11y.rs` is gone because `action_run` no longer calls it.

Only the Action Wizard output path changes. The OCR folder output in the same file is tracked separately in #1795.

**Tests**

`action_run_never_replaces_an_entry_that_exists_check_misses` (Unix) puts a dangling symlink at `results/report.pdf`, so the name is taken but `exists()` returns false. Without the fix the run writes over the link and returns `results/report.pdf`. With the fix the output is `report (2).pdf` and the link is still there.

title: M4: retry an autosave snapshot whose recovery write failed (#1803)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1803.

`Session::autosave_snapshots` marks a document's generation as snapshotted before the UI writes it to the recovery store. When `store.write` failed, `autosave_now` only logged the error, so later ticks skipped that generation even after storage came back. A crash before the next edit lost the work.

Changes:
- `RecoverySnapshot` now carries the `generation` it captured.
- New `Session::autosave_failed(doc, generation)`: if that generation is still the last one handed out, it is offered again on the next `autosave_snapshots` call. If the document was edited and snapshotted since, it does nothing, so an old failure never hides or repeats a newer snapshot.
- `autosave_now` (ui-egui) calls it when `store.write` fails. This is the only caller of `autosave_snapshots`.

A successful write still marks the generation as stored, so unchanged documents are not written again.

Test: `autosave_failed_offers_the_same_generation_again` (engine) checks that a failed snapshot comes back once without a new edit, is not repeated after that, and that a stale failure report after a newer edit leaves exactly one pending snapshot.

title: ocr: discard a recognition result if the document changed while it ran (#1801)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1801.

`Recognize text` captures the document's pages when it starts and runs in the background, but `OcrRun` kept only the document id. When the run finished, `poll_ocr` applied the words to whatever the document had become in the meantime. After a reorder, crop, redaction, undo or automatic reload, the invisible text could land on the wrong pages or bring back text that had been removed.

- `OcrRun` now also stores the document's `edit_generation()` from when the pages were captured.
- `poll_ocr` compares it with the current generation before `apply_ocr`. If it changed, the result is thrown away and the user sees "The document changed while text was being recognized, so the result was discarded. Run Recognize text again." This goes through `notify_tr`, like the other "the document changed while you were choosing a file/folder" messages in `files.rs` and `lib.rs`.
- Every edit, undo, redo and reload already increments the generation, so one check covers all of the conditions in the issue.
- An unchanged document is handled as before: the words are added as one undoable "Recognize text" step.

Two paths are unchanged on purpose:
- The headless `recognize_text` (CLI and agents) runs synchronously, so nothing can change the document while it runs.
- Recognizing multiple files writes new copies from bytes and never touches an open document.

## How you verified it

Two unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/ocr_ui.rs` run a finished recognition result through `poll_ocr`:
- `result_is_applied_when_the_document_is_unchanged`: the words are added and the undo label is "Recognize text".
- `result_is_refused_when_the_document_changed_meanwhile`: an Add text edit is made after the pages were captured. Nothing more is added (the undo label is still the Add text step), and the toast explains why.

Without the fix, the second test fails because the stale words are applied and the undo label becomes "Recognize text". I could not run the tests or clippy on…

title: Reject an Indexed colour space with an Indexed base before following it (#1799)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1799.

`space()` in `crates/create/src/extract.rs` resolved an Indexed colour space's base by calling itself first, and only then checked whether that base was Indexed too. When the base pointed back at itself, or two Indexed arrays pointed at each other, the check was never reached and image export recursed until the stack overflowed.

The check now runs before the recursive call: if the resolved base is an `Indexed`/`I` array, the image is skipped with the same "nested indexed colour spaces aren't valid" message as before. Indexed is the only branch of `space()` that recurses, so after this check the recursion is at most one level deep. Self-cycles, two-object cycles and deep chains all stop at the first Indexed-in-Indexed. Valid Indexed images are unchanged, and `indexed_and_one_bit_images_decode` still covers them.

Test: `indexed_colour_spaces_with_an_indexed_base_are_skipped_not_followed` gives an image a colour space whose base is a self-referencing Indexed array. The test checks that `extract_images` skips the image with that error. Without the fix the test overflows the stack.

title: Keep existing files when recognizing text in multiple files (#1795)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1795.

`ocr_recognize_files` wrote each result to `folder/<input name>` with `write_atomic`, which replaces whatever is there. Two inputs called `report.pdf` from different folders ended up as one file, and an output folder that already held a file of that name (or was an input's own folder) lost it.

It now publishes through `batch::publish`, the no-clobber writer that `doc_batch` already uses: the name is taken atomically, and a name in use gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on. Each entry in `files` reports the name actually written, so two entries never point at the same file. `publish` is now `pub(crate)`; nothing else in it changes.

The tool description now says that a taken name gets a number and existing files are never replaced, like the `doc_batch` description.

Test: `ocr_recognize_files_keeps_existing_and_same_named_outputs` recognizes `one/report.pdf` and `two/report.pdf` into `one/`, where `report (2).pdf` already exists. It checks that the two outputs are different, that the first is `report (3).pdf`, and that the source and the existing file keep their bytes. On main the first output overwrites `one/report.pdf` and the test fails. Like `ocr_recognize_files_writes_searchable_copies`, it skips when the OCR models are not installed.

title: Check the remembered path of a pathless doc_save against the root (#1791)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1791.

`doc_save` with a `path` sends it through `resolve(path, true)`, so with `--root` the save is refused when the target lands outside the root. Without a `path`, it took the document's remembered `doc.path` as is and passed it straight to `write_atomic`. If a folder on that path had become a link to somewhere outside the root since the document was opened, a pathless save wrote outside the root.

**Fix**

- With no `path`, the remembered path now goes through the same `resolve(path, true)` as an explicit one. Every other tool that writes a file (`write_output`, `doc_reduce`, image export, convert) already resolves its target, so this was the only write that skipped the check.
- A pathless save still counts as a save to the same file. It stays incremental unless `full` is set, as before, even when `resolve` returns the canonical spelling of the path.
- Without `--root`, `resolve` returns the path unchanged, so nothing changes there.

**Test**

`a_save_without_a_path_stays_inside_the_root` opens two documents under a root. The first remembers a path inside the root and still saves there without a `path`. The second remembers a path outside the root: the pathless save is now refused with "outside the allowed directory" and no file is written there. Before the fix that save wrote the outside file, so the test fails. The test uses a remembered path outside the root rather than a swapped-in directory link, because directory links need extra privileges on Windows. Both cases go through the same branch.

The issue also mentions descriptor-relative confinement against a directory that is changed during the save. That is a larger change to how every tool writes, so this PR does not do it. This fix brings the pathless save up to the same check that explicit paths already get.

title: Do not build a trust chain through an intermediate with unrecognized critical extensions (#1789)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1789.

## What was wrong

`build_chain_noted` accepted an issuer when it could issue, its path length allowed it and it was valid at the signing time, but it never looked at `unknown_critical`. That list was only checked for the signer itself (`signing_problem`). So a trusted root -> intermediate -> signer chain came out Valid even when the intermediate carried a critical extension PdfCraft does not process, such as critical `nameConstraints` (2.5.29.30), and the constraint it imposes was silently ignored.

## The fix

- In `build_chain_noted`, a candidate issuer that is not self-signed and has unrecognized critical extensions is refused, next to the existing may-issue / path-length / validity refusals and in the same style: a whole sentence with the two certificates' names, shown as a detail when the chain does not reach a trusted certificate. Self-signed certificates (trust anchors) are left to trust policy, as the issue recommends; the chain already stops at them.
- The new sentence is added to `sign::pdf::WORDINGS` and translated in `es.tsv` and `lt.tsv`, the two catalogs that carry the sibling chain-refusal sentences (`spanish_covers_what_the_engine_says` requires the Spanish one).
- `build_chain`'s doc comment, `docs/pdf-spec-parity.md` (which listed "issuer critical extensions missing") and the "Validate all signatures" parity note now say what is checked. Name constraints are still not enforced; a constrained intermediate is now refused instead of trusted.

## Tests

`crates/sign/tests/chain.rs::an_intermediate_with_an_unrecognized_critical_extension_does_not_vouch` builds root -> intermediate -> leaf chains where the intermediate has (a) an unknown critical extension and (b) a critical `nameConstraints` extension: the chain stops at the leaf and the reason names the critical extensions. The same unknown extension marked non-critical still builds the full chain. Without the change in `x509.rs` the first two cases build the full chain to the root and t…

title: Keep tiling pattern cells at least one pixel wide (#1770)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1770.

A tiling pattern whose `/BBox` is far wider than its step (`/BBox [0 0 100000 10] /XStep 10`) caps the cell scale at `MAX_PIXMAP_SIZE / bbox.width()` = 0.03, so `x_step` is 0.3 and `pix_width` rounds to 0. vello_common then indexes the empty 0 x N cell pixmap and panics (`index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 4294967295`), and the page fails to render.

**Fix** (`vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`): the cell pixmap's width and height are kept at least 1 pixel. This is the other end of the bound the existing patch (3) (`tiling_cell_scale`, at most 3000 px a side) already puts on the same pixmap, so `vendor/README.md` lists it under patch (3) with its test.

**Test:** `raster::tests::tiling_cell_narrower_than_a_pixel_does_not_crash`, next to `tiling_cells_stay_small_whatever_the_step`, renders the reporter's case (same page as that test, with `/BBox [0 0 100000 10] /XStep 10 /YStep 10`). It checks that the page renders without an error and that the content drawn after the pattern still appears. Without the fix the render panics and `page.error` is set.

title: Refuse a legacy encryption key length above 128 bits instead of panicking (#1769)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1769.

## Problem
An encryption dictionary `/Filter /Standard /V 2 /R 3 /Length 256` made hayro-syntax panic in Algorithm 2 (`decryption_key_rev1234`): the revision 2–4 file key is cut from a 16-byte MD5 hash with `hash[..byte_length]`, and `/Length 256` asks for 32 bytes. The open safety net caught it and reported "the parser crashed".

## Fix
`crypto::get` already refuses a zero key length with `InvalidEncryption`. It now does the same when the revision is 2–4 and `/Length` asks for more than 16 bytes, before any key is derived. Revisions 5–6 (AES-256, 32-byte key) are unchanged. `/Length` values up to 128 bits behave exactly as before. `pdfcraft-render` already turns any non-password `DecryptionError` into `OpenError::Unsupported("encryption not supported: InvalidEncryption")` (`inspect.rs`), so the file is refused with an open error instead of crashing.

The check is marked `PdfCraft patch:` in the source and described in `vendor/README.md`, like the other vendored patches.

## Test
`crypto::pdfcraft_password_tests::legacy_key_length_above_128_bits_is_refused_not_a_panic` (hayro-syntax, `std` feature) builds the issue's `/V 2 /R 3` dictionary: `/Length 128` stays `PasswordProtected` (the control), `/Length 256` returns `InvalidEncryption`. Without the fix, the `/Length 256` case panics with `range end index 32 out of range for slice of length 16`.

title: Render: skip the decode size hint when an image's drawn size is not finite, so a huge cm value no longer panics the JPEG 2000 decoder (#1761)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1761.

`draw_image` (`vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`) took the decode size hint from the image's drawn lengths with `.ceil() as u32`. A JPEG 2000 image drawn with `100 0 0 9223372036854775807 0 0 cm` makes one of those lengths NaN, `NaN as u32` is 0, and hayro-jpeg2000 divides the image size by that 0 (`codestream.rs:150`). The page safety net caught the panic, but the whole page failed to render.

A new `PdfCraft patch:` helper, `decode_target_size`, gives the hint only when both lengths are finite and positive. Otherwise it gives `None`, and the image decodes at full size as it does without a hint. Ordinary images get the same hint as before. Both decode paths, stencil and raster, use the helper.

This PR does not add a zero check inside hayro-jpeg2000. That is a crates.io dependency, not a vendored one, so the fix stays at the one place in our tree that made the 0.

`vendor/README.md` lists this as hayro patch (16) with its tests. The README currently has the hayro row twice, so both copies get the entry.

## How you verified it

No local Rust toolchain on this machine, so CI is the check.

- `raster::tests::jpx_image_drawn_with_an_out_of_range_cm_does_not_stop_the_page` is an end-to-end test. It uses the existing synthetic 1x1 JPX fixture (`jpx_midpoint_pdf`, now with a variant that takes the `cm` operands), draws the image with the matrix from the issue, and checks that the page renders without an error and that the red square after the image still draws. Without the fix, the decoder gets a 0 hint and the page reports `renderer crashed`.
- `decode_target_tests` in the hayro crate (`cargo test -p hayro`) checks the helper directly. NaN, infinite and zero lengths give `None`, and finite lengths round up as before.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests
- [x] No `unsafe`
- [x] The crash has a small synthetic regression test

## Provenance

- [x] No assets; the JPX test fixture is the existing contributor-…

title: audit: harden finding classes with golden tests and docs
author: ejbarraza
body:
Follow-up hardening on #110: tests + docs only, zero behavior change.

What this adds to `crates/audit`:

- **Golden tests pinning the full `AuditFinding` struct** for both finding classes (`covered-text`, `unapplied-mark`) — page, kind, exact rect, and covered text, not just "a finding exists".
- **`FindingKind::id()` stability contract** — a test locking the `"covered-text"` / `"unapplied-mark"` strings, plus docs stating the no-rename rule (these IDs are the crate's public vocabulary for CLI output and any future machine-readable format).
- **Depth-limit boundary tests** in the fail-closed style: 32 nested form XObjects audit clean, 33 fail with `TooDeep` instead of reporting the page clean with a possible cover unseen.
- **Doc fixes**: the crate docs still said only `re` rectangles count as covers — updated for the `m`/`l` axis-aligned rectangles from #1510. Also documented `AuditFinding.rect` normalization and `covered_text` joining.

Verification: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit` 18/18 pass, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-audit --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

title: Use PingFang from the reserved font directory on macOS 26 (#1716)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1716.

On macOS 26 the Simplified Chinese interface was drawn with Hiragino Sans GB W3 instead of PingFang. `han_candidates()` only looked for `/System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc`, and macOS 26 no longer has that file: PingFang now lives at `/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc`, so the first file found was `Hiragino Sans GB.ttc`.

**Fix (macOS only).** The macOS list moves into `macos_han_candidates()`, which adds `PingFangUI.ttc` as a candidate:

- Simplified Chinese: right after `PingFang.ttc`, ahead of Hiragino Sans GB. A system that still has `PingFang.ttc` keeps using it.
- Traditional Chinese: after the two STHeiti files. Face 0 of `PingFangUI.ttc` is the SC UI face (as the issue notes), so Traditional keeps its current STHeiti face, and PingFang is used only when STHeiti is missing.

The file is about 61 MiB, under the existing `MAX_HAN_BYTES` cap (96 MiB), and face 0 has both probe characters (欢 and 說), so `read()` takes it unchanged. Windows and Linux lists are unchanged, and the order of the other macOS files is unchanged.

**Tests.** Two unit tests on `macos_han_candidates()` (it is a plain function, so they run on every platform): Simplified puts `PingFangUI.ttc` second, after `PingFang.ttc` and before Hiragino Sans GB; Traditional has it after STHeiti. I could not run them on macOS 26 myself.

title: fix(ui): validated signature display, snapshot tab reuse
author: chiranjeevi-max
body:
## What this changes

This contribution by @chiranjeevi-max improves the verification UI and signed-version workflow for signed PDFs, including password-protected files.

- Show verification badges over signed widgets in the page viewer, alongside the existing banner and signature panel. Trusting a signer revalidates signatures and refreshes the renderer and UI caches so the displayed verification state stays current.
- Reuse signed-version and revision snapshot tabs instead of opening duplicates. Tabs include the source title and revision suffix, and a notice bar identifies the revision and provides a Close button.
- Preserve the document's original signature artwork and appearance bytes. Verification badges are viewer UI; they do not rewrite PDF content or enter exported page images, exported text, vector printing, Print as Image, or saved documents.

The scope was narrowed after regression tests demonstrated that generic appearance identification could overwrite decoration or signer details. The generic appearance rewriter and its `verdict_shown` API field have been removed. See the [scope explanation and follow-up decision](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/1895#issuecomment-6204415008).

**Issue #79 remains open.** Baked-in “Not Verified” text is unchanged, even after trust is established. Replacing existing signature artwork is deferred until a safe, positively recognized format is available.

title: PKCS#11 tokens and smart cards (sign.pkcs11 partial)
author: pechnikov2026-star
body:
Partial implementation of `sign.pkcs11`: USB tokens and smart cards sign through user-chosen PKCS #11 modules on the desktop OSes. Refs #1578, #238, #85, #318, #195 (none closed: no run against SoftHSM or a real token yet).

## What works

- **Engine** (`crates/sign/src/pkcs11.rs`, via `cryptoki` 0.12.1): module loading by explicit path only (a DLL executes code — nothing is searched for or auto-loaded), slot/token listing (label, serial, manufacturer, PIN need, pinpad), cert+key pairing by `CKA_ID`, RFC 7512 references (`pkcs11:token=…;object=…;id=…;type=cert`; queries refused — a PIN never belongs in a reference), RSA `CKM_RSA_PKCS` over a locally built `DigestInfo`, ECDSA P-256/P-384 `CKM_ECDSA` over the digest (raw `r ‖ s` to DER via the existing converter). Strict tokens hide private keys until login, so listing logs in with a non-interactive PIN it was already given — never a prompt, never the pinpad.
- **PIN**: asked per signature (env var, UI dialog, reader pinpad) as a zeroized `SecretString`, never stored or persisted. Wrong PIN reports itself; a `user_pin_final_try` flag appends a last-try warning (tokens report flags, not counts).
- **CLI/MCP**: `sign_token_ids {module}`, and `sign_document` takes `pkcs11:` with `module` + `pin_env` (module resolved under `--root`; `module`/`pin_env` with any other ID are refused, not ignored).
- **Desktop UI**: Preferences ▸ Signatures module list (Browse/Remove, persisted, per-OS driver name hints), token identities in the Sign dialog with a `Token PIN` field, unusable certificates greyed with the reason (#179 pattern).
- **Tests**: unit (URI, DigestInfo, error mapping, broken modules), a SoftHSM round-trip test that provisions RSA-2048 + P-256 pairs on a scratch token and CMS-validates both — skipped with a message without `PDFCRAFT_PKCS11_TEST_MODULE` (craft-fonts pattern). New tool covered by `hostile_args` (no panics, no `--root` escape). New UI strings in all 17 full-coverage catalogs; `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes up…

title: fix(audit): an applied redaction at the end of a line is not a faux redaction
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`doc_audit_redactions` (and `pdfcraft-cli audit`) reported a correctly applied redaction as a faux one when the redacted text ended its line. The check meant to prove a redaction worked raised a false alarm on the file an agent was about to send.

Repro: one A4 page (842 pt high) with `Mail the team: someone@example.com` (Helvetica 11), `redact_mark {pattern: "email"}`, `redact_apply`, `doc_audit_redactions`. The address is gone from the text layer (PyMuPDF and `text_extract` agree), yet the audit says (the tests below use the same line on a US Letter page, 792 pt high):

```json
{"count":1,"findings":[{"covered_text":"Mail the team:","kind":"covered-text","page":1,"rect":[144.138,739.8,265.952,750.8]}]}
```

Why: Apply Redactions rewrites the line as `[(Mail the team:) -11354] TJ`. The adjustment moves past where the address was, and the box `text_lines` gives the line spans it (`[72, 90.1, 267.43, 102.75]` while the last glyph ends at x 141.1). `covers` compared the redaction box with that box: about 54% of it lies under the box, over the 40% threshold. In the middle of a line the same gap is usually under 40% of the line, so it went unnoticed there; a wide gap between short words fails the same way.

The fix measures what a cover hides on the words a line draws, and keeps the old measure where a word is really under the cover:

- `pdfcraft_edit::TextLine` gets `ink`: the boxes of its words in user space, from each word's first glyph to the end of its last, without the spaces and `TJ` adjustments around them (kerning keeps a word together; a jump of more than 0.2 em ends it). It is filled where the line's box is built, and merged where runs and lines are merged. A word's box is the union of its glyphs, so it stays whole when they run backwards (negative font size or `Tz`).
- `pdfcraft_audit::covers` flags a line when the cover hides 40% of the area of its words, or, as before, 40% of its box together with a positive-area intersection with the…

title: fix(a11y): bookmarks from structure keep the words of glyph-by-glyph headings
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`bookmark_from_structure` (Bookmark options ▸ New bookmarks from structure) spelled headings letter by letter when the producer draws each glyph with its own `Td`, as Chromium's `page.pdf()` does (`17.55 0 Td <006F> Tj 14.33 0 Td <0075> Tj …`). On a tagged PDF printed by Chromium, bookmarks came out as `1 C h a p t e r 1 ti t l e` and `O p e r a ti o n s R u n b o o k ( s y n t h e ti c )`: a space between every glyph, and the real spaces between words lost. `text_extract` reads the same lines correctly.

Cause: `mcid_texts` (`crates/a11y/src/headings.rs`), which gathers the text each MCID shows, pushed a space on every `Td`, `TD`, `T*` and `Tm`, and on `TJ` adjustments under -200, whatever the geometry.

It now follows the text matrix the way a reader places glyphs (text matrix and line matrix, CTM with `q`/`Q`/`cm`, `Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz`, `TL`, glyph widths from `Metrics`) and decides word breaks from where the glyphs are: a glyph starts a new word when it is on another line (more than half an em up or down), more than 0.2 em after the end of the previous glyph of the same MCID, or back over more than an em. Kerning, small `TJ` adjustments and per-glyph `Td`/`Tm` placement no longer split words (an adjustment that leaves more than 0.2 em still does, as -200 did); a drawn space glyph is kept as before. Distances are measured in text space through the inverse of the text rendering matrix, so a font set to size 1 and scaled by `Tm` (common in other producers) works the same. The horizontal em is the absolute value of the font size times `Tz`; the vertical threshold uses only the absolute font size, and "after" follows the way glyphs advance in text space, which is backwards when the size or `Tz` is negative.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-a11y --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-a11y`: 33 …

title: fix(audit): report faux-redaction rectangles in top-left page points
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`doc_audit_redactions` and `pdfcraft-cli audit` returned each finding's `rect` in PDF user space (origin at the bottom-left of the media box), while `comment_list`, `doc_info`, `text_lines` and the redaction tools give points from the top-left of the page as displayed. Both surfaces now report the same rectangle, in the space every other tool uses:

- `doc_audit_redactions` converts each finding with `view_rect`, the helper `doc_info` uses since #129, on top of the conversion `comment_list` uses (after `/Rotate`, rounded to 0.01 pt). Its tool description says so.
- `pdfcraft-cli audit` converts with the same helper, now `pub` in `pdfcraft-automation` so the two cannot drift. It reads the page geometry (`inspect`) only when there is a finding to place: a clean file never touches the renderer.

title: fix(text): read an embedded Identity-H font without a usable ToUnicode through its cmap (#1699)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1699.

A Type 0 font whose descendant is an embedded TrueType (`CIDFontType2`) extracted no text when it had no usable `/ToUnicode`: either no `/ToUnicode` at all, or `/ToUnicode /Identity-H` (a name, not a CMap stream). The page rendered, but search, copy and text export found nothing.

**Cause.** `Type0Font::char_code_to_unicode` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/cid.rs`) only consulted `self.to_unicode`. With no `/ToUnicode` that is `None`. With `/ToUnicode /Identity-H`, `read_to_unicode` loads the predefined Identity-H CMap, which has only CID ranges and no bf entries, so every lookup returned `None` too.

**Fix.** When the ToUnicode lookup gives nothing, `Type0Font::unicode_from_embedded_glyph` takes the glyph the code draws (code → CID → `/CIDToGIDMap`, the same `map_code` the renderer uses) and looks it up in the embedded font's own `cmap` (Unicode → glyph, reversed once per font and cached in a `OnceLock`). If several code points share a glyph (space and no-break space), the lowest one wins. This handles both shapes in the issue, and it does not depend on the codes being UTF-16, so it also works when the producer numbers CIDs as glyph indices.

Scope:
- Only embedded TrueType-based descendants (`FontType::OpenType`, not `fallback`). A non-embedded substitute's `cmap` says nothing about the PDF's codes, so substitutes are unchanged (the PDFium `bug_921.pdf` case mentioned as related in the issue needs a different fix).
- A ToUnicode CMap that does map the code still wins. A code it leaves out now also falls back to the font's `cmap`, the same order the simple TrueType path uses since #1477 (`TrueTypeFont::char_code_to_unicode`: ToUnicode first, then the font's own data).
- Rendering is unchanged; only `char_code_to_unicode` is touched.

Docs: the fallback chain in the `Glyph::as_unicode` doc comment lists the new step, and `vendor/README.md` records it as hayro-interpret patch (28) with its test.

**Test.** `text::tests::embedded_identity_h_font_withou…

title: Do not join text from different clipping paths into one paragraph (#1680)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1680.

Table cells that clip their own content (`q … path W* n … Q`, as Hancom/HWP exports do) were grouped into one paragraph when two cells sat side by side on one baseline. Editing that paragraph rewrote everything at the first cell's `BT`, inside the first cell's clip, so the second cell's text was clipped away.

**Fix.** Edit text now tracks the clipping path, as the issue suggests:

- `interpret` collects the user-space bounding box of each path (`m`, `l`, `re`, `c`, `v`, `y`, mapped through the CTM). At the path-painting operator after `W`/`W*` (`n`, `S`, `f`, `B`, …) it intersects that box with the current clip in `Ts`. `q`/`Q` save and restore it with the rest of the graphics state.
- Each `TextLine` stores the clip it was shown in.
- Lines, rows and blocks with different clips are never joined: `text_lines` (both join checks and `compatible_word`) and `same_plane` in `text_regions.rs`, which `group_layout` uses for both row and block joins. This covers all the rewrite paths the issue lists: the mixed-style `rewrite_styled_block`, the single-style `rewrite_block` (cells stacked vertically) and `replace_line` (runs in adjacent clips), because none of them can get a paragraph or line that spans two clips any more.

Text under the same clip, or under no clip, groups as before.

The `PCEdHelvetica` substitution that the issue mentions under "Related" is a separate problem and is not changed here.

**Test.** `text_in_different_clips_is_not_one_block` uses the issue's synthetic two-cell page (12 pt blue `Note1`, 22 pt black `Heading FAQ`). It checks that the page reads as two paragraphs, and that after `replace_block` on the heading, the saved and reopened page reads `Note1` / `Changed FAQ` with the heading still inside its own cell (x 115–540). A control checks that the same two runs under one clip are still one paragraph. Without the fix, the page reads as one paragraph `Note1 Heading FAQ`, so the test fails.

title: fix: render CCITT Group 4 images that declare /Rows 0
author: ehinderer
body:
## What this changes

Scanned PDFs whose pages are CCITT Group 4 images with `/DecodeParms << /K -1 /Columns 1704 /Rows 0 >>` rendered as blank pages. ISO 32000-2 Table 11 defines `/Rows 0` (the default) as "the image's height is not predetermined", but the vendored `hayro-syntax` CCITT filter read the value literally and decoded zero rows. It now treats `/Rows 0` the same as an absent `/Rows` and falls back to the image's `/Height`, as it already did when the key was missing.

The patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/ccitt.rs` and listed as hayro-syntax patch (17) in `vendor/README.md`. It should also go upstream to hayro.

title: fix(automation): a missing path under --root says where it was looked for (#1890)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1890. With `--root`, a relative path that doesn't exist below the root is refused with the resolved path and the root, instead of the path as typed plus the system's localised message.

Before, for the issue's script (`"path": "sub/a.pdf"` with `--root sub`):

```
pdfcraft-cli: step 1 (doc_open): sub/a.pdf: Le chemin d'accès spécifié est introuvable. (os error 3)
```

Now:

```
pdfcraft-cli: step 1 (doc_open): sub/a.pdf not found (looked for /abs/work/sub/sub/a.pdf, --root /abs/work/sub)
```

**Where.** `Automation::resolve` in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs`, in the branch for a path whose deepest existing ancestor is inside the root but whose remainder doesn't exist. A `NotFound` from the system becomes the message above; any other error keeps the system's text and gains the same `(looked for …, --root …)` suffix.

**Confinement is unchanged.** The new message is only produced after the existing check that the deepest existing ancestor is inside the root, and the path it names is the root joined with the request, so it reveals nothing about what exists outside. Every path outside the root keeps the uniform refusal from #136.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2`: all passed (154 in `tests/automation.rs`)

**Test.** `a_missing_path_under_the_root_names_where_it_was_looked_for` opens `root/inside.pdf` (the issue's mistake: the root's folder repeated in the path), `missing/deeper/x.pdf` and `./sub/../root/inside.pdf` under a root that contains `inside.pdf`, and requires the exact message for each, with the resolved path normalised. title: M3: touchpad swipes glide on after the fingers lift on Wayland (#531)
author: mlkonrad
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #531. #1708 (Linux Wayland, with a video) reports the same thing and can be closed as a duplicate.

On Wayland a two-finger touchpad swipe now keeps gliding after the fingers lift and slows to a stop, the way GTK apps and Firefox behave. Wayland compositors leave momentum to the client: libinput reports the swipe as pixel deltas and the lift as an axis stop, which winit passes on as `TouchPhase::End`. The page view stopped dead there.

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/fling.rs`** (new): measures the gesture's speed over its last 0.1 s and, on `End`, keeps scrolling with exponential decay (time constant 0.35 s). No glide below 150 pt/s or when the finger rested before lifting (> 50 ms since the last motion); speed capped at 8000 pt/s; non-finite deltas ignored.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`** (+29): reads it right after the #759 precise-touchpad block and feeds the glide through the same un-eased `scroll_with_delta_animation` path, so it also triggers the existing pan-settle hold for tiles.
- **Stops on:** any wheel input (a new swipe, a notch), a click (including a pressed touchpad or tap-to-click), any key, a zoom, keyboard or auto-scroll, a dialog or palette, losing window focus, or two frames against the document's edge.
- **Never glides:** in single-page layout (the pager owns the swipe), for ⌘/Ctrl or Shift swipes, or with **Preferences ▸ Animation effects** Off (or System with the OS asking for reduced motion). No new preference.
- **Platforms:** off on macOS (AppKit sends its own momentum, as a second `Start`…`End`) and the web. Windows and X11 report no touch phases through winit 0.30, so no `End` ever starts a glide there.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib fling`: 5 unit tests (glide distance ≈ speed × τ, slow drag / pause → no glide, new input stops, disabled / not wanted / ⌘ zoom, edge / stale pass / sp…

title: fix(redact): the tail of a longer number is not a phone number (#1884)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1884. `redact_mark pattern=phone` (and Search & Redact ▸ Phone Numbers) no longer marks the last digit groups of a longer number: a French social security number (NIR), an IBAN or a SIRET. Those were being half-redacted, with the identifier's start left visible.

**Cause.** `find` tries the matcher at every position. The whole run `1 85 05 78 006 084 36` is too long for a phone number, but once the scan reaches `05 78 006 084 36` that tail looks like a trunk-0 national number, and `456 782 00010` inside a SIRET looks like an 11-digit NANP number.

**Fix.** A phone number is a whole run of digit groups (`crates/redact/src/patterns.rs`):

- a candidate reached from a digit before it through separators only is the tail of a longer run, so it's not a phone number;
- a run that still goes on past the matcher's 28-character cap is the head of one, so it isn't either.

Nothing else about the pattern changes: the existing phone tests, including `01 23 45 67 89` and `+33 1 23 45 67 89` as in the issue, still match whole.

title: fix(forms): new text and date fields take Acrobat's Auto font size (#1888)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1888. New text and date fields get Acrobat's **Auto** font size instead of a fixed 12 pt, so a field in a short box no longer clips its value.

**Cause.** `add_field` in `crates/forms/src/author.rs` wrote `/DA (/Helv 12 Tf 0 g)` for text and date fields. In the issue's 8 pt box, the 12 pt text is cut at the edges, and a script that creates many fields can't see that.

title: Security: bind signature verdicts and redaction to what the page can show
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #1631, from the same security review. Signature validation and redaction read a file through `pdfcraft-cos`; the page is drawn by a renderer with a parser of its own. Where the two read an appended revision differently, the signature verdict described the signed object while the page showed another, and a redaction verified on one view left content in the other. Four changes close that, each with a regression test that was red before the fix:

- **`M1` cos records cross-reference entries another reader resolves differently.** On top of the entries already set aside (#1631): a classic entry whose 10-digit offset exceeds 32 bits (set aside: a 32-bit reader gives up on the whole table), a classic entry not in the fixed 20-byte form, a cross-reference stream whose `/W` makes the type field anything but one byte, a row `/Index` declares that the data does not hold (kept, but recorded: a byte-counting reader reads other entries there), and a hybrid file's stream `/Prev` chain where it disagrees with the table's chain this reader follows (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.8.4). Capped at 1024 per section.

title: fix(organize): bound how deep an import follows the object graph (#1800)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1800. Copying pages between documents (Insert Pages from File, Combine, Extract, Split, Duplicate, and `page_as_form`) no longer overflows the stack on a source whose page reaches a long chain of indirect objects.

**Cause.** The `Copier` in `crates/organize/src/import.rs` recursed once per reference and once per nested array or dictionary, with nothing but the memo map, which only cuts cycles. Each object in a chain `6 0 R → << /Next 7 0 R >> → << /Next 8 0 R >> → …` is shallow enough for the parser, but copying the first one recursed through all of them.

**Fix.**

- The `Copier` keeps a depth counter. `copy_value` takes one level per reference, array, dictionary or stream it enters and gives it back on the way out; past `MAX_COPY_DEPTH` (256) it returns `OrganizeError::Invalid("the pages refer to objects nested more than 256 levels deep")`. The parser already caps inline nesting at 128, so a legitimate object can't come near the budget on its own; real resource graphs (resources → font → descriptor → file, nested form XObjects, field trees) are a few levels each.
- `copy_ref`, `copy_value`, `copy_dict`, `copy_object` and `collect_attachments` now return `Result`, and every caller propagates with `?`. The six `Copier` struct literals became `Copier::new`.
- `import_pages_with` undoes a refused copy: it frees every object number the attempt added (`Document::add` numbers monotonically, so these are exactly the objects ≥ the first new number), so the destination is as it was. The error can only arise during the copy, before the page tree, `/AcroForm` or `/OCProperties` of the destination are touched.

The engine already runs edits on a working copy under `catch_unwind`, but a stack overflow is an abort, not a panic, so it was never caught there; the CLI and the library had no protection at all.

author: LabDennis

Duplicate references are rejected before inheriting attributes; the existing million-node bound now also bounds the visited set.

title: M11: Preserve resolution across shared Form image uses (#1811)
author: LabDennis
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1811.

A shared image behind seven nested Forms, drawn at both 72 and 288 points, was measured only at the first small invocation (600 instead of 150 ppi in the regression). The optimizer could then permanently downsample the image below what its larger use needs.

Replace global Form-reference deduplication with active-path cycle detection. Every invocation contributes its transform, including uses on later pages. A document-wide 1,000,000-operator budget bounds repeated invocations. If a cycle, the existing depth limit, the work budget or unreadable content prevents complete measurement, return no image measurements and skip image processing for that run; ordinary cleanup remains available. Do not downsample using incomplete PPI values.

## How you verified it

- Both new integration regressions failed before the fix: 600 vs 150 ppi, and partial measurements returned at the depth limit.

title: fix(audit): a cover over a TJ displacement hides no text (#1885)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1885. The redaction audit no longer flags the program's own applied redaction. All three acceptance criteria in the issue hold.

**Cause.** `redact_apply` keeps the text left on a line in place through a `TJ` displacement of the removed glyphs' width: `[(Call ) -6672] TJ`. `pdfcraft_edit::text_lines` measured a text show from its origin to the end of its advance, displacement included, so the "Call " line's box ran on under the black box the redaction drew. The box covered more than 40% of that box, and the audit reported `covered_text: "Call"`. The same happened with a leading displacement (`[-6672 (is mine)] TJ`, "is mine" flagged) and would with one in the middle.

**Fix.**

1. `crates/edit/src/text.rs`: a show's box spans the glyphs it paints. A displacement before, between or after them (a tab stop, the width of text a redaction removed) paints nothing, so it is in no box. Glyph runs separated by a large displacement (the existing "reads as a space" threshold) become separate boxes, and a `TextLine` keeps the boxes of every show it joins (`TextLine::spans`). The line's `rect`, `advance`, `start_x`/`end_x` and the line-joining rules are unchanged, so editing, reflow and move/resize behave as before (the edit crate's 132 tests and the engine's text tests pass).
2. `crates/audit/src/lib.rs`: `covers` measures the cover against those spans, not the line's whole box: the covered fraction is the overlapped span area over the total span area. Unapplied-mark findings use the same measure.

The audit's documented behaviour, "a properly applied redaction removes the text, so it never flags", is now true for the program's own output as well as for other producers' streams with the same shape (tab stops drawn as `TJ` gaps under a filled box).

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit -p pdfcraft-audit -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit -j 2`…

title: M11: measure every use of an image drawn through deeply nested forms (#1811)
author: mlkonrad
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1811. The findings and reproduction are in [the issue comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1811#issuecomment-6150031148).

`effective_resolutions` skipped a form XObject it had already visited once (anywhere in the document) when it was nested more than four deep. A later, larger use of that form was never measured, so Reduce File Size and Optimize PDF resampled the image for its smallest use. On `main`, a 1200 px image drawn 1 in and 8 in wide through six nested forms is resampled to 150 px, about 19 ppi on the large copy. With the fix it measures 150 ppi and is left at 1200 px.

The walk (`crates/optimize/src/images.rs`) is now a small `Walk` struct:
- **Cycles** are detected on the current path of forms, not with a document-wide seen-set.
- **Repeats** are skipped only when they can't change the result: same form, its own `/Resources`, same linear part of the CTM (ppi doesn't depend on translation). A form tiled many times at one size is still walked once. That's also cheaper than before, since shallow forms used to be re-walked on every page. A form without `/Resources` draws its caller's images, so it is always walked.
- **Work is bounded.** Each form's first walk is free (bounded by the object count). Repeat walks are capped at 100,000. If that cap or the existing 12-level depth limit leaves a use unmeasured, every image gets `INFINITY`: recompressed as the settings say, never resampled. Before, those uses were silently ignored.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-optimize --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize` (17 passed), plus the optimize/reduce tests in `pdfcraft-engine` and `pdfcraft-automation`

title: fix(edit): flattening keeps a widget it cannot draw and an undrawn reply (#1794)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1794. Flattening no longer deletes what it could not draw.

**1. A widget with no appearance to draw stays a field.** `flatten_which` skipped widgets when building appearances, and its "keep what wasn't drawn" rule applied to comments only (`!widget && !drew`), so a widget with no `/AP`, or with none for its `/AS` state, was removed from the page and pruned from `/AcroForm /Fields` with nothing drawn in its place: the field's value was gone. Now a widget whose appearance stream doesn't exist stays on the page and in the form, like a comment that can't be drawn.

A widget that *has* an appearance stream which draws nothing (an empty stream, as in the engine's form fixture) is still removed: it shows nothing in any viewer, so nothing visible is lost, and flattening is meant to drop the field. That keeps `flattening_keeps_the_look_and_drops_the_objects` true.

**2. An undrawn reply stays.** The second pass removed every annotation whose `/IRT` pointed at a flattened one, including a reply the first pass had deliberately kept because it had no appearance and none could be built. Such a reply is now left out of the second pass. A reply note, whose appearance exists and draws nothing, still goes with its comment, as before (`flattening_draws_appearances_into_the_page_and_removes_the_comments` is unchanged).

The module doc and the two `parity/` entries say this: the fields entry now notes that a form with such widgets is not fully flattened, because PdfCraft doesn't regenerate widget appearances before flattening the way Acrobat does. That regeneration (the issue's first suggested remedy) belongs in the engine, where `pdfcraft_forms` is available, and would be a separate change; this one stops the data loss.

title: M10: Sync automation saves before replacing the destination (#1804)
author: LabDennis
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1804.

Automation output writes now sync the staging file before replacing the destination. A delayed writeback/sync error is returned while the original file is still intact; staging is removed and doc_save retains the dirty document and its history for retry. The handle still closes before rename for Windows compatibility.

The shared helper covers doc_save and other existing atomic outputs. Filesystems that reject sync return an error, with no unsynced fallback. This flushes staged file contents; it does not guarantee the parent-directory rename survives a power failure. That boundary is documented explicitly.

title: M2: Bound retained text extraction storage per page (#1797)
author: LabDennis
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1797.

Text extraction now has a conservative, monotonic 64 MiB per-page allowance for retained text and glyph bookkeeping. Every ActualText invocation is charged before copying or decoding, including repeated references to the same named property. Original glyphs and replacement copies used to reconcile unmarked redraws consume the same allowance.

If the allowance is exceeded, extraction returns a page-specific error instead of accepting partial text. Pixel rendering remains available and each other page gets a fresh allowance. Existing search, copy and automation callers receive the normal extraction-error result.

## How you verified it

- All 274 pdfcraft-render tests pass, including five new regression tests.
- The repeated named-property regression failed before the budget checks were added: reused property strings were accepted beyond the test allowance.
- Tests cover oversized and empty replacements, repeated named properties, UTF-16/UTF-8/PDFDocEncoding, per-page reset, and replacement copies for unmarked redraws.
- A PageRenderer regression exercises the actual production limit with one 128 KiB property referenced 80 times, checks that no partial text escapes, renders the rejected page, and extracts text from the next page.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --profile low-disk -j 2`
- Native all-target Clippy with `-D warnings`, formatting, wasm32 check, layers and asset checks pass. The wasm check retains existing target-specific dead-code warnings.

No unsafe, new panic paths, assets, fonts or dependencies. Input-derived allocation charges use saturating arithmetic and checked subtraction. Fixtures are generated in memory. The change flows through the existing renderer and headless callers; no new tool, parity claim or roadmap edits.

title: fix(control): a deadline and a cap for connections that have not authenticated (#1806)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1806. A local process that connects to the `--control` port and never presents the token can no longer hold a thread for ever, nor exhaust them.

**Cause.** `serve` spawned a thread for every accepted connection and read its first line with no deadline. The 4 KiB pre-auth line cap (#1653) bounds what is buffered, not how long or how many.

**Fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`), all before `auth` only; an authenticated connection behaves exactly as before:

- **Authentication deadline, absolute.** Each connection has 10 s from acceptance to authenticate. The reading half is wrapped in `Reading`, which sets the socket's read timeout to the time *left* before every read, so a client feeding a byte every few seconds cannot push the deadline back. When it passes, the server writes `-32004 not authenticated within 10 s` and closes. On `auth`, the deadline is cleared.
- **Cap on connections waiting to authenticate.** At most 8 at once. A further connection is refused on the accepting thread itself (`-32003 too many connections waiting to authenticate; try again later`, then closed), so a refused connection costs no thread. A place is a `Slot` guard: it is given back when the connection authenticates and, through `Drop`, on every way its thread can end (end of stream, overlong line, parse error, deadline, `try_clone` failure).
- **Write timeout.** 30 s per write, so a client that never reads its replies cannot block a connection thread either.

The limits live in one `Limits` value (`LIMITS`); `serve` uses it and the tests use a small one through `serve_with`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`

author: jcl-bit

title: fix(ui): a file version found before a save is not applied over it (#1802)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1802. A version of a file that the watcher read and queued *before* the user saved is no longer applied over the saved document.

**Cause.** The worker thread reads a changed file and queues `Changed { doc, stamp, bytes }`; the UI thread applies it on its next frame. `file_changed` rejected only a stamp equal to the one PdfCraft last wrote. So when the user saved version C (or Save As to another file) between the read of version B and its application, B's stamp was different from C's, and B replaced C in memory, clearing the undo history. After Save As, the old file's bytes landed under the new path. (And because the known stamp was then set to B's, the watcher re-read C and reloaded it, so the document flickered back without its history.)

**Fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs`):

- Every watched file carries an **epoch**: how many times PdfCraft has read or written it. `known_now` (a save) and `known_as` (an open, a reopen, Reload) bump it. The watcher gets it with the watch list and returns it, with the path it read, in each result.
- `file_changed` applies a result only when it is for the document's current path *and* current epoch. Anything found for an earlier epoch or another path is older than the document in memory and is dropped; the watcher already has the newer version to compare against.

Nothing changes for the normal case: a rebuild of the open file is still found, settled and reloaded, and PdfCraft's own saves are still recognised by their stamp.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --lib file_watch::tests`: 2 passed

title: fix: add the Turkish letters WinAnsi lacks (Ğ ğ İ ı Ş ş) to Add text
author: TallTalha
body:
## What this changes

Edit a PDF ▸ Add text (and `page_add_text`) refused the Turkish letters that WinAnsi has no code for: **Ğ ğ İ ı Ş ş**. For example, `İstanbul` was rejected with `the standard fonts can't draw "İ" (U+0130)`, so most Turkish text could not be added. Ö ö Ü ü Ç ç were already in WinAnsi.

This follows the approach suggested in the review of #1513, and the per-font slot idea in #1608:

- **`pdfcraft-fonts`: new `LatinEncoding`** (`latin.rs`). It encodes text as WinAnsi plus a code for each extra letter the text actually uses. A code is chosen **per text** from codes the text doesn't otherwise use: the five undefined WinAnsi upper-half codes first, then unused upper-half codes, then DEL. It never inspects bytes to guess a language, and `win_ansi_byte` is unchanged. So `ı` next to `ý`, or `İ` next to `Ý`, keeps both letters (the case that blocked #1513). The encoding writes a `/Differences` dictionary over `/WinAnsiEncoding` with the standard glyph names (`Gbreve`, `gbreve`, `Idotaccent`, `dotlessi`, `Scedilla`, `scedilla`) and a ToUnicode CMap for every code, so copy and search return what was typed.
- **`std14.rs`: `EXTRA_LATIN`** gives the Core14 AFM advance widths of those six glyphs for the twelve text fonts. `Std14::extra_latin_width` exposes them. Wrapping and center/right/justify alignment use the real widths (Helvetica `dotlessi` is 278, `i` is 222).
- **`edit::added`**: an item whose text needs extra letters gets a Type1 standard font of its own (`/PCLat<n>`, never a name already on the page), so items never share or overwrite one another's encoding. Like the Arabic `PCAr` fonts, the item's font is dropped when the item is retyped or deleted. Text that WinAnsi holds on its own is written exactly as before (`/PCFHelvetica`, byte for byte). `first_undrawable` uses the same encoding, so the editor's warning, `validate` and `draw` agree.

title: fix(sign): a signed revision of a password-protected file opens with the document's key (#1808)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1808. A document opened with a (nonempty) user password keeps its earlier signature valid after it is counter-signed or otherwise changed in a permitted way.

**Cause.** When a signature no longer covers the whole file, `DigestCache::revision` reopened the signed bytes with `Document::open`, i.e. with no password, to compare the revisions. An encrypted file that needs its user password cannot be opened that way, so `classify_changes` saw no revision and reported `Disallowed(["the signed version could not be read"])`: the first signature was Invalid although the current document had been authenticated. The existing encrypted-signing tests all use an empty user password, which is why it passed them.

**Fix.**

- `pdfcraft_cos::Document::open_with_same_credentials(&self, data)`: opens `data` (an earlier revision of this file, or another save of it) with this document's own security handler, when the data's `/Encrypt` dictionary and `/ID` are the same as this document's: the same file key, so nothing is derived again and no password is needed or kept anywhere. Unencrypted data opens as `open` does; data encrypted differently fails with `NeedsPassword`, as before. Internally `open` gained a `Credentials` enum (password or handler) in place of the bare password; the password path is unchanged.
- `pdfcraft_sign`'s `DigestCache::revision` takes the current document and uses that. The cache key is still the revision's length and fingerprint, which identifies the bytes and therefore their encryption.

Opened as owner, the same handler is used, so both verdicts agree.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos -j 2` (all) and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2` (all) pass; `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine -j 2 --lib sign` passes

author: CouchRiv
body:

Combining tagged PDFs (a guide and its appendices exported tagged by an office suite or Chromium) gave an untagged PDF: the copy dropped `/StructTreeRoot`, `/MarkInfo` and `/Lang`. title: feat(organize): Insert pages from file brings the file's bookmarks
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

Inserting an annex into a guide (`page_insert_file`, Organize ▸ Insert ▸ From file) brought the pages in without the annex's bookmarks. `doc_combine` keeps every file's bookmarks, nested under one bookmark named after the file, so the same two files gave a navigable result one way and not the other:

```text
page_insert_file {doc, path: "dest-src.pdf", at: 2}   (dest-src.pdf has one bookmark)
bookmark_list -> []
```

Insert pages from file now does what Combine does for each file:

- the inserted file's bookmarks are read with their destinations mapped to the copied pages (`source_outline`, the same code Combine uses: `/XYZ` positions kept, named destinations resolved, bookmarks to pages left out keep their title and lose their destination);
- they go, collapsed, under one new bookmark titled with the file's name (without the extension), which opens its first inserted page (`/Fit`, as Combine's per-file bookmark);
- that bookmark is placed among the document's top-level bookmarks before the first one that points at a page after the inserted ones, so the outline follows the page order; it is appended when none does;
- a file without bookmarks adds none, and a document without an outline only gets one when there is something to put in it.

`organize::insert_file_pages` does this (import as `import_pages_with`, then the bookmark); the engine's `InsertPagesFrom` edit calls it, so the app, `page_insert_file` and undo all get it. Duplicate pages and Replace pages, which also copy pages, are unchanged.

title: XFA: flatten a form into a plain PDF, or convert it to a static form
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: flatten a form into a plain PDF, or convert it to a static form

Follow-up to #121, #230, #301, #414, #1175, #1355 and #1589. This closes `form.xfa-flatten`, the last XFA parity entry that was still planned.

### The problem

Flattening the fields of a laid-out XFA form baked them into the pages but left the XFA in the file. Adobe's viewers see the packets and `/NeedsRendering`, lay the form out again from the template over the baked pages, and show a live form; every other viewer shows the flattened pages. The "flattened" PDF was two different documents depending on the viewer.

### What changes

* **`pdfcraft_xfa::strip`** takes the XFA out of a document: the packets (template, data, config, everything), `/NeedsRendering` on the catalog and the AcroForm, the layout mark, the overrides, Reader usage rights (`/Perms /UR3`, which changing the form voids anyway), and the private keys PdfCraft put on every field down the Kids tree (`/PCSom`, `/PCXfaClick`, `/PCXfaImage`, `/PCItems`). The packet streams are freed so an incremental save carries no unreachable copy of the data. Each field dictionary is walked once (a seen-set checked before pushing, and a cap); a document without XFA is left untouched.
* **Nothing goes in silence.** `strip` reports what the packets held beyond the fields: the packets by name, data values no field showed (counted against the fields' data paths), buttons that ran XFA scripts and image fields (inert from now on), the layout mark's own warnings (now permanent), the usage rights. The engine turns the report into document warnings prefixed `XFA removed:`, adds a count of fields whose value differed from the form's data (data PdfCraft could not read into them, now lost), and shows them in the app's warnings and the tools' output. On undo the XFA's own warnings apply again and the strip's go.
* **Only a form that has one to keep.** A dynamic form that was never laid out (its template unreadable) has only placeholder pages: converting it i…

title: M1-M9: audit run-4 medium fixes: signature verdicts, fail-closed redaction and sanitizing, bounded work
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What this changes

The medium-severity findings of a defensive security review of the codebase (synthetic fixtures only, no personal data), one commit per finding, each with the red-before-fix evidence in its message. The high-severity findings are in #1916; this branch is based on `main` independently of it, so whichever merges second needs a rebase (both touch `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` `classify_changes`, the sign README and the parity notes).

**Signatures (M9).** An OCSP responder carried in a response is a delegate by how it was found, whatever subject name it copies. A certificate trusted for signing is not thereby a time authority: a timestamp token is trusted time only from a certificate with id-kp-timeStamping. The byte range must exclude exactly the `/Contents` of the object carrying the signature dictionary, so a second field borrowing a genuine signature's range and value is invalid. Defining an object the signed revision referenced but never defined is page content. Form changes after signing are judged by what changed, not by where: a field is form fill only when nothing but its value and what is regenerated from it changed, a new field or widget is a comment-level change unless it is a signed signature field, and under P=1 the one signature change permitted is a document timestamp. A field the signer locked (FieldMDP references, else the signed field's `/Lock`, which signing now writes as a reference) may not be filled in afterwards.

**Scripts (M6).** Source a script builds at run time for `eval()` or `Function()` is screened as the script itself was (boa `HostHooks::ensure_can_compile_strings`).
