author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2591.

While editing existing text, **Load font…** and **Installed fonts…** only registered the face on the page: the paragraph kept its source font, and the loaded face had to be found again in the document-font menu above the Helvetica/Times/Courier list, which is easy to miss. Now the loaded font is applied to the paragraph being edited (or to the selected range), through the same path as choosing it from that menu (so it is an ordinary undoable change). I moved that apply step into a small `apply_line_format` helper so the panel and the file picker share it.

What this leaves open from the report:
- TTFs like Arial and the other macOS system fonts are refused on purpose: only fonts that declare an open licence can be embedded (docs/editing-existing-text.md). The toast says so. Variable fonts, like most Google Fonts downloads, need a static instance first, and the toast says that too.
- **Add text** still offers only the standard families. Letting it use loaded fonts would mean embedding them for added text, which is a product call I left to you.

Happy to switch to just selecting the font in the menu, without applying it, if you'd rather keep that a separate step.

title: Shorten over-long part file names in doc_split by bookmarks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/automation/src/lib.rs:1747` (no existing issue): doc_split with bookmarks: true fails with "File name too long" when a bookmark title is long, after already writing earlier parts.

## Cause
`doc_split` with `bookmarks: true` built each part's file name as `{stem}-{sanitized title}.pdf` with no length limit. A title over the 255-byte NAME_MAX made `write_atomic` fail with ENAMETOOLONG, and the split stopped after earlier parts were already written.

## Fix
The name before `.pdf` is now cut to at most 200 bytes, on a char boundary. That leaves room for the extension and a `-N` suffix. The uniqueness suffix (`-2`, `-3`, …) is added to this shortened base, so names that collide after truncation stay distinct and within the limit.

## Verified
- Regression test `bookmark_split_with_long_titles_shortens_the_file_names`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation bookmark_split_with_long_titles_shortens_the_file_names`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The file-name sanitizing rules, the `-N` numbering scheme and the `partN` names used for non-bookmark splits are unchanged. `write_atomic` and the staging-file naming are unchanged too; they already shorten their own temporary names.

title: Don't treat a date ending in "Sep" as PM in AFDate/AFTime parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/forms/src/af.rs:590` (no existing issue): AFDate/AFTime keystroke parsing treats a typed text ending in "p" (e.g. "Sep") as PM and shifts the time to 12:00.

## Cause
`parse_date` decided PM with `lower.ends_with('p')`, which also matches month names such as "Sep". Typing `2026 05 Sep` for `yyyy dd mmm HH:MM` therefore took the PM branch and turned hour 0 into 12. `format_value` and `keystroke` go through `parse_date`, so they were affected too.

## Fix
A bare trailing `p` now counts as PM only when it follows a digit, ignoring spaces. "5:30p" and "5:30 p" still give PM, and "pm" is handled as before. "Sep" no longer does.

## Verified
- Regression tests `month_name_ending_in_p_is_not_pm`, `bare_p_after_a_time_is_still_pm`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms --lib pm_marker_tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `am` detection (`lower.contains("am")`) and the lack of a bare trailing `a` shorthand are unchanged. They are separate behaviours from this bug.

title: M14: no PdfCraft lion over PDF thumbnails and the preview pane
author: magdale76
body:
## What this changes

With PdfCraft as the default PDF program on Windows, Explorer paints PdfCraft's app icon, the lion, over the lower-right corner of every PDF thumbnail and of the preview pane. It is large in the preview pane and covers part of the page, so in a folder of scans you can't read that corner.

Windows takes thumbnail overlays from the ProgID's `TypeOverlay` value. If the value is absent, it uses the default program's icon; an empty string means no overlay ([Thumbnail Handlers, Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/thumbnail-providers#thumbnail-overlays)). The installer now writes `TypeOverlay = ""` on `PdfCraft.Document`, next to its `DefaultIcon`.

Related to #2206: this doesn't add thumbnails, it only stops covering them.

## How you verified it

On a Windows 11 office PC with PdfCraft (MSI) as the default PDF program, I set the same value per user (`HKCU\Software\Classes\PdfCraft.Document`, `TypeOverlay = ""`) and restarted Explorer. The lion disappeared from the preview pane of a scanner folder.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`: passes (no Rust changed)
- [x] clippy / tests: no Rust changed, so nothing new to lint or test locally; the CI test jobs pass
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`: both pass

The MSI with this change is built and installed by CI: the `windows-arm64 / package` job builds it from `packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs` and `install and run on ARM64` installs and runs it, both green. title: M3: touchpad scroll speed setting for Wayland (#1904)
author: ibraheem15
body:
## What this changes

On Wayland a two-finger swipe reaches egui as point deltas, and the page moved exactly as far as the fingers. The same swipe under XWayland (or X11) arrives as fractional wheel lines, about one per ten points, which egui multiplies by the line speed. So the same gesture scrolls about 4× as far there, and the existing Scroll speed preference never touched touchpads on Wayland. That's the report in #1904 (and the touchpad half of #1072).

This adds **Preferences ▸ Scroll speed (touchpad)** (Slow / Normal / Fast). It scales touchpad point input in `raw_input_hook`, before egui reads it:

| | Slow | Normal (default) | Fast |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux (Wayland) | 2× | **4×** (as far as XWayland scrolls in egui's scroll areas) | 8× |
| macOS | 0.5× | 1× (unchanged) | 2× |

- Because the scaling happens once at input, everything follows it: every egui scroll area (Preferences, panels, dialogs), the page view's lag-free path (#759) and its momentum (#531).
- ⌘/Ctrl-wheel zoom keeps egui's rate.
- X11 and Windows report touchpads as lines, so they keep following the wheel setting. The row is hidden on Windows and the web, and on Linux its tooltip says X11 follows the wheel setting.
- The setting is saved as `touchpad_scroll_speed`. It's set after the settings `json!`, which is at serde_json's recursion limit, as `redact_prefs` already is. It can be set on the control channel (`touchpad_scroll_speed` = `slow` / `normal` / `fast`) and is translated in all 22 catalogs.

Fixes #1904

title: fix(ui): Reveal in File Explorer selects files whose path has a space (#2579)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2579. On Windows, **Reveal in File Explorer** opened Documents instead of the file's folder whenever the file's path contained a space. That often happens after Save As (a new name like `report copy.pdf`, or a folder like `R:\My files`).

- **Cause.** Explorer expects `/select,"<path>"`, with the path quoted after the comma. PdfCraft passed `/select,<path>` as one ordinary argument, and Rust's Windows argument quoting wraps an argument containing a space in quotes as a whole: `"/select,C:\a b\x.pdf"`. Explorer doesn't read that as a selection and opens Documents. A path without a space isn't quoted, which is why the file worked when first opened and broke after Save As.
- **Fix.** `reveal_command` builds `/select,"<path>"`, and the Windows runner passes its arguments as written (`CommandExt::raw_arg`). Windows file names can't contain `"`, so the quotes can't be closed early; a path that does contain one is refused rather than passed on.
- Save As itself already updates the tab's path on `main`: a probe opened `first dir\in.pdf`, ran Save As to `second dir\out copy.pdf`, and the document's path followed. The 0.7.1 tooltip symptom in the report doesn't reproduce.

title: fix(ui): one layer-aware page pointer for page hovers, cursors and tips
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Page hovers decided "the pointer is over me" from the raw pointer position tested against the whole, unclipped page rectangle. That ignores egui's layers, modals and the viewport clip, so page cursors and link tips leaked onto things drawn over the page:

- the Stamp (and other placement-tool) crosshair over the command palette's and the quick bar's margins
- the crosshair, or a hidden link's pointing hand, over the chrome above a page scrolled under it
- a link's hover tip above the Unlock prompt (the hand-kept `page_covered` list had drifted from `modal_open()` and missed `unlock_prompt`)

`document_area` now computes one `page_ptr` per frame from the page content `Response`. It is the pointer while the content widget contains it and the top layer there is the page's, or while a press or drag that began on the page is held. It reaches the page modules through `comments::PageCx` and as an argument, replacing their raw reads.

Switched in this PR:
- the canvas link and annotation hover and their tip (`page_covered` is gone)
- the placement tools: stamp, custom stamp, measure, crop, sign, marquee zoom/snapshot, camera, redact and Fill & Sign

This is the first step of a cursor redesign. The gesture-heavy modules (forms, comments, edit text, content, objects, prepare) and resolving competing cursors once per frame come later. Until then, the per-frame cursor reset under modals from storytold/pdfcraft#2556 is still what keeps form-field cursors off under dialogs. The two PRs touch disjoint files and merge cleanly.

title: Place backgrounds below content on white pages
author: outragedevs
body:
## What this changes

Office and accounting PDFs often paint an opaque white rectangle before their text, hiding backgrounds placed behind the page. title: Let the page range select page 1 alone
author: outragedevs
body:
## What this changes

In the Page Range Options shared by Add Header and Footer, Add Watermark, Add Background and Export pages as images, "Pages from 1 to 1" could not be set. The range field set `to` back to the last page on every frame while `from` and `to` were both 1, so typing 1 into "to" jumped straight back to the page count (38 of 38 on the document where this turned up). Any other single page (5 to 5) worked, which made page 1 the only page that could not be chosen alone; the workaround was 1 to 2 with "Odd pages only".

The per-frame reset was meant to start the range on the last page. `PageRange::default()` now starts `to` past any page count, and the range field clamps it to the document's last page when it is shown (`DragValue` clamps existing values to its range), so the dialog still opens on "1 to <last page>" and a typed 1 stays 1. `PageRange::pages` already caps `to` at the page count, so nothing else reads the unclamped value.

author: danielmigueltejedor
body:
## What this changes

GNOME/Wayland does not provide server-side window decorations. These desktop builds enable eframe's Wayland backend with default features disabled, which leaves winit's Adwaita frame disabled as well. This can leave decorated windows without usable window controls.

No font files are added to the repository. The README documents the behavior and its limits; this does not claim GTK theme parity.

title: Print ▸ Properties…: the driver's options in the UI language
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What this changes

CUPS drivers ship their option names in other languages as PPD localization lines. Examples:

- `*cupsLanguages: "de es fr …"`
- `*de.Translation KMDuplex/Druckart: ""` for option and group names
- `*de.KMDuplex Double/2-seitig: ""` for choices

The macOS and CUPS print dialogs use these lines, but PdfCraft's Properties… panel showed the PPD's default (English) names in every UI language.

`spool::printer_options_in(printer, lang)` now applies the lines for the UI language to option, group and choice names. The Print dialog passes `i18n::current().code()`.

- **Language codes:** the UI code maps to the PPD's code, region first, then the language alone: `pt-br` → `pt_BR`, `pt`; `zh-hans` → `zh_CN`, `zh`; `zh-hant` → `zh_TW`.
- **Encoding:** each localization line is decoded as UTF-8 on its own. Drivers write them that way even when the rest of the file is Latin-1 (`*LanguageEncoding: ISOLatin1`, as in Konica Minolta's PPDs). Decoding the whole file as Latin-1 would garble them.
- **Fallback:** a missing or empty translation keeps the driver's name.
- `printer_options` (automation) is unchanged and still returns the default names.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-print --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: Add output quality presets when combining files
author: Buiko32
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1894.

Adds a quality selector to Combine files, so a smaller PDF can be created as part of combining rather than by running Optimize PDF afterwards. The same choice is available through `doc_combine`.

- **Original** is the default and keeps the combined bytes as they are.
- **Balanced** downsamples images above 225 ppi to 150 ppi, with JPEG quality 60.
- **Compact** downsamples images above 144 ppi to 96 ppi, with JPEG quality 45.

The two compression presets reuse the existing optimizer. If its output is no smaller, the combined PDF is kept instead. Text and forms remain editable, and source files are left alone. On desktop, compression runs in a worker so the interface stays responsive.

These are quality choices, not target file sizes: already compact PDFs may not shrink, and unsupported image formats stay as they are. Existing combine limitations still apply. The web build runs compression inline, like the existing optimizer.

title: Read the Annex D.2 alias codes as the ink they draw, in both tables
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What this changes

Text drawn through WinAnsiEncoding's `0xA0` or `0xAD`, or MacRomanEncoding's `0xCA`, now extracts
as the ordinary space and hyphen it paints, instead of as the invisible U+00A0 and U+00AD.

Annex D.2 gives those codes the glyph names `space` and `hyphen` — the same names it gives `0x20`
and `0x2D`. Our tables called them `nbspace` and `sfthyphen`, whose Adobe Glyph List values are
*formatting* characters, so extraction hid ink the reader can plainly see: `well-known` drawn with
the `0xAD` byte matched no search and no redaction pattern, and a non-breaking space did not match
the space a reader typed.

This finishes #2305, which fixed `0xAD` in `crates/fonts` and closed naming two loose ends:

1. **The user-visible path still had it.** `pdfcraft-cli text`, the viewer and copy go through
   hayro, not that table, so they kept reporting the invisible character. The product had two
   tables disagreeing about the same byte — that is the defect this really removes.
2. **The same note makes `0xA0` the `space` glyph**, and MacRoman `0xCA` with it.

### Evidence

Two independent transcriptions of the table agree — an Annex D implementation's documentation, and
the `WinAnsi.enc` encoding vector R ships, which puts `/space` at octal 240 and `/hyphen` at 255 —
and a black-box check settles the part they do not cover. On a synthetic fixture `pdftotext` reads

| drawn as | pdftotext | us, before | us, now |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `/WinAnsiEncoding`, codes `0xAD` `0xA0` | `a-b a b` | `a\xADb a\xA0b` | `a-b a b` |
| `/Differences [88 /sfthyphen 89 /nbspace]` | keeps U+00AD | keeps U+00AD | keeps U+00AD |

Over the 989-file pdf.js corpus the soft hyphens we extract fall **117 → 13** and the non-breaking
spaces **30 → 26**. `XiaoBiaoSong.pdf` alone accounted for 104 of the hyphens; its extraction is now the
same 690 characters as `pdftotext`'s, differing only in the order of five adjacent pairs.

author: MaxFairwinds
body:
## What this changes

The Paper list was a fixed set of 20 sizes, so a label printer's 4 × 6 in (or 2.25 × 4 in) and an office printer's envelopes could not be chosen: the sheets were laid out on a size the printer lacks, and on Windows craft-print then refuses the job ("… has no 2.25 × 4.00 inch paper"). The queue's own sizes were deliberately kept out of Properties… (`HANDLED_OPTIONS`) and never sent. Answers #2131 (a 102 × 152 mm printer) and #1931 (62 × 100 labels) with the sizes the printer itself reports, rather than growing `PAPERS` or asking the user to type them.

- **The printer's own sizes in the Paper list.** `spool::printer_papers(printer)` reads them (CUPS: the queue PPD's `*PaperDimension` entries, named by their `*PageSize` labels, in PPD order; custom-size placeholders, translations, repeats and impossible sizes left out; capped at 400). title: M10: match PDF page paper when opening Print and send CUPS media for all papers (#2651)
author: lollinoo
body:
Fixes #2651

### What was happening

1. **Missing `-o media=<paper>` in `v0.8.0` and earlier alphas:**
   - Up through `v0.8.0`, `impose()` laid out sheets at the requested paper size in `/MediaBox` (e.g. `[0 0 1190.55 841.89]` for landscape A3), and `PrintDraft::job()` / `Automation::doc_print()` submitted the PDF to `craft_print::submit`.
   - On macOS and Linux (CUPS), `craft_print::lp_args` ran `lp ... -o fit-to-page=false` without any `-o media=...` (and filtered out `PageSize` via `HANDLED_OPTIONS`).
   - Without an explicit `media` job option, macOS's CUPS filter chain (`cgpdftopdf` / `cgpdftoraster`) always used the printer queue's default paper size (`DefaultPageSize: A4` on metric systems), printing on A4 even when A3 was selected in the Print dialog.
   - Commit `980bd900` (#1583, landed after `v0.8.0`) added `cups_media` for 7 papers (`Letter`, `Legal`, `Tabloid`, `A3`, `A4`, `A5`, `w288h432`) and chained it into `PrintDraft::job()`, but left three gaps:

Opening an A3 PDF (`420 × 297 mm` = `1190.55 × 841.89 pt`) and printing without manually changing `Paper:` imposed the A3 page scaled down onto a US Letter sheet (`-o media=Letter`).
     2. **Incomplete `cups_media` mapping:** 13 of the 20 standard paper sizes in `PAPERS` (`A6`, `A2`, `A1`, `A0`, `ARCH A`–`ARCH E`, and `ANSI C`–`ANSI E`) returned `None` from `cups_media`, so selecting any of them on macOS/Linux still omitted `-o media=...` and silently printed on the queue's default paper (e.g. A4).

title: Round FormCalc Str and Format exact ties away from zero
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2169 (Str) and :2258 (Format number picture)` (no existing issue): FormCalc Str() and Format() round exact .5 ties to even instead of half away from zero (Str(2.5) gives 2, Format("9", 2.5) gives 2).

## Cause
FormCalc `Str` and `Format` passed the number straight to Rust's `format!("{:.N}")`, which rounds exact halves to even. `Str(2.5)` gave 2, `Format("9.99", 0.125)` gave 0.12, and so on. FormCalc rounds half away from zero, as its `Round` built-in does.

## Fix
A new `fixed` helper scales by 10^decimals, rounds half away from zero, scales back and then formats. `Str` and the `Format` number picture both call it.

## Verified
- Regression test `str_and_format_round_exact_ties_away_from_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js str_and_format_round_exact_ties_away_from_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change `Round` or `number_text` in `crates/forms/src/af.rs`. Values like 1.005 whose binary form lies just below the tie keep their existing result. I did not move the helper into a crate shared with `af.rs`.

title: fix(annot): percent-encode non-ASCII bytes written into link /URI
author: charan-rathore
body:
Refs #2670 (item 3).

## What this fixes

Add a link whose target has non-ASCII characters (for example `https://example.com/ação`) and save: the bytes were written into the PDF `/URI` string as raw UTF-8. URIs in PDF are 7-bit ASCII strings (ISO 32000 §12.6.4.8), so the saved file carried an out-of-spec URI that strict readers can reject or misparse.

## The change

`write_action` now passes the URI through a small `uri_bytes` helper that percent-encodes every byte outside `0x21..=0x7E`. Bytes already inside the printable ASCII range pass through unchanged, so existing percent-escapes like `%20` are preserved as-is.

## Tests

New regression test `link_uri_is_percent_encoded_to_7_bit_ascii` round-trips a non-ASCII URL and an already-escaped URL through save/reload and asserts the stored URIs are pure ASCII. It fails on main (raw UTF-8 bytes come back) and passes with the fix.

## Gates

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot`: 43 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo xtask layers`: OK, 37 crates, no layering violations

title: Score reading order in the text oracle, which word F1 cannot see
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What this changes

`cargo xtask text-oracle` now reports a second score per file: **reading order**, the longest
common subsequence of our word sequence and `pdftotext`'s, as a share of the longer one.

Word F1 is a bag of words. It catches a character read wrong, a glyph not read at all, a font we
cannot map — and it is blind to order, so a page emitted back to front scores a perfect 1.000.
Reading order is most of what text extraction has left to get wrong: a column read into the
middle of its neighbour (#2387), a figure's labels threaded through a paragraph (#2586), a form's
value parted from its label.

The hole is not hypothetical. Reviewing #2431 — a change that moves text and alters nothing else —
word F1 called **26 of the 29** files whose output changed *identical*, while scoring the word
sequence separated 18 improvements from 6 regressions and pointed at the shape of the
regressions (forms: a checkbox's number parted from its label). The harness could not see the
only thing that PR does.

Both sides are cut to the first 3,000 words, because the comparison is quadratic and three pages
is plenty of signal; the run reports how many files that bit, so the cap cannot quietly become
the measurement. It reports; it does not gate.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

**The score is a disagreement with Poppler, not a verdict** — the same caveat gap 12 and the
oracle README already carry for the pixel score, and it bites harder here. The same split scored
as a win on one file and a loss on another in the #2431 measurement, purely because `pdftotext`
happens to make it in one place and not the other. Both the function's doc comment and the README
say so.

title: Replace Text: give the caret its own /NM (#2666)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
Closes #2666.

### What happens

`add_text_replacement` builds the StrikeOut and the Caret from a single `Meta`:

```rust
let s = add_annotation(doc, &NewAnnotation { shape: Shape::TextMarkup { .. }, .. }, meta)?;
let c = add_annotation(doc, &NewAnnotation { shape: Shape::Caret { rect }, .. }, meta)?;
```

and `add_annotation` stamps `/NM` from `meta.id`, so both annotations end up with
the same name. XFDF names a reply by the `/NM` of what it replies to:

```rust
if let Some(irt) = d.get(b"IRT").and_then(Object::as_ref).and_then(|r| names.get(&r)) {
    let _ = write!(attrs, " inreplyto=\"{}\"", esc(irt));
}
```

With one name for both, that writes `<caret name="X" inreplyto="X">`: a comment
replying to itself. On import the two records collide on the name, the later one
replaces the earlier, and the pair is lost, which is the reported symptom of a
second document listing no comments. FDF is unaffected because it keeps the pair
by structure rather than by name.

### The change

`add_text_replacement` takes a second `Meta` for the caret. The ids stay supplied
by the caller, which is how the rest of the crate keeps edits deterministic, and
the single production caller already has a generator and simply calls it twice.
`/IRT` still points at the strikeout, so the group still moves, lists and deletes
as one.

I changed the signature rather than deriving the caret's id inside, to match that
"the caller supplies the id" design. Only one production caller and two tests use
it. If you would rather keep the signature and derive the second id internally,
that is a small change and I am happy to make it.

### Tests

- `replace_text_groups_a_strikeout_and_a_caret` now asserts the two names differ
  and that the caret's `/IRT` resolves to the strikeout's `/NM`.
- `a_replace_text_pair_survives_an_xfdf_round_trip` exports a Replace Text pair
  and imports it into another document, asserting both comments arrive and the
  thread is intact.

title: M2: retain readable pages and content after bad array entries (#2660)
author: agostinidavid
body:
## What this changes

A dangling reference or wrong-type entry in `/Kids` currently ends traversal, hiding all later pages; the same failure in `/Contents` hides later drawing streams. This retains readable entries in their original order in both content-reading paths and reports skipped-slot counts through `DocInfo.warnings`.

title: fix(ui): one page pointer per frame, so taps work and nothing over a page lets it through
author: alehel
body:
## Why

Bugs about "what the cursor registered" kept coming back in the page view, and each fix only covered one pair of tools. A review on 15 October found the cause: the page view had no single place that decided what was under the pointer.

- **One widget, many readers.** All pages are one egui widget. About twenty tool modules then each read egui's raw pointer state themselves (`hover_pos`, `interact_pos`, `latest_pos`, `press_origin`) and tested it against the page's whole rectangle.
- **The raw state is the wrong source.** It knows nothing about what is drawn over the pages, and `hover_pos()` is `None` on the frame a finger or a Windows pen lifts. So taps went nowhere, and page cursors showed through the palette, the quick bar and dialogs.
- **The cursor and the press drift apart.** Each module sets the cursor on its own, and the last write in a frame wins, while different code decides who acts on the press. In two weeks that produced nine one-off ownership helpers (#822, #917, #1116, #1481, #1528, #1539, #2099, #2242, #2362).

Sixteen probe tests written for the review found eight live bugs on `main`. The fix is a page pointer router, in three PRs:

1. **This PR:** one pointer snapshot for all page modules, and a test that keeps it that way. It fixes four of the eight bugs, plus one found along the way: taps inside the form field and paragraph editors.
2. **One cursor writer:** modules say which cursor they want and how high it ranks, and the page sets it once.
3. **One hit test and press-time capture:** each module answers "what is here?" once, for both the cursor and the press, and a press owns its gesture until release or cancel.

Follow-up PRs for the other areas are coming next. PR 2 covers the cursor across every tool. PR 3 covers hit testing and gestures in comments; Fill & Sign and the placement tools; forms and Prepare a form; and Edit text. Together they fix the four remaining bugs.

This one goes first because the guard only protects `main` once it…

title: fix(inspect): report /OpenAction JavaScript in document info
author: charan-rathore
body:
A catalog `/OpenAction` with `/S /JavaScript` is the standard way a PDF runs JavaScript on open. title: M11: linearized save for Fast Web View (#2645)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2645.

PdfCraft can now save a linearized PDF, which Acrobat calls Fast Web View: a reader fetching the file over HTTP can show page 1 before the rest arrives. Parity `core.linearization` (P1) moves from planned to partial.

**cos** (`crates/cos/src/writer/linearize.rs`, new): `SaveOptions::linearize` lays a full rewrite out per ISO 32000-2 Annex F:
- linearization parameter dictionary, first-page cross-reference section and trailer
- catalog and document-level objects, then the primary hint stream (page offset, shared object and outline hint tables)
- the first page and everything it reaches, each later page with the objects only it reaches, the objects later pages share, everything else, then the main cross-reference section

Inheritable page attributes move from the page tree onto the pages. A dictionary or array several pages inherit becomes one shared object. Encryption keeps working: every object, the hint stream included, is encrypted with its new number. `is_linearized(bytes)` tells a linearized file from one an update was later appended to.

**engine / automation:**
- `Session::save_linearized_bytes`
- `doc_save` takes `linearize` (a full rewrite; refused for signed documents, like any full rewrite)
- `doc_optimize` takes `fast_web_view` (off by default, so Reduce File Size keeps writing compressed object streams)
- `doc_info` reports `linearized`

**Not in this PR:** a desktop control (Save As option, Optimizer checkbox, "Fast Web View: Yes" in Document Properties). Each new label would touch all 22 catalogs, so it is better as a small follow-up.

title: M1: saving refuses to replace a read-only file (#2658)
author: mtlcl410

## What this changes

title: M10: Windows without the print DLLs still starts (#2630)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2630 (and its earlier report #2360). `pdfcraft.exe` and `pdfcraft-cli.exe` import `windows.data.pdf.dll` (`PdfCreateRenderer`, through craft-print → winprint) and `prntvpt.dll` (PrintTicket) at load time. Trimmed Windows installations (NTLite) can lack them, and then the loader refuses to start the program at all — "windows.data.pdf.dll cannot be found" — even though only printing needs them.

- **Build** (`apps/pdfcraft{,-cli}/build.rs`, MSVC targets only): `/DELAYLOAD` both DLLs plus `delayimp.lib`, via `rustc-link-arg-bins`. They now load on the first print.
- **Runtime** (`crates/print/src/spool.rs`): a call into a missing delay-loaded DLL would end the process, so `printers()`, `submit` and `submit_with_progress` first check that both exist in `%SystemRoot%\System32`. Without them the printer list is empty and a job fails with "printing needs windows.data.pdf.dll, which this Windows installation lacks; use Save as PDF instead". When the system folder is unknown, nothing changes (the loader decides, as before). `printers` is now a wrapper instead of a re-export; its signature is unchanged.

The fix stays in this repo: craft-print and winprint are untouched. PhotoCraft has the same report (storytold/photocraft#6249) and could do the same.

title: Remove security also from files with /Encrypt inline in the trailer
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2661.

MuPDF writes the `/Encrypt` dictionary inline in the trailer. Removing it there changes no object, so `Document::is_modified()` stayed false after Remove security, and the engine took the document as unedited: the refresh after the edit, and `save_bytes`, reused the original, still-encrypted bytes, which then failed to reopen without a password. With an indirect `/Encrypt` (our files, qpdf/pikepdf) `remove_encryption` frees the object, which is why those worked. The fix counts a security change as an unsaved edit in `is_modified()`; the writer already handled the inline case correctly. Probably also what #1762 hit, though that one has no details.

Validation:
- `crates/cos/tests/encryption.rs` `removing_an_inline_encrypt_dictionary_leaves_an_unencrypted_file` (all four algorithms): fails on main (`removing security is an unsaved change`), passes here
- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` `remove_security_from_a_file_with_its_encrypt_dictionary_in_the_trailer`: fails on main (`Reopen("the document is protected by a password")`, the error in the issue), passes here
- Both build their fixture by moving our own `/Encrypt` dictionary into the trailer, so no MuPDF output is committed; I also checked by hand that a PyMuPDF AES-256 file goes through `doc_unprotect` now.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos --test encryption`, the engine protection/security tests, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Go to page brings the page into view horizontally too
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2665: the Go to page half. What Fit width should fit in continuous layout (the current page, as Acrobat does) is left for its own ticket, as the triage comment suggested.

When the page view consumes a `goto` it only set the vertical scroll offset, so the horizontal one stayed where it was. Next to a very wide page the normal pages sit far to one side, and going to one changed the counter while the page stayed out of sight. Now the page is brought into view horizontally too: a page that already shows whole, or that fills the window's width, keeps the scroll (so paging through a zoomed-in document stays on the same column); otherwise a page that fits is centred, and a wider one is scrolled just far enough to fill the window. Centring is a judgement call, happy to switch to the smallest scroll that reveals the page if you prefer.

This touches every `goto` (page turns, layout and fit changes), but in a document whose pages all show whole nothing moves.

Validation:
- `viewer::go_to_page_brings_the_page_into_view_horizontally` (three A4 pages and a 6000 pt wide one, at 100%): fails on main (`page 3 on screen` — the page is not drawn), passes here

title: fix(edit): keep the right edge of a right-aligned one-row paragraph (#2582)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #2582

## What this changes

Part of #2582 — see the caveat at the end, which is the important part.

A one-row paragraph aligned to the right margin, or level with other text's right
edge, kept its **left** edge when words were added to it. The longer text ran past
the edge it was aligned to, and then wrapped into whatever column was left over —
the "six rows in a 126pt column" from the report.

Such a row is now recognised as right-aligned and keeps its right edge, growing
leftwards and wrapping every row to that same edge. The machinery already existed
for right-to-left text (`anchored_right`); this extends it to left-to-right rows
that carry the evidence.

- **Detection needs evidence from the page.** Either the right edge sits on the
  right margin, or it lines up with another row's right edge while the row's own
  left edge lines up with nothing.
- **A row with neither keeps growing right from its left edge, as before.** That is
  deliberate: anchoring a left-aligned row on the wrong edge would move text in
  documents that are already correct, which is a worse failure than the one being
  fixed.
- **The tolerance is a few points, not the text size.** The house precedent in
  `rewrite_styled_block` uses the text size for its centred-paragraph test, but there
  the size is compared against other rows *in the same block*. Here it is compared
  against the whole page, and the size comes from the document: a font stated at
  100pt would otherwise swallow every row on the page. `an_oversized_font_does_not_
  make_every_row_look_right_aligned` is the regression test.
- **A turned row is never treated as right-aligned.** Its edges are not horizontal.
  The angle comes out of `atan2`, so the test is an epsilon rather than an exact
  zero.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-edit`, all targets)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-edit`, 136 tests)

title: fix(comments): Add a text box takes a drag that sizes the box
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2669 (point 3, the text box drag). The other four points are untouched; this is independent of #2704, which takes another point of the same issue.

Add a text box only reacted to `resp.clicked()` in `comments::page_input`, and the composer always sized the box with `text_box_rect` from the click point, so a drag did nothing. Now, as in Acrobat, a drag draws the box (shown while you drag) and the posted box keeps that size, measured in the page's view space so it lands where it was drawn with the view turned too (View ▸ Rotate View). The text wraps to the drawn width inside the padding and border its appearance uses. If the text needs more lines than the drawn height, the box grows down and moves up as needed to stay on the page; when even the whole page height is not enough, it keeps the drawn size and the text is clipped, as the appearance already does. A click, or a drag of a few pixels, still gives the box sized to its text as before. Growing rather than clipping is my call; happy to switch if you'd rather keep the drawn height exactly.

Validation:
- `a_text_box_is_sized_by_dragging`, `a_dragged_text_box_follows_a_rotated_view`, `a_dragged_text_box_wraps_inside_its_border` (tests/comments.rs): fail on main (nothing is drawn or opened after a drag), pass here; each was also checked to go red when the part it covers is taken out (move-up on the page, the clip guard, the border in the padding, the click threshold)

title: fix(forms): correct qualified-name validation and reconstruction on rename
author: Ratstack2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes two bugs in AcroForm field renaming involving fully qualified field names.

These bugs were discovered while investigating #2696, but are independent of the field-creation and UI-display problems reported there.

### 1. Incorrect duplicate-name validation

Previously, `set_props` compared a proposed partial field name against other fields' fully qualified names.

This caused two problems:

- Renaming `MASTER.first` to `last` succeeded even when `MASTER.last` already existed, producing duplicate fully qualified names.
- An unrelated top-level field named `middle` incorrectly prevented renaming `MASTER.last` to `middle`, even though `MASTER.middle` was available.

The fix validates the fully qualified name the field would have after renaming.

### 2. Incorrect full-name reconstruction

Previously, `set_props` reconstructed a field's resulting name by splitting its old full name at the last period.

This fails for malformed PDFs whose own `/T` contains a literal period, such as `ADDRESS.street`. ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2 prohibits periods in partial field names, but such documents can still occur.

Renaming this field to `street1` could update `/T` while reporting the incorrect name `ADDRESS.street1`, causing the subsequent redraw operation to fail with `NoSuchField`.

A malformed non-text `/T`, such as `/T 5`, could trigger the same issue.

The fix derives the parent prefix from the walked field name and the field's actual `/T`, matching the existing `fields()` traversal behavior.

Renaming a field to its existing name remains a no-op.

### Relationship to #2696

**Related to #2696; this PR does not resolve it.**

Specifically, this PR does not:

- Implement creation of dotted field names such as `MASTER.account_firstname` through a proper parent/child hierarchy.
- Change how fully qualified field names are displayed in the UI.
- Change `add_field` or implement broader field hierarchy construction.

Those user-facing requests remain open.

title: fix(automation): tools on a file the viewer reads fewer pages of answer instead of panicking
author: cortenburg28-arch
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2660 (the "related effects" section): `pdfcraft-cli run` with `link_list` panicked on a file whose page tree has a dangling `/Kids` entry.

The viewer stops at the dangling entry and sees 3 pages; the editing layer sees all 6. Two tools indexed the viewer's pages with a page number from the editing layer and panicked:

- `link_list` — `index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 3` (`links.rs:73`)
- `form_set_props` with `rect` on a field on one of the later pages — `the len is 3 but the index is 5` (`forms.rs:392`)

title: fix(ui): saving keeps a turned view as the pages' /Rotate (#2674)
author: cortenburg28-arch
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2674 ("pdfcraft not saving after page rotate", Windows 11).

**Reproduction.** Every *page*-rotate path already saves: `page.rotate` / `page.rotate_ccw`, the Organize buttons, Rotate Pages… and the `page_rotate` automation tool all mark the document dirty and write `/Rotate`, both for an in-place incremental save and for Save As, and the value survives a reopen. I checked this headlessly, including an inherited `/Rotate` on the page tree. What doesn't save is the **view** rotation: View ▸ Rotate View, Ctrl+Shift+Plus / Minus, and the rotate button in the page toolbar (the only rotate control on the main view). They turned the display only. The document stayed clean, Save wrote nothing new, and the file reopened upright. That matches the report.

**Fix (ui-egui only).**
- `DocView::unsaved_turn(doc)` returns the view's turn when it is non-zero and the document allows page changes.
- A turned view now counts as unsaved work: the tab's dirty dot, the close and quit prompts (`has_unsaved_work`), and the on-disk-change reload guard.
- Before the bytes are taken, Save and Save As (native and wasm) apply one undoable **Rotate Pages** edit to every page by the view's turn. They then set the view back upright, so the page looks the same and the file opens the way it was shown. If that edit fails, nothing is written and the user is told why.
- A document that refuses page changes keeps the turn display-only, as before.

This departs from Acrobat, whose turned view is never saved; whether PdfCraft should do this is an open question (see the end of this description). The `view.rotate-view` parity entry no longer claims "without changing the file", and its notes say so.

title: fix(edit): keep a one-row centred title centred when it grows (#2581)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #2581

## What this changes

Fixes #2581. A one-row centred title (centre 306) lost its centring when edited: it kept its left edge and grew rightwards (centre drifted to 398.025), and wrapped rows all started at that old edge. The single-style path stretches width to the page's right margin, and centring detection needed several ragged rows, so a one-row title was never recognised. A new `is_centred` helper (`text_regions.rs`) is the single source of truth for both paths; a centred block with no explicit width or alignment is centred in the box it already sits in.

title: M3: closing PdfCraft while minimized no longer saves a 0 x 0 window
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Closing PdfCraft while it is minimized (from the taskbar's "Close window", Alt+F4 on the taskbar button, or a sign-out) saved a window the next start could hardly use. eframe stores the window's settings just before `App::save`, from the window as it is then; Windows reports a minimized window as 0 × 0 at (-32000, -32000). egui-winit then opens the next start at its 64-point floor (`clamp_size_to_sane_values`) and clamps the position into the screen's corner. Found while testing on a 6K display at 225%: a 172 × 223 px window at (0, 0), and the 820 × 520 minimum size did not apply to the restored size. Reproduced on current main by minimizing and closing.

- `window_state::WindowState` (desktop only) remembers the settings eframe stored while the window was shown, starting from those it started with. In `App::save`, while the window is minimized, it puts them back; if there are none, it removes the entry so the next start opens at the default size.
- On the first frame whose size is known, a shown window at egui's floor in both directions (only reachable from such settings) gets 1440 × 920 points, at most nine tenths of the monitor, and the broken settings it started with are dropped. So people who already have such settings get a usable window once.
- `apps/pdfcraft` seeds the state from `cc.storage`. Nothing changes for a window closed while shown.

title: Layers panel: Reset to Initial Visibility
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Layers panel: Reset to Initial Visibility

The Layers panel now has a "…" Layer options menu with Reset to Initial Visibility, as in Acrobat's Layers options menu. It puts every layer back to how the file opens: the default configuration in `/OCProperties /D`, meaning BaseState, then `/ON`, then `/OFF`, which wins. title: Extract RTL lines with numbers and punctuation in logical order
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2667

## Cause
`reverse_rtl` only reversed unbroken runs of strong right-to-left glyphs, with at most one blank glyph allowed inside a run. A digit or a neutral mark such as ':' or '.' ended the run, so each Hebrew or Arabic word was reversed on its own. The words themselves stayed in the left-to-right order they were drawn in, and the punctuation stayed at the visual end of the line.

## Fix
`reverse_rtl` now runs a simplified UAX #9 pass over each line's glyphs and word gaps. The line is treated as right-to-left when it has more right-to-left glyphs than left-to-right ones. A separator between digits joins the number, and so does a %/currency sign next to it. A number that follows left-to-right text becomes left-to-right. Neutrals take the direction of the text on both sides, or the line's direction when the sides differ. Then runs are reversed by level, highest first, so numbers keep their left-to-right digit order and word gaps move with the glyphs. A regression test covers Hebrew with a number, Hebrew with punctuation, Arabic with a decimal number, and a left-to-right line with one Hebrew word.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtl_line_with_number_and_punctuation_reads_in_logical_order`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib rtl_line_with_number_and_punctuation_reads_in_logical_order`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Glyph mirroring for brackets (N0/L4), explicit embeddings, and the difference between Arabic-Indic and European digits (AN vs EN) are not modelled. Lines with no right-to-left text keep their order.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Combine files from Finder (macOS): a Quick Action the app installs, whose list of files opens as one Combine (#585, follows #2541)
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What does it change?

The Finder half of #2541 (#585): **"Combine files in PdfCraft" under Finder's right-click ▸ Quick Actions** on macOS. Select PDFs or pictures, choose it, and Combine files opens with them listed in order, in the running PdfCraft or a new one. Nothing is combined until Combine is pressed, as on Windows and Linux.

This branch is stacked on #2541 (`pr/combine-right-click`): the diff shows both until that one merges. Its own change is one new file, `apps/pdfcraft/src/finder_combine.rs` (409 lines, 4 tests), and three lines in `main.rs` and `apple_events.rs`.

## Why a Quick Action, and not the other ways

Finder does not start an app with the files as arguments, so the `--combine` route of Explorer and the Linux desktop action does not exist here. The ways that do:

- **A Services provider (`NSServices` in the app's Info.plist + an Objective-C method).** The proper one, but the provider is an Objective-C class with a selector that Finder calls, which means `objc2` and `unsafe`; this workspace forbids `unsafe`, and `fmv_macos_events` (what the app already uses for Apple events) delivers only Open and Quit. Ruled out by the workspace's rule, not by taste.
- **A Finder Sync extension or an app extension (Action extension).** Needs a separate signed extension target and a developer-signed bundle to be loaded; this app ships ad-hoc signed, so it would load for nobody.
- **AppleScript / `osascript` from a Services menu item.** Still needs a Services provider, or a Quick Action.
- **A Quick Action (Automator workflow in `~/Library/Services`).** What macOS offers for exactly this: Finder lists `.workflow` services from that folder, no signing, no extension, no `unsafe`. Its one "Run Shell Script" step receives the selected paths as arguments, writes them one a line to `files.pdfcraft-combine` in a fresh `pdfcraft-combine.*` folder in the user's temporary folder, and runs `open -b ai.storyteller.pdfcraft` on that file. The open arrives as an ordinary Ap…

View ▸ Show/Hide ▸ Cursor coordinates shows where the pointer is on the page, as Acrobat's Cursor Coordinates panel does.

Acrobat shows a small panel with the pointer's X and Y, counted from the top-left corner of the page and given in the unit set in Preferences. The values are in the Preferences unit and are counted in view space, so a shifted crop box, /Rotate and /UserUnit are already taken into account: X/Y measure the page as you see it, not PDF user space. It is also the `view.cursor_coordinates` command in the palette and over `ui.command`. There's no automation tool, since it only reads the pointer, the same as `view.page-size-hover`. Line weights, which shared its row in ui-parity.md, are still planned.

title: Keep leading spaces and tabs when wrapping plain text into a PDF
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:79 (wrap_with), called from crates/create/src/lib.rs:set_text` (no existing issue): Creating a PDF from plain text drops leading spaces and tabs, so indentation is lost.

## Cause
`wrap_with` split each paragraph on ' ' and used `line.is_empty()` to mean that no word had started the line. A leading space yields an empty first word, so the next word replaced the candidate instead of being appended. Every leading space, and every tab that `set_text` had already expanded to 4 spaces, was dropped.

## Fix
`wrap_with` now tracks whether a word has started the line with a separate `fresh` flag, so leading spaces are kept. When a word is too long for the width, indentation-only text before it is dropped and no whitespace-only line is emitted. One leading space and several therefore behave the same, as they did before.

## Verified
- Regression tests `wrap_keeps_leading_spaces`, `text_keeps_leading_spaces_and_tabs`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts --lib wrap_keeps_leading_spaces && cargo test -p pdfcraft-create text_keeps_leading_spaces_and_tabs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Wrapping of over-long words on lines without leading whitespace, the CJK measuring path, and tab expansion in `set_text` are unchanged. Over-long words on indented lines now start without the indentation that precedes them, as described above. The output for lines without leading whitespace is unchanged.

title: M7: a paragraph number keeps naming the paragraph text_paragraphs listed (#2516)
author: hcchung1
body:
## What this changes

Paragraph numbers are positions in a list regrouped from geometry on every read. An edit that makes a paragraph's last row close enough to its neighbour merges the two, so the next `text_edit` by the number `text_paragraphs` returned rewrote a different paragraph and its text was lost (#2516).

- After `text_paragraphs`, `text_edit` and `text_edit_layout` resolve a number against that listing: the paragraph is found again by its text and box (`BlockKey`, `block_overlapping` in `pdfcraft-edit`). - Editing paragraph 3 and then paragraph 1 still edits the two the listing showed, and the same paragraph can be edited repeatedly by its number.
- An edit's result reports `stale_paragraphs`, the numbers that no longer exist. Listing again renumbers the page. Without a listing a number is a position, as before.

title: fix(ui): Save asks where to keep an Apple Mail attachment
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2751.

`is_mail_temp_copy` only knew Outlook's cache folders, so a PDF opened from Apple Mail was saved in place. Mail opens attachments from `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.mail/Data/Library/Mail Downloads/<UUID>/` inside its sandbox container, where other apps can't write, and the staging file in `write_atomically` fails with EPERM. This adds that folder to the same rule #601 introduced for Outlook, so Save asks where to keep the file and leaves Mail's copy alone. Thanks for the clear report and the pointer to the existing rule.

I kept it to the folder match and left out the second suggestion in the issue (falling back to Save As on any permission error): that changes how every failed save behaves, so it seemed better as its own decision. Happy to add it here if you prefer.

title: M4: the Bookmarks panel highlights the current page's bookmark
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The Bookmarks panel now highlights the bookmark of the page you're reading, as Acrobat does.

Acrobat's Bookmarks panel has a "Highlight Current Bookmark" option: as you scroll, the bookmark for the part of the document on screen is highlighted. Here the highlighted bookmark is the last one in document order whose destination is on the current page or an earlier one, so a page between two bookmarks belongs to the earlier one. It moves as the page changes and never expands or collapses anything. Bookmarks with no destination are skipped. When the current bookmark is inside a collapsed one, the collapsed row the reader can see gets the highlight instead. I couldn't confirm that last detail in Acrobat's public docs, so happy to switch if you know it behaves differently. The row uses the panel's existing selected wash and reports itself as selected to accessibility, as page thumbnails already do. One related fix: a bookmark whose action is not GoTo (GoToR, URI, …) no longer reads its /D as a page of this file. Before, a GoToR bookmark pointing at page 1 of another file jumped to page 1 of this one, and it would also have counted as current here; links already made this check. Left out: Acrobat's Options toggle for turning the highlight off (it is always on here).

title: fix(engine): validate signed XFA forms as the file was read (#2759)
author: kavishkashehan726-sudo
body:
Opening an XFA form appends PdfCraft's own revisions to the working file: the dynamic layout, the field values taken from the XFA data, and what the open scripts change. Signatures were then validated against that working file, so a certified (DocMDP P=2) form opened untouched was reported invalid, "altered since signed (pages added or removed, comments)", before the user had changed anything. This is the symptom the IRCC IMM forms show.

Keep the file as read for a signed document whose opening appended revisions, and validate the signatures against it while the working state is still just the opened one: on open, on trust changes, after undo back to it, and after Revert. Once the user edits or saves, the file Save writes is judged as before, open-time revisions included, so the verdict never hides what saving will write.

Part of storytold/pdfcraft#2759: the false "altered" on open. The trust lists and TSA trust it also asks for are separate problems.

title: M9: sign in the web build with a PKCS #12 file (sign.web-signing)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

The web build (`apps/pdfcraft-web`) can now sign. Until now its Sign dialog had no file picker and its
last step did nothing, so a .p12 could not be used in the browser at all.

- **The same Sign flow as the desktop.** Digitally sign and Certify, visible or invisible, a new or an
  existing field, PAdES B-B (`ETSI.CAdES.detached`). Configure New Digital ID ▸ Browse… opens the
  browser's file picker. The .p12/.pfx (at most 1 MiB) is held in memory for the session, listed as
  `browser:<name>`, and never written to the settings; its password is asked at each signing, as for a
  file on disk. The signed file goes where the web build's saves go: a download
  (`<name>_signed.pdf`), or the embedding page with `?host=parent`.
- **RSA through Web Crypto.** ECDSA P-256/P-384 keys sign in Rust as on the desktop (RustCrypto,
  RFC 6979). RSA keys, which most issued IDs are, sign through the browser's Web Crypto
  (`RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5`, the key imported as not extractable), because ADR-0009 keeps the `rsa` crate to
  verifying (RUSTSEC-2023-0071). Browsers offer Web Crypto only in secure contexts, so RSA signing
  needs HTTPS or localhost and says so in the dialog; ECDSA works anywhere.
- **Signing in two steps (engine).** Web Crypto answers asynchronously, so `Session::signing_request`
  runs the signer with an `ExternalKey` that only records what it is asked to sign (the CMS signed
  attributes), and `Session::complete_signing` checks the value it is handed against the certificate
  and runs the signer again with a key that answers with that value, for exactly those bytes. The
  signing time is pinned in the request, and an edit to the document in between refuses the second
  step. The result is byte for byte the file one-step `Session::sign` writes (tested for RSA and ECDSA).
  ECDSA may come back as DER or raw `r ‖ s`; the file gets DER.
- **Headless: `sign_prepare` / `sign_finish`.** The two steps as tools, for any key PdfCraft can't use
  itself (an …

title: M11: Preflight with profiles, single checks, results, reports and safe fixups (optimize.preflight)
author: guillehr2
body:
**Stacked on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR** (`feat/pdfx-validate`, "M11: verify PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4"): the PDF/X profiles wrap that verifier, so this branch carries its commit too. Review that one first; once it merges, this PR's diff is only the Preflight commit. Both are rebased on `main` at f0c9901c.

## What this changes

PdfCraft gets Preflight: pick a profile, run it over the document, read the results by severity and check, go to each problem, fix what is safe to fix, and save a report. Seven checklist features move from planned to partial: `optimize.preflight`, `optimize.preflight-profiles`, `optimize.preflight-single-checks`, `optimize.preflight-results`, `optimize.preflight-reports`, `optimize.preflight-fix` and `optimize.preflight-single-fixups`.

- **Engine (`pdfcraft_preflight::profiles`, re-exported as `pdfcraft_engine::preflight`):**
  - A `Profile` is a named set of checks, each with a severity (error, warning, information). Profiles and every check's parameters are serde data, so a custom profile is a JSON object; `Profile::validate` refuses what a profile from outside may get wrong (no checks, more than 256, negative or non-finite thresholds, an unknown level or version).
  - `run(doc, profile, host)` returns results grouped by check: status (passed, found, skipped with a reason), and each hit's message (wording and values apart, for translation), 0-based page, object number, box in user space, the verifier's rule id or clause, details, and the fixup that addresses it. Nothing is changed.

title: M11: Save as PDF/X (PDF/X-1a, -3, -4) and PDF/A levels u and a (optimize.pdfx-convert, optimize.pdfa-accessible-levels)
author: guillehr2
body:
> **Stacked on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR** (`feat/pdfx-validate`, "M11: verify PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4 (optimize.pdfx-validate)"). This branch is cut from it and checks each conversion with that verifier. Review and merge that one first; this diff then shrinks to the conversion.

## What this changes

Save as PDF/X ships, and Save as PDF/A learns levels u and a and CMYK output intents. Both work the same way. The conversion runs on a copy of the document, and the copy is kept only when PdfCraft's own verifier then finds nothing. Otherwise the document is left exactly as it was, and the dialog (or the tool) lists what stands in the way. **A file that claims a level and fails it is never written.** That is a behaviour change for Save as PDF/A, which until now wrote the PDF/A identification and left the problems it couldn't fix (a text document with an unembedded Helvetica came out "PDF/A-2b").

`optimize.pdfx-convert` and `optimize.pdfa-accessible-levels` move from planned to partial. `optimize.pdfa-convert` and `optimize.output-intents` stay partial, with their notes rewritten.

### Save as PDF/X (`crates/preflight/src/conform.rs`)

Levels: PDF/X-1a:2001, PDF/X-1a:2003, PDF/X-3:2002, PDF/X-3:2003 and PDF/X-4.

- **Printing condition.** It becomes the one `GTS_PDFX` output intent:
  - with none chosen, the document's own PDF/X output intent is kept;
  - otherwise a characterization in the ICC registry, named without a profile (PDF/X-1a and -3 only). FOGRA39 is the default; FOGRA51, FOGRA52, FOGRA47, CGATS TR 006, CGATS TR 001, JC200103 and IFRA26 are offered;
  - or the user's own ICC profile, embedded. PDF/X-4 and colour conversion need one.

  The profile must be an output (`prtr`) profile, and CMYK for PDF/X-1a. Intents with profiles share one object.
- **Identification:**

title: XFA: explicit data bindings, keep rules, and hiding one row at a time
author: ysrdevs
body:
## Summary

The three XFA leftovers that were worth doing, closing the series on the layout side: explicit data bindings, `keep` rules, and hiding one row of a repeating subform without hiding them all.

### Explicit data bindings (`<bind match="…" ref="…">`)

Designer forms bind fields to data nodes other than their own name more often than the default-binding-only model allowed: a field bound to `$record.header.customer`, a wrapper subform marked "none" so its children bind under the parent, a repeating subform bound to `$record.order.line[*]`, a field bound "global" to the first node of its name. Until now those read nothing and wrote their values under the field's own name, which Acrobat then ignored.

* `model::Bind` (`Once`, `None`, `Global`, `DataRef(ref)`) on every object's `Common`, parsed from `<bind>`.
* `data::Binder` is the one resolver (`data_path(tpl, data, som) -> Option<DataPath>` is its one-call form; it was `data_path(tpl, som) -> DataPath`). It walks the template along the SOM path as before and applies each object's binding: `none` on a subform is transparent (its children bind under the parent's node), `none` on a field is `None` (no data node), `global` finds the first node of the name in the data (by name when there is no data), `dataRef` resolves `$record` (the data's first child; the root subform's name without data), `$data`, `$.`/relative, `[n]`, `[*]` (the instance's own index) and `a..b` (first descendant). Anything the resolver doesn't follow (`$form`, predicates, functions) binds by name with a parse warning, so a value still has somewhere to go. A `Binder` remembers the paths of one layout or live form and indexes the data by element name once, so `global` and `..` lookups don't walk the data per object.
* `Binder::instances` counts a repeating subform's instances at the node it binds to, so a table bound to `order.line[*]` gets one row per `line`; a subform bound to nothing or to one node (no `[*]`) keeps its `occur` count.
* Every …

title: M3: the Pages panel follows the current page
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The Pages panel now follows the current page, so the highlighted thumbnail never stays out of sight.

In Acrobat, when the page changes (scrolling, Page Down, Go to page, a bookmark), the page thumbnails panel scrolls to show the current page's thumbnail. This PR does the same: when the current page changes and its thumbnail is out of view, the panel scrolls just enough to show it. It doesn't recentre on every page change, so a thumbnail already in view, or one you just clicked, stays where it is. A page change while you're dragging thumbnails doesn't move the panel either. Turning the wheel or dragging the scroll bar already beats a scroll-to in egui, and the change then counts as seen, so the panel doesn't jump once you let go. I went with the minimal scroll rather than centring the thumbnail. Happy to switch if you'd rather centre it, as #2781 describes.

Closes #2781

title: fix(organize): preserve page labels across extract, split, and combine (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Addresses #2670

## Problem
When extracting pages (`extract_pages` / `page_extract`), splitting a document (`split`), or combining documents (`combine`, `combine_selected`, `Combiner`, and `combine_grouped`), the source document's `/PageLabels` number tree was not carried over to the resulting document(s). Extracted, split, or combined documents lost custom page labels (such as Roman front matter `i`, `ii`, `iii` or prefixed section numbers `A-1`, `A-2`) and reverted to default `1, 2, 3...` numbering.

## Root Cause
`extract_pages`, `Combiner`, and `combine_grouped_with` in `crates/organize/src/import.rs` constructed new `Document` instances and copied pages, document info, outlines, attachments, and PDF/X output intents, but never projected or wrote `/PageLabels` ranges from the source document(s) into the output catalog.

## Solution
- Added `collect_page_labels` and `finish_page_labels` (along with shared `push_merged_range` deduplication) in `crates/organize/src/labels.rs` to project each selected run of source pages onto its destination page indices:
  - Preserves each page's resolved style, prefix, and starting number (`first_range.number(src_start)`) at the start of each contiguous source page run, plus any interior range transitions within the run.
  - Coalesces adjacent ranges that continue the previous range's numbering sequence (or share the same prefix under `LabelStyle::None`).
  - Synthesizes an explicit default decimal range (`1, 2, ...`) for unlabelled sources or leading pages prior to the first `/PageLabels` entry when combined with labelled sources so earlier labels do not bleed into unlabelled pages, while leaving outputs untouched when no source carries `/PageLabels`.
- Wired `collect_page_labels` and `finish_page_labels` into `extract_pages` (which also powers `split`), `Combiner::add` / `Combiner::finish_with_renames`, and `combine_grouped_with`.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets …

title: M7: anchor a watermark to an edge or corner, with a distance in page units
author: Byxis
body:
> **Prerequisite:** this branch contains the commit of #1083 (repeat as a grid), which the anchor builds on. Merge #1083 first, or merge this one and #1083 is included with it. #1165 is not needed and not included.

## What this changes

A watermark could only move by an offset from the page centre, in points. A corner placement meant working out half the page minus the mark's size by hand, and it was wrong as soon as page sizes varied.

Acrobat places a mark by a vertical anchor (Top, Center, Bottom) and a horizontal one (Left, Center, Right), plus a distance. This does the same.

- **Engine (`pdfcraft-edit`).** `Watermark::anchor` (`Anchor`, `HorizontalAnchor`, `VerticalAnchor`). Centre/centre, the default, is the old placement exactly. From an edge, the distance is the gap between the page edge and the matching edge of the mark (turned by its rotation), positive inward. From the centre it keeps today's meaning (+x right, +y up). One calculation (`anchored_centre`) feeds drawing, validation and `watermark_centres`.
- **Repeat (#1083).** The anchor places one tile, the one the grid is built from, and the grid repeats outward from it, so a corner anchor puts a whole tile in that corner.
- **Page as shown.** It is measured on the page as displayed, so `/Rotate`, `CropBox` and `/UserUnit` hold: bottom-right is the bottom-right you see.
- **Tool.** `doc_watermark` takes `horizontal_from` (`left|center|right`) and `vertical_from` (`top|center|bottom`), default `center`. Any other value is an argument error. `offset_x` / `offset_y` become the distances. Existing calls keep working.
- **Dialog.** A 3×3 grid picks the anchor (Acrobat's nine combinations). The distances show in pt, in, mm, cm or picas; the engine and the tool always hold points. No new strings to translate: the labels reuse words the 11 catalogs already have, so no `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes change.

Fixes #2527.

title: fix(print): read the printers at startup so the Print dialog opens with them listed
author: hade0ntema
body:
## What this changes

On the desktop app the printer list was read in the background only when the Print dialog opened. On Windows that read can take seconds (it asks each driver for its capabilities), so the first Print after launch showed **"Looking for printers…"** with no printers to choose from.

The app now starts the same background read at startup (`PdfCraftApp::preload_printers`, called from `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` right after `printer_source` is set). title: M9: signed appearances show their real validation state (#79)
author: chiranjeevi-max

Now it draws the real one. - **When:** the widget's `/N` draws exactly one Form whose resources hold both `n1` and `n3`. title: fix(select): a picked picture that is edited away no longer leaves its highlight behind
author: hade0ntema
body:
## What this changes

With the Select tool, clicking a picture picks it and draws a blue highlight over it (`image_pick`). The pick was only cleared by Escape, a drag/double click, or another click. title: M7: fix Thai editing and offer a bundled fallback font
author: dekkeng
body:
## What this changes

Existing Thai paragraph edits can fail when the PDF embeds only a source subset. For matching Noto Sans Thai, paragraph rewriting tried to embed the approved variable face through the static-font path. For another unavailable Thai source family, the app required a full font but offered no bundled replacement in the document-font menu.

Reuse the existing HarfRust Thai shaper and bounded Type 3 outline writer. Complete matching Noto Sans Thai subsets automatically while keeping usable complete source programs first. The inline editor prefers complete matching Thai layout/coverage so vowels and tones stay in one shaping run. Use OpenType mark/mkmk positions and accept GPOS-only Thai fonts: GSUB is optional for this script.

Also offer **Noto Sans Thai** in the existing document-font menu and `text_fonts` inventory. Explicitly selecting it replaces the paragraph or selected range without installing a font. Headless clients pass the returned `builtin:thai` choice to `text_edit`/`text_edit_layout`; its token avoids collisions with source resource names and is never saved as a PDF resource. Missing-font errors name the source family and point to this choice or loading the complete original font. Keeping source fonts never silently substitutes another family.

title: Tests: make timing-dependent render and UI tests deterministic
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Seven tests failed at random on slow or busy machines, on PRs and on `main` alike (FreeBSD run 38834256439 at 5fdd820b). Each one assumed something would finish within a deadline or a fixed number of frames. They now count the work, or wait for the state they check, so they give the same answer on every machine. No assertion was removed or loosened, and none of them retries.

**pdfcraft-render**

- `raster::tests::spot_colour_images_run_their_tint_transform_once_per_sample_value` gave a 2048 × 2048 spot-colour image 10 s to draw. Patch 28 made it take about 20 ms here, but a busy CI VM still went past 10 s. The test now counts the runs: a new vendored hayro-interpret patch (34), `color::tint_transform_runs()`, counts the colours a thread has run through a Separation or DeviceN tint transform. It is a thread-local cell, bumped once per `convert_f32` batch. The test checks there are exactly 256 runs (one per possible 8-bit sample value) where there used to be 4,194,304 (one per pixel), and checks both colours as before. The render runs on the test thread, with no deadline.
- `raster::tests::shadings_with_large_sampled_functions_paint_quickly` gave 30 paints of a 2,097,152-sample ramp 10 s. Here they take 0.14 s with patch 31's flat table and 14 s with the old hash map, so the deadline barely caught the regression on this machine, and a busy FreeBSD VM went past it with the fix in place. No counter can tell the two apart, because both read every sample on every build, and the hash map only made each sample cost about a hundred times more. So the test now compares two times taken on the same thread instead of using a deadline. title: fix(edit): show backgrounds on pages that paint their own white backdrop
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

A YouTube review showed **Add Background** "not working". It works on plain pages, but on a page that first fills itself with opaque white (browsers' Save as PDF, print drivers, many generators), the background is drawn behind that fill and is completely hidden. A near-white default colour (`[1, 1, 0.85]`) made it look broken even where it did work.

- **`pdfcraft-edit`: new `backdrop` module.** Strict detection: one `re`, axis-aligned, opaque white in DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK, painted before anything else, covering the crop box (clip and ExtGState honoured). To replace it, that one fill operator becomes `n` in a **per-page copy** of its content stream, and the original stream object is left untouched for other pages that share it. The copy carries `/PCBackdrop << /Original ref /At /Len >>`, so **Remove background restores the original**, but only if the copy is still exactly what we wrote. An edit made since is kept. A page-sized picture (a scan) is reported only, never touched.
- `Background` gains `replace_backdrop` (default on). The default colour is a light yellow that is visible on screen.
- **Dialog:** shows "N pages paint their own white backdrop… Replace it" (ticked) and a warning for scanned pages. It checks 24 pages a frame with one page-tree walk per frame, cached by doc id and edit generation. Measured in release on synthetic flat page trees: a frame costs 0.8 ms at 1,000 pages, 4.5 ms at 5,000 and 19 ms at 20,000, and the whole check takes 17 ms, 0.95 s and 16 s. title: M10: running text is not a table row in Word, HTML and PowerPoint export (#2806)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2806. On the FIDE Women's Grand Prix 2024–25 regulations (the public file the report describes, `calendar.fide.com/event_files/2551/Regulations.pdf`, 14 pages, Microsoft Print to PDF), Word export lost text that `pdfcraft-cli text` extracts. The cause is table detection in `crates/export` (`tables()`), shared by Word, HTML and PowerPoint export:

- **A link inside a sentence became table columns.** The link in 6.3.2 is drawn in a second font and colour, so the page's blocks are `6.3. 2. All content shown at` · `http` · `s` · `://women` · `g` · `randprix.fide.com`, each starting where the last one ends. Two of the pieces (`s`, `g`) start within the column tolerance of the link in 6.3.3, so they formed a "column".
- **A paragraph's lines became a cell beside its first line.** In 6.3.3 the block holding the paragraph's later lines (`is managed in a professional way …`) has a box that reaches up into the first line, so it overlapped `6.3. 3. … that` and joined its row as a second column. When the table was built, the first line's cell spanned that column and the paragraph text in it was dropped.

The export put "All content shown at" and "g" in table cells, pushed the rest of 6.3.2 after the table, and lost "is managed in a professional way … capable of handling … Statistics …" entirely.

Two rules decide whether a row counts as a table row:

1. **A block that continues another adds no column.** A block that starts where another block on the same line ends (up to half its font size later, or 1 pt earlier for rounding) is the same line of text running on: a link, a change of font, a superscript. It still sits in its row, but it doesn't make the row multi-column. Found page-wide over blocks sorted by their right edge (binary search, at most 64 candidates each).
2. **The cells of a table row don't overlap.** Blocks of a row that overlap by more than the column tolerance are a paragraph's lines, not cells side by side.

title: fix(cli): info, text, render and audit take the owner password of R2–R4 files
author: enesoglu
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli info`, `text`, `render` and `audit` now accept the **owner** password of revision 2–4 files (RC4-40, RC4-128, AES-128), as `run doc_open` already did. Before, they failed with "the password is incorrect". This is item 8 of #2670 only; the other items are covered by #2799, #2789, #2744, #2687 and #2679 or remain open.

**Cause.** The renderer (vendored hayro) authenticates only the *user* password of R2–R4 files. `Session::open` works around that by handing the renderer the user password that owner authentication recovers (`pdfcraft-crypt`, Algorithm 7). The CLI subcommands passed the typed password straight to `inspect` and `PageRenderer`.

**Fix.** New `pdfcraft_engine::render_password_for(bytes, password)` returns the password the renderer takes: the recovered user password for an R2–R4 owner password, otherwise the password as given. `Session::open` and the new function share one helper (`recovered_render_password`), so there is one source of truth. The CLI uses it for `inspect`/`PageRenderer` only. The engine session and the cos document still get the typed password, so the owner password still lifts copy restrictions in `text`.

Refs #2670 (item 8 only — the issue covers several separate problems, so this PR does not close it).

title: Drop XML-illegal control characters from PDF/A XMP packet
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/preflight/src/xmp.rs:37` (no existing issue): PDF/A conversion writes XML-illegal control characters from /Info into the XMP packet.

## Cause
`xmp::esc` only replaced & < > ", so C0 control characters in /Info values (Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Producer, Creator) were copied into the XMP packet. XML 1.0 forbids those characters, so the packet was malformed and the PDF/A output invalid.

## Fix
`xmp::esc` now drops the characters XML 1.0 forbids before escaping. These are the C0 controls other than tab, LF and CR, plus U+FFFE and U+FFFF. This matches `export::esc` and `organize::pdfx::esc`. The regression test builds a document with control characters in each /Info field and checks the packet.

## Verified
- Regression test `xmp_packet_drops_xml_illegal_characters_from_info`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight --lib xmp_packet_drops_xml_illegal_characters_from_info`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
DEL (U+007F) is legal in XML 1.0 and is still passed through. Reading XMP back (`unescape`) and the other XMP fields are unchanged.
