title: fix(annot): drop Apple Markup's stale copy when a page's annotations change
author: Kiwi-Kwi
body:
## What this changes

A page signed with **iOS Markup** carries Apple's private copy of its markup: `/AAPL:PPK` and `/AAPL:PPKHash` on the page, and `/AAPL:AKExtras` on each Markup annotation. After PdfCraft adds a signature to such a page, iOS (seen on iOS 26.6.1) displays the Markup signature **twice**: in its own place and over the signature PdfCraft added. Every other viewer we tried, PdfCraft included, renders the file correctly. The saved PDF is valid; Apple is drawing from its now-stale private copy.

`set_annots` is the single place where a page's annotation list changes (add, delete, reply, links, inline-dict promotion). It now removes those three keys from the page and from the page's annotations first, so Apple falls back to drawing every annotation from its appearance stream, as other viewers do. The Markup annotation itself, its `/AP` and its flags are kept, and Apple keys are only touched when present (no extra objects in an incremental save otherwise).

## How you verified it

On a real document (signed with iOS Markup, then signed in PdfCraft 0.8.0), opened on an iPhone:

| variant | iPhone shows |
|---|---|
| as saved by 0.8.0 | Markup signature twice ❌ |
| page `/AAPL:PPK` + `/AAPL:PPKHash` removed | Markup signature twice ❌ |
| page keys **and** the annotation's `/AAPL:AKExtras` removed (what this PR does) | both signatures correct ✅ |
| PdfCraft signature flattened | both signatures correct ✅ |

So the page-level keys alone are not enough; `/AAPL:AKExtras` has to go too.

title: fix(render): clip extracted text to the page CropBox (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2670 (item 5: **Text outside the CropBox**).

When a page's `CropBox` is smaller than its `MediaBox`, `hayro::render_into` clips visual rendering to `page.intersected_crop_box()` transformed by `page.initial_transform(true)`, but `TextDevice` recorded every glyph drawn anywhere on the page without checking whether its view-space bounding box intersected the visible crop region. As a result, `pdfcraft-cli text`, `text_extract`, `text_search`, and the UI text layer extracted and matched hidden text outside the `CropBox`.

- In `TextDevice::draw_glyph`, skip glyphs whose view-space bounding box has no positive overlap with `self.page` (`b.x0.max(self.page.x0) >= b.x1.min(self.page.x1) || b.y0.max(self.page.y0) >= b.y1.min(self.page.y1)`), while keeping glyphs that lie inside or straddle the `CropBox` boundary.

body:
Prepare a form: Use Current Properties as New Defaults for form fields

In Acrobat's Prepare Form you can right-click a field and choose Use Current Properties as New Defaults. title: Page box: page labels with the physical position as a secondary hint
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Since 0.8.0 the page box already prefers the page's label over the physical index, but the label machinery behind it had two gaps: the label for a page was derived ad hoc where it was needed, and the box gave no idea where you are in the document when the label differs from the physical position ("page 35" in a bundle with roman-numbered front matter means two different pages depending on where you look).

This pulls the label computation into a testable core and finishes the indicator:

- `LabelRange` / `label_for_page` in `pdfcraft-cos` handle the `/PageLabels` number tree end to end: styles `D`, `r`, `R`, `a`, `A`, a textual `/P` prefix, and `/St` start values per range — the document from the issue comes out as `i, ii, 1, 2, 3`;
- `render inspect` and the page box now share that one implementation instead of deriving labels twice;
- where the label differs from the physical position, the count under the box shows the physical position too (`1 (3 of 180)` style: the hint reads `3 of 180`), and stays the plain total when they agree.

Tests: the label table for all five styles plus prefix and start offsets (failed on main for the `i`/`ii` case — the old path produced `1` for the third page where a label belongs), and the hint's four cases.

Fixes #2834

title: Redaction audit: an opaque filled Square annotation over text is a cover
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A `/Square` annotation with a black interior colour is what markup tools produce when someone draws a filled rectangle over text instead of redacting — macOS Preview's rectangle shape with a fill, for example. The audit only looked at `/Redact` annotations, so the text under such a box stayed extractable and `audit` reported the document clean.

Annotation covers now come in two kinds: an unapplied `/Redact` keeps its existing `UnappliedMark` finding, and an opaque filled `/Square` (its `/IC` fill darker than the COVER_CONTRAST threshold against the line's colour) counts as a cover over any text line it hides, reported as `CoveredText` like an in-content rectangle. Translucent fills are not flagged, and the module's documented limits (unrotated user space, `/Rotate` pages) apply to these rectangles as before.

Test: the issue's shape — a line of text with a black-filled Square over one name — produces a finding; it fails on main and passes here. The audit suite passes.

Fixes #2787

title: Treat CRLF as a single line break in fonts::wrap
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:79 (wrap_with: `text.split(['\n', '\r'])`)` (no existing issue): fonts::wrap treats a CRLF line break as two breaks, so Windows-style text gets a blank line between every line.

## Cause
`wrap_with` split paragraphs on every `'\n'` and every `'\r'` separately, so a `\r\n` pair counted as two breaks and produced an empty paragraph. Callers that don't normalise line endings, such as multiline form field appearances and auto font sizing, drew Windows-style text double-spaced.

## Fix
`wrap_with` now turns `\r\n` into `\n` before splitting. A CRLF pair is one break, and a lone `\r` or lone `\n` still breaks. The regression test covers CRLF, lone CR, lone LF, two CRLF pairs in a row, and `\n\r`, which stays two breaks.

## Verified
- Regression test `crlf_is_one_line_break`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts --lib crlf_is_one_line_break`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The callers in `crates/forms/src/appearance.rs` and `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` are unchanged, because they get the fix through `wrap_with`. The test exercises `fonts::wrap` directly, not the form-appearance path.

title: ui: fix single page scroll flashing and prefetch adjacent pages
author: anishguduru
body:
When scrolling with the wheel in non-continuous (single-page or two-page) view, turning pages caused an empty canvas flash followed by a blank "Rendering…" placeholder.

This resolves the issue by:
1. In-Frame Row Recomputation: Updating the active row bounds in-frame immediately after mouse wheel paging updates `view.current`, ensuring the target page is laid out and drawn immediately in the very same frame without an empty background flash.
2. Adjacent Page Prefetching: Prefetching adjacent pages in non-continuous layouts within the texture cache budget, ensuring rasters are already rendered before coming into view.
3. Regression Tests: Adding regression tests in `view.rs` proving immediate turn rendering without empty frames (`single_page_wheel_turn_renders_new_page_immediately_without_empty_frame`) and adjacent page prefetching (`single_page_mode_prefetches_adjacent_pages`).

Fixes #2841

title: fix(ui): turn off horizontal scroll when fitting and lock axis during vertical scroll (#2803)
author: rangoDJ
body:
Fixes #2803.

When pages fit within the window width, the scroll area still allowed horizontal scrolling. On tall documents where a vertical scrollbar appears, egui treats the content as slightly wider than the inner viewport, causing the centered page to drift horizontally during vertical scrolling.

This turns off horizontal scrolling on the scroll area whenever content fits the available width, locking the horizontal offset to 0. It also adds axis locking for precision trackpad gestures so horizontal jitter is ignored while scrolling vertically. Intentional horizontal scrolling and Shift-wheel scrolling when zoomed in continue to work normally.

Added tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/view.rs` for fitting documents, jitter suppression during vertical scroll, and horizontal scrolling when zoomed.

title: fix(render,cos): tolerate scientific-notation numbers and huge page boxes (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Addresses #2670 (item 6: Huge MediaBox / UserUnit).

### Problem
A page with `/MediaBox [0 0 1e30 1e30]` or `/UserUnit 1e20` failed to open with `the file is not a readable PDF: the document has no pages`, whereas MuPDF and qpdf open it with 1 page:
1. `hayro-syntax` (`object::number::Number`) and `lopdf` (`parser::real`) did not accept scientific-notation exponents (`[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`). In `hayro-syntax`, `1e30` in `/MediaBox [0 0 1e30 1e30]` stopped at `1`, leaving `e30` as an invalid array element so `/MediaBox` failed to parse and the page was skipped; in `/UserUnit 1e20`, `1` was read as the value and `e20` caused the rest of the page dictionary to be discarded, losing `/Type /Page`.
2. Numbers exceeding `f32::MAX` (`~3.40e38`, such as `1e40` or 400-digit reals) or `f64::MAX` (`1e400`), or page dimensions whose width/height or `base_dimensions * user_unit` product exceeded `f32::MAX`, overflowed to `±INFINITY`, causing downstream dimension checks and area-cap calculations (`w * h` in `raster::effective_scale`) to fail or collapse.
3. Re-saving a document with `1e30` via `pdfcraft_cos::write_full` formats `1e30` as a 31-digit plain integer, which `lopdf` rejected when `i64::from_str` overflowed.

### Solution
- **`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/number.rs` & `src/page.rs`:**
  - Parse optional scientific-notation exponents (`[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`) in `Number::skip` and `read_inner` when preceded by at least one digit and no trailing minus, rewinding if `e`/`E` is not followed by `[+-]?[0-9]` (preserving token boundaries like `123endobj`).
  - Combine integer overflow digits, fractional shift, and scientific exponent into `net_exp: i64`, clamping overflowed magnitudes to `±f64::MAX` in `f64` and `f32::MIN..=f32::MAX` in `Number::as_f32`.
  - Clamp `Page::base_dimensions`, `Page::render_dimensions`, and scaled `base_height` in `Page::initial_transform` to `f32::MAX`.
- **`vendor/lopdf/src/parser/mod.rs`:**
  - Accept scientific-notation exponents in `real` and clamp to `…

title: M10: export pages to SVG (#2879)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
## What this changes

Export to Image can now write SVG: one standalone vector file per page (`create.export-svg`, planned → shipped). Fixes #2879.

- **parity and docs:** the entry says what is missing (below). Rows in the format, gap, roadmap and architecture docs are updated, plus a progress-log line.

Paths, fills, strokes, clips and shadings come out as SVG, and images are embedded as PNG. Text is drawn as glyph outlines, so a page looks right without its fonts but its text isn't selectable.

title: M9: rewriting a certified form's XFA data is a form fill (#2759)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2759 (the IRCC IMM forms reported as altered). Together with #2763 it clears the false "altered" verdict. Trust (the Sectigo/USERTrust roots) and timestamp verification are separate parts of the issue and aren't touched here.

The IRCC forms are certified (DocMDP P=2) and then saved once more with Reader Extensions. In `imm5257e.pdf` the second revision adds the usage-rights signature (`/Perms /UR3`, object 130) and rewrites the AcroForm and the XFA **`datasets`** packet (object 117, labelled `/Type /EmbeddedFile`). `classify_changes` judged any rewritten stream that wasn't page content or the catalog's XMP as "other changes", so the untouched form validated as invalid. #2763 removes the revisions PdfCraft appends when it lays out the form; this is the part that is in the file itself.

- The roles come from the signed revision, like the page and resource roles in the same function. A later revision that renames the template "datasets" doesn't make rewriting it a form fill.
- A form whose XFA is a single stream holds its template too, so it isn't covered and stays as before.

title: Forms: measure a field's own simple font, not Helvetica, when laying out its text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2894.

Since #1044 a field is drawn in the `/DA` font from `/DR` when it can encode the value, but `FontText::width` still measured that font with Helvetica's table, so wrapping, quadding and `0 Tf` auto size were laid out for a different face. In Courier (0.6 em) mixed-case text overflows: the issue's field gets a 128-character first line in a box that holds 94. This measures a reused simple font with its own `Metrics`, i.e. its `/Widths`, or the standard-14 table when it has none (Courier, Times, Helvetica and their styles), which is what @MONUABST suggested in the issue, thanks for the clear write-up and the repro. Helvetica fallback and the CJK path are unchanged; Symbol and ZapfDingbats never get here, since `dr_font` already sends them to Helvetica. The module comment said widths were Helvetica's, so it's updated too.

#2466 adds a `Composite` arm next to the same line with the same measurement, so whichever lands second has a one-line conflict in that `match`, happy to rebase.

Validation:
- `reused_standard_fonts_wrap_and_align_with_their_own_widths` (crates/forms): the issue's Courier field plus right-aligned Courier and Times-Roman fields. Fails on main (`every line fits the box in Courier: [128, 71]`), passes here; measuring every simple font as Courier makes it fail on the Times field (`Times: 174`)
- The issue's PDF and script through `pdfcraft-cli run` and `render`: the text now wraps at "going" and stays in the box
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms --lib` (appearance tests), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(ui): scroll the right rail instead of overlapping its controls in short windows
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2891.

The right rail laid the navigation cluster out bottom-up in the same fixed-height panel as the panel buttons, so once the window was shorter than both groups (about 770 pt on main, which is a 1080 px screen at 150 % interface size) the cluster simply grew up over Tags and Signatures. Thanks to @musaad-sharikh for the measured thresholds, they made this quick to pin down. Now, when the heights measured on the previous frame don't fit, the rail's content goes into a vertical scroll area: the cluster sits right below the panel buttons and the rail scrolls as one column, so every control stays visible and clickable. A rail that fits keeps exactly the layout it has today, so normal windows and the canvas beside the rail don't move by a pixel. Since it works from measured heights, it doesn't depend on how many buttons either group has, and also covers the extra layout and scrolling toggles in #2828.

I went with scrolling rather than folding the cluster into an overflow menu because it needs no new strings or duplicated actions and keeps the bottom-up order people know; happy to switch to an overflow ("more") button if you'd rather match Acrobat's collapsing behaviour.

Validation:
- `a_short_rail_scrolls_instead_of_overlapping_its_controls` (tests/ui.rs, 1920×1080 at 150 % and 200 % interface size, no two rail controls may overlap): fails on main (`150%: "Signatures" … overlaps "" …`, the page box), passes here

title: M2: an open or diagonal five-point path is not drawn as a rectangle (#2911)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2911 (and #235, the same "M" in the ROMANS font).

`path_as_rect` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (`src/context.rs`) took any five path elements that touch the four corners of their bounding box as a rectangle, and fill, stroke and clip all use it. The "M" of AutoCAD SHX text is an open `m l l l l` with two diagonals that happens to touch all four corners, so it was stroked as a box.

The shortcut now also requires a **closed** path (ending in `h`, or a last point back at the start) whose **every side is horizontal or vertical** (`closed_axis_aligned`). Anything else is drawn as the path it is. Recorded as PdfCraft patch (34) in `vendor/README.md`. The reporter suggested the same rule in the issue.

Two more shapes were wrong the same way and are fixed by it: the same "M" **filled** came out as a full rectangle, and an **open** path with four horizontal or vertical sides was stroked with the side it doesn't have.

## How you verified it

Each case rendered at 288 dpi and compared with MuPDF (mean absolute difference, 0–255):

| content | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| the issue's `5 35 m 35 35 l 5 20 l 35 5 l 5 5 l S` | 37.63 (a box) | 0.04 |
| the same path filled (`f`) | 71.68 (a filled rectangle) | 0.08 |
| open `5 35 m 5 5 l 35 5 l 35 35 l 20 35 l S` | 4.78 (fourth side added) | 0.00 |
| `5 5 30 30 re f` | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| closed `m l l l h S` | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| `m l l l l S` back to the start | 0.16 | 0.16 |

New test `crates/render/src/raster.rs::an_open_or_diagonal_five_point_path_is_not_drawn_as_a_rectangle` checks pixels on a 40 × 40 page:
- the M's top is stroked and its missing left side isn't;
- the filled M's notch stays empty;
- the open path's missing top part stays empty;
- a closed rectangle still strokes all four sides.

It fails with the new check disabled and passes with it.

title: fix(render): draw comma-below letters in non-embedded standard fonts …
author: TiagoCK
body:
…(refs #1666 and the blank "ș" that remains in #1566)

## What this changes

Fixes blank ș reported in #1666
The stand-ins for the standard fonts (PDFium's Foxit fonts) have neither the comma-below letters nor a commaaccent glyph, and the composite-letter patch from #1409 left comma accents out. A non-embedded font naming /scommaaccent therefore drew nothing, which is the blank "si" left in Romanian XFA forms, and /tcommaaccent drew a cedilla through the glyph list's alias to U+0163. This problem also extended to Latvian letters, where `/kcommaaccent` `/lcommaaccent` `/ncommaaccent` `/rcommaaccent` and capitals, `/Gcommaaccent` would also just produce a blank. 

Romanian s/S/t/T and Latvian k/K/l/L/n/N/r/R/G with a comma below are now built from the letter and the font's comma, scaled to three quarters and set just under the baseline, moved back along the slant in italics. The uni021A and uni021B names of T and t with a comma below, which the glyph list does not name, resolve by code point. Lowercase g with its turned comma above is still not built.

However, notably, this only will work once /scommaaccent is actually named, which it will once #1566 is merged.

`vendor/README.md` patch (26) now describes this and names the new test.


## How you verified it

title: CLI: view draws PDF pages in the terminal through the kitty graphics protocol
author: dobladez
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli view report.pdf` draws PDF pages straight into the terminal, through the [kitty graphics protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/) (kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm and others): on macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, directly, over SSH and inside tmux 3.3 or later.


[!demo video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42836641-1084-4241-aa9c-5b4fc77385d2)


- **A pager, like `less`.** More than one page opens a pager on the alternate screen: one page at a time, or two side by side when the window is wide enough, turning like a book. It has less-like keys, fits the page or the width, and follows the window when it is resized or split.
- **Single pages print, like `cat`.** A single page (`--pages 3`), `--no-pager`, or output to a file (with `--protocol kitty`) prints at the cursor instead. The page stays in the scrollback, like text.
- **Fast.** Two render threads work ahead, so turning to a page only places it.
  - On this machine, pages go through temporary files of raw pixels once a one-pixel probe shows the terminal takes them. kitty takes a page that way in about 10 ms, against 50–65 ms as a PNG.
  - Otherwise pages go as PNGs, compressed fast on this machine and small over SSH.
- **tmux.** Escape codes go through passthrough, and pages are Unicode placeholders that tmux keeps as text. Pages tmux threw away, or that a hidden pane or a newly attached terminal missed, are sent again.
- **`docker exec` and `kubectl exec`.** These pass rows and columns but no pixel size, so `view` asks the terminal how big its cells are (`CSI 16 t`) once at start. Pages come out as sharp as over SSH.
- **`pdfcraft-engine`.** It gains `PngEffort`, `encode_png_with` and `unpremultiply`. These are additions only: `encode_png` is unchanged.

Usage is in [`docs/cli-view.md`](docs/cli-view.md). How it works inside, with the measurements behind each choice, is in [`apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/view/README.md`](apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/view/README.md).

title: Rename the open file from its tab (Rename… and double-click), with names that work on every system (#2102, #2867)
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What does it change?

Rename the open document's file from its tab (#2102, #2867).

- **Rename…** on a document tab's right-click menu (beside Reveal), or a double-click on the tab, opens a small dialog with the name selected (without its extension). The file is renamed on disk in its own folder; the tab, its undo history and the view stay. Recent files, Reopen Closed Tab and the file watcher follow the new name.
- The name is checked as it is typed: the reason shows under the field, the resulting file name in grey, and Rename stays disabled until the name is usable. Enter renames.
- **Unsaved changes:** the button reads "Save and Rename"; it saves in place first and renames only if the save went through (a "file changed on disk" question from that save still appears).
- A document without a file shows Rename… disabled, as Reveal is.
- Automation: `doc_rename {doc, name}`, marked destructive, held to the write root for both the old and the new name.

## The rules for a name (`crates/engine/src/rename.rs`)

The same on every system, so a file renamed on one keeps working in a folder synced to another:
- no `/ \ : * ? " < > |`, no control characters, no trailing dot; surrounding spaces trimmed; at most 255 characters;
- no Windows device names (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`9`, `LPT1`–`9`), also with an extension (`aux.notes`);
- the extension is kept, and added back when left out (`notes.txt` becomes `notes.txt.pdf`); a case-only rename is allowed.

Refusals say why: name taken, read-only, in use or no permission, file gone, never saved, unsaved changes.

title: feat(annot): resize highlights, strikeouts, notes and redaction marks
author: FerrisEanfar
body:
## What this changes

Extends the existing native annotation resize path to **Highlight, StrikeOut, Text (note icon), and Redact (review mark)**. Available through `annot::set_rect`, `Edit::ResizeAnnotation`, and the existing `comment_edit` tool's `rect` field; no new tool or GUI controls.

title: M7: shape Arabic in Edit text with the craft-fonts Arabic face (#2878)
author: eulerfan271
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2274. Fixes the save half of #2878 and #1039.

Editing Arabic in a paragraph whose font is a subset failed to save:

> Edit text failed: the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+0633

Arabic draft text takes the styled-paragraph path (`rewrite_styled_block`). There, each letter the
subset couldn't encode went, one at a time, to the Type 3 fallback, which only has the Japanese
(and Hebrew) faces. Even with a glyph, each letter would have been drawn in its unjoined form.

Now a run with Arabic that its own font can't shape is drawn with the craft-fonts `Arab` face
(Noto Sans Arabic):

- **Shaping:** each row is shaped with the shaper Add text already uses (`shape_arabic`, with
  UAX #9 runs).
- **Drawing:** each distinct cluster (a letter in one of its joining forms) becomes one glyph of a
  Type 3 font, built by Add text's `type3_shaped`, inside an `/ActualText` span. So letters join,
  and copy, search and re-editing all get the typed text.
- **No font file is embedded.** The face is variable, which `embedding::validate` refuses, so the
  styled path's existing `embed_mapping` route can't take it.
- **Alignment:** right-to-left rows keep their right edge and grow toward the left margin, as the
  Hebrew path already does.
- **Clear refusals:** a build without the face refuses with a message naming the Arabic font
  rather than the Japanese one. So do the paths that don't shape: a single line (`text_edit` with
  `line`), turned text, text that also has Hebrew, and a paragraph given another font family or
  weight.

Not in this PR: how Arabic looks *inside the edit box* while typing (the other half of #2878 and
#1039). That is UI work, covered by #1572 and #2233.

All runs were scoped per crate with `-j 1`. `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` pointed at a craft-fonts checkout

**Open EPUB books** (#2620, #2628; the import half of #493, whose export half is #2930). title: fix(ui): keep a closed right panel closed when a PDF asks to open on its outline (#2884)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2884.

`apply_initial_view()` opened the right panel for a document's Initial View (`/PageMode /UseOutlines`, and likewise Pages, Attachments and Layers) without checking `right_panel_closed`. It now skips that step when the user has closed the panel. This is the same rule #1603 added to the automatic Comments/Bookmarks choice in `commit_open`. Layout, magnification and the initial page still apply.

Because the document no longer reopens the panel, a closed panel is no longer saved together with `docking_right: "Bookmarks"`, so it stays closed after a restart. `restore()` is unchanged. Other features (Accessibility, Signatures, comment tools) still open the panel directly without clearing the flag, so a panel they opened is still restored as it was left.

Tests:
- New `closed_right_panel_stays_closed_for_a_document_asking_for_its_outline` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui.rs`: close the panel, open a `/PageMode /UseOutlines` copy of the fixture, then persist, restore and open it again. Both times the panel stays closed. Without the fix it fails on the first check, because the panel opens on Bookmarks.
- `read_mode_rail_buttons_open_their_panels` closes Bookmarks with the rail button before checking that an outline document shows its outline in Read mode. It now resets `right_panel_closed` first, because closing the panel there is now (correctly) remembered.

title: Redact email addresses whose local part starts with punctuation
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:141-146 (email)` (no existing issue): Redact email pattern misses addresses whose local part starts with '_', '-', '.', '%' or '+', so they are not redacted at all.

## Cause
`email()` only started a match at an alphanumeric character and refused to start after a local-part character (`._%+-`). An address like `_john@example.com` therefore had no valid start: `_` is not alphanumeric, and `j` follows a local character. The address was never found and stayed visible after redaction.

## Fix
A match may now start at any local-part character, as long as the previous character is not a local-part character. The local run must still contain at least one letter or digit. Addresses with a leading `_`, `-`, `.`, `%` or `+` are matched whole.

## Verified
- Regression test `emails_with_a_leading_punctuation_character`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --lib emails_with_a_leading_punctuation_character`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The domain and TLD rules and the handling of scripts written without spaces are unchanged. A run made only of punctuation, such as `..@example.com`, still does not match.

title: M2: a post table version with swapped halves doesn't make a font unusable (#2946)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2946.

`OpenTypeFontBlob::new` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (`src/font/blob.rs`) refuses an embedded font whose `post` table version isn't 1.0, 2.0, 2.5 or 3.0, a guard taken from pdf.js issue 9462. ScanSoft PDF Create! writes the version of every font it embeds with its 16-bit halves swapped: `00 00 00 03` instead of `00 03 00 00`. Those fonts were refused, `Type0Font` fell back to a substitute, and the Hebrew text was drawn as Latin look-alikes or not at all. As the reporter found, fixing only those four bytes makes the file render correctly.

1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 written with swapped halves (`00 00 00 01..=03`) are now accepted as well. Any other unknown version is still refused, so the pdf.js 9462 case keeps its guard. Recorded as PdfCraft patch (34) in `vendor/README.md`.

title: Apply JPEG EXIF orientation when creating PDFs from images
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2944

## Cause
The create path (`from_images`, used by `doc_create` from images, `doc_combine` and `doc_create_multiple`) embedded JPEGs from their stored pixels and never read the EXIF Orientation tag. Only the engine's stamp and image-placement code turned the pixels first, so portrait photos came out as sideways landscape pages.

## Fix
The EXIF-orientation helper (`upright_image`) now lives in `pdfcraft-create`, and `embed` runs every JPEG through it. Pages made from images get the turned pixel size and the swapped JFIF density, and `image_xobject` (stamps, added images) still gets the same result. The engine no longer calls the helper separately.

## Verified
- Regression test `a_jpeg_with_an_exif_orientation_becomes_an_upright_page`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-create --lib a_jpeg_with_an_exif_orientation_becomes_an_upright_page`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Orientation=1 and JPEGs without the tag are still embedded byte for byte. Other formats (PNG, TIFF, etc.) are unchanged. The helper's behaviour (re-encode at quality 92, 64 MP size cap) is unchanged.

title: fix(forms): name detected check boxes from the nearer neighbouring label (#2943)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary
Closes #2943

When `pdfcraft_forms::detect::detect` named small square check boxes, it only inspected words to the right of each box within a 24 pt gap. On forms that place labels immediately to the left of their check boxes (such as `Monsieur [ ]   Madame [ ]` on French form 2042, where `Monsieur` ends ~5 pt before the first box and `Madame` starts 23 pt after the first box and ~4 pt before the second), the first box claimed `Madame` and left the second box as `Check Box1`.

### Root Cause & Fix
- **Consider both sides of each check box in reading order (`checkbox_label`):** Sort detected check boxes (along with any existing check-box widgets on the page) into reading order and evaluate both the unclaimed phrase immediately to the left and the unclaimed phrase immediately to the right on the same line, bounded by adjacent check boxes on that line.
- **Prevent stealing a neighbour's label:** Reject a right-hand phrase when it sits closer to the next check box on the line than to the current box (or split a multi-word span when a subsequent word sits closer to the next box than to the preceding word), and reject a left-hand phrase when it sits closer to the previous check box.
- **Choose the nearer label (preserving colon prompts):** When a box has valid unclaimed candidates on both sides, prefer the nearer one (or the left candidate when the right candidate is also immediately followed by the next box at equal distance), while treating colon-terminated row prompts (`Status: [ ] Single [ ] Married` or `Civilité : Monsieur [ ] Madame [ ]`) as headings rather than option names unless the prompt is the box's only label (`Married: [ ]`).

title: M7: replacing a line keeps the source font for the words it can show (#2378)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2378: the single-line path (`text_edit` with `line`, which is what the issue's `edits.json` uses).

`replace_line` decided once for the whole text: if the line's font couldn't encode every character, the whole line was set in Helvetica. An embedded TrueType subset lacks every character it didn't use, so on the issue's `scheda.pdf` (subsets `BAAAAA+DejaVuSans`, `CAAAAA+DejaVuSans-Bold`), "Giovedì" → "Venerdì" (no `V` in the bold subset) and adding "Zürich" (no `ü`) redrew those whole lines in Helvetica, at another width.

Now the replacement is split into words:
- a word the source font can show keeps it (through the existing `source_show`, so a subset without a space glyph still draws spaces with a displacement);
- a word with any character the font lacks is set in the substitute, as a whole. One font per word, so no word switches face letter by letter;
- only the substitute's runs are checked against WinAnsi, so a character only the source font has no longer blocks the edit;
- reordered text (right to left, Indic) and the Type 3 fallback path keep their single-run behaviour.

`substituted` still reports `Helvetica` when any word used it.

**Not in this PR:** the paragraph rewrite (`text_edit` with `paragraph`, which the inline editor uses) still substitutes the whole paragraph for a Latin character its subset lacks. #2778 is reworking that single-style path for missing non-Latin glyphs, so I've left it alone rather than conflict with it.

The issue's fixture and `edits.json`, saved and read back with PyMuPDF:

| edit | `main` | this PR |

| line 10 → "Venerdì 16 ottobre " | whole line `Helvetica-Bold` | `Venerdì` in Helvetica-Bold, ` 16 ottobre ` in **DejaVuSans-Bold** |

title: M6: dotted field names make parent fields (#2696)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2696.

**The problem.** Prepare a form refused any field name containing a period: "field names can't be empty or contain a period". Templates for Conga and similar tools rely on names such as `MASTER.account_firstname`. It also showed an existing `MASTER.account_firstname` as `account_firstname`, both in Field Properties and on the name tags.

ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2 does say a field's own (partial) name can't contain a period. A dotted name is therefore a *full* name: `MASTER.first` is a field `first` under a parent field `MASTER`, and that is what this PR builds.

**Changes:**
- **Adding a field** (`add_field`, `form_add_field`): a dotted name creates the parent fields it names, or reuses them if they already exist. A second `MASTER.` field joins the same `MASTER` parent.
- **Renaming** (`set_props`, `form_set_props`):
  - A dotted name is the full name. The field moves under the parents it names, and what it inherited (`FT`, `Ff`, `V`, `DV`, `DA`, `Q`, `MaxLen`) is first copied onto it, so its value and flags are kept.
  - A plain name still renames the field within its parent, as before. The existing test, where `address.city` → `town` gives `address.town`, is unchanged.
- **Clash checks:** a new full name may not equal another field's name, sit inside one, or contain one. A field with a value can't also be a parent of fields. This also closes an existing gap: renaming a field to `address` while `address.city` existed used to be accepted.
- **Reused parents:** a field joining an existing parent gets an explicit `Ff 0` / `Q 0` if it has none of its own, so it doesn't pick up the parent's flags or alignment.
- **UI:** Field Properties ▸ General and the Prepare a form name tags show the full name, as the Fields panel already did.
- **Limits:** names are capped at 32 parts, and empty parts (`a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `a. `) are refused.
- `delete_field`'s tree removal moved into a `detach` helper, shared with rename.

title: Keep lines with footnote references in paragraph reading order (#2929)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #2929

### Problem
When a paragraph contains a line with a footnote reference (superscript) or subscript:
1. In `arrange` Step 1a, a raised superscript (or a script drawn out of content order in a separate pass) splits into its own `Seg` whenever its vertical centre is more than `0.5 * ph` from the preceding glyph's centre, and Step 1b only merges segments with matching heights (`(sa.h / sb.h - 1.0).abs() < 0.35`) and centres (`(sa.cy() - sb.cy()).abs() < h * 0.3`).
2. In Step 2 (`Blocks`), segments are sorted top-down by `bbox[1]`. Because a superscript's top edge `bbox[1]` is higher than its host line's top edge, `by_top` visits the superscript **before** its host line and appends it to the paragraph block (`members.last()`).
3. When the host line is visited next, `vgap = line.bbox[1] - sup.bbox[3]` is negative (`< -0.5 * sup.h`), so the host line is rejected from the paragraph block and pushed into a separate block emitted **after** the paragraph. Meanwhile, the next line below has a positive `vgap` from the superscript and joins the first block.
4. Drag-selecting across the paragraph selects `Block 0` (`Line 1`, the superscript, `Line 3`, ...) and completely skips the host line containing the footnote reference both visually and when copying.

### Solution
- Add `is_script_on` and `Seg::extend_box` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` so superscripts and subscripts widen their host line segment horizontally without pulling its vertical baseline band (`bbox[1]..bbox[3]`) up or down.
- In `arrange` Step 1a, keep inline superscripts/subscripts in the current segment and allow the following body text on the segment's baseline to continue the run across normal and justified word gaps.
- In `arrange` Step 1b, merge any remaining out-of-order superscript/subscript segments into the closest wider host line segment they sit on.
- In `collide`, do not treat a script overlapping an adjacent host glyph (e.g. a superscript kerned over a period or comma) as a run-level overpr…

title: M7: paragraph edits keep what a dropped ' or " did
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

There's no existing issue: I found this by probing `text_edit` on synthetic content streams.

**What `'` and `"` do.** By ISO 32000-2 §9.4.3, Table 107:
- `'` is `T*` followed by `Tj`: it moves to the next line, then shows its text.
- `aw ac string "` also sets `aw Tw` and `ac Tc` first.

Both effects outlast the text they show. The next `Td` starts from the line `'` moved to, and the spacing set by `"` applies to all later text until something resets it. That includes later text objects, since the text state isn't reset by `BT`/`ET`.

**The bug.** Editing a **paragraph** (`replace_block` / `rewrite_block`, `text_edit` with `paragraph`) removes the paragraph's show operators and inserts the new text. When a removed operator was `'` or `"`, its line move and spacing were removed with it. As a result:
- Text later in the same text object that is placed with a relative `Td` moved **up by one leading**.
- Text that inherited a `"` spacing **lost it**, in the same text object or a later one.

The line path (`replace_line`) and the editing preview already wrote these effects back. The paragraph path and the region path (`text_regions.rs`) did not.

Example: `BT /F1 12 Tf 14 TL 72 714 Td (Target line here) ' 0 -100 Td (Footer stays put) Tj ET`. Editing the "Target" paragraph moved the footer from y = 600 to y = 614.

**The fix**
- `show_side_effects(op)` returns what a show operator does besides showing: `T*` for `'`, and `aw Tw`, `ac Tc`, `T*` for `"`. It only emits `Tw`/`Tc` when the operand is a number, matching how `interpret` reads them.
- `dropped_side_effects(ops, i, keep, split_at)` leaves those operators in place of a dropped `'` or `"` in the paragraph and region splices. It skips the one operator the text object is split at, because the rewrite's `Tm` (`o.tlm`) and its state restore (`o.state`) are taken *after* that operator's effects. Emitting them again would move the text twice. One fixture covers exactly this case.

title: Keep seconds in FormCalc Time2Num/IsoTime2Num for ISO 8601 times
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2348-2352 ("time2num" | "isotime2num")` (no existing issue): FormCalc Time2Num / IsoTime2Num drop the seconds when they carry a 'Z' suffix or a fractional part ("12:30:45Z" gives 12:30:00).

## Cause
Time2Num/IsoTime2Num split the text on ':' and kept only the parts that parse as a plain integer. A seconds part such as "45Z" or "45.250" was dropped and read as 0. A leading "T" dropped the hour part, so the later parts shifted left. The calculation also used whole seconds only.

## Fix
The function now removes an optional leading "T" and trailing "Z", then reads hours and minutes as integers by position. It reads seconds as a decimal number, so "12:30:45Z" gives 45045000 and "12:30:45.250" gives 45045250. The existing cap on very large values is kept.

## Verified
- Regression test `built_in_functions_cover_the_common_set`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js built_in_functions_cover_the_common_set`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Time zone offsets such as "+02:00" are still not interpreted. Num2Time and the other time and date functions are unchanged.

title: M7: paragraph edits keep the advance of the text they drop
author: mtlcl410
body:
> **Stacked on #2961.** This branch contains #2961's commit (`47184ce6`, the `'`/`"` side effects), because this fix extends the same splice. Please review only the last commit (`1bf752ea`). I'll rebase once #2961 is merged.

## What this changes

There's no existing issue: I found this by probing `text_edit` on synthetic content streams.

**The rule.** Each `Tj`/`TJ` moves the text matrix by the width of its text (ISO 32000-2 §9.4.4). A run shown later in the same text object without its own `Td` or `Tm` is placed by those advances. Examples are a raised run in another colour, or a column after a `TJ` gap.

**The bug.** The paragraph and region rewrites (`replace_block` / `rewrite_block`, `text_edit` with `paragraph`) removed the paragraph's show operators outright. A following run that isn't part of the paragraph then jumped left by the removed text's width, often onto the new text:

| Content after `BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (Target words) Tj` | main: run's x after a paragraph edit | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `1 0 0 rg 3 Ts (Red) Tj` | 72 (on top of the new text; was 142) | 142 |
| `[-20000] TJ (Far) Tj` | 312 (was 382) | 382 |

**Why only these paths.** Deleting a paragraph (`clear_block`, also used for the editing preview) already replaces each dropped operator with a numeric `TJ` of the same advance. The rewrites now do the same.

**The fix.** `dropped_advances` interprets the page and returns, for each dropped show operator, `[-1000·advance/(Tfs·Th)] TJ`, which moves the text matrix the same distance without drawing. Advances a `TJ` can't express (spacing at a zero font size) are left out, which is the previous behaviour, rather than refused. Both splices insert this after the operator's `'`/`"` side effects from #2961.

Line edits (`replace_line`) are unchanged. There, the runs after the edited text move to follow the new text (here 142 → 134), which is the line editor's existing reflow.

title: Find credit card numbers followed by an expiry, year or CVV
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:180-190 (credit_card, via digit_run at :53)` (no existing issue): Redact credit-card pattern misses a card number when another number follows it after a space (expiry date, CVV, year).

## Cause
`credit_card` took the longest run of digits joined by single spaces or hyphens and ran the Luhn check only on that whole run. A valid card followed by a space and another number (an expiry like `12/26`, a year or a CVV) made the run too long or failed the checksum. The card was then not found and stayed visible after redaction.

## Fix
`credit_card` now tries the longest run first, then each shorter run that ends at a group boundary (before a space or hyphen), longest first. It returns the first run with 13 to 19 digits and a valid Luhn checksum. The trailing number stays outside the match.

## Verified
- Regression test `credit_card_followed_by_another_number`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --lib credit_card_followed_by_another_number`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`digit_run` and the other patterns are unchanged. A run with no valid checksum at any group boundary, such as `4111 1111 1111 1112 12/26`, still matches nothing.

title: fix(render): blend modes over an empty part of the page keep their colour (#2970)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2970.

**Cause.** Bisected between v0.8.0 (correct) and `main` (924c4da4). The first bad commit is ab45a185, #1557 "Keep annotations readable under reading colours". Its vendored hayro patch (18) moved the page background *inside* the page transparency group, as the group's initial backdrop. That way a Multiply highlight under reading colours blends with the dark background (#1548).

The commit reasoned that "white backgrounds are unaffected: multiplying with white is the identity". That holds for Multiply, but not for most other blend modes. With document colours, every object then blended with the white paper:
- A green `/BM /Screen` fill over an empty part of the page came out white.
- Difference and Exclusion came out magenta.

Only Normal, Multiply, Darken and HardLight looked right, because for them blending with white gives back the source colour.

**Fix.** A page's objects composite with an initially transparent backdrop, and the page group is then put on the paper (ISO 32000-2, page group). `render_into` now paints the background inside the group only when reading colours are on, which is where #1548 needs it. Otherwise it paints it outside, as before #1557.

The reading-colours behaviour is unchanged. Its test, `reading_colors_keep_highlight_annotations_readable`, still passes.

title: fix(render): knockout transparency groups knock out (#2971)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2971: knockout transparency groups (`/K true`) now knock out for every kind of element: paths, strokes, text, shadings, images and nested groups.

**Cause.** In a knockout group, each element composites with the group's initial backdrop, not with the elements drawn before it in the group, over the element's shape (ISO 32000-2, knockout groups). hayro-interpret already read `/K` (patch 28). The renderer, though, drew a knockout group like any other, so overlapping semi-transparent elements in it blended with each other.

**Fix.** There are two commits.

1. **Direct draws.** While the innermost group is a knockout group, fills, strokes, glyph outlines and shadings are drawn with `BlendMode::new(Mix::Normal, Compose::Copy)`. vello_cpu weights Copy by coverage (result = coverage · source + (1 − coverage) · destination), so an element replaces what the group drew under its shape.
   - hayro-interpret patch (35): `Device::set_knockout`, called when a `/K true` group is pushed.
   - hayro patch (19): a knockout flag per pushed group, popped with it.

2. **Images and nested groups.** These are drawn into a layer of their own. The layer covers the whole canvas and is transparent where nothing was drawn, so compositing it with Copy would erase everything else. Copy on a clipped layer doesn't work either: vello renders it into an empty clip buffer first and composites that with SrcOver. Instead, what is under the element's shape is cleared first, and then the layer composites over it as usual.
   - **Unmasked image:** its shape is its placement rectangle. The interpreter passes it to `Device::knockout_shape`, and the renderer clears it with a transparent Copy fill.
   - **Nested group:** its shape is the union of its elements' shapes. When `Device::knockout_erase_wanted` is true, the interpreter draws the group's content once between `begin_knockout_erase` and `end_knockout_erase`. In that pass every paint clears under its shape instead of painting…

title: fix(render): a stencil mask is drawn at the fill opacity once (#2975)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2975.

**Cause.** `draw_image_xobject` (hayro-interpret) draws every image XObject inside a transparency group whose opacity is the fill alpha `ca`. A stencil mask (`/ImageMask true`) is painted in the fill colour, which `get_paint` builds with that same alpha, and the renderer applies the paint's alpha again. So the opacity was applied twice:
- at `ca 0.5`, a mask came out 25 % opaque
- at `ca 0.25`, about 6 %

Rectangles and raster images, which have no paint colour, were right. This was already the case in 0.7.1.

**Fix.** Vendored hayro-interpret patch (36): once the image's group is pushed, the fill alpha is set to 1 before the stencil's paint is taken. The state saved at the start of `draw_image_xobject` is restored after the image, so nothing after it changes.

Stencils inside Type 3 glyphs and uncoloured patterns are unchanged: their wrappers ignore the group and substitute their own paint. Inline images (`BI … EI`) use the same `draw_image_xobject`, so they're fixed too.

## How you verified it

title: Fix overflow panic for i64::MIN index in content_update/delete
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/automation/src/content.rs:141` (no existing issue): content_update / content_delete panic with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' when index is i64::MIN.

## Cause
`Automation::item` computed `(index - 1).max(0)` before checking `index >= 1`. With `index = i64::MIN` the subtraction overflows, so debug and test builds panic instead of returning the usual 'has no added item' error.

## Fix
The item lookup now computes the position with `index.saturating_sub(1)` and `usize::try_from`. Any index below 1 maps to a position that matches no item, and the existing `index >= 1` filter still rejects it. `i64::MIN` now returns the normal failed error. A regression test covers `i64::MIN`, `i64::MIN + 1`, -1, 0 and `i64::MAX` for both tools.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(render): resolve accented TrueType glyphs across Symbolic flags, Unicode cmaps, post v2.0, and ToUnicode (#2159, #2426)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2159
Fixes #2426

Embedded TrueType fonts containing Central/Eastern European accented glyphs (such as Czech `ř` U+0159, `ě` U+011B in `"předmět"` from #2426, or Slovak `č` U+010D, `ľ` U+013E from #2159) skipped or misrendered those characters while rendering ASCII and Latin-1 vowels normally.

### Root Cause

In `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs` (`EmbeddedKind::map_code`):

1. **`Symbolic` flag (`/Flags 4`) + `/Encoding` / `/Differences` (ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 & §9.8.2 Table 121):**
   Per ISO 32000-2 Table 121, any font containing glyphs outside the Adobe Standard Latin character set sets the `Symbolic` bit (`/Flags 4`) in its `/FontDescriptor`. Previously, `EmbeddedKind::map_code` only consulted `self.differences` and `self.encoding` when `FontFlags::NON_SYMBOLIC` was set (and `FontFlags::from_bits` discarded the entire flags word if any producer-specific bit was set). For TrueType fonts marked `Symbolic` (or carrying extra flag bits), `/Encoding` and `/Differences` were bypassed in favor of looking up the raw 1-byte code in the `(3, 1)` Unicode `cmap`, where ASCII and Latin-1 characters `<= U+00FF` matched while glyphs `> U+00FF` (`ř`, `ě`, `č`, `ľ`) failed.
2. **`PlatformId::Unicode` `(0, *)` and Windows UCS-4 `(3, 10)` `cmap` subtables ignored (#2159):**
   TrueType font subsets produced on macOS frequently carry a `PlatformId::Unicode` `(0, 3)` / `(0, 4)` `cmap` subtable and a `(1, 0)` MacRoman subtable, with `post` v3.0 (no glyph names) and no `(3, 1)` Windows subtable. title: fix(render): a visibility expression decides what an OCMD shows (#2986)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2986. This may be the cause of #2986; that depends on how cadwork marks its layers, which a sample file would show.

**The gap.** An optional content membership dictionary (OCMD) can carry a visibility expression, `/VE` (PDF 1.6): `[/And e…]`, `[/Or e…]` or `[/Not e]`. Each `e` is an optional content group or a nested expression. When `/VE` is present it takes precedence over `/OCGs` and `/P` (ISO 32000-2 §8.11.2.2). hayro-interpret evaluated only `/OCGs` and `/P`, so content under an OCMD with `/VE` stayed visible after its layers were hidden in the Layers panel.

**The fix.** Vendored hayro-interpret patch (37) evaluates the expression in `OcgState::begin_ocmd`, nested up to 32 deep. A malformed expression falls back to `/OCGs` and `/P`, as before. Malformed means:
- an unknown operator
- `/Not` without exactly one operand
- `/And` or `/Or` without any operands
- an operand that is neither a group nor an expression
- nesting deeper than 32

An operand given by reference is taken as a group, which is how producers write them.

**What I checked.** I ran 11 optional-content structures with layer A hidden through the same override the Layers panel uses:
- *Already correct:* `BDC /OC` (also nested, and inside a form), `/OC` on a Form XObject, on a form nested in a form, and on an image, OCMDs with `/P` `AnyOn`/`AllOn` and a single `/OCGs` reference, and a layer that is off in `/D /OFF`.
- *Not hidden:* the OCMD with `/VE`, fixed here.
- *Not hidden:* `/OC` on an annotation, which is covered by #2176.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -j 8 --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: render: average a minified 1-bit source into its snapped device rectangle (#1700, follow-up to #2288)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
<!-- Stacked on #2288 (head 1a42f48). Until #2288 is merged, only the last commit, f796686, belongs to this PR. -->

## What this changes

This follows up #2288 for #1700, as agreed in [the review thread](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2288#issuecomment-6190802399). It is stacked on #2288 (head 1a42f48); only the last commit, f796686, is new.

**The problem on #2288.** A minified 1-bit source is averaged into a raster `ceil(s × scale)` px wide, and that raster is then drawn `s × scale` px wide with `ImageQuality::Low`. So it is nearest-sampled a second time, and a whole averaged column or row (a one-pixel stroke) can fall between two pixel centres. At 9 pt and 96 dpi, for example, the 18 px Type 3 glyphs of `mask_downscale.pdf` are averaged to 9 px and drawn 8.1 px wide. An 18×1 mask inked only in column 8 or 9 then renders all white. On the fixture this shows as missing stems in several glyphs of that row; that part is a visual reading of the render, and the table below has the counts.

**What this PR does.** A shrunk 1-bit source, Type 3 glyph masks included, now takes the path that #1377 added for interpolated images:

- `snap_minified_image` gives the whole-pixel device rectangle.
- The source is averaged straight into that size and drawn 1:1 at its corner. A Type 3 glyph's raster keeps its two-pixel transparent frame, so there its corner is offset by −2 px.
- **A side shrunk by less than one pixel** gets no resize planned (`ceil` gives the source size back). On #2288, nearest sampling at the fractional scale drops a column there (18 px drawn 17.1 px wide). That side now keeps its source size and is drawn 1:1 at the snapped corner, at most one pixel wider than asked. Averaging it into one pixel fewer instead would turn crisp strokes into pairs of 50 % grey pixels wherever the two grids beat (6000 px drawn 5999.6 px wide at x = 0.6).
- If resizing fell back to the source size (allocation failure), the raster is drawn scaled as before, not placed 1:1.

title: fix(sign): explain 0x8009001D and 0xC0000225 when a store key's provider fails
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2207.

When PdfCraft lists the certificates in the Windows store for signing, a certificate whose key provider fails to load was shown only as "its private key's algorithm couldn't be read: Windows error 0x8009001D". `0x8009001D` is `NTE_PROVIDER_DLL_FAIL`: the DLL of the key storage provider holding the private key failed to load. The usual causes are smart card or token middleware that is missing or broken, or a provider that exists only as 32-bit code, which the 64-bit app can't load.

`describe` (`crates/sign/src/windows.rs`) now explains it, as it already did for a missing card, a missing provider or an unsupported operation:

> its key provider's software failed to load (a smart card or token driver that is missing or broken, or a 32-bit-only provider) (Windows error 0x8009001D)

Only the message changes. A certificate with this error is still left out of the list as before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -j 8 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`, including `errors_are_explained_with_their_code`, which now covers `0x8009001D`
- [x] **Seen failing:** with the new mapping removed, the test fails

## Never-crash

- [x] One added `match` arm; no `unwrap` or `unsafe`.

## Provenance

- [x] No assets or copied code. The error code's meaning is from `winerror.h`.

## Security

- [x] No paths, channels or network touched

Also refs #1535: `0xC0000225` is the NTSTATUS `STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, which some smart card and token providers pass through when they can't find the key. It is the code an A3 certificate (key on a token) produces in that report. It is now explained as "its key provider can't find the key (the smart card or token holding it isn't connected, or its driver doesn't see the key)". The same test covers it, and fails with the new arm removed.

title: Render month and weekday names in XFA date patterns
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/xfa/src/data.rs:265-281 (iso_to_pattern, with date_tokens at :242 and pattern_to_iso at :285; pattern built in crates/xfa/src/layout.rs:396 date_pattern)` (no existing issue): XFA date fields with a month-name picture (e.g. date{MMM D, YYYY}) show the literal text "mmm" instead of the month.

## Cause
`iso_to_pattern` only knew the tokens yyyy, yy, mm, m, dd and d. Tokens like `mmm`, `mmmm`, `ddd` and `dddd` were copied through as literal text, so `date{MMM D, YYYY}` showed `mmm 3, 2001`. `pattern_to_iso` could not parse them back either.

## Fix
`iso_to_pattern` now renders abbreviated and full month names and weekday names. The weekday is computed from the date. `pattern_to_iso` parses those names case-insensitively and rejects a weekday that doesn't match the date. A y/m/d run the converter doesn't know, such as `mmmmm`, now returns the ISO value unchanged from `iso_to_pattern` and `None` from `pattern_to_iso`, as the doc comment says.

## Verified
- Regression test `month_and_weekday_names_in_date_patterns`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa --lib month_and_weekday_names_in_date_patterns`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`date_pattern` in layout.rs is unchanged. It already accepts these pictures and lower-cases them. Its `E`→`d` mapping is also unchanged. I did not add a layout-level test.

title: M10: Export to Word keeps the page background colour (#2992)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2992.

**The problem.** A page coloured with Edit a PDF ▸ Background exported to Word as a white page. The text kept its colour, but the background was gone. `export::Page` carried only text blocks and images, and the Word writer had nowhere to put a page colour.

**The fix**

- **`pdfcraft_edit::page_background(doc, page)`** (new `crates/edit/src/background.rs`) reads the page's content up to the first thing it paints. That first paint is a page background when it is:
  - an opaque fill: `ca` 1, no soft mask, Normal blend
  - in a plain gray, RGB or CMYK colour (`g`/`rg`/`k`, or `cs`+`sc` in those spaces)
  - of a path with one rectangle covering the visible page (crop box, within 0.5 %), under the current `cm`
  - not clipped smaller

  Anything else painted first (text, a stroke, an image, a shading), a translucent or blended fill, a pattern, a fill with a hole, or a fill that doesn't cover the page gives `None`. This is how Edit a PDF ▸ Background draws a colour, and how many producers fill their pages.
- **`export::Page::background`** carries the colour. The engine fills it in `export_pages`.
- **The Word writer** sets it as the document's page colour: `<w:background w:color="…"/>` before `<w:body>`, plus a `word/settings.xml` with `<w:displayBackgroundShape/>`, which Word needs before it shows a background. It's added when **every page shares one non-white colour**. Word has a single background per document, so differing colours are left out rather than applying one page's colour to all.

HTML, RTF and PowerPoint exports are unchanged. They could use `Page::background` too, as per-page backgrounds, in a follow-up.

author: PerchAnton

## What this changes

Fixes #2592.

Adding `шалом` to a Helvetica paragraph while keeping a line break wrote five Type 3 fonts and five fallback text objects, one per distinct letter. A replacement with 300 missing glyphs was refused after 240 instead of using another font.

The styled writer now prepares the missing outlines by their **actual selected fallback face**, then reuses the existing Type 3 writer to pack up to 240 glyphs per font. title: Fix cursor leaking from the PDF canvas onto the top mode bar
author: mr-mahfuj
body:
## Summary

The top mode bar (Menu / All tools / Read / Edit / Convert / E-Sign) sits above the PDF
canvas as a foreground panel, but the cursor over the bar was being driven by the
canvas's per-frame hover detection. Result: hovering the bar over a text box showed

title: Zero-pad required integer digits in FormCalc Format()
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2240-2276 ("format" builtin, number branch)` (no existing issue): FormCalc Format() ignores the integer part of a number picture: '9' does not zero-pad (Format("99999", 42) gives "42").

## Cause
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2240-2276` ("format" builtin, number branch), no existing issue. FormCalc Format() ignores the integer part of a number picture: '9' does not zero-pad, so `Format("99999", 42)` gives "42". The number branch of the `Format` builtin only counted the `9`/`z` characters after the `.` to get the decimals. It never read the integer part of the picture, so `9` behaved like `z`.

## Fix
The number branch now counts the `9` characters before the `.` as the minimum number of integer digits (capped at 20). It zero-pads the number to that width, including the decimal part, before grouping. The `$` prefix and the sign are applied afterwards. `z` stays optional, and numbers wider than the picture are not truncated.

## Verified
- Regression test `format_nine_pads_the_integer_part`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib format_nine_pads_the_integer_part`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Date pictures and `Parse` are unchanged. The grouping, `$` and sign code is unchanged, but it now receives zero-padded digits for pictures with `9`.

title: fix(cos): write whole reals past the 32-bit integer range as reals
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

This came out of the review of #2877 ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2877)).

`pdfcraft_cos::writer::write_real` printed a whole-number real in one of two ways:
- below 1e15, as an integer (`r as i64`);
- above that, through `Display`, which never prints a decimal point for a whole number either.

So `Real(4e9)` was written as `4000000000` and `Real(1e30)` as `1000000000000000000000000000000`. Both are **integer** tokens:

- Our own lexer reads `4000000000` back as `Int`, so a real silently changes type across a save.
- ISO 32000-2 Annex C gives integers a range of ±2³¹−1 (reals go to about ±3.4×10³⁸). A reader with 32-bit integers may overflow on these tokens. `lopdf` rejected the 31-digit one outright, and #2877 works around that on the reading side.

Now:
- A whole-number real is written as an integer only within ±2³¹−1. Every ordinary coordinate keeps its current output (`595`, `-0` → `0`).
- Past that range it gets a trailing `.` (`4000000000.`, `1000000000000000000000000000000.`). §7.3.3 allows that form (its examples include `4.`). The digits are still `Display`'s shortest round-trip form, without an exponent.

Non-finite reals are still written as `0`. That is a separate fidelity question, raised in the #2877 review, and this PR doesn't change it.

`crates/content/src/lib.rs:401` has the same `< 1e15` integer cut-off for numbers it writes into content streams. I left it alone to keep this PR to `cos`; it can follow the same rule if wanted.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos`: all pass (56 lib tests)

title: fix(ui): the password prompt takes typing on Linux again
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Typing into the "Password required" prompt works again on Linux. Before, the cursor blinked in the field but nothing typed appeared, so encrypted files could not be opened. Fixes #2818.

**Cause.** The prompt's field called `request_focus()` on every frame. Since egui 0.36, `Memory::request_focus` also interrupts the input method (its doc comment says so). The field owns the IME output, so every frame's output set `ime.should_interrupt_composition`. egui-winit answers that with `window.set_ime_allowed(false)` and then `set_ime_allowed(true)`. In winit 0.30, that destroys and recreates the window's XIM input context on X11 and disables and re-enables text-input on Wayland. On Linux, typed keys go through the input method (on X11, winit passes every key press to `XFilterEvent` while the IME is allowed). Recreating it on every frame dropped each key while the input method still held it, so nothing reached the field. Windows delivers plain Latin keys as ordinary key input, which is why the prompt kept working there. #603, mentioned on the issue, is a different problem: a file with an empty owner password opens without asking for its password, so no prompt appears. @ch0kemeister's fix for that, on the branch [`fix/empty-owner-password`](https://github.com/ch0kemeister/pdfcraft/tree/fix/empty-owner-password), is waiting for a maintainer decision. It changes how a password is tried on open (crypt, cos, render, engine, CLI) and touches no UI code. This PR changes only the prompt's field, so the two don't overlap and either can land first.

**Fix.** Request focus only when the field doesn't have it. It still takes focus when the prompt opens and gets it back after Enter or a click elsewhere in the box. #1638 fixed the command search the same way (#1252, a Chinese IME on Windows). This prompt was the other field that asked on every frame. `password_modal` also draws the permissions-password prompt (Unlock…, and changing security), so that prompt is fixed…

title: fix(edit): a paragraph's width handle rewraps it from its whole handle, not just the inner half (#2276)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

In **Edit text & images**, hovering a paragraph draws a width handle on its left and right edges, and the pointer turns into the resize arrow a few pixels either side of the edge. Only the part of the handle inside the paragraph's box worked, though. A press on the outer half of the handle, or in the reach just outside it, started an **area selection** instead:

- its thin rectangle followed the pointer, which reads as the box being resized;
- on release it selected the paragraph at its old size, or nothing, and the text never moved.

That is what #2276 and its comment describe: the frame follows the mouse, then snaps back.

The cause is the order of the two handlers. Object selection (`object_ui`) sees the press first. It hands a press to the paragraph tool only when the press is on the paragraph's box, i.e. the text rect grown by 2 px. The paragraph tool (`edit_text_ui`) draws its 7 px handle centred on that box's edge and grabs the edge from up to 6 px outside. So in the gap between those two zones, object selection started a marquee and cleared the pending drag.

The fix: object selection now also leaves a press on a closed paragraph's edge grip to the paragraph tool.

- It uses the same edge test (`edge_at`), box (`paragraph_box`) and upright-page rule (`has_edges`) as the paragraph tool, through one new `edit_text_ui::grabs_edge`. The two can't drift apart again.
- `page_input` now uses those helpers as well, so neither the box nor the upright rule is written out twice.
- It applies only while no paragraph is open for typing on that page, which is the same condition under which the paragraph tool starts an edge drag. With a paragraph open, a press there still selects an area as before.

Nothing changes in the engine. The rewrap is the existing `EditTextBlock` with a width, so undo and redo restore the old and new widths, and the result is saved like any other text edit.

Fixes #2276

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x]…

title: fix(ui): the header, footer and watermark previews show the page under the marks (#2837)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2837.

The Add/Update Header and Footer, Watermark and Background dialogs drew their preview on a blank white sheet. You could not see where the marks would land on the page's text and pictures. The preview now shows the page itself, with the marks drawn on top where the engine puts them.

- **The page's own picture.** The preview reuses the page's thumbnail from the canvas cache (`need_thumbnail` / `thumb_id`), as the Print dialog already does. It renders off the UI thread with the other thumbnails, so nothing is rendered on the UI thread. Until the thumbnail arrives the dialog shows the blank sheet it showed before. If the pages panel is open, the thumbnail is usually there already.
- **Which page.** It is the current page when the Page Range Options select it. Otherwise it is the first page the range does select, for example page 2 for "Pages from 2 to 2", or the first even page for "Even pages only". "Preview: page N of M" names that page. Before, the dialog always showed the current page, even one the range left out.
- **Size and rotation.** The page is drawn at its displayed size, after `/Rotate`, which is the frame `pdfcraft-edit` lays the marks out in. The thumbnail is rendered the same way, so a turned page shows turned, with the header along its displayed top.
- **Background colour.** It now tints the page picture (multiply) instead of being painted over it, because a background sits behind the content. White areas take the colour and the text stays on top. On a blank sheet the result is the same colour the dialog showed before.

No new strings, no engine change.
