title: fix(ui): the mode tabs keep the hand over a page scrolled under them
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2755.

With the All tools panel closed, the first page sits under the mode bar's Read, Edit, Convert and E-Sign tabs, but not under All tools, which is left of the text. Once the page is scrolled up so that its text runs under the bar, those four tabs showed the page's cursor instead of the hand. With the panel open the page starts right of the tabs, so they kept the hand. That is the difference the issue describes.

**Why.** The mode bar is drawn first in a frame, and the page view runs after it, and the last cursor set in a frame wins. The page code took egui's raw hover position and tested it only against the page's whole rectangle. That rectangle goes on past the visible document area when the page is scrolled, and the top bar is on the same egui layer as the pages, so nothing else stopped it. Three things on the page did this:

- **The Select tool's text layer** (the default tool) gave the I-beam over any text under the tabs.
- **Edit text** gave the four-way arrow over a closed paragraph, or the I-beam once a paragraph was open (the issue's "click on a text").
- **The open paragraph's editor** is a foreground `egui::Area` placed on its paragraph. Scrolled up with the paragraph, it was drawn over the tabs. It showed its I-beam there and took their clicks: a click on Convert placed the caret in the paragraph instead of switching mode.

**The fix**, at each of those:

- The text layer and Edit text set their cursor only while the pages' own widget `contains_pointer()`. egui clips that widget to the visible document area, and Fill & Sign already uses the same check for its cursor. A selection being dragged keeps the I-beam past the edge, as before. Edit text's hover still returns what it did, so nothing else on the page changes.
- The paragraph editor's `Area` is `constrain_to` the document viewport with `constrain(false)`. Its contents are clipped and hit-tested only where the document shows, and it stays on its paragraph. The four-wa…

title: M12: the page side of a measuring scale takes a unit, so 1:50 is 1 mm = 50 mm (#2752)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

A plan drawn at 1:50 now measures correctly when its scale is entered as 1 = 50 in millimetres. Before, a 10 mm line on the page read 1417 mm instead of 500 mm, and the reporter had to enter 1:17.5 to get the right lengths. Fixes #2752.

**Cause.** The page side of the Measure panel's drawing scale was always in PDF points. Its field had a fixed `pt` prefix, and Apply scale divided the real distance by that number of points. So "1 = 50 mm" was stored as 1 pt = 50 mm. One millimetre is 72 / 25.4 = 2.835 pt, so every length came out 2.835 times too big. To get the right lengths you had to enter 1 pt = 50 × 25.4 / 72 = 17.64 mm, which is the 1:17.5 the reporter found by trial and error.

**Fix.** The page side of the scale now has a unit, as a scale ratio on a plan does: "X unit on the page = Y unit in the real world".

- **Panel.** The `pt` prefix is replaced by a pt / in / mm / cm picker next to the page-side value. Until you pick one, it uses the real-world unit (in the Unit field). So 1 = 50 with Unit `mm` is 1 mm = 50 mm, which is what "1:50" means. When the real-world unit isn't one of the four (for example `m` or `ft`), it uses the display unit from Preferences (mm or in). Calibrate from two points fills in the page-side length in that unit, not in points. When you open the panel on a page, it shows the page's current scale as 1 page unit = its real length, instead of 72 pt = its real length.
- **Engine.** New `Scale::ratio(a, b, page, page_unit, real, unit, precision)` and `measure::PageUnit` in `crates/measure`. The page side is converted to points before the scale is built, so the PDF data keeps its meaning (ISO 32000-2 §12.9): the /X, /D and /A number formats convert user-space units to the real-world unit, here 50 / 2.835 = 17.64 mm per point. The /R ratio string keeps the units as entered: `1 mm = 50 mm` (it used to say `1 pt = 50 mm`).
- **Unchanged.** Scales read from files are used as stored (`Scale::read` is untouched), so existin…

title: M11: Optimize keeps a JPEG's colour transform (#1201)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Part of #1201: the "Optimization has a more serious problem" item (DCT `/ColorTransform` lost by Optimize). The `/Default*` colour spaces and the renderer's own CMYK/YCCK gap in #1201 are separate and not touched here.

Optimize read JPEG samples with the `image` crate's decoder. That decoder converts three components from YCbCr to RGB unless the JPEG itself says otherwise, and the rewritten image then lost its `/DecodeParms`. So an RGB JPEG stored untransformed (`/ColorTransform 0`, no Adobe marker) was converted anyway, and came out in other colours whenever Optimize touched it. That covers recompression, resampling, and merging page pictures printed as strips. In the test fixture the colours moved by 75 levels on average.

ISO 32000-2 §7.4.8 says an Adobe APP14 marker's transform flag decides, overriding `/ColorTransform`. Without a marker, `/ColorTransform` decides, and its default is 1 (YCbCr) for three components. `pdfcraft-optimize` (`images.rs`) now follows that:

- **Reading.** `pixels` finds the transform (`ycc_encoded`): it reads the APP14 flag from the JPEG's segments before the first scan, and `/ColorTransform` from `/DecodeParms`. It then decodes with `zune-jpeg` directly, the decoder `image` and the renderer already use (already in the lock; `pdfcraft-create` depends on it the same way). YCbCr samples are converted to RGB, and untransformed samples are taken as stored.
- **Writing.** Nothing changes. The new image is a plain YCbCr JPEG (no Adobe marker) or Flate, which is exactly what a missing `/DecodeParms` means, so dropping it stays correct.
- **Left as it is** when readers can disagree:
  - the marker and `/ColorTransform` contradict each other. The standard lets the marker win, but PdfCraft's renderer lets `/ColorTransform 0` win over a YCbCr marker;
  - either holds a value other than 0 or 1;
  - `/DecodeParms` isn't paired with the filter as §7.4 pairs them (a dictionary for a filter name, a one-element array for `[/DCTDe…

title: fix(forms): renaming a nested field checks the full name it would take
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

When you rename a field that has a parent, the new name is now checked against the other fields' names correctly, so it can't take one that's already in use. Before, `set_props` compared the new *partial* name with the other fields' *fully qualified* names. The check missed the clash it was there to catch, and it could also refuse a name that was free.

There's no issue for this; I found it reading the code. #2696 is related (periods in field names, and how dotted names are shown), but this PR doesn't resolve it.

**The defect.** A field's fully qualified name is its parents' partial names and its own `/T`, joined with periods (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2). A rename changes only the field's own `/T`, so `MASTER.a` renamed to `b` becomes `MASTER.b`. The duplicate check in `crates/forms/src/author.rs` compared the bare `b` with every field's full name:

- **A clash got through.** With `MASTER.a` and `MASTER.b` in the form, renaming `MASTER.a` to `b` succeeded, because no field's full name is the bare `b`. The form then held two fields with the same fully qualified name. Per the spec that is one field, so their values merge: filling one fills the other.
- **A free name was refused.** With a top-level field `c`, renaming `MASTER.a` to `c` failed with `a field named "c" already exists`, although `MASTER.c` was free.

**The fix.** The new full name (the parents' part, then the new partial name) is now computed before the check, and the check compares that. The field itself is left out of the comparison, so a kid renamed to the partial name it already has still succeeds, as before. The error now gives the full name (`a field named "MASTER.b" already exists`), so it says which field is in the way. Top-level fields behave as before, because their full name is their partial name.

Nothing else about the rename changes. It still writes only the field's own `/T`: a kid stays under its parent, a field merged with its widget stays its own widget, and a field's wid…

title: fix(ui): the Read mode command leaves Edit as the Edit tab does
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Running Read mode as a command (View ▸ Read mode, Ctrl+H / ⌃⌘H, the command search) from the Edit tab now puts Edit text & images down the way choosing another tab does. A paragraph still open in the editor is applied and its editor closes.

**The defect.** #2241 made the Edit tab turn Edit text & images on, and made leaving Edit put the tool down again through `put_down_edit_text`, which also applies a paragraph still open in the editor. That code sits in `select_mode`, which only the mode bar reaches. The Read mode command goes through `switch_mode(.., false)`, whose `else` branch only set `self.mode`. Running the command from Edit therefore entered Read mode with:

- Edit text & images still the current tool, with every paragraph and image on the page boxed for editing;
- a paragraph open in the editor still open and editable over the page (`edit_text_ui::overlay` draws whenever `line_editor` is set, whatever the tool), and its edit not applied.

**The fix.** A new `enter_mode` sets the workspace together with its tool: Edit turns Edit text & images on, and leaving Edit calls `put_down_edit_text`. `select_mode` (the mode bar, and the default workspace when a document opens) and the `select_tools == false` branch of `switch_mode` (the Read mode command) both go through it, so the two routes can't drift apart again. The Read mode command still leaves the panels alone, as before. Only the tool changes.

**Relation to open PRs.**

- **#2809** (Read mode hides the quick toolbar, #2646) sets the tool to Select when entering Read mode, on both routes. That fixes the stale tool on its own, but not the paragraph: it doesn't go through `put_down_edit_text`, so an open paragraph stays open and unapplied in Read mode. This PR is the other half. The two compose: `enter_mode` applies the paragraph and puts Edit text down first, then #2809's line resets any other tool. They touch different lines of `switch_mode`, so either can land first and the other reba…

title: fix(comments): the note editor takes the keyboard once, so V and H pick tools again
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

After you add a highlight, its note editor in the Comments panel no longer holds on to the keyboard. You can still type the note straight away, as in Acrobat. Once you click the page or draw another comment, V and H pick the Select and Hand tools again instead of being typed into the note.

Part of #2669 (item 2). The other items have their own PRs: #2704 (item 1), #2706 (item 3), #2724 (item 4) and #2805 (item 5).

**Cause.** There were two causes, and each was enough to cause the bug on its own.

- The editor asked for the keyboard on every frame, whenever no other widget had it (`comments_panel.rs`, `card`). egui gives the keyboard up when you click outside a text field, so the next frame the editor took it back. Clicking the page or the toolbar never freed the keyboard.
- Adding another comment left the editor open on the earlier highlight (`editing.rs`, `apply_edit`, `Edit::AddAnnotation`). Only another highlight replaced it. Drawing a rectangle, an oval or a pen stroke is a drag, not a click, so egui never took the keyboard from the editor during it. The rectangle was added, the empty note stayed open with the keyboard, and the next V or H was typed into it.

**Fix.**

- The editor asks for the keyboard once, when it opens. `CommentView::open_editor` sets a one-off `EditorFocus::Take` and the card uses it up the first time it draws the editor. A new highlight, a double-click on a card and the card's Edit menu item all open the editor this way. After that, the keyboard goes where the user clicks, the way `search_focus` already works for the panel's search field.
- When a comment is added, `CommentView::comment_added` closes an empty editor left on another comment. An editor that already has text in it stays open with that text, so nothing typed is lost, but it gives the keyboard back (`EditorFocus::Release`, which calls `surrender_focus` the next time it draws). A new highlight then opens its own note as before, unless a note with text is …

title: M5: sticky notes stay upright where they are placed on rotated pages (NoRotate, #2583)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

On a page with `/Rotate`, a new sticky note's icon came out turned with the page (#2583: the bubble is "rotated 90 degrees"). It also did not start where it was clicked: the click was a different corner of the turned icon.

**Cause.** PdfCraft saves notes (and file attachments) with the NoRotate flag (`/F` bit 5), and draws their icon in an unturned 20 × 20 box. ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3 says what a viewer does with that flag: the appearance does not turn with the page, and the upper-left corner of `/Rect` stays where it is on the page. Neither the note's appearance nor the vendored renderer did anything with the flag. hayro-interpret fitted the appearance to `/Rect` (Algorithm 8.1) and the page turn rotated it with everything else.

**Why the renderer, not the appearance.** Rubber stamps (#1398) and typed text (#1710) are counterrotated in their appearance with a form `/Matrix`. That works for them because they do not carry NoRotate. A note does, so a counterrotated appearance would be turned twice by every viewer that honours the flag, and would still be wrong once the page is turned again later or for notes other programs wrote. Only the renderer knows both the flag and the page's current `/Rotate`. hayro-interpret is also where the other display flags are honoured: Hidden upstream, and NoView by an earlier PdfCraft patch.

**Fix.**
- **Renderer** (vendored hayro-interpret, patch 37, with a `vendor/README.md` entry). For an annotation with NoRotate, the appearance fitted to `/Rect` is then turned against the page's rotation about the rectangle's upper-left corner `(x0, y1)`. As displayed, the icon's top-left is that corner, and its width runs across and its height down, as on an unturned page. Form fields and links are left in `/Rect`, because PdfCraft takes their click targets from it (see below).
- **Where the note is drawn, for everything that points at it.** `pdfcraft_render::Annotation` (and `pdfcraft_annot::Summary`) gain `no_rotate`, and `A…

title: fix(ui): the Hand tool moves the page with the pointer
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

With the Hand tool, the page now stays under the pointer point for point, in the same frame the pointer moves. Before, it trailed behind the pointer and stuttered. Fixes #924. #1992 asks for a "mouse sensitivity" setting for the same tool. The cause there is the same lag (the reply on that issue says the hand "just needs to follow the mouse cursor"), so this should cover it too.

**Cause.** The Hand tool panned with `ui.scroll_with_delta(resp.drag_delta())` from inside the page view's `ScrollArea`. egui applies that delta in `ScrollArea::end`, after the frame's pages have been laid out and drawn. So every move showed up a frame late. Until #1986 made the page view's `ScrollArea` `animated(false)` (merged 2026-10-15, after these issues were filed), that delta was also eased in over several frames, with the target moving on every frame. That was the stutter. On top of that, the page widget senses both clicks and drags. egui only marks it dragged once the pointer has gone further than a click may wander (6 points). The points moved before that were never scrolled, so the page never caught up with where it had been grabbed.

**Fix.** The pan now runs before the `ScrollArea` lays the pages out, through `ScrollArea::scroll_offset`. When the page widget is being dragged with the Hand tool, the new offset is the last frame's offset minus this frame's pointer delta. On the frame egui recognises the drag, it subtracts everything the pointer has moved since the press instead. The offset is clamped to the content, as egui clamps it, so pulling past an end doesn't show the page there for a frame and spring it back. The page widget's id is kept from the previous frame, so the drag can be found before the widget is laid out again.

Unchanged:
- Clicks inside the click distance still don't move the page, so a right-click for the context menu doesn't nudge it.
- Letting go still stops the page where it is. The Hand tool had no fling and doesn't get one; egui's …

title: fix(web): host mode can wait for the page to confirm a save (opt-in, #1792)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

In host mode (`?host=parent`), a save counts as done as soon as `pdfcraft:save` is posted. The document is marked saved, the leave-page warning goes, and Save in the "save changes?" prompt closes the document at once. If the page has no listener, fails its upload, or navigates away, the edits are gone and nothing can bring the closed editor back. Fixes #1792.

This adds an **opt-in** acknowledgement. A page that answers saves says so once, and from then on a document counts as saved only when the page says it stored the file:

| Message | Direction | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `pdfcraft:init` (new, optional) | from the page | `acknowledgeSaves: true`, `saveTimeoutMs` (optional, default 120000, kept between 1000 and 3600000) |
| `pdfcraft:save` | to the page | `name`, `saveAs`, `bytes`, and, after `acknowledgeSaves`, `saveId` (an opaque string) |
| `pdfcraft:saved` (new) | from the page | `saveId`: the file of that save is stored |
| `pdfcraft:save-failed` (new) | from the page | `saveId`, `error` (a string the user sees) |

With the opt-in:

- The document keeps its unsaved state until `pdfcraft:saved` names the save's `saveId`, so `pdfcraft:dirty` stays `true` and the browser keeps warning before leaving.
- Save in the "save changes?" prompt (closing a tab, Close all) closes the document only then.
- `pdfcraft:save-failed`, or no answer within `saveTimeoutMs`, leaves the document open and unsaved with the notice "Couldn't save *name*: *error*" (or "...: the website did not confirm that it stored the file"). The user can save again, and a late answer for that save is ignored.
- The answer is bound to the version that was saved. If the user edits while the page stores the file, `pdfcraft:saved` leaves the newer edits unsaved and does not close the document. Typing not yet committed to a field also keeps it open.
- An answer whose `saveId` matches no waiting save (another save's, one already answered, made up) changes nothing. Ids start with a rand…

title: fix(render): draw each ICC profile through itself when two have the same stream dictionary (vendored hayro-interpret patch 40)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

No issue was filed for this. I found it while fixing #1201: its tests use several synthetic ICC profiles of the same length in one document, and some of them drew through the wrong profile.

**The defect.** The vendored hayro-interpret caches the colour space it builds from an `/ICCBased` profile stream in the interpreter's object cache. The key was `icc_stream.cache_key()`, and for a stream that is the hash of its **dictionary's bytes only**. Two different profiles whose dictionaries are byte for byte the same therefore shared one entry. That is common: `<< /N 3 /Length 3144 >>` describes any two uncompressed RGB profiles of one size. Whichever profile was read first won, and colours in the second space were converted through the first profile. The cache lives as long as the document, so this affected every page drawn after the first read, not just one page.

**The fix** (hayro-interpret patch 40, recorded in `vendor/README.md`). The space is now keyed by what its profile is read from (`IccProfileKey`), in two steps:

- **By object.** A space that names its profile stream by reference (`[/ICCBased 7 0 R]`, the normal case) is looked up by that object first. A lookup that hits does not read or hash the stream, so repeated lookups (every image drawn in an ICC space calls this) cost what they cost before.
- **By content.** On a miss, the space is looked up by the old dictionary key plus the stream's own bytes, decrypted but not decoded. Those bytes and the dictionary's filters decide the decoded profile, and the dictionary decides `/N` and `/Alternate`, so this key covers every input. A byte-for-byte copy of a profile in another object (merged documents often carry one per page) still shares one parsed profile and one transform.
- **Streams written directly in the array.** A stream written inside the colour space array has no object of its own. Its dictionary reports the object that holds the array, which every other stream written there reports …

title: fix(print): pages with Type 3 fonts go to Windows printers as pictures (#2684)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Printing to a printer on Windows no longer hands the Windows print component pages that draw with Type 3 fonts. Those pages are rendered by PdfCraft at the Print as image resolution (300 dpi unless changed in Advanced) and sent as pictures; every other page of the job stays vector, as before. Fixes #2684.

**Why.** @mtlcl410 reproduced the crash on Windows 11 with a virtual printer (FinePrint) and narrowed it to the Type 3 font Chrome wrote for the recipe's text: a glyph followed by code `0x0F` was enough. Windows.Data.Pdf renders the same page fine on its own, so the crash is in the print path (Windows.Data.Pdf drawing into Direct2D's print control, through craft-print). It is native (`0xC0000094` or `0xC0000005`), so nothing in PdfCraft can catch it and the whole app closes. Print as image (#1965) avoided it. This takes direction 2 of that comment: only the pages that need it become pictures, and only on Windows.

**How.**
- `pdfcraft_print::type3_pages(doc, pages, content)` finds the pages whose print draws with a Type 3 font. It reads resources, not content streams: the page's fonts (inherited ones too), and through form XObjects (forms in forms), tiling patterns, soft-mask groups (a shading pattern's too) and the appearances of the annotations that print under the chosen Comments & Forms. It never panics and is bounded: a seen-set per page, a depth limit (64) and a budget of 20,000 reads per page. A page whose resources go past the limit or the budget counts as using a Type 3 font, because the picture is the safe side. Broken entries (a `/Resources` that is a number, missing objects, a `/SMask` that is `/None`, cyclic forms) are not Type 3 fonts.
- `print::Settings::type3_raster: Option<Raster>` asks for this. `Session::print_pdf` renders the pages found the same way Print as image does (`print_raster::pictures`, sharing its render step with `rasterize`) and `pdfcraft_print::impose_with_pictures` draws each picture in its page's place, ove…

title: fix(ui): on-page text editors leave the mode tabs their pointer when scrolled under them
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Follows up #2755. The fix for #2755 handled the Edit text paragraph editor. Three other editors on the page had the same problem: the form text field editor, the Fill & Sign text box and the Add text box. Scroll the page up so one of them lies under the mode bar (All tools panel closed) and the Read, Edit, Convert and E-Sign tabs showed its I-beam. A click on a tab went to the editor, so the mode didn't change.

**Why.** Each editor is a foreground `egui::Area` placed at its spot on the page. egui keeps an `Area` inside the window by default, not inside the document view. So when the page scrolled under the mode bar, the editor was drawn over the tabs and hit-tested there. It sits above everything on the page's layer, so its `TextEdit` set the I-beam and took the click. Two of the tools also set their own page cursor from egui's raw hover position, tested only against the page's whole rectangle. That rectangle runs on under the chrome once the page is scrolled:

- **Form text fields** (`forms_ui::page_input`): the field's I-beam (or the hand, or the not-allowed sign) over any field under the tabs, open or not.
- **Add text** (`content_ui::page_input`): the tool's I-beam over the empty page, and the four-way arrow or a resize arrow over added text.

Fill & Sign already gates its page cursor on `resp.contains_pointer()`.

**The fix**, the same as for the Edit text paragraph editor in #2755:

- The three editors' `Area`s are `constrain_to(view.viewport_rect()).constrain(false)`. They are clipped and hit-tested only where the document shows. They stay where they belong on the page, cut off as the page is, rather than being pushed back into the window. Add text already had `.constrain(false)`.
- The form field and Add text cursors are set only while the pages' own widget `contains_pointer()`, which egui clips to the visible document area. That is the check Fill & Sign uses. What these functions return, and the clicks and drags they take, are unchang…

title: M10: exported images keep the page's CMYK and ICC colours (#2269)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2269.

The issue doesn't include the comparison image, so I built a synthetic PDF for each common kind of image. For each one I compared the centre pixel the page renderer draws with the same pixel in the exported file. Export all images, Save Image As and Word export all write images through `pdfcraft_create::image_file`, so they had the same problem.

Two things were wrong:

- **CMYK.** Export converted CMYK with its own formula, `(1 − c)(1 − k)`. The page converts it through the renderer's CMYK profile. Cyan ink came out as (0, 255, 255) where the page draws (0, 174, 239). Magenta was up to 115 levels off, and black ink came out pure black.
- **ICC profiles.** Export ignored `ICCBased` profiles: an Adobe RGB or Display P3 image came out as if it were sRGB, about 30 levels off.

Some JPEGs were also written as they are, so viewers and Word showed them in other colours: CMYK JPEGs, and JPEGs drawn through an ICC profile the file doesn't carry.

The fix reuses the renderer's own conversion rather than writing a second one:

- **Vendored hayro-interpret patch (39).** `color::device_cmyk_to_srgb` and `color::IccToSrgb` make public the conversions the renderer already uses for DeviceCMYK and `ICCBased`. Both check that input and output hold the same number of pixels.
- **`pdfcraft-render` wrapper.** `pdfcraft_render::cmyk_to_srgb` and `IccProfile` wrap them, catching panics like the rest of the crate. This keeps hayro behind `pdfcraft-render`, the bootstrap rule (ADR-0004).
- **`pdfcraft-create` (`extract.rs`).** Image export now depends on `pdfcraft-render` (L4 → L3, which `xtask layers` allows) and converts through it:
  - DeviceCMYK;
  - `ICCBased` grey, RGB and CMYK;
  - indexed palettes over those spaces, converted once;
  - 16-bit and inverted CMYK;
  - `/Matte` colours, now converted like the image, the way the renderer does.
- **JPEGs written as they are.** A JPEG is still written unchanged when the file shows the page's colours:
  …

title: fix(ui): the watermark and background previews show a file's picture (#2817)
author: guillehr2
body:
> Builds on #3009, the #2837 fix (branch `fix/2837-preview-page-content`: the marks dialogs' preview draws the page's own thumbnail). Merge that one first; this branch is one commit on top of it.

## What this changes

Item 14 of #2817, "Watermark Preview Show Image and PDF Content".

In **Add/Update Watermark** and **Add Background**, Source ▸ File (an image, or a page of a PDF) was previewed as a grey frame with the file name. You couldn't see how big the picture would come out, where an offset put it, or how its turn and opacity looked. The preview now draws the picture itself, where OK puts it.

- **Rendered the way OK brings it in.** A new engine function, `pdfcraft_engine::mark_picture`, takes the file through the same `mark_source` path OK uses: an image turned upright by its EXIF orientation (JPEG 2000, CMYK, TIFF's first page included), or a PDF page as a form, upright after `/Rotate`. It draws the picture alone on a page of its shape with `pdfcraft_edit::add_watermark` and renders it small (512 px a side for the preview). It renders twice, on white paper and over black, and takes the transparency from the difference. A PNG's alpha and whatever a PDF page leaves unpainted come through as transparent, while white the page really paints stays opaque. A file OK would refuse is refused here too.

author: guillehr2
body:

body:

Builds on #2771 (Verify PDF/UA): **stacked on `feat/pdfua-validate`**, one commit on top. Until that merges, this PR's diff includes it; rebase once it lands.

title: M11: Save as PDF/X-1a converts Lab, Cal, spot alternates, shadings and pictures of any depth (optimize.pdfx-convert)
author: guillehr2
body:
> **Stacked on Save as PDF/X** (storytold/pdfcraft#2777, branch `feat/pdfx-pdfa-convert`, itself on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR). This branch is cut from it at `bcea9dd0`. Review and merge those first; this diff then shrinks to the colour conversion.

## What this changes

Save as PDF/X-1a converts RGB and ICC-based colour to CMYK, and until now refused everything else: shadings, Lab, CalRGB and CalGray, spot colours with RGB or device-independent alternates, and pictures that weren't 8-bit or had a decode array. It now converts all of these. As before, the conversion runs on a copy and is kept only when PdfCraft's PDF/X verifier finds nothing. **What can't be converted exactly still refuses**, and the refusal names the reason.

`optimize.pdfx-convert` stays partial, with its notes rewritten.

- **CalGray, CalRGB and Lab** (ISO 32000-2 8.6.5.2–8.6.5.4) convert through ICC profiles made from their parameters (`icc.rs`):

  - Lab goes through a version 4 Lab profile that passes values straight to the connection space, after the values are adapted from the space's white to D50.

  `DefaultRGB` may be CalRGB too. A `BlackPoint` isn't compensated, as relative colorimetry doesn't.

title: fix(ocr): the text layer restores the rendering mode it sets (#3029)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3029. Thanks to @monkeyhut for the precise diagnosis.

`pdfcraft_ocr::text_layer` wrote its invisible text as

```
/OCR BMC
BT
3 Tr
/PCHelv 1 Tf
…
ET
EMC
```

The text rendering mode (`Tr`) and the font (`Tf`) are part of the graphics state, and `ET` doesn't reset them (ISO 32000-2 §9.3.1). `stamp` appends the layer as its own content stream, and a page's content streams share one graphics state, so every stream after the layer started in `3 Tr` (invisible). A header or footer added after OCR was in the file and `text` returned it, but neither PdfCraft nor MuPDF drew it.

The layer is now `/OCR BMC q BT … ET Q EMC`: the `q … Q` sits inside the marked content and restores the graphics state before anything later on the page runs.

**Not covered here.** Files already saved by 0.8.0 with an OCR layer still carry the unbalanced layer, so text added to them later would still be invisible. The issue's second suggestion is for the writers of added text (header/footer, watermark, `page_add_text`) to set `0 Tr` themselves. That would cover those files and any producer that leaves `Tr` set, but it touches several writers, so I've left it for a follow-up. Happy to send it.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-ocr -- --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ocr --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ocr --lib`: 10 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine ocr`: passes
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK

**New test.** `the_layer_restores_the_graphics_state_it_changes` walks the layer's tokens. It checks that every `Tr`, `Tf` and `Tm` sits inside a `q … Q` and that the nesting ends balanced. With the fix reverted (the old `BT … ET` bytes), it fails with `` `Tr` outside q … Q ``.

**Render check.** A synthetic page has two content streams: the OCR layer, then `q /Artifact BMC BT /PCHelv 20 Tf 0 g 10 10 Td (Header) Tj ET EMC Q`, the shape the issue shows for the header. Dark pixels at 72 dpi:

title: fix(render): draw missing Cyrillic glyphs in non-embedded fonts (#2908)
author: robertobulltech
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2908. Non-embedded ArialMT, Arial-BoldMT, Calibri and TimesNewRomanPSMT now draw the complete Bulgarian text in the reporter's original synthetic PDF.

Decoding already worked: CLI extraction returned the complete text on unchanged main, but the bundled standard-14 CFF substitutes mapped the Cyrillic names to `.notdef`, whose outline is suppressed. A font-level resolver cannot choose an alternate for an individual missing character.

Hayro PdfCraft patch (34) adds `FontQuery::MissingGlyph` and bounded per-code outline/face caches in the non-embedded simple-font path. Encoding/Differences names (including afii and uni/u names) take precedence; single-scalar ToUnicode is a last resort. Supported primary glyphs, Unicode aliases and existing accent composites retain priority. Alternate outlines fit the PDF advance; spacing operators, transforms, baseline and extraction remain with the original font. Alternate programs are never exposed as embedded data. Known printable text without a usable outline gets an original missing-glyph box; controls/default-ignorables remain invisible, and multi-scalar semantic mappings are not guessed into a first-character outline. Malformed Differences indices also saturate instead of overflowing.

The renderer supplies existing approved OFL Inter Regular/SemiBold and JetBrains Mono; optional approved Mincho faces preserve serif where coverage permits. No new font binaries, installed-font lookup, network access or document-writing path. Resolver bytes/coverage are lazy and shared; each simple font has at most 256 cached mappings and eight parsed alternate faces. The vendored seam is documented for separate upstream submission.

title: fix(render): mesh triangles that share an edge leave no seam
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

No issue was filed. I found this while reviewing #3020: a synthetic Type 4 (free-form triangle mesh) shading drew a pure white line along the diagonal where its two triangles meet.

**The defect.** `TriangleSampler::sample_one` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/encode.rs`) fills a mesh shading pixel by pixel. For each pixel it tests the pixel's corner `(x, y)` with `Triangle::contains_point`, which uses `kurbo`'s winding number and so is strict on edges. A corner that lies exactly on an edge two triangles share belongs to neither of them. That pixel gets no sample and is drawn in the shading's background (none, so white). The same happens to corners on the mesh's own sides. Shared edges that run through the sample grid are common: axis-aligned and 45° cuts of a grid, and any lattice (Type 5) or patch (Types 6/7) mesh, whose triangle grids are regular.

A red 30 × 30 square from 10 to 40 on a 50 × 50 page, cut along its diagonal, drawn with `sh` at 72 dpi:

| | MuPDF | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| two triangles, red pixels | 900 | 812 | 900 |
| the upper-left triangle alone | 465 | 406 | 465 |

**The fix** (hayro-interpret patch 41, listed in `vendor/README.md`):

- `Triangle::covers` is a barycentric point test that includes the edges, within 1e-9. A degenerate triangle covers nothing, because its zero denominator gives NaN or infinite coordinates that fail the test.
- A pixel whose corner no triangle holds strictly goes to the triangle that covers its **centre**, edges included.
- It still takes the colour **at its corner**, like every other pixel, and only if no triangle that holds the corner strictly gives it one (`entry().or_insert_with`).

So every pixel that was drawn before keeps exactly its colour. Only the pixels that were missing are filled. On the existing Coons and tensor fixtures from `patch_meshes_keep_their_corner_colours`, every pixel is unchanged from `main` (mean difference from MuPDF 0.58/255, max 2, the same as `main`).…
